News.title: BA jet packed with 256 passengers in heart-stopping near-miss with mystery ‘UFO’ at 5,800ft after leaving Heathrow
News.content:
'TOO CLOSE FOR COMFORT' BA jet packed with 256 passengers in heart-stopping near-miss with mystery ‘UFO’ at 5,800ft after leaving Heathrow







Next

A BRITISH Airways plane came within yards of crashing into a UFO at 5,800ft, a report said.

The pilot contacted air traffic control after the mystery shiny silver object “the size of four toasters” whizzed past.

It was heading in the opposite direction, “very close” to the right wing and around 50ft above it.

The close call happened on June 24 over Guildford, Surrey, shortly after the Boeing 777-300ER took off from Heathrow for New York.





The plane, carrying 256 passengers, continued on to its destination.

But the UK Airprox Board launched an official probe into the incident.

An Airprox report said: “The B777 pilot reports that they were climbing to altitude 6000ft on departure from LHR.

“Passing 5800ft, a shiny silver object passed in the opposite direction, very fast and very close to the right wing of the aircraft at no more than 50ft above aircraft altitude.”



It added: “The LTCC controller reports that [the pilot of the B777] reported that a drone had just flown over their right wing.

“They said it was moving very fast, was probably of silver colour, metallic and reflective.

“After an enquiry as to its size, the [pilot] reported to them that it was about the “size of four toasters”.

It went on: “In the Board’s opinion the reported altitude and/or description of the object were such that they were unable to determine the nature of the unknown object.



“The Board considered that providence had played a major part in the incident and/or a definite risk of collision had existed.”

Just days before the scare, an A320 pilot coming in to Heathrow ducked in fright when his jet also came within yards of a dark UFO.

And in February an RAF pilot was shocked when a UFO whizzed past during refuelling.

News.title: Thank God Thomas Markle didn’t walk Meghan down aisle… his failure to attend is now the best outcome for her & royals
News.content:
Next

NO daddy’s girl wants their father to be missing from their wedding day.

But Thomas Markle being absent from Meghan’s big day in Windsor was an absolute blessing.

And it will be one of the few things that will give her some real comfort right now.





The fallout began when he posed for those ridiculous paparazzi photos just days before she and Prince Harry were due to walk down the aisle.

She was undoubtedly angry.

And she would have been raging when her father then lied to her about them.

I am sure she wasn’t best pleased when he and her notoriously hot-headed fiancé managed to have such a humdinger of a row that he slammed the phone down.

Then when he claimed to have had a heart attack that stopped him attending her big day, she must have been so worried.

But looking back, this sequence of events has turned out to be one of the best possible outcomes for her — and our Royal Family.

It meant that she glided down that aisle in St George’s Chapel on the arm of the future King, rather than someone now accused of possessing a collection of child sex abuse images.

There are no wedding photos of her and Harry’s family smiling and chatting to the man who is now engulfed in scandal.

At the time she would have been utterly devastated because then she didn’t know about the allegations; she just knew that the Daddy she adored had betrayed her so publicly.





And undoubtedly felt such sadness that he wasn’t at her side sharing her joy.

But what a relief now. Every bride deserves to look back on that pivotal day in their life with happiness and joy. Thankfully, she can.

At least that means this event wasn’t tarnished for her.

Because there will be so many happy memories that are now destroyed for this poor woman.

It began not long after, when she was shown that letter by the police with “disturbing allegations” against her dad about “child sex abuse”.

Her world would have crashed down around her.

She would have been distraught. It would have been torturous for her.

Maybe Megxit in 2020 was a way to try and run away from her old life, as she struggled to trust anybody and lashed out at others to deal with her own hurt.

Maybe speaking about him afterwards was some kind of therapy.

Only Meghan truly knows.

It was in 2021, during her CBS television interview with Oprah Winfrey, that she opened up about their estrangement saying, “I grieve a lot. I mean, I’ve lost my father.”



No matter the circumstances, it would be impossible not to grieve.

She couldn’t talk about it because of any possible investigation but, looking back, maybe it speaks volumes about what was going on behind the scenes.

A year later, in their Netflix series, she said: “I was a daddy’s girl my whole life . . .”

Now her critics are picking over that and slamming her for it, but why shouldn’t she say that?

That is a fact. A sad one for Meghan but a true one: she was always a daddy’s girl. Another fact is you can never eradicate the past.

So although Meghan would have once dearly wanted Thomas Markle to walk her down the aisle.

She will be so relieved that he didn’t.

HIT M&S KYLIE

WHOEVER measured Kylie Jenner up for that $50million diamond-encrusted Fantasy Bra for the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show deserves to be sacked.

Yes, of course, it was beautiful and, yes, of course, she looked incredibly sexy.



But couldn’t they have made sure it fitted?

It was digging in awkwardly at the sides and her boobs were bulging out at the top.

If she was getting measured up by the lingerie ladies at M&S, they’d have told her to whip it off and go up a size . . . or two.

GREEN FRENCH FANCY

HAVE you felt inspired by the protests in France? I know I have.

If I see cars being burned, shops looted, homes destroyed and livelihoods lost, I am inspired to run for safety in the opposite direction as fast as I can.

But the Green Party’s youth wing thinks very differently from me.

The Hackney Greens shared an extraordinary message from one of their councillors urging those “inspired by protests in France” to join the “march against austerity” on the eve of next week’s Budget.

To legitimise and condone riots is mind-blowing and irresponsible.

Those terrifying scenes abroad, which saw thousands of masked rioters arrested, proved some people simply love violence, smashing shopfronts and looting for the fun of it.



It may have started over education, the rising cost of living and soaring fuel prices, but it ended with mindless thugs having an excuse to riot.

Now loony lefties are encouraging protests here and to back the “brave students abroad”.

A legitimate protest is challenging, moderate and mature. Violent riots are for pathetic thugs.

Encouraging that behaviour here is terrifying because, as Kemi Badenoch has made clear, we don’t have enough police to cope with widespread unrest.

She told the Police Federation of England and Wales annual conference that she wants to get more officers on the streets.

She’s right. And if the Greens keep pushing for riots, we will need them more than ever.

OH, to be a teacher. Under bonkers new Labour plans to introduce “flexibility” into working patterns, they could meet their requirement of clocking up 195 days a year by doing longer hours over four days. Nice.

Who doesn’t love a four-day week? Parents certainly don’t want their kids to lose any time in the classroom.

So unless the pupils stay at school longer over those four days, the teachers won’t have anyone to teach, will they? That’s one way to attract lazy new recruits.

BIG BREKKIE TO MAX… DISCOMFORT



MAX Stanford is a competitive eater – and surely a liar, too.

After polishing off 14 sausages, 14 bacon rashers, 14 fried eggs, 14 hash browns, ten black pudding slices, toast, beans and mushrooms in 30 minutes, Max said: “Right until the end I was still enjoying it.”

No you weren’t, Max. I’ve got a stomach ache just thinking about it.

HOW refreshing that, like me, James McAvoy has got a memory like a sieve.

The Scottish actor has revealed his sister once asked who he’d most like to meet and work with.

He replied “Margot Robbie” only to be reminded that he’d previously met the Barbie star at an awards ceremony where they got so giddy they were “stealing each other’s shoes and chucking them behind the DJ booth”.

Sounds like a fun night. Shame he can’t remember it.



AGEING happens to us all, and you’ve just got to roll with it, like Liam Gallagher.

He has a new hobby that will happily see him through into retirement – metal detecting.

He says: “I do it for the buzz ’n’ the bing.” The Oasis frontman used to get that from other things, and it wasn’t just cigarettes and alcohol.

DEFENCE Secretary Wes Streeting says we should have three days’ worth of non-perishable goods at home in case of severe weather or cyber-attacks.

In my house those kitchen cupboards would be empty again within hours.

I’d go down the Angela Rayner route and have sauvignon blanc in my emergency kit.

During times of strife, it’s an essential.

AFTER slamming the decision by the BBC last week to ditch DIY SOS, I am thrilled a petition has been set up to get it back on our screens.

Maybe if Nick Knowles pitched the show to another channel, the BBC could realise what idiots they have been. After all, it worked a treat for The Great British Bake Off.

While we’re at it, let’s get Miranda Hart back on The Traitors. Seeing her skipping around the castle has been a joy.

News.title: We now know Meghan protecting her kids was not her being ‘difficult’ – under these circumstances who could blame her?
News.content:
Next

WHEN the British public were denied the customary first glimpse of baby Archie, we were more than a little peeved.

For generations, the arrival of a royal baby had been celebrated directly with the nation from the hospital steps.



But the Duchess of Sussex was having none of that.

Today, viewed against the backdrop of devastating allegations against her father, Thomas Markle Snr, can we truly blame her?



Archie arrived four months after she received a letter in January 2019 containing allegations that her father was a child abuser.

She and Harry were still carrying out royal engagements, and one can only imagine her distress at receiving such news while preparing to become a mother for the first time.

With the benefit of hindsight, that disclosure is significant.

Viewed in light of the police probe in the Philippines, Meghan’s shielding of her children now takes on a different complexion.

The private christenings, the obscured photographs, and their absence from royal pageantry were never simply a case of being “difficult.”

In retrospect, we see a mother determined to build a wall around her family — protecting her young children despite relentless pressure.



Meghan placed family before royal duty. Under such terrifying circumstances, who could fault her?

I feel immense sympathy for her predicament.

To confront monstrous allegations against one’s own father — which he vehemently denies — inevitably provokes profound mistrust. It is little wonder her emotional drawbridge went up.



Two days after Archie’s birth, on May 8, 2019, Harry and Meghan appeared inside Windsor Castle for a brief photocall.

Archie was bundled tightly in a white blanket and cap, offering barely a glimpse.

Only when a photographer asked to see him was the blanket eased back.

When an official photo of Archie meeting Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip was released, the staging felt similarly guarded.

His christening two months later followed the same pattern. While royal baptisms are private, the Press is customarily allowed to photograph arrivals and departures.



Barring cameras frustrated the media and hardened public sentiment.

The pattern persisted after Lilibet’s birth in June 2021.

The first public image of her did not appear until six months later on the Sussexes’ Christmas card.



To this day, both kids remain protected, with faces obscured in birthday photos.

Meghan has faced persistent criticism for declining to adhere to traditional royal expectations.

Yet recent revelations may soften opinions toward a figure who has been so heavily maligned.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And as the police investigation proceeds, she will know, once the wheels of justice have turned, whether her instincts to protect her children were right all along.

News.title: Meghan ‘concerned’ over Met cops’ failure to act on letter as ex royal protection chief calls decision ‘extraordinary’
News.content:
Next

THE Duchess of Sussex was tonight “concerned” that the Met Police did not act on a ­letter accusing her estranged father of child sexual abuse.

Meghan said she was told its contents were looked into but the force — sent the note in January 2019 — admitted that it did not notify any other relevant police force.



A friend of the mother of two told The Sun on Sunday: “She’s concerned that they didn’t do anything with it seven years ago.

“They had the opportunity to pass it on to other relevant law enforcement agencies but chose not to.”



Dai Davies, former head of the Scotland Yard’s Royalty Protection Unit, said: “I’m gobsmacked the Met didn’t inform US authorities about the letter and its contents.

“It’s extraordinary that they didn’t think it should be acted on.”



Following The Sun’s world exclusive revealing Thomas Markle Snr was under investigation, Meghan said that a letter containing “troubling and disturbing” allegations was shared with her in 2018.

In fact, the Met’s Fixated Threat Assessment Centre received the undated letter in January 2019, eight months after Meghan married Prince Harry at Windsor Castle.

It is understood it was addressed to the unit as it assesses intelligence on obsessives feared to be a risk to the Royal Family and VIPs.

The letter, seen by The Sun on Sunday, raised concerns about the Sussexes’ safety and accused Markle Snr, now 82, and another person of being a serious risk to them.



The author also said Markle Snr had sexually abused a child and said he wanted to go to Thailand or the Philippines to have sex with youngsters.

The age of consent in the Philippines at that time was 12.

On Friday, the Met said it could not confirm if any such document had been shared with Meghan.



Yesterday, it acknowledged that, following a thorough review of systems and records, it received a letter in January 2019 detailing alleged offending outside the UK.

The Met added: “The letter was reviewed and a decision was made that it should be passed to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness.

“The details of the allegations in the letter were not shared with other law enforcement agencies.”

The force said it is “reviewing the handling of this matter in 2019” and may contact the Independent Office for Police Conduct.

A friend of Meghan, 45, said the Duchess was “pleased” the Met was considering referring itself to the watchdog.



Explaining Meghan’s confusion regarding the date she saw the letter, a spokesman said: “In recalling events from more than seven years ago, without the benefit of a diary entry or contemporaneous record, it is understandable that she may have been mistaken by a few months.

“If the MPS holds a time-stamped record confirming that the letter was reviewed in 2019, that should be treated as the accurate reference point for when it was received and shared with the Duchess.”

The Met said previously that it had not investigated Markle Snr after he was identified in the letter.

It had no jurisdiction to do so as the child abuse offences alleged took place outside the UK.

Former royal protection boss Mr Davies said: “The Met should’ve done everything possible to verify the letter’s legitimacy and notified relevant legal enforcement authorities abroad of the contents. I’d have notified the liaison officer to the FBI at the American Embassy in London. I find it incredible that it was left effectively untouched.



“Given that Meghan was married into the Royal Family there was also their reputational aspect to consider and, more important than anything, child protection.”

He questioned why Meghan and Harry had not pursued the matter with US authorities.

A source said Meghan could not speak publicly to avoid jeopardising any investigation and doing so could have led to legal action against her.

Meghan was able to speak out after we revealed an alleged horde of child porn had been found by his son Thomas Markle Jnr, 60, at their father’s old home in the Philippines. He told the FBI.

In a statement, she said: “Any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children was for one reason: to protect them.



“Although the breadth of what’s now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served.”

Markle Snr moved to the Philippines in 2025.

His left leg was amputated in December and he is convalescing in Florida.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Meghan wrote to him after the operation when he said he did not want to die while estranged from her.

He called the child abuse allegations “sick lies”.

News.title: I know you are an abuser… you will never see your grandkids – What Meghan Markle told dad Thomas in last letter to him
News.content:
Next

THE Duchess of Sussex told her estranged father she knew he had abused young girls in a letter she sent him last year, The Sun on Sunday can reveal.

Meghan, 45, told 82-year-old Thomas Markle Snr it would be the last time he ever heard from her — and that she would never allow him to meet his grandchildren.



It is understood she accused him of sexually abusing children and said that the authorities were aware of his vile behaviour.

Meghan learned of allegations in 2019 but was given assurances these were being investigated. She was advised speaking out could jeopardise any potential legal case.



Markle Snr received the letter while in hospital in the Philippines after his leg was amputated in December 2025.

At the time, Meghan came in for flak for failing to contact her estranged father while he was so ill.

To ensure she knew he had read the letter, she arranged for hospital management to take it to his bedside. Markle Snr was made to sign a form confirming receipt and was videoed accepting it, and read it several times.

The bombshell revelations came as the Met Police was last night under scrutiny for failing to investigate child-sex claims made in a 2019 letter.



Meghan said she was “concerned” no action had been taken by Scotland Yard to alert other authorities.

The Met said it would look at referring itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct watchdog.

The Sun told in a world exclusive on Friday how Markle Snr’s son Thomas Jnr, 60, had found boxes of alleged child-abuse images and delivered them to police.



IMeghan’s half-brother begged for her forgiveness after siding with their dad in a series of public spats — then discovering an alleged hoard of child abuse images linked to their father.

Thomas Markle Jnr mocked the Duchess of Sussex on social media and his own YouTube channel, even donning a wig and dress to impersonate her in rows amid her marriage to Prince Harry in 2018.

Thomas Jnr, who had been caring for frail Thomas Markle Snr for four years at a house in the Philippines, spoke to The Sun on Sunday after handing over four boxes of vile images to child protection cops in Cebu City.

The 60-year-old window fitter said: “I’m so, so sorry Meghan.

“I now know I have been protecting the wrong person for the past nine years.



“Having seen what I have seen, I believe the man I’ve been defending and caring for is a monster.

“I now know exactly why you don’t talk to him any more and why you won’t let him meet Harry or his grandchildren.

“And I’m ashamed that I spent years taking his side when you fell out with him.



“I know we’re not close but I can still remember holding you when you were a baby and looking after you when you were small.

“So please accept my apology and know that I wish you and your family all the best for the future.”

Thomas Jnr found the haul while 82-year-old Markle Snr was receiving medical treatment in the US.

It emerged the alleged stash of sick material included an image of Markle Snr having sex with a girl who appears underage.

Following The Sun breaking the story in a world exclusive, Meghan, 45, disclosed she had been told “troubling and disturbing” claims about her father shortly after her marriage to Harry.



And a close friend of Meghan said she was “relieved” that her father is finally being properly investigated.

News.title: Zookeeper in critical condition after ‘being attacked by leopard’ as horrified staff heard ‘cry for help’ from enclosure
News.content:
ZOO ATTACK Zookeeper in critical condition after ‘being attacked by leopard’ as horrified staff heard ‘cry for help’ from enclosure







Next

A ZOOKEEPER has been left in critical condition after being mauled by a leopard, reports say.

The woman was found inside an enclosure this morning with severe head wounds as horrified colleagues reportedly heard her crying for help.

Emergency services including a helicopter rushed to Beekse Bergen in Hilvarenbeek, the Netherlands.

They raced the injured woman, in her 50s, to hospital following the ordeal at around 11am local time.





She is currently undergoing surgery, according to local media.

Reports say the attack unfolded at an indoor enclosure, where the animals were being kept due to a storm on Friday evening.

Head of Animal Care at the zoo Martin van Hees said the victim, who is reportedly from Belgium, was always very alert in terms of safety.

He said: “At this moment, the woman is in the hospital and is undergoing surgery; her condition is worrying.



“We know there is a risk when working with dangerous animals, but you never want to experience something like this.”

Employees are set to have an emergency meeting at the zoo tomorrow.

A probe has been launched to investigate the full circumstances of the mauling.

Van Hees added: “We are investigating that; we do not know exactly what happened.



“Her immediate colleague heard the cry for help and rushed to her aid.”

The animal in question is believed to be one of two of the region’s Persian leopards.

It will not be put down, according to zoo staff.

Van Hees said: “We are not going to do anything with the leopard.

“It just sat in its enclosure and did what it did. The animal cannot help it.”

THIS is the moment an alleged teen burglar is found hiding inside a wheelie bin by cops as they pull him out by his legs.

The boy was discovered after a police chase at 3.50am following reports of a break-in with cops blasting the suspect for his “rubbish” hiding spot.



After arriving on-scene, Bolton Neighbourhood officers discovered a group of people had attempted to break into a garden shed.

They then searched through nearby gardens before undertaking a foot chase.



The body-cam footage shows cops shining a torch into an overturned bin in Farnworth, Manchester.

They then discover two black shoes poking out as the teen’s hiding spot is uncovered.

An officer shouts: “He is inside. Oi, out you come now.”

The 17-year-old suspect is swiftly handcuffed and arrested on suspicion of burglary.



A teenage girl, 16, was also arrested on suspicion of burglary.

News.title: UK weather live: 28 areas on flood alert as Storm Boelo set to bring 80mph winds
News.content:
The Met Office has issued 'danger to life' amber weather warnings for Storm Boelo, which arrives just after Storm Austen caused serious damage in the South West

Storm Boelo is set to bring 80mph winds and 'widespread travel disruption' to the UK this weekend, with forecasters warning of potential flooding, power cuts and problems on the roads.

One amber warning for wind, two yellow warnings for wind and a yellow warning for rain will cover different areas across the UK this weekend.

It comes after Storm Austen led to airports being closed, flights cancelled and even Brighton's iconic West Pier partially collapsing.

Meanwhile, Prime Minister Andy Burnham warned on Friday that the UK could face “a winter of greater flooding” and said we are living in a world where “unexpected events” are “more and more common”.

An amber weather warning is in place across Scotland today, along with the north of England down to Carlisle and the north-east of Northern Ireland.

It comes just a day after Storm Austen battered the South West of England, with schools closed and 31,000 homes at one point left without power yesterday.

Tom Morgan, a Met Office meteorologist, said: “Yesterday’s Storm Austen affected the far south of the UK and northern France and the Channel Islands, whereas today’s Storm Boelo will be affecting the north of the UK."

News.title: Zookeeper seriously injured in big cat attack at Dutch safari park
News.content:
Zookeeper seriously injured in big cat attack at Dutch safari park

It is believed to be the enclosure used by Persian leopards, although the exact circumstances of the attack remain unclear

View 2 Images It is believed the incident happened in the enclosure used by Persian leopards (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

A zookeeper has been seriously injured after being attacked by a big cat inside an enclosure at a safari park in the Netherlands.

‌



‌



The animal keeper, who has worked at Safaripark Beekse Bergen in the Netherlands for 25 years, was discovered by a colleague at around 11am on Saturday morning. The keeper had been working inside an indoor enclosure housing two male panthers when the incident happened.

‌



She is believed to have come into contact with a Persian leopard, although the exact circumstances of the attack remain unclear.

‌



She was conscious when she was rushed to hospital and has since undergone surgery. Park director Rens Willemsen confirmed she had suffered serious injuries, as he expressed his hopes for her recovery.

"It is a deeply, deeply sad day," he said to local news outlet RTL. "With all my heart, I hope she recovers. She has serious injuries."

The woman had been alone inside the enclosure when her colleague found her injured. The discovery left the colleague extremely shocked, and they have since received support, according to the park director.

‌



The keeper is said to be highly experienced, having spent the past eight years working in the predator section at the Brabant wildlife park. Despite her extensive experience, the circumstances surrounding the incident remain a mystery. There are no cameras inside the enclosure, making it difficult to establish exactly what happened.

View 2 Images William Chapman has been described as a 'really sweet' person (Image: Family Handout/PA Wire)

‌



A trauma helicopter was dispatched to the park in Hilvarenbeek as emergency services responded to the incident. Police confirmed the woman's family had been informed.

The animals had been kept indoors because of the storm, in accordance with the park's safety protocols. Willemsen highlighted the unpredictable nature of the big cats, describing the Persian leopard as the fastest animal in the world.

‌



He added that the big cat would not be put down, saying: "We are not going to do anything with the leopard. It just sat in its enclosure and did what it did. The animal cannot help it.”

The attack comes amid renewed attention on the dangers of working with large predators following the death of a man after a tiger attack at Yorkshire Wildlife Park in Doncaster earlier this month.

‌



William Chapman, 24, died on October 10 after entering an enclosure and being attacked by an Amur tiger named Altai.

The tiger was not injured and remained in its enclosure following the incident.

Article continues below

The latest attack has once again highlighted the risks faced by those who work closely with powerful wild animals, even in controlled environments.

News.title: Reform UK's Suella Braverman claims massive taxpayer-funded water bill at home equal to 18 baths a day
News.content:
Reform UK's Suella Braverman claims massive taxpayer-funded water bill at home equal to 18 baths a day

EXCLUSIVE: Benefits-bashing Reform UK MP Suella Braverman claimed £45,000 in parliamentary expenses towards her water bills, newly-emerged files show - leaving the taxpayer on the hook

View 3 Images Suella Braverman's expenses claims have come under scrutiny (Image: Jonathan Buckmasterr)

Reform MP Suella Braverman ran up a huge taxpayer-funded water bill at her family home – equivalent to 18 bathfuls a day.

‌



‌



The former Home Secretary’s family got through 1,504 litres of water daily at her £1.2million four-bedroom pad in a five-month period from June 2024. Mrs Braverman claimed £45,000 for utility bills on expenses from 2017 to 2025. Affinity Water billed her £657.36 for June to November 2024, according to details obtained under the Freedom of Information Act.

‌



The supplier told her it was enough water to “fill more than 18 bathtubs and 368.54% more water than the average similar-sized household”, campaign group Led By Donkeys discovered.

‌



View 3 Images Affinity Water told Braverman she was using enough to 'fill more than 18 bathtubs' each day (Image: In Pictures via Getty Images)

It is also enough water refill a large residential swimming pool every month but satellite images of the Hertfordshire show no sign of a pool. Mrs Braverman was able to claim for bills because she did not claim rent for her second home, which was her parents’ property in her constituency in Fareham, Hants.

‌



The maximum amount an MP could claim in accommodation costs for their own home in 2024-25 was £6,630 – but in that year Mrs Braverman was able to claim £7,316 by stating that the property doubled-up as her home office. Parliamentary authorities can claim for home office costs “additional to those which are part of the normal cost of living in the home”.

View 3 Images The Reform UK MP has previously criticised people who 'rely on taxpayer's money' (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



Mrs Braverman allocated 20% of her water and other utility bills to her home office use. That meant in the summer of 2024, she was claiming office expenses for enough water to fill a thousand cups of tea a day.

In 2023/24, Mrs Braverman claimed a total of £4,565.10 in utility bills – the fourth highest such claim by an MP and nearly three times the average. The year after it was £4,538.76 – the third highest.

Article continues below

In 2022, while running for the Tory leadership, she said: “Too many people in this country are choosing to rely on benefits, on taxpayers’ money, on your money, my money, to get by.”

Mrs Braverman, who defected from the Tories to Reform UK last year, now claims for a new constituency home in Winchester. The Independent Parliamentary Standards Authority said that all the MP’s homes were correctly registered. A spokesman for Mrs Braverman said: “All rules have been followed.”

News.title: Day of the Dead celebrations kick off as photos show dancers line streets in parade
News.content:
Day of the Dead is approaching - but Pike Place Market has started celebrating early as it marks the festival for the first time.

The Seattle landmark hosted a day of music, dancing and remembrance on Friday, October 23, before a parade made its way through the historic market district. Mariachi musicians, folk dancers and lucha libre wrestlers joined the celebrations, which gave visitors a chance to celebrate Mexican heritage and remember loved ones.

Day of the Dead, or Día de Muertos, is traditionally celebrated on November 1 and 2. Rooted in Mexican traditions, the festival brings families together to remember relatives and friends they have lost. Altars, known as ofrendas, are decorated with photographs and offerings in their memory, combining personal reflection with a celebration of their lives.

News.title: Russell Brand trial hears chilling allegations from women accusing him of rape and sexual assault
News.content:
Russell Brand trial hears chilling allegations from women accusing him of rape and sexual assault

WARNING: DISTRESSING CONTENT. Russell Brand has pleaded not guilty to three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one allegation of indecent assault, relating to six women between 1999 and 2009

View 10 Images The comedian and actor faces charges including rape and sexual assault from six female complainants (Image: Getty Images)

Six women have accused Russell Brand of raping and sexually assaulting them, giving evidence across six days of hearings at his Southwark Crown Court trial.

Alleged victims claim Brand switched suddenly after appearing charming, forced them into sexual activity in a toilet, a hotel room, workplace corridors, and his bedroom, and acting as if nothing had happened after the attacks.

Brand has pleaded not guilty to three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one allegation of indecent assault, relating to six women between 1999 and 2009. Jurors have been told the end of the prosecution is expected early next week, to be followed by Brand’s defence case.

View 10 Images Brand has denied all charges as his trial continues (Image: Getty Images)

In her opening remarks to the jury, prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC said Brand, now 51, gave prepared statements when he was questioned by police. Brand, who has turned to podcasting in recent years, has sat rigidly and without emotion in the dock as his trial has unfolded over the last week and a half.

His wife, Laura Gallacher, is one of a set of supporters who have attended every day of the evidence so far. Below, we've broken down what the court has heard so far in relation to the six alleged victims.

Brand 'forced woman to take pictures then raped her' after Labour Party conference event

A woman who attended the 1999 Labour Party Conference says Brand raped her in a hotel room after she had watched him perform at a fringe event. She said Brand showed interest in her as they chatted after the event, and she invited him to her room to continue the conversation, believing he was gay and not posing a threat.

She said after going to the bathroom when getting back to the room, she returned to find Brand had taken his clothes off. She said: "I remember coming out the toilet. He was practically naked. There wasn't much left to the imagination. I remember him prancing around and being silly. I remember asking why he had his clothes off and he said it's normal. He does that at home, he gets hot.

View 10 Images Brand's trial is being held at Southwark Crown Court (Image: Julia Quenzler / SWNS)

"I found his body quite snake like and disgusting. It made me feel sick if I'm honest. I remember him being like an ostrich, like a bird. He's very leggy, but I wasn't laughing. I just remember him jumping up and down being silly. He was literally kicking his legs up, almost Fawlty Towers Basil Fawlty-esque."

She told the court Brand asked her to take pictures of him on her camera. She told the court: "I took pictures of him on my camera – he made me take them. I was frightened. I remember feeling ‘what on earth have I got myself into’ – and then he did rape me."

The woman said Brand's demeanour changed just before the alleged rape. She said: "He just changed, suddenly from this camp and friendly and effeminate to monster-like. I felt frightened. He's half-naked and while I'm naive I didn't think at that point his intentions were good. He was just dark and arrogant and performing. He was demanding like he was the centre of the show. It was like he was back on his stage. He wasn't the person I was chatting to - 100% not that person."

View 10 Images Russell Brand's wife has supported him in court some days (Image: TOLGA AKMEN/EPA/Shutterstock)

She alleges Brand pushed her on to the bed, removed some of her clothing, and raped her. She said Brand told her 'It's normal, enjoy it' during the attack while she was "like a zombie on the bed." The complainant claimed when the alleged attack ended at some point after midnight, Brand got off her and claimed he had remembered he needed to go see his mum.

‌



She said Brand told her she would "love his mum and she would love me". She then said Brand wrote down his email "without me asking" and at that point she was "just willing him to go." She claims Brand told her 'don't worry, I get tested regularly, I go to the clinic a lot, I don't have any disease.'

Woman 'grabbed and pulled into MTV office toilet'

An MTV worker gave evidence that Brand tried to drag her into a toilet at one of the company's offices in 2001. She had struck up a friendly conversation with Brand over his “I am Spartacus” T-shirt, but said he then turned into a “wild-eyed maniac” as he grabbed her by the arm and tried to pull her into the toilet.

‌



She claimed Brand "started to plead almost, 'go on, go on, come in!'." She added: "He grabbed my forearm and was leaning on the door. He was quite forceful in grip. I am pulling back into the corridor. He's trying to pull me back in. By this time he had what I would call quite a wild look in his eyes. I said I'm not going in there with you. I think I might have called him an idiot or words to that effect. It lasted probably about 20 seconds, maybe less."

View 10 Images Brand has denied all allegations against him (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

‌



The woman said she wrenched herself free, and she reported what she says happened to colleagues, who she says told her: "Well, he's crazy." But she said she never reported the incident to bosses. She told the court: "The reason that I didn't was because I was scared. I got away, I thought it would be my word against him. He was a big asset to MTV. I've got a mortgage to pay so whats the point in making life hard for myself?"

‌



She later reported the incident to police after watching a Channel 4 programme about Brand, saying: " I watched the Channel 4 documentary and it came back to me and I thought 'this is not just me'. I thought about it and thought about it more and thought I have managed to get away thanks to my own strength. It could have been very different. Given what could have happened I thought it was the right thing to do to come forward to the police."

Brand's lawyer, Ian Winter KC, challenged her suggesting she only came forward after watching the show and deciding Brand had been trying to rape her rather than pull her in for a consensual encounter. She said: " I don't think it's quite as straight-forward as that. It would have been my word against his. I came away relatively unscathed. He didn't manage to rape me. I managed to get myself out from the situation."

‌



Brand 'groped woman in bar then forced her to perform oral sex in toilet'

Brand is accused of groping a woman during a birthday party at a Soho bar, then dragging her to the toilet and forcing her to perform oral sex on him. The woman said she had been talking to the TV presenter at the bar for less than a minute when he “lunged” forward and grabbed hold of her breasts.

“He literally just grabbed my boobs, out of nowhere, just in the middle of a conversation and I just remember this weird, maniacal grin, looming in front of me as he just grabbed my boobs," she said. “I was completely in shock and was like, ‘what the hell are you doing? I’ve literally just met you’. Then literally he grabbed my arm and dragged me into the toilets.”

‌



View 10 Images An artist impression of Brand last week (Image: Julia Quenzler / SWNS)

‌



She alleges Brand locked the door, jumped on top of a toilet seat lid, unzipped his trousers, and forced her into oral sex, saying “don’t be a spoilsport” when she appeared unwilling. The woman, who was working for MTV at the time, claimed Brand was "grinning like a clown" during the encounter.

She recalled thinking: “Survival tried to kick in: ‘do what he says then you’re out of here and it’s done.’” She told the jury she was “dazed” and in shock afterwards, and remembers a man knocking on the toilet door saying: "Are you ok?". She told police: "Russell just sort of casually walked out and unlocked it and I just walked out in a daze. I remember this really, really clearly - he turned to me and went 'Oh, I guess we should swap numbers now', like it was just all normal, like he hadn't just forced me to do that."

‌



She said she tried to find a friend at the bar but was ushered into the back of a car with Brand, where he "had his penis out again" while two others sat in the front. She claimed he told her 'Com on, com on, suck it', saying: "I was just like 'no'. He took 'no' for an answer then."

Brand’s barrister suggested the woman had been excited to meet the TV star and had willingly gone into the toilet with him, and he argued that the encounter was cut short because of the “disgusting” state of the flooded toilets. When Mr Winter asked if she had been looking forward to meeting Brand that night, she said: "I wasn't extremely excited. I wasn't a giddy schoolgirl."

‌



She added that she was "tipsy" but "wasn't paralytic" at the time, claiming to have had "six or seven" vodka, lime and sodas. Mr Winter suggested she may have gone into the toilet with Brand voluntarily, to which she replied: "I don't agree. I was dragged there against my will."

'Rough and sloppy kisses' after Brand 'leapt on woman in radio station'

An employee of a radio station in London told the court she was pinned against a wall, groped, and subjected to “sloppy” kisses by Brand. She recalled the comedian, then a rising star on Channel 4’s Big Brother’s Big Mouth, saying “aye, aye” as she emerged in front of him from a radio studio.

‌



The woman said she was alone in a room when the incident occurred, telling the court: " I literally opened the door and I’m standing in the space, very cramped, and he’s just leapt on me.” She added: “It was rough, it was very, very rough. It was hard, I would say that his whole body was pressed against me, the kisses were hard and sloppy, going down my neck The reason I used the word frenzied is because it was just, it was violent.”

View 10 Images The allegations were made by six female complainants span a 10-year period (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The woman said she looked to Brand’s entourage to help but no one intervened, and eventually she pushed him away and said, “f*** off”. She added that she saw Brand laugh, and defended her decision not to report the incident to her managers at the time. “There was a culture of fear”, she said, recalling the atmosphere at the time as “people pleasing”.

‌



“Russell Brand was an A-lister star, it was Big Brother, people were watching it, we all watched it," she said. She added that she believes her line manager at the time would have likely responded “you’re lucky” if she had recounted the incident.

Brand’s legal team suggested that the woman had only come up with the allegation against Brand after seeing sexual misconduct allegations being levelled against him in a 2023 Dispatches documentary.

‌



Woman told to 'clear up her mess after being raped at Brand's home'

Brand is accused of raping a 21-year-old fan a few days after they met at his 2009 stand-up comedy show at the Hammersmith Apollo in west London. The woman said Brand invited her and two other women backstage, and she willingly engaged in a threesome with the star.

She later texted with Brand and agreed to go to his Hampstead townhouse for what she thought would be consensual sex. But the woman said the encounter turned odd when Brand forced her to shower and brush her teeth after she arrived at his home, claiming her hair smelled 'funny'.

‌



View 10 Images A photo was issued of Brand’s home in Hampstead (Image: Metropolitan Police/Press Association)

‌



She said they began to have consensual sex but she "felt really uncomfortable" after being told to shower and brush her teeth. However, she said that during intercourse, Brand removed the condom and began to have anal sex without seeking consent. She said she struggled to breathe and repeatedly told Brand: "Can you stop, can you stop, can you stop?"

The woman said Brand “looked horrified” after the alleged rape, but while she thought he was going to apologise he instead told her to “clear up the mess that you’ve made”, the court heard. The woman added: “The thing that I have really struggled with is… that what he said to me after, it really affected me because I did it… exactly what he said. ‘Clear up the mess you’ve made’, I did it and I don’t know why.”

‌



She claimed she used his black toilet roll to clean her blood from his "enormous" bed while he told her he was stepping out to take a phone call. The woman said she had to “sit on an ice cube tray” because she was “in so much pain” after the alleged attack. She added: “It was one of the most painful experiences I’ve ever gone through.”

View 10 Images Jurors were shown photos of Brand's home, including the bedroom with a full-length mirror next to the bed

‌



The woman said that for “years” she told the story as though she “shouldn’t have gone”, as though it was her fault. She told her parents what had happened and was referred for therapy by a sexual health clinic, which she attended after the incident. When it was suggested she was an “obsessed” fan who had agreed to the whole encounter, the woman repeatedly told the court: “I didn’t consent to what happened to me.”

‌



Brand was said to have turned "really nasty" following the encounter. A friend of the woman gave evidence over a videolink. The witness said her friend was “crying, really upset” when they met up after her encounter at Brand’s house, and she told her what had happened. The witness said: "I asked specifically ‘did you say no?’, and she said yes, lots of times.... She told me she was in a lot of pain – ‘he really f****** hurt me’.

The court heard the woman who has accused Brand of rape told her the comedian turned “really nasty” at the end of the incident.

‌



Victim 'forced to massage Brand who put his head in her lap'

The sixth woman alleged she was forced into giving Brand a massage, and that during it he put his head into her lap, leaning in so close she could feel his breath on her intimate parts. The Channel 4 worker said she was "repulsed" after being told that the only way Brand would carry on with a project in 2009 was if she gave him a massage.

She sid she thought they were joking but she "saw by their faces they weren't joking". She told the court Brand said "come on then" after putting his head on her lap. She added that his left shoulder was leaning against her leg while his head was in her lap, saying: "it was quite elongated... it was a weird position for a massage to be in, that's for sure."

‌



View 10 Images His wife Laura Gallacher was in court with him (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

"I could feel his breath against me," she recalled. She said she looked at two members of Brand's entourage, Jack Bayles and Gareth Roy, who were "shrugging" and gesturing to say "are you going to do it?". The woman said she thought at the time: "Oh my god, I have got to do this."

‌



"I was so repulsed by the situation and my automatic reaction was 'urgh, you're so bony'," she said. She added the Bayles and Roy "laughed" at what she said, but Brand "didn't laugh." The woman said Brand made a series of offensive comments, suggesting that he and Mr Roy had been “wanting to know: is it a girl or a boy?”

She said Brand got up after she told him he was "bony" and the mood shifted in the room. She claimed Brand got up and went over to a glass of water with a calculator and said 'Ooh, I'm a calculator, look at me, look at me', pretending to make the calculator drink from the glass. She said: " It was just a bit of a charade, just a change of tune, and then he said, right are we going to get on with this… or not?”

Article continues below

She said she reported the incident the following day to her line manager at Channel 4, and she believes it was passed on to the head of her department.

The trial continues.

News.title: Chancellor to unveil £1billion boost to build up to 10,000 new council homes in Budget
News.content:
Chancellor to unveil £1billion boost to build up to 10,000 new council homes in Budget

EXCLUSIVE: The Chancellor is set to announce more than £1billion of new funding for social and affordable housing, taking the total capital investment to more than £40 billion over the next 10 years

View 2 Images The Chancellor is set to announce more than £1billion of new funding for social and affordable housing (Image: David Hartley/Shutterstock)

Britain is set for a £1billion boost to council housing which can deliver up to 10,000 homes in the Budget.

‌



‌



The announcement next week by Chancellor John Healey will take the total capital ­investment in the Social and Affordable Homes Programme to more than £40bn over the next 10 years. The government also plans to help more councils borrow for ­housebuilding by extending ­preferential rates.

‌



A Treasury spokesman said: “For years families have been locked out of a secure and affordable home because we simply haven’t built enough. The Prime Minister promised to restore the public housing stock.

‌



To see more of the stories you value from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Northern England Olympics bid backed with £7million in Budget READ MORE :

View 2 Images The PM had promised a council house building 'revolution' (Image: Michael Bowles/Shutterstock)

“This Budget will go further on that ambition through significant ­investment in affordable housing and helping councils borrow to build so we can replace what has been sold and give people a place to live.”

‌



Since the 1980s, more than two million council homes have been sold through Right to Buy. But after ­successive governments failed to replace them, millions of people have been left struggling to find a first home.

More than 1.3 million households are on social housing waiting lists in England, and only 12,250 social rent homes were delivered in 2024/25. A record 177,500 children are living in ­temporary accommodation – up 5% in a year.

‌



And earlier this year, the boss of Britain’s largest housebuilder, Barratt Redrow, said it is the toughest time for first-time buyers since the 2008 financial crisis. The average monthly private rent rose by 3.8% in the 12 months to September. House prices rose by 0.9%, to £273,000, having gone up 1.2% the year before, figures out this week show.

PM Andy Burnham has ­promised the largest post-war council and social housebuilding programme, including the exemption of new builds from Right to Buy for 35 years. It forms part of a strategy to transform housing, with Housing Secretary Angela Rayner telling the Labour conference last month that the government would cap “outrageous” fees for leaseholders and regulate managing agents behaving like “cowboys, crooks and con artists”.

‌



It was also announced councils will be able to take back empty homes after six months. Mairi MacRae, acting chief executive at housing charity Shelter, said: “As we head into winter, record numbers of children are stuck in homelessness in grotty temporary accommodation, while countless more families struggle to cope with soaring housing costs.

"With rents tied to local incomes, social rent homes are the only genuinely ­affordable option for many families, but over the last few decades, supply has plummeted. This funding injection is another important step in the right direction, but to deliver the council house building revolution it promised, the government must go further.

Article continues below

"The autumn Budget is the Prime Minister’s chance to remove unsustainable housing debt from council balance sheets and truly ­turbocharge the delivery of social rent homes.”

News.title: Westlife serve up nostalgia in spades at Manchester’s Co-op Live
News.content:
Westlife serve up nostalgia in spades at Manchester’s Co-op Live

Now touring as a trio, the Irish favourites delighted Mancunian fans with a set stuffed full of their biggest hits in a feelgood performance worthy of the Noughties☆☆☆☆☆

View 5 Images Westlife brought the house down at Manchester's Co-op Live

Before Westlife were even on stage, the screaming had begun. A sea of millennial women and their mums prepared to party with Ireland’s biggest exports.

‌



‌



"Are you ready for two hours of nostalgia?” asked Shane Filan as the band kicked off the first of three sold out Westlife 25 shows at Manchester’s Co-op Live arena with 2002 banger World of our Own. “Who had a Westlife poster on their wall? This should bring that poster to life,” added Nicky Byrne.

‌



And so began a 20-song set stuffed with all the band’s biggest hits from the last quarter century. With 14 UK and Irish number one singles, and 11 number one albums, they have plenty to choose from.

‌



Uptown Girl, What About Now, Starlight… They came one by one, a stellar line-up of nostalgic pop dominos, served up with pure unadulterated serotonin in spades.

View 5 Images Westlife have been at the epicentre of British music since 1998

Flying Without Wings writer Steve Mac was in the audience, watching his hits land one by one. Kian Egan took to the electric guitar for When You're Looking Like That, mashing it up with Guns & Rose’s Sweet Child of Mine to create the collaboration we never knew we needed.

‌



Take That, Backstreet Boys, Blue - and now Westlife - have all been on the nostalgia tour circuit this year, making 2026 as the year the boyband came back and providing a comfort blanket for the masses.

For Westlife, this year marks 25 years since their inaugural tour. Their first single, Swear It Again, was released two years earlier in 1999. Whether they’re a guilty pleasure or straight up pleasure, the band has been a huge player in pop ever since.

‌



View 5 Images Shane, Kian and Nicky of Westlife

Initially a five-piece, original member Brian McFadden left in 2004. And now, they are performing as a trio since Mark Feehily announced a break due to ill health. But despite their reduced numbers, Westlife were on fine form in Manchester.

‌



And from confetti and fire to synchronised dancing, it was a veritable bingo card of delight from the ballad kings. There was even a drone light show during You Raise Me Up.

An acoustic section on a central B stage lent an intimacy to the 22,000-capacity stadium. Nicky brought his 13-year-old daughter onto the platform for a rendition of happy birthday and a sparkler-topped cake.

‌



View 5 Images Shane on the B stage

Shane’s voice was as pitch perfect as in in 1999. And with Mark amiss, Nicky and Kian were able to shine all the more brightly. Harmonies were tight, key changes euphoric.

‌



“They look like they’re having a brilliant time,” noted my mum, who I’d brought along for the ride. Her camera roll is now 99% pictures of Shane. And she was right. Shane, Kian and Nicky beamed like cats with Waitrose finest cream all night long. And so they should. With every song, their fans grew more and more delighted.

New arrangements kept things fresh. And while Westlife taking me to "da club" during Hello My Love was not on my bingo card, it was much better than Infernos. I’d make a return visit.

‌



View 5 Images Westlife wore white for the encore

For Flying Without Wings, Westlife’s national anthem, Mark’s bits were done by the band’s incredible backing singers, breathing new life into the song and providing a fitting tribute. Kudos to their live band too, who were brilliant.

‌



By the time the encore came, ending the set with Swear It Again, the song that started it all and sent Westlife's star into the stratosphere, you could have powered a small town with the joy in the room. Fabulously feel good, I left the Co-op Live feeling lighter, a hot cup of nostalgia providing much needed nourishment on a stormy Friday night.

And with two more nights to go in Manchester, before they move on to Belfast, Westlife are just getting started. A masterclass in pop perfection.
