News.title: How an aid initiative maimed thousands of children in war-torn Africa
News.content:
Tormented by pain from severe internal burns, Amza Kebbie is one of thousands of children in Sierra Leone damaged for life by an aid intervention which went horribly wrong.

It has been five days since the four-year-old boy drank caustic soda, one of the two main ingredients for making soap, after mistaking it for drinking water. The highly corrosive liquid, also known as sodium hydroxide, has stripped the lining of his oesophagus and part of his stomach, causing life changing damage.

He’s now in intensive care, clinging precariously to life. An intravenous drip provides fluids and there’s a nasal cannula that enables him to breathe. Medics and relatives look over him around the clock.

If he can gather enough strength (which the nurses say is by no means guaranteed) the dangerously sick child will undergo a gastrostomy, an operation that will see a tube directly inserted into his stomach so that he can be fed long term.

Amza drank caustic soda while being looked after by a neighbour who was making soap at home Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

He can no longer swallow properly and may never be able to do so again, say his doctors.

This is not an isolated tragedy. Across Sierra Leone, there are thousands of children like Amza, and their number is growing every year.

At the Goderich Surgical Centre in the capital Freetown, around 200 children are admitted annually with caustic soda poisoning. Many more are thought to die in remote regions where emergency medical treatment is unavailable.

Behind the calamity is a humanitarian initiative that has spectacularly backfired. It’s a prime example of the law of unintended consequences; of a seemingly sensible and undoubtedly well meaning public health intervention doing more harm than good.

Fatmata Kamara accidentally drank caustic soda at her grandmother’s house in 2014 and has had a feeding tube ever since Credit : SImon Townsley

The story starts in the aftermath of Sierra Leone’s vicious civil war, which ran between 1991 and 2002.

Fought between the government and the Revolutionary United Front – backed by Liberian warlord Charles Taylor – the war claimed an estimated 50,000 to 70,000 lives, displaced 2.5 million people and left the country brutalised and in ruins.

In its aftermath, international aid agencies and NGOs desperately sought ways to revive the country and alighted on DIY soap making as a way of killing two birds with one stone.

Siblings Aminata Fofana and Salieu Bangura help out with the family soap-making business Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

Organisations including UNHCR, UNICEF and World Vision thought the practice would both improve sanitation in the country’s disease-ridden shanty towns and provide home-bound women with the means to earn a sustainable income.

It seemed like an obvious “win-win”, and schemes to help women set up in the soap making business rapidly proliferated.

An annual report by the International Federation of the Red Cross, published in May 2002, promoted a micro-finance scheme to fund small-scale soapmaking.

Saieu Bangura, 13, with a tub of soap flakes Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

In 2005, the Centre for War Affected Women in Sierra Leone’s Kono district, backed by the UNHCR, listed soap making as one of the main training courses for war widows and female amputees.

And at about the same time, the Freetown-based Safer Future Youth Development Programme, supported by UNICEF and the charity War Child, provided “a tool kit for soap production” at its training workshops.

As recently as 2020, Action Aid ran a promotional article on its Sierra Leone website showing how soap making had enabled women to become financially independent of their husbands.

The article ran under the headline: “With Soap Making Skills – I'm Empowered!”

Mabinty Bangura is taken to theatre for an endoscopy Credit : Simon Townsley

It is for good reason that the ancient Greek physician Hippocrates urged doctors “first, do no harm”.

To follow the rule literally is not possible as all health interventions entail some risk but it's a reminder never to underestimate the capacity of a new intervention to backfire.

There are plenty of examples from history to choose from.

During the British Raj in India, the government offered a cash bounty for every dead cobra as a way of reducing the danger of venomous snakes.

The surgical team examine the internal damage via an endoscopy Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

But rather than leading to a decline in snake numbers, the plan resulted in entrepreneurial individuals breeding cobras just so they could kill them and then claim the reward.

Once officials realised what was happening and the scheme was stopped, thousands of the then worthless cobras were released into the wild, greatly increasing the risk of snakebite.

In the late 1950s, the Chinese Communist regime introduced an equally calamitous public health campaign involving sparrows.

They issued a directive ordering the birds to be destroyed because they were thought to spread disease and destroy crops.

A child’s gastrostomy scar with a feeding tube in place Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

What those behind the idea failed to consider was that sparrows are natural predators. As their numbers declined, the locust population exploded, decimating agriculture and contributing to the Great Chinese Famine in which millions died.

So what went wrong in Sierra Leone? What did those behind the soap making scheme fail to foresee?

Experts say the initiative simply failed to consider the danger inherent in encouraging people to use toxic chemicals in their homes.

The brightly coloured buckets in which caustic soda is made, and then mixed with oil and scent to make soap, are the same buckets used across the country to fetch and hold drinking water. And just like drinking water, the lethal solution is cool, clear and inviting.

Just a drop is enough to cause the most horrific burns. So when a thirsty young child like Amza runs in from play and mistakenly scoops up a cup of it to quench their thirst they will lose their oesophagus, if not their lives.

Giuseppe Meucci, chief surgeon at the Goderich Surgical Centre Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

Giuseppe Meucci, chief surgeon at the 56-bed Goderich hospital in Freetown where four year old Amza is being cared for, has been treating patients burned by sodium hydroxide nearly every day since arriving in Freetown in 2019.

Three quarters of patients seen by the hospital’s specialist programme for oesophageal burns, set up in response to the crisis and run by the Italian medical charity Emergency, are under five.

“It’s a struggle in this country,” says Dr Meucci. “Almost every family knows someone who has suffered because of this problem. But they just keep coming.”

Hospital director Jasna Sundic Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

“In most countries you remove the source of danger for the child, but here that doesn’t seem to happen,” he says.

“It’s one of the main health problems of this country. Soda is there with malaria, malnutrition and typhoid complications. It’s one of the reasons why so many children die before they reach five years old.”

Hospital director Jasna Sundic agrees.

“This is a very severe issue but one which is very preventable,” she tells the Telegraph. “[But] however much we do here, we have not been able to decrease the overall number of soda patients being admitted.

“We cannot stop mothers who have no other source of income except making soap.”

Ibrahim Kerah is fed by his father Mohamed Credit : SImon Townsley

In a handful of rare cases, burns victims are sent abroad for complex oesophageal reconstruction surgery but this is not an option for the vast majority of children injured in Sierra Leone.

More than 60 per cent require surgery, but for these children, like Amza, a feeding tube that bypasses the oesophagus is the only option.

The hospital has many of these gastrostomy patients.

Critically underweight Mabinty Bangura Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

In a ward dedicated to soda burns, four-year-old Ibrahim Kerah is being fed through his stomach tube by his father Mohamed.

They travelled together on the back of a motorbike taxi for nearly 10 hours to get here for his third check-up appointment.

The Telegraph watches as Mohamed carefully prepares his son’s meal, adding spinach leaves to the porridge-like mix which is fed into a syringe at the end of the tube.

At an adjoining bed two-year-old Mabinty Bangura is critically underweight after ingesting soda about six months ago. Nurses have put her on a high protein drip so she can regain enough strength to undergo the same bypass surgery.

In the courtyard outside, mothers whose children have just had a gastrostomy are being taught how to prepare the liquid food.

Ibrahim and his father Mohamed endured a 10-hour motorbike journey to attend his hospital check-up Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

Isatu Alie, 24, has been living with a stomach tube for 12 years, and now works for Emergency as a patient ambassador.

She is eight months pregnant with her second child and proud to have overcome her injury and the stigma of having to feed through a tube.

“I remember what happened so well,” she says. “I had just got back from school. I took my cup and dunked it into the water bucket. My aunt made soap and, on that day, I didn’t ask about the liquid in the bucket. The pain was incredible”.

More than a decade has passed since her surgery, and Isatu has adjusted well.

“I’m okay with it now. I feel like a normal human being; I’m blessed to be here,” she says.

“Now I speak to children and their parents who have just experienced the same thing and tell them not to lose hope.”

Pregnant Isatu Alie now works as a patient ambassador Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

A small proportion of the patients needing treatment following caustic soda burns are adults.

Among them is 21-year-old Junisa Bundeh, who is on a follow-up visit to check his stomach tube. He explains that he gulped down what he thought was a cup of water from a basin while eating at his grandmother’s house three months ago.

“It was so painful,” recalls Junisa. “I realised what it was straight away because it was so harsh. I tried to spit it all out but the liquid was already going down my throat.”

Mothers are taught how to prepare liquid food; Junisa Bundeh shows his feeding tube Credit : SImon Townsley

In the muddy lanes of Freetown’s Waterloo district there are makeshift soap making operations all over.

The coloured plastic buckets full of either soda or water are everywhere.

Against the backdrop of the rainy season’s persistent gloom, the containers symbolise a measure of cleanliness for families sheltering from torrential downpours under mouldy concrete awnings.

As the Telegraph watches Yabom Kapro, a village elder, making soap, the risks involved are immediately obvious.

Chief Yabom Kapro makes soap at her Waterloo town home, near Freetown Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

As she tips a purple bucket of caustic soda solution into a large basin and then adds palm oil from a plastic jerrycan, local children hover round the cluster of colourful containers.

Yabom uses a wooden paddle to stir the mixture into a creamy paste and then pours it into a mould held in place by an old motorcycle tyre.

Buckets containing caustic soda dissolving, top. Caustic soda crystals, below Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

Once set, the beige-coloured cake of soap is cut into blocks which are then grated on a wire mesh contraption to be sold at the local market.

“When you dilute the caustic soda, it is completely clear like water at first,” says another soap maker, 43-year-old Cilina Bangura.

“Afterwards a white scum forms on the top, but you cannot be watching all of the time, [even] with all of these children around.”

Cilina knows the risks but says she can't afford to stop making soap. It has, as the NGOs intended, become an economic lifeline for her and her family.

“Of course, I know how dangerous soda is – it has burned my skin many times – but I don’t have another option.”

News.title: Carrick weighs up stripping Bruno Fernandes of Man Utd captaincy
News.content:
A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a new low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”

Sports.title: Sunderland legend highlights three key men Regis Le Bris’ side MUST stop to beat Leeds in crunch Premier League clash
Sports.content:
Next

KEVIN PHILLIPS says Sunderland have to stop more than just Dominic Calvert-Lewin to end the Premier League rot.

The Black Cats face the Whites on Sunday at the Stadium of Light sitting bottom of the Premier League following a run of four-straight defeats.



Daniel Farke’s Leeds, meanwhile, head to the North East riding high and have only tasted defeat once this term, away to champions Arsenal.

Their striker Calvert-Lewin, expected to play despite a bruised foot, has already scored five and will be out to inflict more misery on the Mackems.



However, legendary former striker Phillips says the England international is not the only problem Regis Le Bris needs to solve as he looks to ease the pressure at Sunderland.

Speaking to Sun Sport via BestBettingSites.co.uk, he said: “It’s a big, big game for Sunderland. They need a result, but they’re coming up against a team that’s got some really, really good players, a very good team, and physically a very good team as well, so they know they’re going to be in for a battle.



“The obvious one that stands out is Dominic Calvert-Lewin. He’s an absolute handful on his day. He’s a nuisance, he’s good in the air, he’s good at holding it up, he’s got energy, his work rate, and he can score goals. You put the ball in the box, and he’s very, very good in the air. So he’s the most obvious one.

“James Justin on that right-hand side, up and down, energy, he creates goals, gets into good positions. And again, he’s a constant threat. And Anton Stach in the midfield area, he’s been one of their better players this season, a very, very accomplished midfielder and very good at set plays as well.

“Those are just three, but you need to be wary of the whole team. They need to match them. So a big, big game, but those three are the players to look out for.”

Le Bris is facing flak on Wearside for the first time since his arrival in the dug-out back in the summer of 2024.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Despite Thursday’s 1-1 draw at Lech Poznan maintaining their unbeaten start in the Europa League, another defeat to Leeds in the Prem would lead to more pressure mounting on the ex-Lorient coach.

Le Bris has enjoyed a fairytale so far at Sunderland, winning promotion in his first year and following that up with a seventh-place finish in their debut campaign back in the top-flight.

But he says he is enjoying this new challenge of trying to guide them clear of danger while managing the extra workload of European football.

He added: “We forget quickly because we always remind ourselves of the last feeling. First season the playoffs at Wembley. The second season and last game at home against Chelsea to qualify for Europa League.



“So it’s been perfect, but before, we had lows as well and went through difficult situations before. Five games in the Championship we lost that we didn’t want to lose.

“And the same last year, when we lost 5–0 at home [to Nottingham Forest]. It was a pure disaster, we gave up, we were not us.

“But the players reacted well, we stayed consistent, and we are in this situation, facing a new challenge. Hard to take, but the most important is to enjoy the challenge to get better and stronger.”

Sports.title: Goal-crazy EFL star told by manager Tony Mowbray ‘be careful son, otherwise you’ll end up at Barcelona like your dad’
Sports.content:
Next

CHELSEA icon Eidur Gudjohnsen’s son Andri is sensationally following in his dad’s giant footsteps amid a stunning campaign that has seen him set the EFL goalscoring charts alight.

So much so, that his Blackburn manager Tony Mowbray warned him he will soon find himself at Barcelona, where Eidur, 48, played some of the best football of his 22-year career.



Andri, 24, has already amassed a staggering total of nine goals and one assist in 12 appearances with the Rovers, which places him as the Championship‘s second leading scorer.

The striker has also registered two goals and one assist in his last four caps with Iceland.



Andri’s goalscoring exploits allow Blackburn to dream of finally returning to the Premier League since their relegation in 2012.

Mowbray’s side is currently tenth in the Championship table with only two points separating them from the play-off spots.



However, the 62-year-old gaffer worries he may soon lose his star centre-forward if he keeps it up as one of his father’s former clubs could look to snatch him.

Mowbray said after today’s 2-0 victory against Wrexham at Ewood Park where the Iceland international scored a brace: “Be careful son, otherwise you’ll end up at Barcelona like your dad.”

Barcelona are famous for picking up some of the best young talent in the world.

And Eidur knows all about it as he spent three years within Barca’s ranks and helped the Spanish giants win a historic treble in 2009.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The legendary striker amassed a total of 19 goals and ten assists in 114 appearances with the Blaugrana until his departure on the same year he won LaLiga, Copa del Rey and the Champions League.

The Icelandic great also stood out for the likes of Chelsea and Bolton in the Premier League from 1998 until 2006, when he swapped Stamford Bridge for the Nou Camp.

And if Andri keeps piling up the goals for Blackburn he could soon find himself in the Prem carrying his famous dad’s torch.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta reveals he has dossier on rival Premier League bosses showing they are far worse than him on touchline
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA has bizarrely claimed he has been putting together video footage of other managers leaving their technical area.

The Arsenal manager received a yellow card from referee Tony Harrington in the 2-0 win over Everton for repeatedly leaving his area.



But Arteta reckons a Premier League rival left his area 36 times in 10 minutes.

Arteta said: “I do have to be careful. And we need to have good sensors there.



“There are managers that have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes leave the touchline, no yellows.

“So I’m clipping all of that. I have a massive storage of images. Somebody else has the record.



“Then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the manager. I don’t know where we’re going to be.”

It was a second yellow card for Arteta who was also cautioned away to Sunderland in September.

Arsenal also have an injury concern over defender Riccardo Calafiori, who was struggling at the end of the game and played as a left winger with Noni Madueke ending up as a left-back.

Arteta said: “I wasn’t that mad to change those two from their positions. It was because he had a slight issue.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“We don’t know what it is, it seems to be something very small, but he was cautious about it.”

Bukaya Saka is set to be sidelined for at least six weeks with a thigh injury.

Arteta also hailed the mindset of his players, especially after Gabriel scored just minutes after having treatment for a hamstring injury.

He said: “The mentality of the team is the mentality of the individuals in the team. Gabi is a great example of that because we were all scared.



“Not because of the way he went down, but the reaction of the players that were next to him.

“Immediately, he said that he wanted to continue and then he scored a goal to help us win the game. That’s what we need from our players.

“So yes we’re very happy with the victory, with the performance and with the week, because we were given a terrible schedule.

“Sunday afternoon (v Nottingham Forest), then Wednesday night in Munich and having to play again in the Premier League against a really tough opponent on Saturday at 3pm.

“We have overcome every hurdle, on top of some injuries, and I love the mentality of the team and the quality that we’ve shown.”

Sports.title: Chelsea ratings: Palmer’s immaturity and attitude see him sent off vs Spurs as Penders’ full debut flatters to deceive
Sports.content:
Next

CHELSEA decided to play without a recognised centre-forward against Tottenham with Joao Pedro injured – and it showed as they lost 2-0 to their London rivals for the first time in EIGHT years.

With their top scorer out, Xabi Alonso raised eyebrows by selecting Geovany Quenda to play ahead of Estevao in attack.



And his side struggled to find the back of the net without their No9.

What was expected to be a walk in the park for Chelsea against their struggling rivals, who have an abysmal record at Stamford Bridge, turned out to be quite the opposite.



Spurs dominated large parts of the first half, with James Maddison untouchable on the ball and a huge chance for Omar Marmoush, which called Mike Penders into action in the absence of Emiliano Martinez.

The second half was much of the same, until Tottenham found a winner through a Mike Penders own-goal on his full Premier League debut, which Mathys Tel capitalised on five minutes before full-time with a fine long-range shot.

This is how SunSport’s Chelsea reporter Lloyd Canfield rated Xabi Alonso’s players…

MIKE PENDERS – 2

It feels really harsh to give such a young goalkeeper a poor rating on his full Premier League debut, but it’s impossible to say much else.



He didn’t look totally confident in the first half, particularly when coming for crosses, despite making a few routine stops to deny Omar Marmoush, and in the second half it was his poor punch that found it’s way into his own net to see Chelsea lose it.

JOSH ACHEAMPONG – 4

Struggled a little bit against Mathys Tel, perhaps because he didn’t have Pedro Neto helping him out defensively as much as usual.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Frenchman burst away from him and scored a brilliant individual goal to double Tottenham’s lead on a monumental day for the visitors.

MAXENCE LACROIX – 6

Won everything at the back for the Blues against Marmoush and wasn’t really troubled by the Egyptian forward, making several blocks, tackles and clearances throughout.



Did his best to keep out Mike Penders’ punch, but it was too little too late by the time he hooked it out of the goal.

LEVI COLWILL – 6

Strong in his duels throughout the first half and good when playing out from the back and made some really good interceptions too.

Levi Colwill is a leader in this Chelsea side and very vocal, as someone who understands better than most what this rivalry means.

JORREL HATO – 6

Wasn’t caused many problems by Tottenham‘s right hand side of Mohammed Kudus and Archie Gray, which perhaps would have been different if Pedro Porro started.

MOISES CAICEDO – 6

Set the pace in midfield for Chelsea after a few fouls to try and keep James Maddison quiet, which he struggled with a bit, and he would’ve been pleased to see him trudge off early in the second 45 minutes.



Made some important tackles and interceptions, as ever, but wasn’t at his monstrous best.

JORDAN HENDERSON – 4

Denied by Antonin Kinsky on the edge of the box who was making up for a poor pass after 35 minutes, but really it wasn’t Jordan Henderson’s day in midfield.

His weight of pass was all off, and while showing plenty of energy he just wasn’t the tempo-setting midfielder we have seen in recent weeks.



PEDRO NETO – 5

Much has been made of Neto’s defensive work, and he was defending from the front in this one rather than coming back so much.

Started on the right and switched to the left before half-time, where he tested Kinsky with a low shot which was well saved.

Should have done better with a ball over the top early in the second half, but was let down by a poor first touch in the rain.

COLE PALMER – 2

Tested Kinsky after 13 minutes with a curling effort towards the top left corner which was well saved, but was quiet for most of the first half – a trend that continued in the second 45, before he got sent off.

It was his own immaturity and attitude that saw that happen.



His first booking was for exactly that, immaturity, as he bashed into Fernandes over a handball incident before making a late tackle on Conor Gallagher later on in the half.

GEOVANY QUENDA – 3

Similarly to Penders, Geovany Quenda had a lot of faith shown in him by Xabi Alonso who controversially threw him into the team ahead of Estevao in a London derby.

He was quiet for large parts of the first half, and despite an attempt to burst into life after swapping wings with Neto, he was quiet again in the second.

Alonso should have started Estevao ahead of him.

Much was made of Morgan Rogers’ impressive record against Spurs ahead of this game, but he wasn’t overly impactful this time around.



Tested Kinsky once before the end of the first half only to have the offside flag raised against him anyway, and struggled to make things stick despite a few nice combinations with Cole Palmer.

Sports.title: Chelsea 0 Tottenham 2: Cole Palmer’s red card and Joao Pedro’s absence see Spurs claim shock win at Stamford Bridge
Sports.content:
Next

CHELSEA goalkeeper Mike Penders handed Tottenham an historic win on his first Premier League start.

And Cole Palmer earned the first red card of his career before Mathys Tel ensured Spurs would emerge triumphant from a small-scale re-enactment of the Battle of the Bridge



Nothing will ever make up for the 2-2 draw here which ended Tottenham’s title hopes in 2016.

But Penders’ own goal with 12 minutes left set Roberto De Zerbi’s side on the way to achieving a rare distinction in this London derby.



Only once since 1990 had Spurs won at Stamford Bridge.

Some historians believe that, during the first half of the second century AD, the Christians had a better record in their tricky away fixture against the Lions in Rome’s Colosseum.



It seemed as if Tottenham would have to settle for just a moral victory.

But then Mateus Fernandes swung in a corner and Penders, in for the injured Emi Martinez, could only punch the ball backwards into his own net under pressure from Jan Paul van Hecke.

Palmer had earlier been booked for retaliation on Fernandes after the Spurs man handled the ball to stop a break.

That incident led to a touchline dust-up between the two benches.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But the consequences became worse when Palmer trod on former Blue Conor Gallagher and was shown a second yellow card by referee Chris Kavanagh.

The visitors were soon two goals as well as a man up, as Tel capped a fine afternoon with a good finish that beat Penders at his right-hand post.

It was no more than Spurs deserved, who were much the better side as they built on their first win of the campaign, against Coventry last weekend.

Transport for London put everyone in a good mood by closing the District Line again and leaving those on foot to get soaked on the walk from Earls Court.



And for a little while, it seemed the awful conditions would also seriously limit the quality of the football.

After a very scrappy opening of misplaced passes, Palmer had the first chance and saw his curling effort well saved by Antonin Kinsky.

But then James Maddison started to assert himself in his battle of the No 10’s with Palmer and, with the assistance of Sandro Tonali and Fernandes, helped Spurs take control.

De Zerbi’s side defied the rain to ping the ball around well at times, without particularly hurting the hosts until close to the half hour.



Tel, always a lively outlet down the left, returned a sharp pass from Andy Robertson and the former Liverpool man pulled the ball back to Omar Marmoush.

The Egyptian should have buried the chance, but fair play to Penders for making a smart stop to his left.

Moments later De Zerbi held his head in his hands again. Marmoush played in Tel, only for Penders to make his 6ft 6 ½ inch frame even bigger and save from a narrowing angle.

Chelsea hit back. Kinsky was guilty, not for the first time, of a poor clearance and Chelsea worked the ball well to Jordan Henderson.



The veteran midfielder had scored two peaches from distance in the 5-1 win over Bournemouth earlier in the month. But from closer range allowed the Spurs ‘keeper to make another good stop.

When Tottenham lost the ball again, Palmer fed Morgan Rogers, who replaced the injured Joao Pedro at centre forward, but once more Kinsky saved.

Unfortunately for Spurs and the spectacle, poor Maddison did not last even five minutes after the break.

Injury forced him off, and Gallagher, whatever his qualities, was not a like-for-like replacement.



Spurs continued to have most of the ball yet were unable to recreate the level of opening they had already wasted.

Chelsea, meanwhile, continued to rely on transitions. Rogers has had a fine start to his Blues career, but was unable to provide quite the same range of centre forward attributes as Pedro.



But the next chance did fall to the Blues. Some decent work by Rogers seemed to have gone to waste only for the ball to fall for Pedro Neto.

The shot was fierce, but straight at Kinsky, who batted it away.

The game was in danger of petering out, so both managers made changes.

When Fernandes stopped a Chelsea break by falling and holding the ball, Palmer retaliated and the Spurs bench charged towards the fourth official.

The Blues staff responded and squared off, with Alonso and set-piece coach Austin MacPhee in the thick of it.



On the field, Alonso turned to Estevao to provide the spark, taking off the disappointing Geovany Quenda, who was lucky to have lasted so long.

But Chelsea were undone when their dismal record at defending set-pieces this season continued.

Poor Penders was left a bit exposed but it was a horribly weak punch which sent Fernandes’ corner looping back into his own net.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Nor does Palmer have any excuse for the crude foul on Gallagher which was well worthy of a second booking.

Tel punished Chelsea with a well-hit second goal and the Spurs fans could go happy for once.

Sports.title: Fans furious as Cole Palmer avoids red card for slamming into Mateus Fernandes… but then sent off minutes later
Sports.content:
Next

COLE PALMER was sent for an early bath just minutes after escaping a red card for slamming Mateus Fernandes.

A rainy day in West London proved disastrous for 21-year-old Mike Penders after the ball slipped into his OWN net to put Tottenham ahead, before Mathys Tel doubled their lead.



Before it all fell apart, Palmer did his best to get down the right flank as he desperately searched for a lead against Spurs, who jump to 12th.

But Fernandes hit the deck amid the action and handled the ball.



The England international reacted with rage and slammed into Fernandes – creating a melee between players.

Micky van de Ven saw yellow for arguing with referee Chris Kavanagh, while Fernandes was also handed the same punishment.

And, of course, for Palmer.

Moments later, Penders’ slippy handling put the Blues on the back foot, throwing themselves into disarray.



And it got even worse after Palmer was shown a second yellow in the 80th minute for going in late on Conor Gallagher just outside the Chelsea box.

SkySports pundit Gary Neville could not believe his eyes when the No10 evaded punishment the first time round.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

He said: “Palmer’s reaction was silly.

“He’s asking for trouble, that’s not great. No idea why he’s doing that.”



And fans rushed online to agree with the former Manchester United skipper, with one writing: “Should be a red for Palmer that he’s extremely lucky.”

Another said: “Palmer should be off. Absolute joke.”

A third asked: “How’s that not a RED CARD for Palmer???”

A fourth even noted: “Same mentality issues. He was lucky not to get two reds. Head loss.”

And after the sending off, Neville added: “Not a good challenge, naughty, really naughty.



“He’s spot on the referee, Cole Palmer has lost his head in the last ten minutes.

“That one is no brainer. That’s just a silly challenge, he knows exactly what he’s doing.”

Roberto De Zerbi‘s Spurs look to be getting back on track, having beaten Coventry 3-1 on Monday, as they find themselves in their best league position since New Year’s Day.

The Lilywhites do not have a League Cup game mid-week after succumbing to a gutwrenching third round defeat to Liverpool last month.

Meanwhile, Xabi Alonso & Co’s slip up means they miss the opportunity to go level on points with third-place Brighton.

They will now travel to Anfield in the Carabao Cup‘s fourth round, before hosting Man Utd next weekend.

Sports.title: Burnley sack manager Nicky Hayen after just 12 games in charge with two-line statement following woeful start to season
Sports.content:
Next

BURNLEY have sacked manager Nicky Hayen after just 12 games following their shock defeat to Lincoln City.

The Clarets have dropped into the Championship relegation zone after a horrendous start to the season.



And their 4-1 thrashing by the Imps was the last straw for the Belgian.

Burnley released a brief 26-word statement confirming Hayen had departed the club on Saturday evening.



It read: “Burnley Football Club has dismissed Head Coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect.

“The Board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season.”



Hayen was only appointed in July and was tasked with helping Burnley secure an immediate return to the top flight.

But he failed to win any of his first EIGHT Championship games and his sole win came in a 4-0 win away at Watford earlier this month.

The dismal loss to newly-promoted Lincoln was Burnley’s second straight defeat after they were beaten 2-1 at home to Wolves last time out.

Hayen was repeatedly asked if he would stay on in the role after the Lincoln game but admitted his future was “out of my hands”.

“I know it’s a really hard defeat and something to think about for the board also.

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho ‘offered contract by LaLiga side Getafe’ worth £240k-a-week LESS than Man Utd deal
Sports.content:
Next

JADON SANCHO could be heading to La Liga side Getafe after reportedly being offered a shock deal.

The former Manchester United star was earning a whopping £250,000-a-week at Old Trafford.



But the 26-year-old’s alleged fresh contract would see him earn £10,000 a week – meaning a 96 per cent pay cut.

The Telegraph reported that Sancho received a formal offer from the Spanish club a little over a week after they made an approach.



But, they have put £350,000 on the negotiating table from now until June 2027.

The winger has been without a club since walking away from Old Trafford in June with his contract running out last month.



Sancho last appeared in a claret and blue shirt in May, featuring for nine minutes for Aston Villa in their victorious Europa League final.

The Watford and Manchester City academy product spent the season on loan at the West Midlands side following previous loan spells at Chelsea and Borussia Dortmund.

Now a blockbuster European move has the potential to rekindle Sancho’s electric career.

The London boy is said to be keen on the opportunity with reports suggesting that he is drawn to La Liga.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Sancho is hoping to meet with manager Jose Bordalas, who has called for his side to improve their recruitment, before he signs anything.

But there is a world of problems that could surface with the league’s specific salary caps.

An independent committee figures out what a player’s minimum acceptable wage is based on factors such as age, career history, previous earnings and market value.

Getafe, who have struggled financially, signed Real Madrid icon Dani Carvajal this October but had problems with matching the criteria.



Carvajal was valued at £2.2million and Sancho’s valuation may present similar issues being a 26-year-old, who was on £250k-a-week after joining United for £73m in 2021.

Getafe sit 16th in La Liga with just two wins from their nine league games this season.

They are due to travel to Athletic Bilbao tomorrow.

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany health update as Bayern Munich give recovery timeline on hospitalised boss
Sports.content:
Vincent Kompany health update as Bayern Munich give recovery timeline on hospitalised boss

Vincent Kompany remains stable in hospital after collapsing during a Bayern Munich training session on Friday and a club chief says it will take "weeks" for him to recover

View 2 Images Vincent Kompany is still in hospital (Image: Stuart Franklin/UEFA via Getty Images)

Bayern Munich chief Max Eberl says the club will have to protect Vincent Kompany from himself, revealing it will take "weeks" for the manager to recover from his illness.

‌



‌



Kompany was hospitalised on Friday, with an air ambulance landing at Bayern's training ground after their manager collapsed. The 40-year-old is in a stable condition in hospital, with tests ongoing to determine what happened after he initially fell ill with a viral infection.

‌



He took charge of Bayern's 2-2 draw with Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday before collapsing on Friday. Bayern will play Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday without their manager and director of sport Eberl gave an update on Saturday.

‌



"Vinnie will be given all the time he needs. We're not starting to put together any timeframes," said Eberl. "We need to firstly figure out what it is and then we'll discuss calmly what the recovery time is to be. We won't be talking about days, but weeks. We need to all be clear on that."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Eberl also responded to suggestions that Kompany should not have been on the touchline for Wednesday's Champions League game, having been ill since last week.

"The fact is, we protect our coach wherever we can," he said. "If a coach says he feels ready to do something, then we're not going to say 'we won't allow that' if we don't know what's going on.

‌



"It's also everyone's own responsibility to say, 'I can't carry on now'. Vinnie's a hard worker. If you don't listen to the subtle signals your body sends, eventually it will scream out in pain. Vinnie will be given that time [now], and we'll continue to try, even more than before, to protect him from himself."

He added: "The good news is he's stable. I spoke with him last night, as well as with his wife. He will have to stay in the hospital for a few more days until everything has been checked and verified.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 2 Images Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital (Image: 2026 FC Bayern)

‌



"The cause has been investigated all along. He already had minor issues last week. The doctors are doing nothing but figuring out what it is. The examinations have already yielded some results. But further results are needed to classify what it is and how long it will take for him to recover. I'm not a doctor. But we can support him energetically and lovingly.

Kompany's assistant Aaron Danks will take charge of Bayern against Freiburg. He has spoken with the Bayern boss in hospital and gave a brief update.

‌



"I explained to him that we would be having no football conversations," said Danks. "It was just checking in on his health and making sure he's OK. All the football operations are in our hands and we'll work together as a team to keep the club moving forward."

Speaking after the 2-2 draw with Arsenal, Kompany said: "As a coach, you always want to do everything and accomplish everything. I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn't listen to my body, and then at some point my body said: 'Stop now.'"

Sports.title: Kai Rooney stuns fans as they call for Man Utd promotion after win over Liverpool U18s
Sports.content:
Kai Rooney stuns fans as they call for Man Utd promotion after win over Liverpool U18s

Kai Rooney has set Manchester United fans' tongues wagging after his performance against Liverpool's Under-18s

View 3 Images Kai Rooney has wowed for Manchester United's Under-18s (Image: Getty)

Manchester United fans have called for Kai Rooney to be promoted to the senior squad after a sensational performance against Liverpool's Under-18s. United's youthful Under-18 squad, managed by Darren Fletcher, won 6-3 on Saturday morning.

‌



‌



Kai, the son of United hero Wayne, has been making waves throughout the club's academy. He joined the set-up aged 11 in 2020 and has progressed through the ranks, earning a two-year academy scholarship deal in July.

‌



Once he turns 17 on November 2, this deal will transition into a three-year professional contract. Last season, Kai featured primarily for the Under-16s and Under-18s, winning the Under-16 Premier League Shield and SuperCupNI. An injury slightly derailed his campaign.

‌



This term, Kai has made his Under-19 UEFA Youth League and Under-21 debuts. But he's mainly turning out for the Under-18s and started up front against Liverpool.

Michael Carrick makes Man Utd vow in emotional six-minute speech as pressure mounts READ MORE :

Wayne Rooney rips into 'selfish' Bruno Fernandes as Man Utd captain brutally exposed READ MORE :

Wearing the No. 9, Kai excelled. He led from the front with his pressing and set up Jaume Camacho, who scored four in the 6-3 drubbing. Fans online have made their true feelings clear on what the future should hold for the young Rooney.

View 3 Images Kai set up Camacho to make it 3-0 (Image: MUTV)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"Kai Rooney is a pressing machine," one fan wrote on social media. A second commented: "Kai played a really good game, top notch. He ran like his dad - chased everything down and made plays."

‌



Other supporters pointed out that Kai should be much closer to Michael Carrick's first team. One comment read: "He is always getting closer to first-team potential."

Another claimed: "Our Under-18s are far more enjoyable to watch than the first team! Pace, hunting the ball collectively, calmness in midfield. It's a breath of fresh air watching them every week!"

‌



One final fan simply remarked: "Can they play tomorrow?" These comments come as first-team boss Carrick weathers a severe storm after some lacklustre results.

View 3 Images Fans were impressed with United's Under-18s (Image: MUTV)

‌



With seven Premier League games played, United have won just once. Their latest outing saw them demolished 4-1 by Como in the Champions League.

Carrick spoke ahead of his team's home game against Bournemouth on Sunday and delivered an emotional address, opening up about recent struggles. He said: "Recently we haven't had a good time, I think that's pretty obvious.

Article continues below

"Wednesday [vs Como] was a bad night and it hurt me to see us play like that. It was unacceptable. My responsibility is to get a team on the pitch that represents this football club and the supporters and they can be proud of in the identity we show.

"We have gone away from that recently. It's important we all recognise that. The foundation and values of this football club have been etched for many years. I totally understand and get every single one of them."

Sports.title: Arsenal capitalise on Man City slip-up but Mikel Arteta still left with glaring concern
Sports.content:
Arsenal capitalise on Man City slip-up but Mikel Arteta still left with glaring concern

ARSENAL 2-0 EVERTON: Goals from Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhaes gave the Gunners a vital victory, moving them level with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League table

View 4 Images Arsenal took advantage of Manchester City losing (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal capitalised on Manchester City dropping points and beat Everton 2-0 to go joint-top of the Premier League table. The Gunners were boosted by City's first defeat of the campaign, with the pacesetters having lost 2-1 away to Aston Villa in the early kick-off.

‌



‌



Ezri Konsa gave Arsenal an early lead, scoring the Gunners' first goal from a corner this season. In truth, the soaking wet conditions at the Emirates made it a slog for both teams.

‌



But Gabriel Magalhaes' goal midway through the second half - one of his many important contributions after having an injury scare - was like a ray of sunshine for Arsenal and a storm cloud for Everton. The Toffees had a decent start to the season but remain winless since the international break and they now go into a cup-league double-header against Newcastle.

‌



After Wednesday's thrilling 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich, and with a trip to Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup coming next Tuesday, Arteta rotated his starting XI. Riccardo Calafiori's run of starting every league game this season came to an end while Viktor Gyokeres got the nod up front over Kai Havertz, with Mikel Merino also replacing Bruno Guimaraes.

Everton's slim resources were on show as David Moyes named two goalkeepers on the bench. Jarrad Branthwaite (concussion) and Jack Grealish (illness) were both ruled out of their trip to face the reigning champions.

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The return of Set Piece FC

It was the match fact that pessimistic Everton fans will've winced at. Seven games into last season, Arsenal had scored from a corner six times on their way to a record-breaking 19. Their record prior to Saturday: zero.

‌



Sadly for the Toffees, was only a matter of time until that changed.

In the seventh minute, a delivery swung in by Martin Odegaard caused chaos and the ball hit the crossbar via an Everton man. Viktor Gyokeres was first to get something on it before Konsa prodded home to score his first goal for Arsenal the day after his 29th birthday.

‌



Will Arsenal win the Premier League? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 4 Images Ezri Konsa scored Arsenal's first goal from a corner this season (Image: Mark Leech/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

‌



Moyes' half-time rant

After Arsenal dominated the first half and missed chances to extend their lead, David Moyes had every right to be upset with his team. But he was also furious with the referee.

Moyes, donning a cap in the pouring North London rain, waited in the tunnel at half-time and was seen telling Tony Harrington exactly what he thought of his performance. Everton captain James Tarkowski also wasn't happy with Harrington, and there was a feeling that the visitors had been on the wrong side of one too many decisions in the opening 45 minutes.

‌



Harrington couldn't please Arsenal either. After Tarkowski won a soft foul from Gyokeres in the second half, the Gunners bench were up in arms and Arteta was given a yellow card for their protestations.

View 4 Images David Moyes vented his fury towards Tony Harrington (Image: Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

‌



Gyokeres' drought leaves Arteta with concern

A goal-a-game for Sweden, but none in 10 for Arsenal. Rarely is a striker so prolific for his country and yet can't score for his club.

Arteta handed Gyokeres first league start of the season, a big opportunity to break his duck. But the Swede couldn't find a way through Everton's backline to even register a single shot.

‌



Kai Havertz replaced him in the 68th minute and remains Arteta's first-choice striker. A goal against Fleetwood could kickstart Gyokeres' season, but right now, Arteta - rather concerningly - can't rely on his £64million signing to get on the scoresheet.

View 4 Images Viktor Gyokeres hasn't scored for Arsenal this term (Image: Henry Nicholls/AFP via Getty Images)

Article continues below

Moyes would love to have two options up front, having been left reliant on Thierno Barry. The 24-year-old did nearly equalise with Everton's best chance of the game on the brink of half-time. Ben White's header back towards goal fell short and allowed Barry to sneak in, only for David Raya to pull off a sharp save low down.

Sports.content:

Sir Jim Ratcliffe didn't waste time making changes when he purchased a minority stake in Manchester United in 2024 and took control of the club's football operations

Former Manchester United chief John Murtough has been appointed director of football at Birmingham City. Murtough left Old Trafford in 2024, having spent 11 years at with the Red Devils.

‌



‌



The 55-year-old's departure via mutual agreement came shortly after Sir Jim Ratcliffe acquired a 27.7% stake, which has since been increased, in United through his petrochemicals company, INEOS, and made several changes to their football department. Murtough went on to join Atalanta, working as that Italian club's director of global development.

Now Murtough, whose CV also includes roles with Everton, Fulham, Coventry City and with the Premier League, is back in England. Birmingham confirmed his appointment on Friday and a statement from the club's board read: "We are delighted to welcome John to Birmingham City.

"We have been clear from the outset about our ambition for this Club and for the city of Birmingham. We want Birmingham City competing at the highest level of English football and we are building for sustained success, both on and off the pitch.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker warns Cesc Fabregas off 'graveyard' Man Utd - 'He'd be mad'
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker warns Cesc Fabregas off 'graveyard' Man Utd - 'He'd be mad'

Former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas has been touted as a potential replacement for Michael Carrick after Como's big win over Manchester United

View 2 Images Fabregas has been warned off the United job (Image: Xinhua/Shutterstock)

Gary Lineker has warned Cesc Fabregas he would be 'mad' to take the Manchester United job.

‌



‌



Red Devils boss Michael Carrick is under huge pressure after United were swatted aside 4-1 by Fabregas' Como side in the Champions League on Wednesday.

‌



The former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder has made a huge impression as a rookie boss at Como and has been touted as a potential replacement for Carrick should the Old Trafford hierarchy opt to make a change.

‌



But Lineker believes he would be foolish to trade what he is building in Italy for the 'graveyard' of the Theatre of Dreams.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"He’s going to have a big decision at some point because if he continues to have even moderate success with Como a big club will come in for him," he said on the Rest is Football podcast.

"It might be United. If he takes that job, he’d be mad! It’s a graveyard really."

‌



Fellow ex-England striker Alan Shearer agreed, adding: "I know it’s a huge football club, but it’s not an attractive job at the minute, because of how many [managers] have been in there and how many have been sacked.

"The only thing attractive about it is he might get a great pay-off in 12 or 18 months’ time."

‌



View 2 Images (Image: Jason Alden/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Fabregas was gushing in praise of Como's demolition of United, and admits he told them to 'slow down' when they went 4-0 up in order to preserve their energy levels for forthcoming matches.

‌



"I regret the last ten minutes because I was the one who told the team to slow down the tempo because there's another match and at 4-0 we could manage things a little," said the Spaniard.

“I told the players to stop running and stay in the middle and that is something I regret because I'm the first to always push them to fight until the end.

Article continues below

“Their goal hurt me because we dropped our intensity and dropped our defensive block, but it was my fault.”

Sports.title: 'Roy Keane ripped into me in blazing row – but I had the perfect response'
Sports.content:
'Roy Keane ripped into me in blazing row – but I had the perfect response'

Roy Keane launched a furious rant at a player who responded in the best possible way

View 2 Images Roy Keane launched a verbal tirade at James McClean in 2017 (Image: Getty )

Roy Keane once ripped into James McClean during a foul-mouthed dressing room row while on Republic of Ireland duty. But the winger, now 37, responded perfectly to his then-assistant manager Keane’s criticism about his application levels by scoring in the following game.

‌



‌



McClean celebrated his 50th international cap for Ireland by captaining his nation in a friendly against Mexico back in June 2017. But the then-West Bromwich Albion star had a poor game as his side lost 3-1, having conceded a penalty himself in the first half.

‌



Manchester United legend Keane, who was Martin O’Neill’s assistant at the time, unleashed his wrath on McClean and his team-mates in the dressing room at half-time. The pundit appeared to be especially triggered by a meeting with Irish boxer Mick Conlan before the New Jersey match.

‌



Writing in his autobiography The Walls, as per the Irish Independent, McClean said: "Martin [O’Neill] had just finished his bit when Roy came over, got right in my face and started f***ing me out of it.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Roy Keane finally breaks golden rule as Gary Neville mocks 'fawning' Man Utd legend READ MORE :

Sir Alex Ferguson was one day from becoming Arsenal boss as contract offer revealed READ MORE :

"'Look at you, the f***ing captain, f***ing giving off, yeah? You were taking pictures before the game with f***ing Mick Conlan. Your head isn’t f***ing in it.'"

‌



McClean remained silent during Keane’s dressing room scolding. But the ex-United skipper doubled down by accusing him of "having a big ego" in another furious rant during a gym session.

McClean continued: "He said he’d never been critical of me in the press or around the group, and now, the first time he’d said anything, I’d pulled him up over it.

‌



View 2 Images McClean had a poor game against Mexico (Image: Getty )

"Then he started going off about the Lamborghini at Sunderland, which was f***ing six years earlier. I was thinking he must have been seething for the afternoon, gathering information."

‌



That was in relation to then-Sunderland manager O’Neill having allegedly dropped the Irishman for buying a supercar. But McClean responded to Keane's comments in the best possible way, scoring in Ireland’s 3-1 friendly win over Uruguay in the following game and performing a selfie celebration.

McClean went on to reach 103 caps for Ireland, scoring 11 goals for the Boys in Green. He returned to his hometown club Derry City in January 2026 but has not played for the side since August due to a bitter public dispute with the club hierarchy.

Article continues below

Keane, meanwhile, left his role as Ireland's assistant manager in November 2018, departing alongside O’Neill and the rest of the coaching staff after a poor run of form where they failed to win across the entire year. His last managerial role was his five-month tenure as O’Neill’s assistant at Nottingham Forest, after which he has focused solely on his successful media career.

Sports.title: Man Utd dream defence next season with £160million duo signed and two stars axed
Sports.content:
Man Utd dream defence next season with £160million duo signed and two stars axed

Manchester United's season has got off to a disastrous start, and the pressure is on for Michael Carrick to turn things around

View 4 Images Michael Carrick can turn things around at Manchester United with the right recruitment (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Two arrivals and two departures could give Michael Carrick a very different Manchester United defence to work with next season. The priority should be to bring in Lewis Hall and Jarrad Branthwaite for a combined £160million, with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martinez making way.

‌



‌



That would leave Carrick able to field a back four of Diogo Dalot, Leny Yoro, Branthwaite and Hall. Matthijs de Ligt and Harry Maguire would offer experienced alternatives in the middle, while Ayden Heaven could continue his development.

‌



United's miserable start to the 2026/27 campaign has made the case for defensive investment increasingly difficult to ignore. Just two months into the season, the optimism generated by last term's surprise third-place finish has faded. United are in the bottom half of the table and struggling in the Champions League, leaving Carrick under intense pressure only months after his permanent appointment.

‌



The problems extend beyond just results. Captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to question Carrick's tactics after the midweek Champions League drubbing at Como. A week earlier, Martinez had criticised senior club figures for failing to strengthen the squad adequately over the summer.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

United signed Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, concentrating their recruitment on midfield after focusing on the attack the previous summer. That strategy has left the defence short of the improvements it needed, while problems persist going forward.

‌



Left-back is the most obvious place to start. United entered the campaign relying on 31-year-old Luke Shaw as their first choice despite his long-standing fitness concerns. It is a gamble that has not paid off.

Signing Hall from Newcastle would be a solid starting point. The 22-year-old England international remains a primary target for director of football Jason Wilcox and Ineos, having been monitored by United in recent months. The Magpies told United he was unavailable in the summer, so securing him would require a substantial offer.

‌



View 4 Images Lewis Hall is a long-term target of Manchester United (Image: Stu Forster, Getty Images)

Hall was reportedly interested in moving to Manchester and remains keen, giving United reason to test Newcastle's resolve again in the next transfer window. Recent reports claim he could cost north of £80m.

‌



Shaw could still feature for the rest of this season. Beyond that, United should look to sell him in the summer, recognising his 12 years of service while moving towards a more reliable long-term option. With 12 months left on his deal, a decision on his future is approaching.

The other major change should come on the left side of central defence. Lisandro Martinez was reportedly considering his departure even before his criticism of Wilcox and the club hierarchy.

‌



View 4 Images Lisandro Martinez has reportedly been put up for transfer (Image: Michael Steele, Getty Images)

Atletico Madrid were linked with him during the summer and interest from Spanish clubs remains. The 28-year-old favours La Liga, with United said to be weighing up whether to let him leave. His contract expires next year, though the club can trigger a 12-month extension to help secure a transfer fee.

‌



Branthwaite, who TEAMtalk claim costs around £80m, is the obvious player to replace him. United are understood to be considering another approach for the Everton defender after having two bids worth up to £50m rejected in 2024.

Aged 24, the left-footed centre-back brings crucial Premier League experience and would seamlessly slot into United's new-look defence, accelerating their much-needed overhaul. His performances so far this season earned him a place in England’s recent Nations League squad, strengthening the argument for United to renew their interest.

‌



View 4 Images Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite would be a top signing (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Alongside him, Yoro is showing signs of progress despite his red card against Atletico Madrid. De Ligt remains a useful option when fit, while Maguire offers the leadership and professionalism that this unsettled dressing room needs.

Article continues below

United are expected to activate the extra year in the 33-year-old's contract, allowing him to help guide Yoro and Heaven. Keeping that experience would make sense while changing two other key positions.

Dalot and Mazraoui may not be outstanding options at right-back, but it is less urgent than the problems on the opposite flank and at centre-back. Hall and Branthwaite would address those priorities directly - and give Carrick a stronger platform from which to rebuild.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Club chiefs jet out on £50m scouting mission as talks set for January switch
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Club chiefs jet out on £50m scouting mission as talks set for January switch

Liverpool may have fallen short in their recruitment efforts over the summer but will reportedly be busy in January as a string of potential deals emerge

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola's staff are reportedly hard at work scouting Valencia's David Otorbi (Image: Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola is beginning to leave his mark as Liverpool manager after piecing together three straight wins for the first time at Anfield. However, the Reds look set to continue their evolution in January as several major deals start to gather traction.

‌



‌



Sunday's clash against Brighton will be a fierce test of just how well things are truly going under Iraola's command. The Seagulls have soared up to third in the Premier League table, two places above Liverpool, after enjoying the fruits of their own transfer labour.

‌



Ahead of a hectic week that also comprises an EFL Cup showdown with Chelsea, the transfer rumour mill remains hard at work. Mirror Football has dissected the latest transfer headlines around Anfield heading into a key weekend clash.

‌



Reds scout £50m gem

Liverpool are reportedly escalating their interest in Valencia winger David Otorbi and have had scouts in attendance to watch the youngster. Their interest comes amid reports the 19-year-old will soon see his price-tag double after impressing this term.

Otorbi put pen to paper on a two-year contract back in April, complete with a £25million release clause and the option of another three-year extension. Reports in Spain now suggest Los Che are on the verge of triggering that option, which would also increase the forward's release clause valuation to £50m.

It would mean Valencia will have the bargaining security to demand that entire fee for his signature. Although Rio Ngumoha has started to show extreme promise as Liverpool's new star on the right wing, more competition for the role wouldn't go astray.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Liverpool have had scouts in attendance at Valencia games to monitor the progress of Harvey Elliott during his loan. However, they may have identified another fine prospect in the process, one Valencia appear eager to keep out of the clutches of English suitors.

‌



As part of keeping tabs on Elliott, Liverpool are also reported to have met with Valencia manager Javier Aguirre and sporting director Braulio Vazquez to discuss the matter. However, it's plausible exploratory talks have also taken place regarding Otorbi's future and whether there's a place for him at Anfield.

Agents meet over Ndukwe solution

View 2 Images Liverpool are meeting with Ifeanyi Ndukwe's representatives to discuss bringing the Levante loanee back in January (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Ifeanyi Ndukwe's stellar start to life in Spain could be set to earn him an Anfield lifeline sooner than expected. In fact, the player's agents are due for talks with his parent club about potentially ending his loan spell at Levante early, according to reports.

After a super pre-season, Ifeanyi was farmed out due to the fact he couldn't obtain a UK work permit and Liverpool had already used up their quota of non-eligible players. He's since started pulling up trees in La Liga and established himself as an increasingly prominent member of Levante's starting XI.

‌



Sky Sports Austria has reported the Reds will discuss the matter with Ndukwe's representatives this weekend. After shining in La Liga, the 18-year-old has accumulated enough points necessary to obtain the proper work permit and is eligible to play in England.

‌



Despite the recent rise in results at Anfield, defensive solidity remains an area of concern for Liverpool. In that sense, another option at centre-back wouldn't go astray, especially after loanee Ronald Araujo has impressed while playing on the right side of defence.

Rave reviews in Spain suggest Ndukwe could soon outgrow Levante, who will not be keen on the idea of losing the player. However, Liverpool could execute a masterstroke after including a clause in his contract to recall the player this winter.

Sports.title: Arteta collating evidence of other managers stepping out of technical area
Sports.content:
Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta says he is compiling footage of rival Premier League managers repeatedly leaving their technical areas after receiving his second yellow card of the season in his side’s 2-0 win over Everton.

Arteta joked about installing sensors on the sidelines, having been booked by referee Tony Harrington in the second half at the Emirates Stadium.

The Spaniard faces a one-match touchline ban if he receives another yellow card but believes other top-flight managers have repeatedly breached the rules without being punished.

Image: Mikel Arteta remonstrates with the fourth offical in Arsenal's 2-0 win over Everton

"I do have to be careful, yeah," said Arteta. "I'm going to put sensors there!

"There are other managers (doing it), there are managers that have the record in the league: 36 times in 10 minutes they leave the touchline, no yellows.

"So I am clipping all of that so I have a massive storage of images, so if somebody comes to me (I can say) I'm not in the record yet, somebody else has the record."

Arteta hails Arsenal 'mentality'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Arsenal and Everton

Arsenal moved level on points with leaders Manchester City thanks to goals from centre-backs Ezri Konsa and Gabriel.

Konsa opened his account for the club in the seventh minute, converting from close range following a Martin Odegaard corner as the Gunners scored from a set piece for the first time this season.

Gabriel sealed victory with a 68th-minute header after recovering from an injury scare which left him down on the pitch requiring medical treatment.

Arteta believes the Brazil international's determination epitomises his team's character.

Image: Arsenal's Gabriel celebrates after scoring the second goal (AP Photo/Ian Walton)

"The mentality of the team is the mentality of the individuals in the team," said Arteta.

"Gabi's a great example of that, because we were all scared, not because of the way he went down, but the reaction of the players that were next to him.

"Immediately he says he wants to continue and then he scores a goal to help us win the game. That's what we need from our players."

Calafiori picks up 'slight' issue

Arteta, who revealed substitute Riccardo Calafiori sustained a "slight" issue, also praised England international Konsa for adapting quickly following his summer move from Aston Villa.

"Unbelievable," said Arteta. "He's come to a huge club like Arsenal with no pre-season when (William) Saliba is here, with other players that are already here.

"And to position yourself in that manner, with that naturality and performing at the level that he's doing and building already a chemistry and a balance with Gabi that seems so solid, it's very, very difficult to do and we are really lucky to have him."

Everton manager David Moyes rued his side's slow start as they suffered a second successive defeat following last weekend's 2-0 loss to Chelsea.

Asked for his overall assessment, Moyes said: "Not an awful lot, really. I don't have big thoughts on it.

"I just felt we didn't really get to a level which I think would have been good enough to win on the day. We gave away a goal very early which meant we were chasing (the game).

"I felt we'd got a bit better in the second half, got a bit back into it a little bit more, got a bit closer to Arsenal and then they come up with the second goal.

"Some good stuff on the defensive side of it. I didn't feel we did enough on the attacking part of the game."

Sports.title: Murrell on target as Falkirk breeze past Kilmarnock stormy conditions
Sports.content:
Two own goals helped Falkirk climb to seventh in the Scottish Premiership table with a dominant 3-0 victory over Kilmarnock.

Visiting centre-backs Cathal McCarthy and George Stanger converted past Calum Ferrie either side of a Jacob Murrell header.

Following a tough start to the campaign, John McGlynn's men have lost just one of their last six games.

It was clear from an early stage that the side who coped best amid torrid conditions would prosper.

That team was emphatically Falkirk, with focal point forward Murrell netting his fifth league goal of the season.

Neither side gained a level of control over the ball, never mind the game as a whole, for much of the first half but the Bairns adapted better.

A wild wind was firmly against the visitors in that 45, making for a fraught opening spell.

Leon McCann's deep cross was blown towards the top corner, forcing Ferrie into emergency action to tip the ball over the crossbar.

The Kilmarnock goalkeeper's kicks barely made it 35 yards.

Owen Eames skewed wide with the first decent chance as Falkirk began to stretch the game midway through the half.

They opened Killie up down the right to seize a 29th-minute lead. Ethan Ross conjured a terrific deep delivery to pick out Murrell at the back post.

The American did not muster much power behind his header and it looked bound for Ferrie's arms. However, on-loan Hull defender McCarthy needlessly thrust out a knee to connect and beat his own keeper.

Image: Falkirk's Jacob Murrell celebrates after Kilmarnock take the lead

Kilmarnock came within inches of a swift reply when a Tom Lowery cross was diverted onto the bar and went over.

Falkirk remained well on top, however, and doubled the lead seven minutes before the break.

Ferrie batted away a Ross drive at his near post to concede a corner. Ryan Strain's delivery found Murrell evading the attention of Erik Ring to flash a header off the underside of the bar and in.

Image: Falkirk's Jacob Murrell (C) celebrates with team mates after scoring to make it 2-0

Torrential rain added to the treacherous conditions as Falkirk rode out a period of early second-half pressure to take change once again.

Liam Henderson headed across goal from Brad Spencer's cross. Murrell could not make a clean connection with the overhead attempt and Ferrie scooped up.

Within a minute of Neil McCann bringing on Mark O'Hara and Nicky Clescenco to provide a spark, all hope of a comeback was extinguished. Stanger's attempted clearance of a Deniss Melniks header from a Falkirk free-kick gave Ferrie no chance.

The Killie keeper made fine stops from Eames and Murrell to keep the score down. And the visitors passed up their one chance for a consolation. With Scott Bain committed well out of his goal, Ieuan Owen missed the empty goal from 30 yards.

What the managers said...

Falkirk boss John McGlynn:

"We played the conditions - it's what you have to do and we make no excuses for that.

"But there were a lot of really good individual performances in our team. Finley Barbrook was excellent in a different position. Big Deniss (Melniks) came into midfield and did so well and Jacob (Murrell) got another goal.

"Jacob is very confident now. Like everything else, you come from America and you've got to adjust.

"Loads of things are different, even driving on the other side of the road is something you've got to get used to.

"He's living in Glasgow, he's now settled down, he's comfortable and his form is really, really good. A couple of goals last week, another one today.

"He takes the header really well. It's a carbon copy of the goal he scored at Tannadice from a corner. From my point of view, long may that last."

Kilmarnock manager Neil McCann:

"It's just a horrible game of football. The conditions were absolutely terrible for both teams.

"But the bottom line is Falkirk did the ugly side of the game and the basics better to get the reward of three points. We, of course, wanted to get the ball on the deck.

"But today wasn't about getting the ball on the deck.

"I said that to them before the game. It's not, 'forget everything we've worked on' - it's just playing the conditions.

"I'm fully aware of that. I'm an experienced guy in football. I understand that you can't be a purist out there."

Sports.title: Hamilton fastest from Verstappen ahead of US GP Qualifying
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton topped final practice from Max Verstappen at the United States Grand Prix to set up a tantalising qualifying in Austin.

Hamilton was 0.168s quicker than Verstappen as Ferrari and Red Bull look set to fight for pole position and victory for a second consecutive weekend.

Charles Leclerc topped both of Friday's sessions and had set the quickest time in final practice by one tenth from Hamilton, only for it to be deleted due to track limits.

Track limits is set to be a major issue for the drivers in qualifying, which takes place at 10pm UK time later on Saturday (build-up from 8.30pm live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event) due to the tarmac run-off areas and the drivers keen to use every bit of track to gain lap time.

Leclerc still finished the session in third, ahead of championship leader Kimi Antonelli whose chances of becoming the youngest world champion look extremely difficult, given he must first win the Grand Prix to give himself an opportunity, and Mercedes are a tad off the pace.

Antonelli was three tenths behind Hamilton's pace-setting time with his Mercedes team-mate George Russell in fifth at nearly half a second down.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater explains how Kimi Antonelli can clinch the F1 world title this weekend at the United States Grand Prix

McLaren's Lando Norris was eighth but would have been in the top five had his best lap not been deleted for track limit, while Oscar Piastri was sixth and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg impressed in seventh.

"There was a feeling in the paddock, and having spoken to other teams, that maybe Ferrari's pace was potentially unrealistic yesterday in terms of how quick they were," said Sky Sports F1's Anthony Davidson.

"But, I would say, when it gets to this stage in the weekend I think it's more genuine than first met the eye yesterday. I know Ferrari often are quite strong in free practice sessions and that melts away in qualy, but I've got a feeling today they are going to hang on to that speed."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Christian Horner explains how he convinced Niki Lauda to sign Hamilton for Mercedes in 2012

Traffic was an issue for some drivers with Hamilton having to take avoiding action at the end of the back straight when approaching Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto, while Red Bull's Isack Hadjar fumed at Alex Albon as he claimed the Williams driver got in his way into Turn 1.

Hadjar was only 10th in final practice and one second off the pace behind Alpine's Pierre Gasly.
