Sports.title: Leicester down holders Northampton as Bristol beat Exeter
Sports.content:
Leicester Tigers' dominant second-half performance earned them an impressive 28-7 victory over defending champions Northampton Saints.

Saints actually led at half-time at a soaking Mattioli Woods Welford Road, but they had no answer as the Tigers turned on the power to score four tries following the restart.

It meant that Leicester enjoyed a third win in four league games, as well as beating their East Midlands rivals at home for a fourth season running, in jumping up to second in the table.

The wet and windy conditions quickly played a part as Northampton grabbed the game's opening try after only seven minutes. With advantage being played, Fin Smith chipped towards the Leicester try line and, after Billy Searle's fumble, James Pater pounced to score, with Smith adding the conversion.

The Tigers were on the board after 19 minutes when Freddie Steward blasted a superbly struck penalty between the uprights from just inside the Northampton half.

It remained 7-3 to Saints at half-time, but a fracas down the touchline as the players made their way towards the tunnel indicated a fiery second half was on the way.

The home crowd was brought to its feet four minutes after the restart when a driving maul rumbled its way over with Jamie Blamire grounding the ball, although Searle's missed conversion meant Leicester's lead was just one point.

But their dominant start to the half brought a second try when the ball was worked out to the left to Gabriel Hamer-Webb whose pass led to Cameron Henderson scoring in the corner. Searle's conversion again slid wide.

The Tigers were more than a score clear, though, when Finn Carnduff crashed over from close range in the 57th minute after a beleaguered Saints defence had illegally collapsed a maul.

Having not converted any of his side's three tries to that point, Searle extended the hosts' lead further with a penalty from in front of the posts.

Northampton's afternoon continued to disintegrate when they had Tom Lockett sin-binned for making head-on-head contact with Solomone Kata with 10 minutes left.

And the Tigers rubbed their noses in it by claiming a bonus point not long after when Searle's long pass found Steward and the England full-back glided in under the posts.

Bristol see off Exeter in stormy conditions to move third

Bristol Bears moved third in the table with a hard-fought 20-7 win over Exeter Chiefs in appalling conditions at Ashton Gate.

It was their fifth successive league victory over Rob Baxter's men after an old-style-rugby war of attrition in heavy rain and strong winds.

Exeter had the better of the opening exchanges and enjoyed a period of pressure on the home line. However, hanging on to the slippery ball in the tackle was proving a major problem for the visitors and several potential scoring opportunities were squandered.

Even though they had their own difficulties, Bristol's handling was much better and it enabled them to put a lot of pressure on the Exeter line, but the Chiefs' defence held firm.

It looked likely that the interval might be reached with the game still scoreless until a long pass by England scrum-half Harry Randall found Gabriel Ibitoye in space on the left wing, and he made light of the attempted cover tackles to cross in the corner and give the Bears a 5-0 lead.

Centre James Williams slotted an excellent touchline conversion and he was also on target with a 35-metre penalty three minutes later, when Olly Woodburn was penalised for not releasing in the tackle after catching one of many high balls he had to deal with in the first half, to increase the Bears' lead to double figures.

Chiefs had a chance to break their duck nine minutes into the second half when Henry Slade tried to get on the end of Sam Wolstenholme's grubber kick through the home defence, but the ball squirmed from his grasp.

Moments later, though, Chiefs kicked a penalty to the corner and Greg Fisilau was driven over in emphatic style, with Slade converting to get the Chiefs right back in the contest.

They even had chances to draw level in the last 10 minutes when they turned down two kickable penalties inside the 22, but when Bristol got their own opportunity three minutes from time, Williams was immaculate with the boot.

And when Luka Ivanishvili forced his way over moments later, the win was sealed and Chiefs were denied the losing bonus point.

Sports.title: Ramsay and Sule fire St Mirren to victory over Dundee
Sports.content:
St Mirren ended a run of five straight defeats as goals from Calvin Ramsay and Eseosa Sule secured a 2-1 win over Dundee.

Wing-back Ramsay fired Saints ahead in the 20th minute with his first goal since joining the club on loan in the summer.

Sule doubled the lead for the Buddies in the 57th minute to give his side a real grip of the game.

Dundee pulled a goal back in the 73rd minute through Bradley Fink after a decent spell of pressure but the visitors could not find an equaliser.

St Mirren were first to threaten as the wintry conditions played a role in the early stages. Ismeal Kabia unleashed a shot from the edge of the box, but it was held by Dundee goalkeeper Owen Goodman.

The home side made the breakthrough when Sule broke down the righ before playing the ball across goal into the path of Ramsay, whose shot trickled over the line with the block from Goodman unable to keep it out.

Image: St Mirren's Calvin Ramsay celebrates after scoring to make it 1-0

The Saints loanee almost doubled his tally when he rose to meet a free-kick from the left. His header fell straight into the arms of Goodman, who then spilled the ball before it was scrambled clear.

Sule turned scorer in the second-half to give St Mirren full command of the match. A cross from Killian Phillips was met by the head of the attacker on the edge of the six-yard box to double the home side's lead.

Dundee pushed to get a foothold back in the game with Ashley Hay bulleting a header narrowly wide from close range.

The visitors did eventually pull a goal back through Fink. St Mirren keeper Jacob Chapman saved the initial shot only for the Dundee striker to knock the ball home at the second attempt.

The away side pushed for an equaliser in the latter stages, but the Buddies held on to claim all three points, much to the delight of a delirious but sodden home crowd.

What the managers said...

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish:

"I'm delighted for the group. They probably needed something like that.

"It's easy for me to keep saying the same messages and keep talking to them about their confidence and belief and what we're trying to do, but when you go on a run like we've been on, it can be difficult for the players at times.

"We had one really good run, we've had a poor run, hopefully that's us coming out of it now as well."

Dundee boss Steven Pressley:

"In the first half we showed a lot of bravery in possession, in terms of our build-up and in controlling the game, but we didn't ask enough questions of them defensively.

"We spoke prior to the game about that particular fact: that we must ask questions of them defensively in a variety of ways. We didn't ask enough of them.

"Credit to St Mirren. They've gone through a difficult period, and they showed a lot of resilience today."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Burnley sack head coach Hayen with 26-word statement
Sports.content:
Burnley have sacked head coach Nicky Hayen.

The Belgian took charge in the summer but has overseen just one win from their club's first 12 Championship fixtures and the Clarets were beaten 4-1 at Lincoln on Saturday.

Hayen apologised to the Burnley supporters for the performance after the game.

In pre-season, Burnley had been among the favourites for promotion and to make an immediate return to the Premier League but are third-bottom and in the Championship relegation zone. They have the joint-worst defensive record in the league.

A 26-word statement from Burnley announcing his sacking read:

"Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect. The Board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season."

Hayen's reign began with a Carabao Cup penalty shootout win over League One Notts County but they were knocked out in the next round on spot kicks by Bradford.

Hayen's only other win came in a 4-0 victory at Watford on October 10.

Speaking to the media following the loss to Lincoln, Hayen said: "It's the same story of the season for us that we keep conceding easy goals and you saw that in the second half.

"They want to work hard, but you have to show it. What we do in training is really good, but we can't execute that the same way in the games. Is that pressure? I don't know.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Lincoln City and Burnley.

"It's frustrating for everyone, especially the fans. I want to apologise to them, but I know it doesn't matter because it's another hard defeat for them and I can understand their criticism.

"We haven't got the results. I will keep on working hard as long as I have the chance. But there will be a day if it carries on like this that it stops.

"I don't know (if I will still be in charge). I know it's a really tough defeat and something to think about for the board."

Sports.title: Giant Sequoia stakes Classic claims in Futurity
Sports.content:
Giant Sequoia produced an eyecatching performance to win the William Hill Futurity Trophy at Doncaster and in the process virtually guarantee Aidan O’Brien the trainers’ championship.

It was stablemate Sergei Diaghilev who set a brisk pace at the head of the Group One field, before the race began to take shape as they hit the two-furlong pole, with all the runners on the stands side.

Ryan Moore and favourite Noble Exhibit put down their challenge a furlong and a half out, but Giant Sequoia (11-1) was travelling strongly upsides and really picked up when asked by Dylan Browne McMonagle, stretching three lengths clear of Andrew Balding's staying-on Gran Dia.

It was a record-extending 13th success in the race for O'Brien, who had been happy to draw a line through the winner's disappointing effort in last month's National Stakes.

He said: "He disappointed the last day, but that was when our horses were off colour.

"I'm over the moon with him really, he travelled well, quickened very well and I'm delighted for everyone at home. It's a big team effort.

"He's very classy, he could be anything next year. He was just under the weather the last day. We gave him time, his work has been lovely.

"We weren't sure about that ground, but you never know until you try. He's very classy."

O'Brien has won the Town Moor feature with three subsequent Derby winners and added of the Frankel colt: "We always thought he was a Classic horse, a mile or a mile and a quarter would be no problem, but he could get a mile and a half. His dam (Pink Dogwood) was very good and she stayed.

"We always thought he was very good, a proper horse. I'd say he's a Guineas, Derby, French Derby horse, all those things.

"One of his owners is American (John Stewart), but we had four others for the Breeders' Cup so we tried to space them out a bit!"

On Noble Exhibit, who was edged for second by Gran Dia, O'Brien said: "He was a bit green, he was running around a lot.

"He won making the running twice and probably didn't learn a lot. Maybe in that ground he gave him the chance to run green and he got there and ran around a bit."

While Browne McMonagle has been winning countless big races for O'Brien's son, Joseph, this was his first Group One for the Ballydoyle handler.

"He's a great rider, that's all you can say," said O'Brien.

The jockey himself said: "He's a horse who has developed plenty throughout the year, he's a big boy to sit on.

"The race worked out perfect, it was a nice even tempo and he relaxed. I felt like halfway on it was just a matter of sitting into him and he reacted quick.

"He quickened well and when I got to the front he was having a nice look, but he's still a big baby and he's going to be a lovely horse next year.

"Everyone was very complimentary of him and they said he was a lovely horse and going up to a mile was always going to be a help to him. I think he'll get further in time and he's very solid. He's definitely a good horse."

He added: "That's a first Group One for Aidan, so a big thanks for the leg-up."

Bengal Tiger far too good for the rest in Prospect Stakes

Aidan O'Brien's Bengal Tiger looked a class apart as he left the field in his wake to land the William Hill Remembering Sue Wright Prospect Stakes at Doncaster.

Ryan Moore was happy to settle the 10-11 favourite on the outside as the keen-going Crystal Queen pulled them along in front in the six-furlongs Listed affair.

Moore shook his mount up with a quarter of a mile to race and as soon as he asked for an effort with a furlong to go Bengal Tiger put it to bed, streaking clear to score by three and a half lengths from Hi Corbett Court.

O'Brien thinks the winner will easily stay further and views him as a Classic contender.

Image: Bengal Tiger, ridden by Ryan Moore, on their way to winning the William Hill Remembering Sue Wright Prospect Stakes at Doncaster

"What he did the last day at Naas shouldn't usually happen, no matter how bad the race was the time was very good," said O'Brien.

"We were going to go to the Horris Hill at Newbury, but that got abandoned. We wanted to go there because we thought he'd love going seven furlongs, but we switched back here.

"The last half a furlong he started to take off, he's going to get seven easily and I'd say he's a Classic horse.

"It's unusual for one by No Nay Never to go through heavy ground like that, but he's out of a good Galileo mare (On Ice), so we shouldn't be surprised.

"It wasn't his speed that won him it today, it was staying, the last furlong he was getting going."

Sports.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
Sports.content:
There were times when Roberto De Zerbi’s frustration threatened to boil over. The Tottenham manager cut a tense figure in his technical area. He bounced around for 90 minutes and let out blasts of fury whenever he saw something that displeased him, but in the end he was able to celebrate leading Spurs to their first win at Stamford Bridge since 2018.

It was not a pretty game. It was not a good game. The breakthrough was a comedy own goal from Mike Penders. The young Belgian goalkeeper, deputising for the injured Emi Martínez, was culpable when Spurs went ahead, flapping at a corner from the excellent Mateus Fernandes and punching the ball into his own net.

Xabi Alonso, who saw his side lose at home for the first time this season, could argue there was an element of fortune to the result. But this was one of Chelsea’s worst performances since appointing the Spaniard in the summer. They were caught out at both ends. Penders’ inexperience proved costly and Chelsea struggled without João Pedro leading the line. It was strange that Alonso did not start Danny Welbeck.

Chelsea were blunt and knew they were beaten when Cole Palmer was sent off shortly after the own goal. Mathys Tel soon made it 2-0 to clinch a second consecutive win for Spurs and lift them into 12th place.

Quick Guide Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham key facts Show • Spurs gained just their second away win in 35 attempts against Chelsea in the Premier League (D11 L22) and their first since April 2018 (3-1). • Spurs have beaten Chelsea in all competitions at Stamford Bridge while keeping a clean sheet for the first time since December 1986 (also 2-0). • Chelsea’s Mike Penders (21yrs 85d) is the second-youngest goalkeeper to score an own goal (pictured) in the Premier League, after Illan Meslier (20yrs 354d) for Leeds against Wolves in February 2021. • Cole Palmer’s sending-off was the 100th red card Chelsea have been shown in the Premier League (excluding rescinded cards), becoming the third team to reach this milestone after Everton (113) and Arsenal (110). Photograph: Tom Jenkins Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

If Spurs were to improve on their dismal record in this fixture then they would have to take care of Chelsea’s fast starts under Alonso. The absence of João Pedro helped on that front, forcing Alonso to modify his attack, and the opening exchanges were muted. Both sides lacked someone to hold the ball up and the closest either went to scoring an early goal came when an error from Fernandes led to Antonin Kinsky pushing a shot from Palmer away.

Chelsea never adjusted to their 4-2-4 system. The experiment with Palmer and Morgan Rogers as false 9s left them without an obvious outlet. Pedro Neto was not receiving the ball in good positions on the right and Geovany Quenda, making his first start since joining from Sporting Lisbon, was tentative on the left.

View image in fullscreen Mike Penders’ punch, under pressure from Jan Paul van Hecke, goes in off his glove, giving Spurs the lead. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Spurs built confidence, their midfield of Fernandes, Sandro Tonali and James Maddison outplaying and outnumbering Moisés Caicedo and Jordan Henderson. As ever the challenge was finding a clinical touch. There was not enough conviction to Spurs. Mohammed Kudus and Tonali sent hopeful efforts off target. Tel wasted opportunities to run at Josh Acheampong and Omar Marmoush failed to take the best chance of the first half, pinging a shot too close to Penders from Andy Robertson’s cutback.

Marmoush, preferred to Dominic Solanke as Spurs’ No 9, buzzed around but was often gobbled up by Maxence Lacroix and Levi Colwill. But it was a similar story at the other end. Kinsky saved from Henderson after giving the ball away but Chelsea created little before half-time.

View image in fullscreen Roberto De Zerbi is jubilant after Mathys Tel doubles Spurs’ lead. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Spurs were comfortable. Too comfortable? Their luck was out at the start of the second half. Maddison, who was a doubt before the game, had played well before making way for Conor Gallagher. Not that there was a response from Chelsea. Fernandes, the best player on the pitch, was running the game for Spurs.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea played in random bursts, Neto testing Kinsky, and a flurry of changes followed. Solanke and Pedro Porro for Marmoush and Robertson were positive moves from Spurs, while the home fans were happy to see Estêvão come on for Quenda.

Estêvão was soon involved, bursting in from the right and shooting into the side netting. The temperature had risen, Chelsea fired up after a clash between Palmer and Fernandes led to some aggro between the benches. But with the quality so low it was fitting that the opening goal arrived in farcical circumstances.

View image in fullscreen Cole Palmer (right) was booked twice in the space of a few minutes, leaving Chelsea down to 10 men for the final 10 minutes. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s set-piece coach, was busy telling four home players to stay high when Spurs won a corner in the 77th minute. The box emptied out, Fernandes delivered from the left and Penders got his angles horribly wrong. The 21-year-old, who struggled in the air when Chelsea beat Leeds in the Carabao Cup last month, was thrown by a challenge from Jan Paul van Hecke and watched in horror when his weak punch spun into his empty net to give Spurs a shock lead.

Chelsea were still coming to their senses when any hope of a comeback disappeared. Palmer, on a booking after his row with Fernandes, could have no complaints when he received a second yellow for a lunge on Gallagher. It was Chelsea’s first red card of the season and came a day after Alonso had spoken about emotional control helping his side improve their disciplinary record.

Not here. Down to 10 men, Chelsea faded. It was over when Tel skipped in from the left and clinched the points for Spurs with a crisp low shot from 20 yards.

Sports.title: Clinical Arsenal earn precious win against Everton thanks to Konsa and Gabriel
Sports.content:
The wait goes on for David Moyes. The 63-year-old Scot must have been hoping that on his 14th visit to this stadium as Everton’s manager, his luck would change. Yet from the moment Ezri Konsa slammed home his first goal for Arsenal as the Premier League champions rediscovered their knack of scoring from set pieces, the writing was on the wall.

While it took until midway through the second half for Gabriel Magalhães to make sure of the victory, Arsenal were never going to let slip the chance of moving level on points at the top with Manchester City after their defeat by Aston Villa earlier in the day.

Asked whether it was strange that his side are again going toe-to-toe with their great rivals but with the added uncertainty of what punishment City will receive after being found guilty of 115 charges by the Premier League, Mikel Arteta said: “[We are] just focusing on what we can do. We are very pleased with 90% of the results and performances that we have.”

This was hardly a vintage performance from the clinical home side after a testing week but it did not need to be against opponents who offered precious little in attack, even if they defended for their lives at times.

Having gone six matches without defeat to start the season, a second in succession will only add to Everton’s concerns after confirmation that the club’s American owners want out.

“It was always going to be hard after conceding the early goal,” said Moyes, whose solitary victory at the Emirates was as West Ham’s manager in 2023. “I want us to challenge the top teams but it’s difficult when you see the strength of their bench.”

Everton’s record at this stadium is almost as bad as their manager’s. They arrived in north London having won twice in 35 matches here and had to do without Jarrad Branthwaite and Jack Grealish, who was ruled out with illness. It did not bode well for them when Arsenal took the lead in the seventh minute with a third corner in succession.

View image in fullscreen Ezri Konsa (No 15) squeezes the ball home for Arsenal’s early first goal against Everton. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Gabriel made the crucial first contact at the near post and Jordan Pickford tipped the ball on to the crossbar, only for Vitaliy Mykolenko’s failed clearance under pressure from Viktor Gyökeres to allow Konsa to ram home from close range. After a record-breaking 25 goals from set pieces last season, it was their first of this campaign.

It was a measure of Arsenal’s exertions against Bayern Munich on Wednesday that Arteta rotated his side more than usual for a Premier League match, making five changes.

Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke spurned good opportunities to extend the lead in front of the watching England head coach, Thomas Tuchel. The latter was left out of the last squad, but could well benefit from Bukayo Saka’s expected long absence due to a thigh injury. He was inches away with an instinctive effort with his right foot from the edge of the area on the half-hour mark and was consistently Arsenal’s most dangerous threat.

Everton must have feared the worst as yet another Arsenal corner – 10 during the first half – was launched into the area. Yet the defence just about stood firm.

A moment’s lapse of concentration from Ben White just before half-time almost gave Everton an equaliser but Thierno Barry could not get enough on his attempt to flick the ball past David Raya in their clearest opening.

Gyökeres looked determined to make an impression on his first Premier League start of the season but the Sweden striker, who has yet to score for his club this term, looked laboured.

Quick Guide Arsenal 2-0 Everton key facts Show • With both Arsenal and Manchester City doing so this season, this is just the third top-flight campaign to have two teams win at least seven of their opening eight matches after 1892-93 (Preston and Sunderland) and 1913-14 (Blackburn and Manchester United). • This was David Moyes’s 400th defeat across all competitions in his managerial career with all clubs. 31 of these have come against Arsenal, more than against any other opponent. • The opener from Ezri Konsa (pictured celebrating) was Arsenal’s first set piece goal (excluding penalties) since May against Crystal Palace, ending a run of 13 games without one. Opta Photograph: Adam Davy/PA Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

He could not believe it when Tony Harrington penalised him for a foul on James Tarkowski and a sheepish Arteta earned himself a booking for protesting. Unsurprisingly, Gyökeres’ number was up soon after as Arsenal turned to their bench.

It took less than 60 seconds for Gabriel to head in at the back post as White offered Tuchel a timely reminder of his qualities with a brilliant cross.

Moyes’ frustration meant he joined Arteta in the referee’s notebook. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall could have made things interesting but his header fizzed just wide of a post.

Arsenal are now breathing down City’s necks, although whether this title race lasts the course remains unknown.

Sports.title: Fulham climb out of drop zone after Oscar Bobb’s late show sinks Coventry
Sports.content:
Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a win against Coventry that lifted Álvaro Arbeloa’s side clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to score in the 80th minute, twisting his way into the area and bending a shot into the far corner. It was his second goal for the club since his £27m move from Manchester City in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by beating Hull 1-0.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s team second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon that bought the Coventry fans back down to earth after their 4-1 win against Newcastle in their previous home match.

“I think we are improving as a team,” Arbeloa said. “We are competing for 90 minutes. I talked to the players. It’s not about if we play well for 60 minutes or 30 minutes, we need to understand that you need to compete for 90 minutes.

“Understand the game, understand what you have to do. Sometimes you need to defend your box, sometimes you will control the game.

“Sometimes you need to win because of the quality of your players. I think it was a good game as a team but at the end the quality of Oscar in one moment decides the game.”

Quality was in short supply between two teams who started the day in the bottom three. King should have broken the deadlock in the 18th minute when afforded too much space in the box, but his powerful shot rebounded off the top of the upright before Alex Iwobi sent a wild follow-up effort high and wide.

At the other end, Bobby Thomas met Jack Rudoni’s free-kick but got his angles all wrong as he headed well wide, before Brandon Thomas-Asante missed from Jay Dasilva’s cross after a good run forward from Rudoni.

A mis-hit back pass from Antonee Robinson offered Thomas-Asante another chance but his shot lacked power as Leno easily gathered.

View image in fullscreen Ephron Mason-Clark is denied by the Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno. Photograph: Paul Currie/Shutterstock

While Coventry were piling up half-chances Fulham were the ones bossing possession but, in keeping with their season so far, struggling to turn that dominance into goals. The Coventry defender Milan van Ewijk almost helped them out, deflecting Robinson’s low cross dangerously close to his own goal as it found the side-netting.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Just before the break Calvin Bassey went down in the box claiming a shirt-pull from Thomas-Asante, but the referee Adam Herczeg waved play on with replays suggesting they each had a hold of the other.

The video assistant referee had taken a look, and was involved again early in the second half when Rudoni’s free-kick from the right struck Iwobi on the arm before he cleared, but the Nigerian’s arms were by his side and play was waved on.

Coventry then suffered a major blow when the in-form Thomas, praised by Lampard in midweek, hobbled off just before the hour, replaced by the teenage Manchester City loanee Stephen Mfuni.

The hosts were starting to build some momentum after a series of substitutions but it swiftly ended as Bobb struck with 10 minutes to go.

Coventry tried to respond but a powerful strike from Matt Grimes was blocked and a late penalty appeal for handball against Shea Charles was waved away with the midfielder having had his arm tucked in.

“If it ends 0-0, I think both say fair play,” Lampard said. “Fulham are a good team, they’ve been creating a lot of chances – you can see why. They didn’t give us massive problems around our box but they found a moment of quality that we couldn’t find.

“We didn’t have any real zip at the top end of the pitch, so that’s disappointing. Sometimes it can happen. This is the Premier League. They’re trying to stop you and if you want more it’s not always there. We’ve got to keep pushing on.”

Sports.title: Relief for Slegers as Russo rescues Arsenal against Tottenham in WSL
Sports.content:
Alessia Russo’s contentious second-half penalty delivered relief, a reprieve and a chance for a reset as Arsenal came from a goal down to earn their second win of the WSL season in the north London derby.

At a rain-lashed Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Gunners were again their own worst enemy, forced to come from behind after Cathinka Tandberg’s headed opener. Georgia Stanway levelled and Russo powered in the penalty that gave them the lead they protected defiantly.

The Tottenham manager, Martin Ho, queried the penalty decision, with the ball hitting the raised arm of substitute Ella Morris from the clearance of one of her teammates. “My interpretation of the rule is if your teammate hits it and it hits your player, if you’re one yard away, the time and distance is taken into account, so there’s no penalty,” he said. “That’s my understanding of it, from when we were told to start the season. I want to understand what they’re saying, because then I can accept the decision.

“I don’t want the game to be about that, but when it decides a game it’s frustrating because it’s not within the law of the game.”

Arsenal’s manager, Renée Slegers, said she was glad to give the fans a win. “They sing us and fight us through the game,” she said. “At the end it’s scrappy, it’s game management and it’s scenarios, and they’re all with us.”

With the pressure building on her and her players after five games without a win, at times it felt like they were trying to disprove the phrase “you can’t dig yourself out of a hole”.

Quick Guide Brighton cruise to victory against West Ham Show Maisie Symonds’ first-half stunner sent Brighton on their way to a 3-0 win against West Ham at the Amex Stadium. The midfielder Symonds’ thunderbolt gave the Seagulls a half-time lead before Fran Kirby and Kiko Seike struck quickfire goals midway through the second period. It was a first clean sheet this season for Arturo Ruiz’s side and lifts them up to eighth in the table, two points above West Ham, who slipped to 12th after their fifth league defeat of the campaign. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Arsenal had looked a little shaky in the opening few minutes but they settled, built possession and started to pose a threat. A failure to carve out clearcut chances and capitalise on any period of dominance has been the running theme of their season. They lacked fight and there was sloppiness too, with too many overhit passes putting the ball out of play or giving away possession.

That the opener came from a Tottenham corner was unsurprising. Victoria Pelova swung the ball in and Tandberg rose above her two markers, Stanway and Emily Fox, who failed to even to jump and challenge, and headed home.

Spurs’ joy was short lived as Stanway made up for her marking error four minutes later by arriving to meet Russo’s cut back and powered the ball in off the crossbar.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Georgia Stanway equalises for Arsenal in the 17th minute. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

After the break there was concern for Tottenham when Alice Sombath’s leg seemed to twist awkwardly as she stretched for the ball. The club’s record signing left on a stretcher to be replaced by Morris, who made her return from an anterior cruciate ligament injury towards the end of last season.

After the lengthy stoppage, Russo forced a huge save from Lize Kop as she attempted to turn in Caitlin Foord’s cross from close range, the forward putting her hands to her head and screaming in frustration at the missed opportunity.

It did not take long for that frustration to transform into elation. The resulting corner from Kyra Cooney-Cross was headed on by Leah Williamson at the near post and Lisa Baum’s effort came back off the post. Spurs’ clearance bounced off the raised arm of Morris and the referee pointed to the spot. Russo sent Kop the wrong way and drove the ball low into the corner.

Arsenal were clinging on as the final whistle loomed but they had “found their fight,” said Slegers. “We had a run of games where results haven’t been good enough. It was frustrating for everyone. I’m so happy we got to win on this occasion, in the north London derby, away from home in the rain and we showed that character in the team.

“This will definitely energise us. We need to back this up in the next couple of games.”

Sports.title: Maresca ‘not worried’ by Guéhi’s gaffes as Aston Villa end City’s flawless start
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches, the Manchester City manager said after seeing his side lose in the league for the first time this season.

Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowed Ipswich to score twice against City last weekend.

“No, I’m not worried about Marc at all,” Maresca said. “I know that he’s played every minute since the season started with us, with the international team, so it’s not easy. But again, the change was also because he was on a yellow card and in the way we want to be aggressive, sometimes to have one yellow card can be dangerous, but I’m not worried at all.”

City had 15 shots to Villa’s eight as they dropped points for the first time this season. Zion Suzuki made a number of important saves to keep City at bay in the second half, and Villa scored with their only two shots on target.

“I think we deserved more from the game, for the amount of chances that we created and for the chances that we conceded,” Maresca said. “We lost because probably we have not been clinical enough in their box and sometimes when you concede the first goal because of the mistake, the second goal again comes from transition in 45 minutes. It’s difficult to avoid that every time, but we learn from the game and we try to move on and to improve.”

View image in fullscreen Nicolas Jackson scores Aston Villa’s first goal past Gianluigi Donnarumma. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

Jackson’s double takes him to seven goals since his move from Chelsea. He was a constant threat to the City centre-backs, who were unable to cope with his speed, physical presence and clinical finishing. Unai Emery said of his forward: “He’s very demanding of himself to improve things. Today he scored two goals, in the last matches he scored goals – but at the beginning of the season, what happened to us was more difficult and he was shooting a lot of balls over the corner.

“Now, he’s getting better at shooting. He’s working fantastically tactically, he’s understanding as well where we need him. Today, he scored two goals, but the most important thing is how he did his work, his task.”

His fellow summer signing Suzuki challenged Jackson for the player of the match award and is starting to show why Villa were so keen to acquire him as Emiliano Martínez’s replacement. Matty Cash told TNT Sport: “He’s brilliant, his first session when he came in, in the possession drill I thought we’d signed a midfielder. His vision is unbelievable, he catches crosses really well which as a full-back is a dream.”

Sports.title: European football: Roma snatch late draw in 3-3 thriller as Como win again
Sports.content:
Roma missed the chance to move top of Serie A, but preserved their unbeaten status as Leonardo Balerdi’s 89th-minute goal snatched a thrilling 3-3 draw at Napoli. Scott McTominay put Napoli ahead with his second goal in the 83rd minute, but Balerdi completed his own double to ensure Roma extended their undefeated start to the league campaign to eight matches.

Como backed up their Champions League victory over Manchester United as Anastasios Douvikas scored twice in 11 minutes for a 2-0 win against Sassuolo. They climbed to fourth in the table, two points adrift of Inter who host Fiorentina on Sunday. Later on Saturday, Lazio host Parma.

Maximilian Beier scored in the 80th minute to send Borussia Dortmund top of the Bundesliga table after a hard-fought 1-0 home win over Eintracht Frankfurt.

In a game lacking clear chances, Jobe Bellingham came off the bench and threaded a clever pass for his fellow substitute Beier to score less than a minute later. The narrow victory was Dortmund’s first in the league since mid-September and took Niko Kovac’s side three points clear atop the Bundesliga table.

Bayern Munich can return to the top of the table with a win at Freiburg on Sunday but will be without their coach, Vincent Kompany, who is being treated in hospital for a mystery virus after collapsing at training on Friday.

Niclas Füllkrug scored for the sixth straight Bundesliga match as Werder Bremen won 3-2 at Mainz. Füllkrug, who returned to Bremen on loan from West Ham in the summer, converted two penalties inside the opening 25 minutes. Ludovit Reis grabbed Bremen’s other goal, while Anthony Caci and Lee Jae-sung scored for the hosts.

RB Leipzig completed a comfortable 4-0 home win over promoted Elversberg. Romulo scored twice while Tidiam Gomis and Christoph Baumgartner also got on the scoresheet.

Paderborn’s Rayan Philippe scored in the 88th minute against Hamburg, his parent club, to grab the promoted side a 1-0 victory. Augsburg drew 1-1 with Union Berlin as both sides finished with 10 men. Cologne and Schalke played out a scoreless draw in a match marred by a head clash between the visitor’s Robin Gosens and Soufiane El-Faouzi, who left the field after a first-half collision.

In La Liga, Georges Mikautadze snatched a late 2-1 win for Villarreal in their derby against Valencia, who had Harvey Elliott sent off as both sides finished with 10 men. The visitors came from behind to triumph, leaving Javier Aguirre’s side 19th.

View image in fullscreen Harvey Elliott, on loan at Valencia from Liverpool, was sent off in the 89th minute against Villarreal. Photograph: Maria Jose Segovia/DeFodi Images/Shutterstock

Pepelu put Valencia ahead from the penalty spot in the first half before the American defender Alex Freeman headed the visitors level after 69 minutes. Iñigo Pérez’s Villarreal had Pape Gueye sent off when the Senegal international hit José Gayà in the face with his elbow.

However, Elliott, who is on loan from Liverpool, was soon dismissed for two quick yellow cards for apparent dissent. Mikautadze broke through in stoppage time, racing through and finishing with aplomb to claim the three points.

Later on Saturday, Atlético Madrid are at home to Deportivo A Coruña in Spain, while in France, Lens visit Paris FC in a game that will send any winner to the top of Ligue 1 overnight, a draw sufficing for the hosts.

Sports.title: Burnley sack Nicky Hayen after Lincoln rout leaves them in bottom three
Sports.content:
Burnley have sacked Nicky Hayen after only 14 games in charge, in the wake of a 4-1 defeat at Lincoln that left the Clarets in the Championship’s relegation zone.

The Belgian was appointed in the summer as the permanent successor to Scott Parker, who left in April with relegation from the Premier League inevitable. He leaves having won just one match, a 4-0 league victory at Watford on 10 October.

Burnley edged past Notts County on penalties in the Carabao Cup in his first match in charge and recovered in the last seven minutes from 2-0 down to draw at home to West Ham in their opening game of the Championship season. However, they then lost badly at West Brom and Norwich, sandwiching a shootout exit from the Carabao Cup at Bradford, and the pattern was set.

Burnley were fancied to push for promotion, which was achieved in their past two Championship seasons, but are now at risk of relegation. Wolves’ come-from-behind win at Turf Moor last weekend left Hayen on the brink and now the club have acted.

A terse, two-sentence statement on the club website said: “Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect. The board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season.”

Hayen had earlier said in his post-match press conference, before news of his dismissal emerged: “It’s frustrating for everyone, especially the fans. I want to apologise to them, but I know it doesn’t matter because it’s another hard defeat for them and I can understand their criticism.

“We haven’t got the results. I will keep on working hard as long as I have the chance. But there will be a day if it carries on like this that it stops. I know it’s a really tough defeat and something to think about for the board.”

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Kelsy fires Rangers to emphatic win; Dundee United pip Aberdeen
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes asked his Rangers side to be “brilliant” against St Johnstone and was rewarded with a 4-0 Premiership win at Ibrox. After dropping two points at Dundee last Saturday, the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from the Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy.

Saints started the second half brightly but goals from the Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. The Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on the midfielder Nico Raskin, before the substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining.

McInnes said: “It’s quite ironic in the sense that we were so good and so brilliant at times in the first half and create so many opportunities, that we were only a goal to the good at half-time. And obviously, we don’t want to let the frustration of those missed opportunities and dominance filter into the second half.

“I think half-time came at a bad time for us because, despite the conditions, some of the play was really good. I asked the players to be brilliant today, not just win the game, can we really commit to being the best we can be, as good as we can be? And I thought we were in the first half. Everything was brilliant except the result at half-time because we should have been more in in front.”

Celtic can restore their four-point advantage over Rangers at the top when they travel to Hibernian, the bottom side, at noon GMT on Sunday.

Dundee United won a rollercoaster game 3-2 against Aberdeen at Tannadice. Zidane Iqbal scored for the hosts before the visitors equalised through Nesta Guinness-Walker – both players scoring their first goals for their clubs.

United took the lead once more thanks to a Dylan Tait strike, with Connor Ronan drawing Aberdeen level after the break. Zac Sapsford secured all three points for his side, with the win moving United up to fourth – one point behind Hearts, who are at Motherwell on Sunday – while Aberdeen dropped to ninth.

Two own goals helped Falkirk climb to seventh with a 3-0 victory over Kilmarnock. Centre-backs Cathal McCarthy and George Stanger scored past their own goalkeeper either side of a Jacob Murrell header. St Mirren ended their losing streak with a 2-1 victory over Dundee with goals from Calvin Ramsay and Eseosa Sule before Bradley Fink pulled one back for the visitors.

Sports.title: James Maddison suffers devastating injury blow as Tottenham secure historic win at Chelsea
Sports.content:
Tottenham pulled off an historic win over Chelsea after a devastated James Maddison picked up another injury.

Maddison, who has not long returned from a nine-month lay-off, was substituted after 50 minutes on Saturday evening.



4 Maddison looked defeated as he appeared to hold back tears while being treated and walking off the pitch on Saturday Credit: Getty

4 But Spurs went on to win the game without one of their key men, making history with a 2-0 victory away at rivals Chelsea Credit: Getty

At the start of the second half, cameras cut to the Spurs midfielder being surrounded by some of his teammates on the pitch.

He then sat down on the grass, looking emotional and holding back tears as the realisation of another potential issue set in.



Maddison recently opened up to talkSPORT about the 'dark days' of his recovery from an ACL injury after making his first start in a competitive match since May 2025 on Monday.

As he left the pitch at Stamford Bridge, he was hugged by some Chelsea players as well as multiple Tottenham stars.



And even Blues boss Xabi Alonso gave him a hug as he walked, head down, off the grass and straight down the tunnel.

Thankfully, Maddison later came out of the dressing room and returned to the bench to celebrate the huge 2-0 victory.



Maddison injury update

Speaking post-match, De Zerbi gave an update on Maddison.

He told talkSPORT: "We have to manage Maddison like a diamond.

"He's a special player, but not just about his qualities, as a personality, as an experienced player.

"Now we have to make the medical check to understand what the problem is. But we need him, absolutely."

4 Maddison pulled up with no player around him and walked off the pitch looking forlorn Credit: Getty

History made at Stamford Bridge

Losing Maddison would be a huge blow for Spurs of course, but they managed to end Saturday evening on a high.



De Zerbi's men went on to beat Chelsea 2-0, picking up just their second ever Premier League win at Stamford Bridge.

It was also their first victory while keeping a clean sheet at Stamford Bridge since December 1986.

An own goal from Blues goalkeeper Mike Penders and a late second from Mathys Tel made history for Tottenham.

The victory came against ten men in the end, as Cole Palmer was shown his first career red card after two yellows.



Chelsea have now received nine red cards in the Premier League since the start of last season, at least four more than any other side.

4 Spurs won at Stamford Bridge for just the second time ever in the Premier League Credit: Getty

The result has the Blues now just four points clear of Spurs, who have now gone three unbeaten and won two in a row.

They are now up to 12th in the top flight after the 2-0 win.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta issues fresh Bukayo Saka update amid reports he faces two months out
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has revealed that Bukayo Saka is facing 'weeks' out in a fresh update on his star winger's worrying injury.

Saka went down in the opening minutes of the Gunners' Champions League draw against Bayern Munich under no pressure.



2 Saka pulled up in pain immediately after making a pass in midweek and went on to miss Arsenal's clash against Everton on Saturday afternoon Credit: Getty

With the score at 0-0, he pulled up after attempting to play a crossfield ball, immediately going ground and indicating that he was unable to continue as medics came on to assess him.

He clutched his thigh as fell over and was then replaced by Eberechi Eze, who went on to score in the match in Munich.

The game finished 2-2 in the end, but concerns remained over Saka after he picked up what looked to be a serious knock.



And Arteta confirmed post-match on Wednesday: "They [the medical staff] are a bit concerned. The player having to come off feeling a sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see."

Saka hasn't trained since and went on to miss Arsenal's 2-0 win over Everton at the Emirates on Saturday afternoon.



How long will Saka be out for Arsenal?

After that victory, Arteta then gave another update on the England international amid reports he could be out for two months.

The Gunners boss told talkSPORT: "We have to wait. It will be weeks.

"I think in a week or ten days we're going to have another scan because there's so much fluid at the moment.



"So the picture is not that clear to give you an exact amount of time.

"But it looks like it's going to be weeks."

2 Arteta has revealed that Saka is going to be out for 'weeks' and he is due to have another scan on his injury soon Credit: Getty

Arsenal and England's injury blow

Saka has made ten appearances in all competitions at club level this season, scoring four goals and assisting once.

Three of his goals have come in the Premier League, while has scored and provided an assist in the Champions League.



Noni Madueke played in his place against Everton, with Arsenal coming out on top with ease, even without Saka.

The Gunners may be able to cope without him, but England are also set to be without one of their stars next month.

If Saka is out for multiple weeks, then manager Thomas Tuchel will be missing him for the upcoming November internationals.

The Three Lions face Croatia and Spain in their final two Nations League group stage fixtures in just three weeks time.



Saka started in three of England's four games in the previous international break, and scored a double in the 7-0 thumping of Croatia.

Sports.title: EFL boss immediately sacked just hours after latest defeat
Sports.content:
Burnley have sacked manager Nicky Hayen following their 4-1 defeat away at Lincoln in the Championship.

Hayen was unable to prevent the Clarets from picking up their sixth loss in 12 games on Saturday.

3 Burnley manager Hayen only won one game in the league since being appointed in the summer Credit: Getty

Burnley, who were only relegated from the Premier League last season, are currently sitting in the relegation zone.

Their loss to newly-promoted Lincoln, in another game in which they took the lead, leaves them in 22nd spot in the second tier having won just one game all campaign.

And Burnley, who haven't won at home since October 2025 - the longest streak in the top four tiers of England - have wasted no time in announcing the axing of Hayen just hours after their latest loss.

A club statement read: "Burnley Football Club has dismissed Head Coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect.

"The Board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season."

talkSPORT understands that Kenny Miller is one of several names appreciated by Burnley for the now vacant position, with the Sotsman impressing in charge of Maccabi Tel Aviv.

Hayen's axing comes shortly after he told talkSPORT that his future at the club is in the balance, where he also apologised to fans.

What did Hayen say after the defeat to Lincoln?

When asked post-match if he fears being sacked, Hayen told talkSPORT: "Fear? I know how it goes in football, especially with the results we have had in the last few weeks.

"I spoke with the owner last week in terms of the injuries that we had and the upcoming game, and also that we had a good training week.

"But for one or another reason, we can't bring the same quality in the game that we show on the training pitch.

3 Burnley were easily beaten by Lincoln in the Championship on Saturday to compound the misery of Hayen and his side Credit: Getty

"That's a little bit of a shame because the boys deserve much better and that is unfortunately the reality."

Then, on whether he hopes to continue in his role as manager, he added: "Yes, of course you hope to continue. But I know how it goes.

"I also feel sorry for the fans as there were a lot of fans here, so I do apologise.

"I know even if I apologise to them it doesn't matter because again we have a big loss and I know they're frustrated and I totally accept it."

'Absolute disaster'

Hayen spoke honestly about his and Burnley's woeful start to the Championship season, but unfortunately for the Belgian, it wasn't enough to save his job.

Burnley legend Ben Mee had declared after the Lincoln defeat that the writing was on the wall for the manager.

3 Hayen failed ti impress during his spell in charge of Burnley Credit: Getty

Speaking on talkSPORT's GameDay Live, Mee, who made 367 appearances for the Clarets, said: "Absolute disaster today.

"Going there and capitulating as they did, going 1-0 up, the quality in the group, the attitude of the group, it seems to be a theme this season.

"Lose a goal, heads go down, whether the players' mentality is right, whether they want to be at the club...

"I think there's players in there that were trying to leave in the summer, maybe didn't get the wish, the heads and the focus aren't quite there.

"The manager's gone in and maybe taken over a squad that's not as together as what he would have liked.

"He's going to find out, he's going to get the brunt of it, I think."

Sports.title: Chelsea name surprise striker for Tottenham clash after unexpected Joao Pedro blow
Sports.content:
Chelsea name surprise striker for Tottenham clash after unexpected Joao Pedro blow

Joao Pedro was not in the Chelsea squad for their derby defeat to Tottenham, with a surprise name taking his place.

Rather than Danny Welbeck taking Pedro's spot leading the line for the Blues, Geovany Quenda was handed a start.

3 Quenda made his first Premier League start against Spurs, replacing Pedro in the Chelsea team over Welbeck Credit: Getty

It was Quenda's first Premier League start since arriving at Stamford Bridge, having played just 28 minutes this season so far.

The natural right winger was preferred to Welbeck, despite the latter being an out-and-out striker to replace Pedro.

Welbeck remained on the bench for Xabi Alonso's side, with Quenda coming in and him, Cole Palmer, Pedro Neto and Morgan Rogers playing fluidly across the front line.

Why is Pedro not in the Chelsea squad?

Chelsea's top scorer Pedro was missing from their squad for their clash against rivals Spurs due to an injury.

His new issue is currently being assessed.

Alonso confirmed pre-match: "Yesterday in training he felt something, and at the moment he has some liquid, so we have to do some tests to know how big the injury is.

"It's disappointing, but we need to carry on."

Pedro had started Chelsea's last two games, scoring two against Bournemouth before playing against Everton.

But he did previously miss international duty with Brazil due to a knock that reportedly saw him visit a knee specialist.

And that came after he also sat out of the Blues' clash against Brentford before the extended international break.

3 Pedro was missing for Chelsea after picking up an injury that is currently being assessed Credit: AFP

Who is Geovany Quenda?

Quenda took Pedro's place in a surprise decision, considering the 19-year-old wide man hasn't started a Chelsea game before.

The Portugal U21 international joined the Blues this summer from Sporting Lisbon in a deal that was agreed last year.

Since his £43.5million move, Quenda hasn't managed to break into Alonso's line-up, competing with Pedro, Rogers and Palmer.

But with Pedro out, he was given a chance.

On deciding to start Quenda, Alonso explained: "He has many qualities, he attacks the space well, he has been training well and all the players will have their opportunities at times.

"Geo has been patient and today's a big game for him."

3 Quenda has never started a game for Chelsea, but he was part of the attacking unit in a huge clash against Spurs Credit: Getty

He ended up playing 72 minutes of the game at Stamford Bridge.

Estevao took his place for the final stages as Spurs shocked Chelsea and came away 2-0 winners in the London derby.

Sports.title: Championship star breaks English football record just 15 minutes into match
Sports.content:
QPR's Richard Kone stunned Swansea on Saturday with the fastest hat-trick from kick-off since English football records began.

Kone took less than two minutes to open the scoring at Loftus Road, before doubling the hosts' lead seven minutes later.

2 Kone's hat-trick is the earliest in the top four divisions of English football for at least 22 years Credit: Getty

And when QPR were awarded a penalty, he did the business from 12 yards to put Julien Stephan's side seemingly out of sight within a quarter of an hour.

In doing so, Kone recorded the earliest hat-trick from the start of a match in England's top four divisions since records began (in the 2004/05 season when the EFL rebrand took place).

He beats the previous record held by Sadio Mane for Southampton against Aston Villa in 2015 by a minute.

Mane still boasts the fastest hat-trick in terms of time elapsed between the first and third goals - scoring all three within two minutes and 56 seconds in that famous 6-1 victory for Saints.

But Kone now has his own little slice of English football history.

Kone out of nowhere

Kone's quickfire treble was made all the more remarkable by the fact that Swansea came into the game boasting the league's best defensive record.

Swansea had conceded just eight goals in 11 Championship matches prior to Saturday.

It's certainly some way to get off the mark for the season – Kone had only scored once in 13 games since March.

But he wasted no time in drawing level with Paul Smyth as QPR's top league goalscorer this term.

This was Kone's second professional hat-trick – and his first at Championship level.

2 Kone's goalscoring talent became clear during his time at Wycombe, where he scored 21 goals in the 2024/25 campaign Credit: Getty

He previously helped himself to three goals for Wycombe Wanderers against Peterborough United in League One in October 2024, completing that hat-trick within 11 minutes of coming off the bench.

The 23-year-old has now scored 34 EFL goals, having been given his big break by Wycombe.

Kone's story so far

The Chairboys signed Kone from non-League Athletic Newham in January 2024.

Born in the Ivory Coast, the striker had initially come to England to play in the 2019 Homeless World Cup.

And since banging in an utterly prolific 42 goals in 48 games in his first season in the Essex Senior League, he's gone from strength to strength.

Kone left Wycombe for QPR in August last year and earned his first senior international cap that November.

Victory for QPR will keep them firmly in the Championship play-off hunt.

This season's play-offs have been expanded from four teams to six, meaning eighth place will be enough for a shot at promotion come May.

Sports.title: National League match abandoned after 14 minutes of chaos
Sports.content:
Barrow's National League match against Forest Green Rovers was abandoned on Saturday after just 14 minutes.

Referee Stuart Morland took the decision to end the game after the pitch became waterlogged due to Storm Boelo.



1 The match was deemed unplayable after just 14 minutes following a pass that held up completely on the waterlogged pitch Credit: Forest Green Rovers

The huge storm has hit the UK this weekend, leading to incredibly windy and rainy conditions across the country.

Barrow, who are based in Barrow-in-Furness, play their football right on the North West coast and the weather has been severe.

A wind warning had been announced for Northern England by the Met Office before kick-off, but the National League clash went ahead.



That was despite the green light being given by referee Morland after a lengthy pitch inspection.

But the game didn't last long, with officials calling time just 14 minutes in after Barrow had already taken an early lead.



With the score at 1-0 to the hosts, they posted on X: "Due to circumstances beyond our control, the game has been abandoned."

Meanwhile, after announcing the same, Forest Green wrote: "We understand this is very frustrating for the FGR supporters who have travelled to Barrow today. We wish you all safe travels back home."



The club then posted a video to X showing just how chaotic the conditions were for both teams at Holker Street.

It showed a Barrow player attempting to pass the ball back to his goalkeeper, but it completely held up in the waterlogged pitch, allowing Forest Green forward Sean Etaluku a chance on goal.

That was the moment that Forest Green labelled the 'deciding factor', and the referee subsequently called the game off.

'It was quite farcical'

Forest Green do not have a manager, but one of their coaches, Yan Klukowski discussed the abandonment post-match,



"It was the right decision," he began. "But it was quite farcical in the end, the game should never have started with the conditions of the pitch.

"It was quite clear in the warm-up that the ball wasn't rolling correctly or truly."

Klukowski added: "The referee had been here two, three hours before kick-off, he had his concerns which he highlighted before we arrived.

"His communication was good...at that point you could sense there was an element of him being extremely worried.



"He had the initial inspection, there was a lot of doubt but he decided we were going to give it a go, but looking back it looks like a poor decision and one he should have made then."

Will the match be rearranged?

According to FA rules, the match will be replayed fully as it was abandonded due to circumstances out of the clubs' control.

A new date will be agreed by the clubs and the National League.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League star desperate to see Trent Alexander-Arnold back at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Liverpool cannot allow Trent Alexander-Arnold to join a Premier League rival if he returns to England - he's too good.

That's the view of ex-Southampton star Charlie Austin, who has commented on reports linking Alexander-Arnold with a move away from Real Madrid amid a lack of game time.



2 Alexander-Arnold has been an unused substitute in three of Real's last five LaLiga games Credit: Getty

And Austin - a Liverpool fan - would welcome the right-back returning to Anfield.

Asked by Andy Goldstein on talkSPORT Drive whether he would take the defender back — whose departure from his boyhood club last year did not go down well with Reds supporters — Austin hesitated, but ultimately said he would, for one main reason.

What did Charlie Austin say about Trent Alexander-Arnold?

"If I'm taking him back to the Premier League, do I want to see Trent Alexander-Arnold at another Premier League club? Absolutely not," the former QPR and West Brom frontman explained.



"He would make teams better... sometimes, you have to just park it and if he comes back [to Liverpool], he's going to have to mend a lot of bridges, but him playing for Manchester City, him playing for Chelsea... that's a horrible thought, it really is."

Alexander-Arnold has fallen out of favour at Madrid, with Jose Mourinho preferring captain Fede Valverde — a midfielder by trade — at right-back.



Austin's comments come after Alexander-Arnold's ex-England teammate and fellow right-back Kyle Walker told talkSPORT the 28-year-old would realistically have to sign for a Premier League club other than Liverpool.

What did Kyle Walker say about Trent Alexander-Arnold?

"Can he go back to Liverpool with the way that he left [Liverpool fans didn't take kindly to Alexander-Arnold's departure just before his contract expired]? I'm not too sure," Walker said.



"Do I see him at another club? He's got to go to one of the big ones: Manchester United, Man City."

Liverpool born and bred, Alexander-Arnold angered the Anfield faithful by running down his contract on Merseyside.

The opportunity to join Real Madrid was understandably a hugely appealing one, but he's generally found it tough going with the 15-time European champions.

2 Alexander-Arnold starred in both of Liverpool's Premier League title wins to date Credit: Getty



Trent might need to leave Madrid to revive England career

Having been recalled to the England squad after missing out on selection for the World Cup, he's been an unused substitute for each of Madrid's last three games in all competitions.

Speaking after his international return against Czechia last month, Alexander-Arnold acknowledge that he would need to 'prove himself' at club level to stay in Thomas Tuchel's plans.

"I've always believed I can play for England and I always want to," he told ITV. "That belief's always been there; it's just about proving it at club level.

"And the manager's [Tuchel] given me the chance tonight to go out there and play and try to follow what he's asked of me to the best of my ability. And hopefully he's happy with how I've played."



That 3-0 win at Wembley, however, was the last time Alexander-Arnold completed 90 minutes for club or country.

He found himself substituted early in the second half of Madrid's 1-0 LaLiga win over Villarreal earlier this month and hasn't featured since.

Sports.title: Duncan Ferguson forced to wait for managerial debut at new club as match postponed
Sports.content:
Duncan Ferguson forced to wait for managerial debut at new club as match postponed

Duncan Ferguson will have to wait for his first game as Glentoran manager.

The Belfast club appointed the Everton legend on Monday, and 'Big Dunc' was set to be in the dugout for Saturday's home Irish Premiership clash with Ballymena.

2 Glentoran are the third club of Ferguson's managerial career Credit: Getty

Why was Ferguson's first Glentoran game called off?

However, with Storm Austen battering the UK, the pitch at Glentoran's Oval ground failed an inspection.

Instead, Ferguson will take charge of the Glens for the first time when they travel to Coleraine next Friday.

The Glentoran job is the 54-year-old former Scotland international's third job in management, following spells north and south of the border with Inverness Caledonian Thistle and Forest Green Rovers.

Ferguson also worked under Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez at Everton, where he had two stints as caretaker boss.

And he's joked about 'buttering up' current Everton manager David Moyes — who he played under — for help in the January transfer window.

Speaking after his latest appointment, Ferguson said: "I am delighted to become manager of Glentoran.

"This is a big club with a tremendous history, and it is a great opportunity for me.

"I understand the responsibility that comes with the job.

"I want to win trophies here. Glentoran should be challenging for the title and every cup and shield we enter.

"I know that success here will be judged on what we win.

"The more I spoke with Ali [Pour, owner] and Paul [Millar, sporting director], the more I wanted the job.

2 Ferguson learned from one of the best in the business in Ancelotti Credit: Getty

"Their ambition matches my own, and I am looking forward to getting onto the training pitch, working with the players and seeing what we can achieve together."

Glentoran's successful history

Glentoran have claimed 23 domestic league titles, though they haven't been crowned champions since 2009.

Their most recent major honour came in the form of the 2019/20 Irish Cup.

Ferguson succeeds Declan Devine as manager and takes over with the Glens third in the table 12 games into the 2026/27 season.

He was appointed almost two years to the day since being sacked by Inverness.

As a player, Ferguson scored 68 Premier League goals — the most by a Scottish player — across two spells with Everton and one with Newcastle.

He was also part of the Everton side that won the club's most recent major trophy, the 1994/95 FA Cup.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer 'lost his head' in Chelsea's defeat by Spurs: Gary Neville hits out at Blues star after sending off and claims Morgan Rogers should also have seen red
Sports.content:
Gary Neville has claimed Cole Palmer 'lost his head' after the Chelsea star was sent off for two quick yellow cards in the defeat by Spurs on Saturday. Palmer was booked after shoving Mateus Fernandes to the ground before being given his marching orders for what Neville called a 'very naughty' challenge on Conor Gallagher just minutes later. His dismissal came after Chelsea had fallen behind when Mike Penders inadvertently punched the ball into his own net from a corner. Ten-man Chelsea's misery was compounded as Mathys Tel doubled Spurs' lead late on as Roberto De Zerbi's side became only the second Tottenham team to win at Stamford Bridge in 36 years. Speaking on Sky Sports during the game, Neville said: 'Cole Palmer has lost his head. To do that five minutes after the challenge on Fernandes is just silly. 'He sticks his studs in on him, he knows exactly what he's doing. It's not a good challenge. It is naughty, very naughty. He's experienced enough to know.' Cole Palmer was sent off for two quick yellow cards in Chelsea's defeat by Spurs on Saturday Neville said Palmer was fortunate not to see red for the push on Fernandes with the Blues forward furious at the midfielder's deliberate handball. 'Why has Palmer done that? I'm not sure why he reacts,' Neville said. 'Fernandes has handballed it and it's a clear yellow card. Palmer's reaction looks silly. He's asking for trouble.' A frustrated Morgan Rogers was then booked in the dying moments for kicking Gallagher, a challenge Neville felt should have seen Chelsea reduced to nine. 'I think that's a red. I do,' Neville said. 'He's absolutely wellied him with no intent. That's ludicrous from Rogers. They have lost it. Xabi Alonso needs to get them off.' Palmer will be available for Chelsea's next league game, at home to Manchester United on Saturday, despite the red card as he will serve his suspension when Alonso's men travel to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday.
