Sports.title: Ric Flair shares alarming photo with health update after falling and being rushed to the hospital in ambulance
Sports.content:
Ric Flair shares alarming photo with health update after falling and being rushed to the hospital in ambulance

Wrestling legend Ric Flair has shared an update after being rushed to the hospital by ambulance after a fall in Florida.

The 77-year-old was at a Tampa restaurant on Friday morning when he fell, according to TMZ. Flair is said to have stood up from the bar, leaving his phone and drink behind, before walking across the street and falling.

TMZ further reported that Flair cut his face and the area around his eye, adding that he may have suffered a concussion.

He shared a photo from his chair wrapped in a blanket on Saturday with an eye patch held over his right eye by tape across his head.

Despite smiling through the pain and trying to reassure his fans, the image was an alarming look at him looking old and frail compared to the muscular figure who became a household name during WWE's rise to prominence.

The 16-time world champion insisted he will respond to all his well-wishes individually over the coming weeks as he thanked those who treated him.

Ric Flair shared a picture and an update on his health after being rushed to hospital in Tampa

Flair, now 77, is one of the most legendary wrestler in history after his glittering career in WWE

Flair's daughter, Charlotte, also a WWE superstar, shared that he is 'going to be OK'

But he also felt compelled to address posts he called 'completely inappropriate' on his official Facebook Page he says he no longer owns, after it posted a number of videos from old moments from his wrestling career during his frightening ordeal.

Flair wrote: 'Thank you all for the messages and prayers! I will get back to you each individually as I get stronger.

'Thank you to all the Tampa General Hospital staff and doctors that put up with me until 4:30am. I appreciate you all and thank you for everything you did for me! I am focused on my healing and recovery right now. I will be okay!

'And just so you know for those who were asking and wondering, I don't own my own Facebook page anymore. I apologize for the reckless posting behavior on my Facebook when I was in the hospital. It was completely inappropriate!'

Just hours before his fall, Flair revealed he had canceled a trip to Seattle for an event as he had been advised not to fly due to blood clots.

He said: 'I want to sincerely apologize to my agent, Washington State Horror Con, and especially all my fans in Seattle for having to cancel my scheduled appearance.

'Unfortunately, I'm dealing with a blood clot in my leg, and my doctors have limited my travel to three to four hours. Seattle falls outside of that range. As disappointed as I am, I have to put my health and recovery first.

'Blood clots are extremely serious and can be life-threatening. We have seen this recently with Jalen Hurts and the complications involving blood clots in his lungs. It is a reminder that this is not something to take lightly, and I must follow medical advice.'

His daughter, Charlotte Flair, shared an update while he was in hospital saying he was 'going to be OK'.

Sports.title: Tiger Woods poses with girlfriend Vanessa Trump in rare picture after announcing she is now cancer-free
Sports.content:
Tiger Woods has posed for a rare picture with his girlfriend, Vanessa Trump, celebrating the news she is now cancer-free.

The legendary golfer and President Trump's former daughter-in-law went public with their romance in March 2025, sharing two loved up pictures.

She supported him as he appeared in court in March and accepted a plea deal in his DUI case after a car crash in Florida, while she also attended a TGL golf event with him last year.

But pictures of the pair together have been few and far between, with the couple declining to share any images since from their personal life.

However, they made an exception to pose celebrating Vanessa getting the all-clear from breast cancer.

In her latest YouTube vlog, Vanessa's daughter, Kai, who went to the same high school as Tiger's son Charlie, shared a picture of the family after her big news.

Kai Trump shared a photo of Tiger Woods with Vanessa celebrating her all-clear from cancer

Vanessa Trump has revealed that she is cancer free in a video alongside daughter Kai

Tiger and Vanessa Trump shared this photo in March 2025 as they confirmed their romance

Tiger and Vanessa stood with her two eldest children, Kai and Donald Trump III, with the bell she rang to mark getting the all clear beneath a 'congratulations' banner.

The 48-year-old Vanessa appeared alongside Kai in a lengthy video with Dr Nicole Saphier, for Breast Cancer Awareness month discussing her journey.

In a short teaser video shared to Instagram on Friday, Kai began: 'My mom was diagnosed with breast cancer in April.

'So we thought we would share her story and how she was diagnosed and how she overcame it.'

Vanessa appeared back on screen and shared: '[Tests] came back clear so I am finally cancer free,' as the mother-daughter duo exchanged a hug.

The mother-of-five had publicly announced in May that she was diagnosed with breast cancer.

Vanessa, the ex-wife of President Trump's eldest son, Don Jr, said at the time that she had undergone a 'procedure.'

'I want to share a personal health update. I've recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. While this isn't news anyone expects, I'm working closely with my medical team on a treatment plan,' she said.

Woods and Vanessa also shared a loved-up picture lying in a hammock in their first post

Vanessa Trump supported Woods in court in March as he took a plea deal in his DUI case

Vanessa also attended a TGL match in March supporting Woods in his new golf venture

'I am staying focused and hopeful while surrounded by the love and support of my family, my kids and those closest to me.

'Thank you for your kindness and support, it truly means more than I can express.'

In June, Vanessa issued a second statement that she was recovering from surgery and preparing to begin the next stage of treatment.

Kai has been candid about her mom's health journey after previously opening up about how the diagnosis gave them an opportunity to spend more time together over the summer.

Speaking to Fox News from the University of Miami back in August, she explained: 'I was very lucky to spend a lot of time with her over the summer, because of cancer and going to treatments with her.

'It was a blessing in disguise, because I was able to spend extra time with her that I would normally probably spend on the golf course.

'It was nice to spend those extra hours with her throughout the day before going to college.'

Sports.title: They're taking the Mik! Arsenal boss reveals he is collecting dossier of other managers breaching technical area in bizarre rant - despite criticism that HE is the worst offender
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta bizarrely claimed he has collated footage of other managers breaching their technical area as a body of evidence after receiving his second yellow card of the season.

Arteta was booked in the second half by referee Tony Harrington for venturing outside his area. Later, assistant manager Gabriel Heinze was yellow carded for a similar infringement.

Yet, the Spaniard said he has evidence of other coaches doing the same ‘36 times in 10 minutes’ without getting a yellow.

Arteta will miss a game on the touchline if he receives a third yellow card this season.

‘I do have to be careful. And we need to have good sensors there,’ he said.

‘There are managers that have the record in the league - 36 times in 10 minutes leaving the touchline, no yellows.

‘So I'm clipping all of that. I have a massive storage of images. So if somebody is going to say, “I'm not in the record yet, somebody else has the record”, then it's 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the (other) manager.

‘I don't know where we're going to be.’

Arteta was booked in the second half by referee Tony Harrington for venturing outside his area

The Spaniard said he has evidence of other coaches doing the same ‘36 times in 10 minutes’ without getting a yellow

He also reiterated the need for his team to focus on their own performances amid the cloud over when sanctions for Manchester City’s breaches of the league’s financial rules could be enacted.

He added: ‘We have to just focus on what we can do and we are very pleased with 90 per cent of the results and performances that we have apart from the Brighton game.’

Meanwhile, David Moyes spoke of his disappointment over an Everton display which gave them a second league defeat of the season.

‘Just OK, done some good bits but not enough,’ said Moyes.

‘To give the goal away early was a problem for us. After them having a game midweek, it gave them something to hang onto and play with.

‘We did a lot of good things but, at that moment, we didn't get it right.’

On the lessons from their defeats to Chelsea and Arsenal, he added: ‘We're competitive against them both. We've not been rolled over in either game.

‘We're lacking a little bit, which we know but I do think that in the main, we've tried to give both games a good effort and I think we did. Today we didn't do as well as we'd like but we still gave it a good effort.’

Sports.title: Arsenal rediscover magic touch at corners as Ezri Konsa and Gabriel punish wasteful Everton and move Gunners level at top with Man City
Sports.content:
A well-worn Arsenal blueprint from previous seasons had finally resurfaced. It was only a matter time before Mikel Arteta’s team of 6ft-plus giants would, inevitably, turn to set-pieces; the rich supply method of goals which previously often decided or prised open matches.

Having not scored from a corner so far this season, the ploy was back, and emphatically so. Odegaard’s floated corner on seven minutes — Arsenal’s third in quick succession — reached Gabriel in the mix, who headed goalward.

The ball gently brushed Jordan Pickford’s fingertips onto the crossbar, falling to Ezri Konsa near the back post amid a sea of Everton bodies. He prodded home to register the Gunners first set-piece goal of the season.

By this stage last season, they were already on six and finished the campaign on a record-breaking 19. Rivals branded them ‘Set Piece FC’ but it’s not been heard around these parts since May.

To their credit, the Gunners were dominant. Whether a rain-sodden Arteta was trying to mount a defence against the recent ‘Unwatchables’ accusations after last weekend’s drab victory against Nottingham Forest, his team certainly made a mockery of that jibe.

The north London club typically found themselves camped outside the opposition’s box, trying to force their way through a low block and peppered their visitors goal with 18 shots.

Gabriel sealed victory for Arsenal with a second-half header

Gabriel rose highest to connect with a Ben White cross to score his first of the season

The Toffees hadn’t surrendered, keen to mount counter-attacks through the pacey Thierno Barry but were overwhelmed by a relentless red-and-white wave. Gabriel, making his 200th appearance, typified Arsenal’s resilience.

Having gone down in agony on 56 minutes after overstretching himself on a clearance, the medical team helped usher the Brazilian off the field. Cristhian Mosquera began to ready himself on the bench.

Gabriel saw this and did some stretches on the touchline, making it known he would not be subbed off. Ten minutes after re-entering the pitch, he latched onto Ben White’s cross to double Arsenal’s lead with a powerful header.

There’s a never-say-die spirit in this team, which makes them so hard to beat. Arteta had rung the changes, bringing in Viktor Gyokeres and Mikel Merino for their first Premier League starts of the season.

The manager is also taking rotation seriously, too. In the previous campaign, certain positions were pretty much fixed, no matter the circumstances. Martin Zubimendi started 34 of the 38 league matches but was, tellingly, on the bench again here. This time around, Arteta has shown a willingness to give players a break where possible. It’s a sensible and needed evolution for the Spaniard; if Bukayo Saka’s recent thigh injury wasn’t a warning sign, then not much else would be.

Arsenal got off to a rampant start, taking no mercy against an Everton side who had only lost once in the league this season. Noni Madueke, a player whose end product had been under scrutiny, impressed with his dribbling skill and intent. He marched forward, only looking in one direction — forward.

He’s a handful to deal with when full of confidence and, after starting the 2-2 Champions League draw with Bayern Munich midweek, Madueke was in full flow.

Ezri Konsa had opened the scoring for the Gunners from a corner

The winger sat an Everton player down on the turf with a swift pivot, his neat cross to Gyokeres desperately cleared. On another occasion, he swivelled just outside the area, before shooting into the side netting.

Odegaard played the conductor role, looking for sharp passes through the opposition’s backline. Five minutes before the break, five Everton shirts circled him, the Norwegian using his dancing feet to get around and go close with his strike.

Eberechi Eze attracted applause for a neat touch from a sky-high ball, which was to be superseded by Max Dowman’s introduction on 80 minutes. The memories of his match-saving display last March against the Toffees, featuring a game-changing cross and a goal, has not been forgotten.

By the time Gabriel’s goal went in, the game was already meandering to a close. Merlin Rohl’s cross momentarily gave David Raya a scare, the ball just curling high and wide from the goalframe. That mattered not. Set-pieces are back on the Arsenal table. Future opponents ought to be wary.

Sports.title: Oscar Bobb's moment of magic breathes life into Alvaro Arbeloa's return from the dead... but Coventry lack cutting edge required for big time, writes JAMES SHARPE
Sports.content:
Oscar Bobb's moment of magic breathes life into Alvaro Arbeloa's return from the dead... but Coventry lack cutting edge required for big time, writes JAMES SHARPE

For a man recently described as a ‘dead man strutting’, Alvaro Arbeloa now has an extra spring in his step. Few fortunes in life lurch quite so violently as a football manager’s but, even for the Fulham boss, this resuscitation is quite something.

Fulham started the day second from bottom in the Premier League table, even after their first victory of the season against Hull, but now have back-to-back wins thanks to Oscar Bobb’s late winner, sit 12th in the table ahead of Tottenham’s game tonight, and just three points off the top six.

That strutting dead man, as one dressing room source called Arbeloa to Daily Mail Sport recently, is very much alive.

And the Oscar goes to…

For a game so sorely lacking in quality, you always got the sense that it would only need one sliver of it to decide this wet, cold, turgid contest in the West Midlands. For all the mountains of possession Fulham had, for all the little openings they created, they rarely looked like scoring after Josh King hit the woodwork early on and Shea Charles forced a save in the 13th minute.

There was one passage of play when Fulham kept the ball for what seemed like an eternity, passed it around, only for Timothy Castagne to lump it out of play.

Oscar Bobb created the most chances all game and, for his late winner, did it all himself

Bobb dribbled into the box, pulled out all the tricks and stepovers before waltzing past Jack Rudoni and curling it into the far corner

But if there was anyone ever likely to provide it, it was going to be Bobb. The former Manchester City winger created the most chances all game and, for his late winner, did it all himself. He dribbled into the box, pulled out all the tricks and stepovers before waltzing past Jack Rudoni and curling it into the far corner for his first league goal for Fulham since joining in January.

'When you are losing it's difficult to say you are doing so many things well but always we have believed we are on the right track,’ said Arbeloa.

'Sometimes you need to win games because of the quality of your players, it was a good game as a team but the quality of Oscar in one moment decides the game and it's important for us because we have players who can make the difference.'

Cov missing cutting edge

Boos rang out from the home supporters as the final whistle blew at the CBS Arena. They knew how big this game was, the first of two back-to-back home games against Fulham and Sunderland, the only two sides below them before a ball was kicked.

Once again, though, they discovered the gap between the Championship and the Premier League. They simply cannot dominate matches as they did on their way to promotion last season.

And when they did have their moments, they just couldn’t make it count. Of their 13 shots, only two were on target.

‘We didn’t have the zip at the top end of the pitch like we would want,’ said Coventry boss Frank Lampard.

‘If you want to find a bit more, it’s not always there for you.’

The lack of cutting edge in the final third made it even more strange to see Lampard leave striker Ellis Simms, who scored in the win against Newcastle, out of the squad.

Coventry simply cannot dominate matches as they did on their way to promotion last season, and when they did have their moments, they just couldn’t make it count

Grimes struggles again

Of all the players who perhaps looked most likely to bridge that gap to the top flight for Coventry, it was captain Matt Grimes. The skipper was so frequently the talisman and tempo-setter in the Championship but is struggling to stop games passing him by.

Bobb breezed past him early on to set up Shea Charles for a shot. He overhit a routine pass to Jay Dasilva that went straight out of play. Coventry don’t have enough of the ball to allow him to dictate play and, when they do get hold of it, he often finds himself with it in between the centre-backs, and without the ball struggles to have the physicality to wrench the game back into his side’s favour.

Frank sweating on Thomas

One man who has proven that he can make that step up is central defender Bobby Thomas. The man mountain boasts some of the best defensive stats in the Premier League and has been a rock for Lampard’s men so far this season. He even had a chance in the first half when he put that massive head on to a Jack Rudoni cross only to head wide.

Thomas, though, picked up a problem early in the first half, tried to continue, but soon sat down on the pitch and limped off before the hour was up. Lampard said he was waiting to find out how bad it was. His replacement Stephen Mfuni went close with a header from a corner but, with a massive home match against Sunderland coming up, his absence will be a hammer blow for Lampard.

Thomas picked up a problem early in the first half, tried to continue, but soon sat down on the pitch and limped off before the hour was up

Arbeloa needs more from his man

If Fulham’s form is to continue, they need more from striker Gonzalo Garcia, who must have wondered what on earth his career has come to as he trudged around the sodden grass, wet to the bone. He used to play for Real Madrid, for heaven’s sake.

Not that you’d know it from his recent performances. He didn’t muster a single shot on target, had the fewest touches of any of Fulham’s starters, including his goalkeeper before being dragged off with 15 minutes to go with the game still level.

Sports.title: Max Verstappen fumes at 'unacceptable' Austin track for US Grand Prix: Red Bull star warns track is 'out of control' and insists drivers' concerns have been IGNORED
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen fumes at 'unacceptable' Austin track for US Grand Prix: Red Bull star warns track is 'out of control' and insists drivers' concerns have been IGNORED

Max Verstappen has said that the ‘unacceptable’ Austin track, home of this weekend’s US Grand Prix, is damaging his spine because it is too bumpy.

The four-time world champion revealed that he and his fellow drivers have complained to the governing FIA about the condition of the Circuit of the Americas layout and asked for solutions but reported that their requests had not been resolved.

He described the circuit, which is 15 miles southeast of Downtown, as ‘out of control’.

‘I love this track, I love this place,’ said the Dutchman. ‘It’s one of the best, one of the best venues, one of the best cities to be at.

‘But the bumps are unacceptable. Over time they’ve found a bit of a solution here and there, but it’s just putting a plaster on the bigger problem.

‘You need to open up the track fully (to sort it out). That costs a lot of money and time but that’s the only way to get rid of it because these bumps are not natural.’

Max Verstappen has complained about the Austin track ahead of the US Grand Prix

The circuit, which hosted its first race 14 years ago, is built on marshland, and was designed by German Hermann Tilke, then the go-to man for such projects.

Verstappen, 29, added: ‘You can say soil is the problem, but you need to make sure you reinforce it more.’

Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli, just 20, can win the title here in the US if he extends his lead from 102 points to 125 with what would then be five rounds remaining.

Sports.title: Man City's perfect record is over and now we'll see what Enzo Maresca's side are really made of, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE - it's easy to ignore the storm when you're winning, but dark clouds loom after Aston Villa defeat
Sports.content:
Man City's perfect record is over and now we'll see what Enzo Maresca's side are really made of, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE - it's easy to ignore the storm when you're winning, but dark clouds loom after Aston Villa defeat

Come on then, Enzo. Let’s see what you’ve got now.

Until lunchtime on Saturday, Manchester City had shown no signs of being affected by the chaos engulfing the club as Enzo Maresca’s men reeled off seven straight Premier League wins. We will know soon enough whether Aston Villa’s fourth straight home victory over City has broken the spell.

It easy enough to block out the noise when you win every league game. Easy to forget your club’s ongoing battle with the Premier League after they were found guilty of breaking financial rules between 2009 and 2018 – a verdict City have appealed.

These players and coaches would not be human, though, if they had been able to avoid worrying about the future. What if our appeal fails? Will we be relegated? If so, how far? What happens to our contracts? Our careers? City’s next fixture, at home to the impressive Brighton, may tell us a great deal about what is to come.

Troubling times for City, and no less unsettling for the Premier League. Because if City escape on a technicality, what then? The damage to the competition’s image would be colossal. Please, just let the verdict be swift.

Nicolas Jackson scored twice to power Aston Villa to victory and inflict Manchester City's first Premier League defeat of the season

City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma was at fault for Jackson's winner after letting the ball slip up his body

City did not play badly here. They hit the frame of the goal twice through Iliman Ndiaye and Josko Gvardiol and were denied by some outstanding work by Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki, who looks one of the buys of the season. So too does Nicolas Jackson, who scored in each half, either side of Erling Haaland’s equaliser. This must have tasted especially sweet for Jackson, who was shoved towards the exit by Maresca at Chelsea a little more than a year ago. Against the world’s best No9, Jackson won the battle of the centre-forward hands down.

Emery: Jackson was shooting like a rugby kicker! Unai Emery claimed that Nicolas Jackson’s shooting had resembled a rugby kicker earlier in the season before roaring into form as Aston Villa ended Manchester City’s perfect start. Jackson’s brace downed the Premier League leaders and the striker now has six goals in his last six games in all competitions following a £65million move from Chelsea in the summer. The 25-year-old has impressed Emery with his grasp of the tactical instructions at Villa and is now repaying the Spaniard’s faith in front of goal. ‘How he was working, how he was defending - wow,’ Emery said. ‘And then he has the power to attack the spaces and the duels. ‘His challenge has been when he can have chances to score [to] always [find] the corner because he was shooting so much in the beginning of the season like up in rugby. ‘He was shooting a lot of balls over the crossbar. He is progressing as well. We need him more running in behind because we need the runners on the field, and one of the runners normally is the striker, and he has quality and power. He’s coachable.’ Gianluigi Donnarumma should have done better with Jackson’s second and Enzo Maresca insisted that City should have left with something from the game. ‘I think we deserved more,’ Maresca said. ‘We haven't been clinical enough in the box. Sometimes when you concede the first goal was mistake, the second goal came from a transition. ‘We spent most of the game in their side, in their box. Sometimes you have to be more clinical but also more precise with the last pass, more accurate. We're going to learn from that.’ JACK GAUGHAN

‘We had many chances,’ said Maresca. ‘We played most of the game in their box but you have to be clinical and avoid mistakes like the two goals we conceded.’

All fair enough, though Maresca must have noticed a softness to City that simply was not there in their greatest days. Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku tormented Villa full-backs Matty Cash and Ian Maatsen throughout and on another occasion, their creativity would have produced more. When it comes to the other end of the pitch, the less said, the better.

Marc Guehi was dragged off at half-time after he was at fault for Jackson’s opener and then picked up a booking for a foul on the Villa forward. Ruben Dias seemed more interested in scrapping with John McGinn than stopping him playing. Enzo Fernandez looked slow and sluggish, a shadow of himself.

Maresca: I'm not worried about Guehi Enzo Maresca insists that he is unfazed by the form of Marc Guehi after another mistake led to Aston Villa's early opener. Guehi – taken off at the break - had also made two errors in victory over Ipswich Town last week. ‘I'm not worried about Marc at all,’ he added. ‘I know he is playing every minute since the season started with us and the national team. ‘It's not easy but the change was also because he was on a yellow card and the way we want to be aggressive sometimes to have one yellow card can be dangerous. But I'm not worried at all.’ JACK GAUGHAN

None of this should detract from Villa or their outstanding coach. Unai Emery has somehow managed to travel under the radar for much of his second spell in English football and has been overlooked by Manchester United twice since he arrived at Villa four years ago.

‘He’s just a tactical genius,’ said Cash. ‘Especially against City at our place, he’s always got a plan for something and he’s always coming up with new ideas.’

The Norwegian rose brilliantly in the box to head home past Zion Suzuki

Erling Haaland scored City's equaliser early in the second-half

MATCH FACTS Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 9; Cash 6, Lindelof 8, Torres 8, Maatsen 6; Kamara 6, Gomes 7 (Goretzka 82min); Alysson 7 (Mbaye 59, 7), McGinn 8 (Barkley 67, 6), Manzambi 6 (Buendia 67, 6); Jackson 8 (Madjo 82) Scorers: Jackson 6, 60 Booked: Cash, Manzambi, Madjo, Buendia Manager: Unai Emery 8 Manchester City (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 5; Khusanov 6, Dias 5, Guehi 4 (Lewis 46, 6), Gvardiol 6; Anderson 7, Fernandez 5; Ndiaye 7 (McAidoo 69, 6), Cherki 6 (Foden 46, 6), Doku 8; Haaland 7. Scorers: Haaland 53 Booked: Guehi, Cherki, Anderson, McAidoo Manager: Enzo Maresca 6 Referee: Peter Bankes 6 Attendance: 36,743

Consider what Emery has had to handle since lifting the Europa League last May. Six of the starting XI from the Final against Freiburg have departed, leaving a squad needing a total rebuild. Daily Mail Sport has been critical before of Villa’s haphazard recruitment but this time they have nailed it.

Suzuki and Jackson have been two of the best in their positions this season. Though he did not have his best day against City, Johan Manzambi looks a £100million footballer in the making. Ibrahim Mbaye came on as a second-half substitute and promptly created the winner for his Senegal team-mate Jackson. At 25, Jackson is the oldest of the quartet. Exciting times.

‘This year started so poorly,’ admitted Emery. ‘We needed time to understand how we needed to improve. Today this was a very good test and the players have shown they can recover the level we achieved in recent years.’

City were caught cold by the speed of Villa’s start. The home side were awarded a corner when City delayed a goal-kick too long and in the sixth minute they seized the lead.

Guehi’s poor control allowed McGinn to find Jackson, who was allowed to cut in unchallenged from the left and fire into the roof of the net.

Now the Holte End was in full voice, telling City exactly what they thought of them but Maresca’s team did not wilt. They took control quickly and Ndiaye and Doku were a constant threat on the flanks. Ndiaye forced a fine save from Zion Suzuki and the Villa goalkeeper produced an even better one from Rayan Cherki. Ndiaye would later hit the post and Doku continued to torment Matty Cash.

Jackson capped off a brilliant start to the game for the hosts by putting them ahead

Jackson has now scored seven goals this season since moving from Chelsea in the summer

Haaland touched the ball only eight times in the first half but when it counted, he made his mark. Ndiaye glided past Manzambi and Haaland climbed to head home at the far post soon after the break.

Back came Villa. Less than a minute after coming on as substitute, Mbaye raced on to Jackson’s pass and picked out his team-mate 20 yards from goal. Jackson’s aim was true and Donnarumma allowed the shot to slip through his grasp and into the net. Moments earlier, Suzuki had done brilliantly again to tip Gvardiol’s effort on to the bar.

‘I’m very happy with the manager and my team-mates,’ said Jackson. ‘It’s been easier for me because of the coach and the players. Hopefully I can score many goals for them and it’s just the beginning. Thankfully we got our first win at home in the league.’

Sports.title: Terrifying moment Cheltenham staff member crawls across track as horses thunder towards him
Sports.content:
Terrifying moment Cheltenham staff member crawls across track as horses thunder towards him

The unusual incident was picked up on the TV footage in the opening race of seven at Cheltenham on Saturday, the William Hill Epic Boosts Novices' Limited Handicap Chase over 2m 4f

View Image The man could be seen on his hands and knees in the Racing TV footage (Image: Racing TV)

Eagle-eyed TV viewers spotted a man crawling across the course at Cheltenham as horses thundered towards him.

‌



‌



The individual was seen in the left-hand corner of the Racing TV footage while the runners were galloping towards the final fence in the William Hill Epic Boosts Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (1.10pm).

‌



Spectacularsunrise held a two-length lead at the time and came down, as another fancied runner Lisbane Park fell independently.

‌



Irish raider Rockonliam was left in the lead but began to idle and was reeled in by Sean Bowen's mount O'Moore Park (25-1), a transfer from Willie Mullins' yard to Martin Keighley's.

However, on a wet and windy afternoon at Prestbury Park, some fans of the sport were left wondering why the man was on the ground in the closing stages of the 2m 4f contest which started the card.

Dan Skelton reveals clue which led him to bargain Cheltenham winner Here Comes Georgie READ MORE :

"Why we got some fella at Cheltenham on his hands and knees scrambling to avoid horse 2 out. What on earth is going on!" one person wrote on social media site X.

‌



And another asked: "Was there somebody crawling along the floor as the horses turned in at Cheltenham?"

A stewards enquiry was held and it was found that they were a member of staff who had slipped while heading across the course.

‌



The report published on the British Horseracing Authority website read: "An enquiry was held to consider the circumstances surrounding why a member of the veterinary team appeared to be attempting to get up off the floor between the final two fences as the field passed.

"The clerk of the course was interviewed and reported that the staff member had lost their footing while crossing the track, as was their routine. He continued that as it was on the outside of the racing line and they did not have time to move, the individual made the decision to remain on the floor until the field had passed.

‌



"After hearing the evidence, a report was forwarded to the Head Office of the British Horseracing Authority for further consideration."

Cheltenham's two-day meeting marked the return of jumps racing there for seven months, after the final fixtures of the 2025-6 season were cancelled to allow a significant drainage project to be carried out.

Article continues below

It was undertaken on the back of the discovery of a hole in the racing surface on Festival Trials Day in late January.

Sports.title: Why Joao Pedro is not in Chelsea squad vs Tottenham as youngster given huge debut
Sports.content:
Why Joao Pedro is not in Chelsea squad vs Tottenham as youngster given huge debut

Chelsea face Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday evening, but Xabi Alonso has confirmed that Joao Pedro will play no part in the Premier League encounter

View 2 Images Joao Pedro misses out on Chelsea's clash with Tottenham Hotspur (Image: Darren Walsh, Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Joao Pedro has been ruled out of Chelsea's squad for Saturday evening's clash with Tottenham Hotspur, having picking up an injury that is currently being assessed. The 25-year-old striker, who has bagged five goals this season, has been deemed not fit enough to feature against Spurs.

‌



‌



Xabi Alonso has raised eyebrows by handing Geovany Quenda a full Premier League debut in his place. The Portuguese winger has been limited to just 28 minutes in the English top flight since arriving from Sporting CP in a £40million move this summer.

‌



Speaking about Pedro's absence ahead of kick-off, Alonso explained: "At the moment has some liquid, so we have to do some tests to know how big the injury is. It's disappointing, but we need to carry on."

‌



Cole Palmer seals Chelsea future as club confirm huge update READ MORE :

Speaking about Quenda's involvement, meanwhile, Alonso added: "He has many qualities. He attacks well the space, he's good with the ball, his goal threat, he's been training well.

"All the players, they will have their opportunities. Sometimes they need to be a bit more patient. Geo has been patient, and today is a big day to make his debut as a starter."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



He continued: "We want to have mobility, we want to be fluid - that we are not very static. And for sure, with Geo, we have those qualities."

Speaking on how the absence of Pedro and the presence of Quenda will change the game, Daniel Sturridge told Sky Sports: "I think, for me, he's going to be more of a focal point. The manager's talked about it being fluid, I think it's more of a false nine.

‌



FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"So again, everyone will be rotating, maybe Neto pops up centrally, Quenda may pop up centrally for a moment. There'll be a lot of communication between [Morgan] Rogers and [Cole] Palmer, two really good friends.

‌



"Those guys have amazing chemistry together. And look, they're all goalscorers. Maybe it's a day now for Cole Palmer to add goals to his tally, he's scored one so far this season. I know Morgan Rogers has the four, but these are goal-scoring, thinking players.

"They want to score goals, they want to get their shots off, they're up there in the shot-taking stats. So when we look at them, they're not short of qualities going forward.

‌



"Young boy Estevao, as well, on the bench who can come on. Fortunate for Quenda tonight, big night for him off that left-hand side."

View 2 Images Geovany Quenda starts for Chelsea (Image: Mike Egerton/the Press Association)

‌



In the only other change from the side that saw victory against Everton last weekend, Mike Penders has stepped in for the injured Emi Martinez. Martinez came through successful surgery on a fractured jaw last weekend following a collision at the Hill Dickinson Stadium and faces a period on the sidelines.

Josh Acheampong retains his spot in defence, alongside Maxence Lacroix and Levi Colwill. Last weekend's match-winner Pedro Neto is set to operate on the right, with Jorrel Hato lining up on the opposite flank.

‌



Jordan Henderson and Moises Caicedo complete the Chelsea midfield. Palmer is expected to start to the right of Rogers, who appears set to fill in as a makeshift No. 9 at Stamford Bridge.

Meanwhile, Roberto De Zerbi has made two changes to the Tottenham side that defeated Coventry City on Monday night. Mathys Tel and Mateus Fernandes have been rolled out in place of Tosin Adarabioyo and Dominic Solanke.

Sports.title: Son of F1 legend, aged 9, in terrifying crash as two vehicles drive over him
Sports.content:
Son of F1 legend, aged 9, in terrifying crash as two vehicles drive over him

The son of a Formula 1 icon was involved in a frightening crash on Friday which involved two karts driving over him after a collision

View 2 Images Toto Wolff's son escaped without injury after being involved in a nasty karting crash (Image: X/thomasmaheronf1)

Toto Wolff's nine-year-old son, Jack, was involved in a terrifying multi-kart crash on Friday. The incident occurred just one month after the Mercedes CEO's son won his first championship: the IAME Series Italy title in the X30 Under-10 category.

‌



‌



Jack competes mainly across Europe and has just completed his debut season. His first race win came in July. His father, Toto, has been at the helm of Formula 1's Mercedes since 2013, currently serving as team principal and holding a 33.3 per cent stake in the outfit.

‌



The Silver Arrows claimed a record eight successive Constructors' Championships between 2014 and 2021 under his leadership. Jack's mother, Susie, is also a former racing driver who now serves as managing director of F1 Academy.

‌



But both parents would have been left shaken on Friday, as they watched their son compete. The nine-year-old was taking part in Qualifying Heat 3 of the X30 Mini category at the Leopard Circuit in Viterbo, Italy. During the closing lap of the heat, Jack, driving No. 25, was locked in a battle for the lead with Nahyl Elgahoudi.

Michael Schumacher pal makes stance clear on public appearance amid health battle READ MORE :

As the two made contact, their wheels collided and Elgahoudi's kart launched violently up and over the front of Jack's machine, balancing precariously on two wheels before narrowly avoiding a full rollover. Jack was then sent into a spin.

View 2 Images Wolff's son was involved in a dramatic crash (Image: X/thomasmaheronf1)

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

With no escape route, trailing driver Dimitar Uzunov smashed into the almost stationary kart, becoming airborne and flying directly over the cockpit while striking Jack's shoulder.

‌



Reports indicate Jack was treated following the incident but emerged unscathed. He exited the kart unaided and was keen to return to the paddock.

The commentator observed during the crash: "Look at that straight over the top there went... went Uzunov. How Elgahoudi did not flip there, I do not know... and Wolff as well, taking a big hit to the shoulder."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Speaking at a karting event this summer, Toto discussed his son's ambition: "This is where it all starts. Formula 1 is basically this on steroids. Same kind of racing and watching the kids is just a super experience.

‌



"It's important to find the right balance because obviously as a parent you're emotionally involved and it's completely normal. But he's nine years old.

"There are so many small kids and you need to strike the balance right and we try. Sometimes we get it wrong. You have difficult moments and he had some difficult moments.

Article continues below

"But in the end it comes all together, and every little failure is a learning for the future. Just give them time. They're so small, let them enjoy the karting and that's the most important."

Sports.title: Man City fall short in Premier League record attempt as Aston Villa's revival continues
Sports.content:
Man City fall short in Premier League record attempt as Aston Villa's revival continues

ASTON VILLA 2-1 MAN CITY: Two goals from Nicolas Jackson either side of an Erling Haaland header gave Unai Emery's team all three points and put them up to sixth in the Premier League table

View 2 Images Manchester City failed to win a Premier League game for the first time this season (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

A brace from in-form Nicolas Jackson ended Manchester City's 100 per cent start to the Premier League season, as Aston Villa continued their revival. Former Chelsea star Jackson scored his sixth and seventh goals in Villa colours to fire the hosts to victory in Saturday's early kick-off.

‌



‌



City headed to Villa Park having won every league fixture since Enzo Maresca took charge. But their quest to become the first side to beat Chelsea's long-standing record of nine wins to start a Premier League season will have to wait another year.

‌



Jackson broke the deadlock with just six minutes on the clock, sending Elliot Anderson for a dummy before finishing high at Gianluigi Donnarumma's near post. Maresca made two changes at half-time, bringing on Rico Lewis and Champions League hat-trick hero Phil Foden.

‌



And it didn't take long for City to draw level after the restart. Who else but Erling Haaland to head home Iliman Ndiaye's cross?

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Parity only lasted eight minutes, though, as Jackson doubled up on the hour mark. The Villa striker was expertly picked out by Ibrahim Mbaye and his low shot went through Donnarumma.

City pushed for an equaliser but Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki was equal to them until the end. Villa Park continues to be an unhappy hunting ground for City, having last won there in 2021.

‌



After suffering their first league defeat since Villa came to the Etihad and beat City in May, Ruben Dias told TNT Sports: "Frustrating, felt like we fought a lot. First 10-15 minutes of the first half we took our time to get into the game.

"They changed the way they set up so we took time to adapt. But we fought, we had chances and they ended up scoring two goals in two transitions - very efficient. Room to improve, we need to do better.

‌



Will Manchester City win the Premier League? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Nicolas Jackson has scored seven goals in 11 games for Aston Villa (Image: ille Williams/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images)

‌



"It is what it is. Whatever happens we need to react to it. The team had a very good reaction. The second one was tough because it was very close to our equaliser. We kept going and tried to create chances. Not our day but we keep moving forward."

In contrast, man-of-the-match Jackson was delighted with the result, saying: "It was incredible, we got the win which is the most important thing. Man City are a strong team, the league leaders. Hopefully now we forget about this one and focus on the next one."
