Sports.title: Christian Mbilli May Not Need His Best Against Canelo
Sports.content:
Christian Mbilli could walk away with a victory over Canelo Alvarez without needing the fight of his life next Saturday, October 31, in Saudi Arabia. His relentless pace and trademark volume might easily suffice against a 36-year-old fighter whose offensive engine visibly sputters when pressed to maintain high-gear work.

Canelo clearly talks like the WBC super middleweight champion needs a miracle.

“He’s going to come 100% because he’s going to need it,” Canelo insisted to DAZN Boxing.

That mindset clings to the idea that defeating him demands career-best perfection. His one-sided loss to Terence Crawford last September completely shattered that myth. Crawford used nothing more than crisp footwork, sharp feints, and an active jab to leave Canelo completely flat-footed, snatching the undisputed 168-pound crown with tactical clarity.

Crawford never looked pushed to the brink. He dictated terms using distance, precision combinations, and smart angles, while Canelo simply followed him around the ring unable to pull the trigger with any consistency.

Mbilli presents a very different stylistic problem. He will naturally offer Canelo cleaner counterpunching lanes, yet he will relentlessly drag the Mexican star into deep water by forcing an uncomfortable pace.

Whenever Canelo turtles behind his high guard, Mbilli will let his hands go. Even if those punches crash into elbows and gloves, judges reward activity, and Canelo will have to respond. Landing an occasional explosive counter cannot bail out long stretches of ring hibernation.

Naturally, Canelo still carries dynamite timing and wicked rib-cracking hooks. Careless, head-down rushes could give the decorated veteran the exact highlight-reel openings he craves. Blind aggression rarely secures a victory against elite counterpunchers.

Nevertheless, Mbilli has no obligation to pitch a flawless twelve-round masterpiece. He simply needs to keep the pressure going, deny Canelo the rest breaks he desperately seeks, and make the aging star sweat for every single exchange.

Canelo might be living on past reputation if he thinks Mbilli must deliver a superhuman performance to win. The real question is whether Canelo can muster enough gas in the tank to survive Mbilli on a routine, rock-solid night.

Sports.title: Andy Ruiz vs Dave Allen Targeted For Spring
Sports.content:
Andy Ruiz Jr. and Dave Allen could meet in Sheffield in March or April 2027, with Allen revealing that Matchroom’s Frank Smith has told him the company is targeting that window for the heavyweight fight.

The Fight Wire reports Allen also indicated that he would likely retire afterward. The fight has not been officially announced, and the proposed dates remain a target.

Ruiz (35-3-1, 22 KOs) would enter the bout coming off a defeat against Damian Knyba in September. His last victory came against Luis Ortiz in September 2022, with a draw against Jarrell Miller and another lengthy absence between that win and the Knyba loss.

That represents a dismal drop for a man who battered Anthony Joshua to win the unified heavyweight crown in 2019. Ruiz held all the gold, dominated global sports headlines, and blew the chance to become a generational heavyweight star. He surrendered the titles in the rematch and spent the next seven years fighting just four times.

Allen keeps fighting to stay relevant and earn a living, but nobody expected him to rule the division. He has spent much of his career taking punishment from better heavyweights. Ruiz reached the top, won three world titles, and then wasted the opportunity.

A win over Allen gets Ruiz back in the win column, but beating a domestic trialhorse proves nothing about his ability to mix with elite heavyweights. An upset loss drops him off the boxing map entirely.

Take Allen’s retirement talk with a grain of salt. Sharing the ring with Ruiz hands him a big-name scalp to target along with a solid payday. Even in defeat, a decent showing will keep promoters dialing his number.

Expect Allen to stick around if matchmakers keep waving checks in his face. Giving a former unified champion a real scrap will open doors for future paydays, not push him into retirement.

Right now, the story is Matchroom penciling in that spring date in Sheffield. Calling it a farewell bout looks like wishful thinking, especially since another decent payday will easily tempt him back into the ring.

Sports.title: WBO Set To Strip Denzel Bentley Of Title
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley is set to lose his WBO middleweight title after allowing the deadline to commit to mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernández to pass, leaving his November 7 fight against Shane Mosley Jr. as his next bout.

WBO president Gustavo Olivieri told EverythingBoxing’s Darshan Desai that the organization received no formal communication from Bentley’s team confirming he would go ahead with the Hernández defense within the allotted 24 hours. According to Desai, the WBO will now strip him.

Bentley has already signed to face Mosley Jr. in his Zuffa Boxing debut. That looks like a more winnable fight than defending against Hernández, although Bentley would enter it without the championship he had hoped to keep.

Hernández (11-0, 9 KOs) would be a dangerous fight for Bentley, with the power to knock him out. A loss like that would be a rough way to begin his time with Zuffa.

Bentley would have a chance against Hernández, but this would be a dangerous defense against a challenger who has been finishing most of his opponents. From a career standpoint, accepting the loss of his belt and going ahead with Mosley Jr. is understandable. He keeps his scheduled fight and avoids the immediate possibility of a punishing defeat.

The WBO cannot justify letting him keep the belt while pursuing a side attraction. Hernandez did the work to earn his mandatory ranking, and he shouldn’t be put on hold just because Bentley decided to take a different path.

Vito Mielnicki Jr. could step into the opposite corner against Hernandez for the vacant belt. Mielnicki holds the number two spot in the WBO ratings just behind the Cuban, positioning the American contender as the frontrunner if he accepts an invitation to fight for the strap. Sanctioning body officials have not made an official announcement regarding the pairing.

Bentley can still get off to a good start with Zuffa by beating Mosley, but he’ll be giving up his world title to take the easier fight.

Hernández would then get his shot at the vacant belt against someone prepared to face him.

Ghana News.title: Mahama links Africa’s conflicts to struggle over natural resources
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama says the struggle for control of Africa’s natural resources and the profits from their extraction are central to the continent’s security crises, warning that powerful interests benefit from prolonged instability.

Addressing the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Peace in Africa in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, President Mahama said Africa, the President said the continent risks remaining vulnerable if its leaders fail to take greater control of their resources and determine their own security priorities.

He said “Let me be clear, Africa is not an empty chessboard for foreign powers to play their games. We are not spectators,” he said.

“But unless we consciously decide to take up the pen and write our own script, someone else will write it for us, and we will not like how the story ends.”

President Mahama said the importance of African minerals to the global green energy transition and digital economy should give the continent greater bargaining power, but communities endowed with these resources often bear the consequences of exploitation without enjoying the benefits.

He argued that sovereignty must go beyond political independence and membership of international institutions.

“Real sovereignty means having the administrative, legal, and economic power to govern your strategic assets, negotiate fair terms, and ensure the wealth beneath our people's feet actually puts food on their tables,” he said. He added that anything less amounted to “cosmetic independence that masks economic subjugation.”

He says African leaders must look beyond weapons proliferation and military operations to confront the political and economic interests that sustain conflicts across the continent.

“The real disease is mostly in the arena of political economy,” President Mahama said when presenting the 2026 State of Peace and Security in Africa Report at the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Peace in Africa in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia.

He challenged leaders to examine who controls natural resources, who benefits financially from their extraction and whose political and financial interests are better served by continued instability than lasting peace.

“In every single theatre of conflict across this continent today, if you want to understand why guns are firing, do not start by counting the rifles,” he said.

“Ask three basic questions, who controls the resource? Who cashes the cheque from its extraction? And whose political and financial fortunes are better served by perpetual chaos than by stable peace?”

President Mahama cited Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Somalia and Mozambique as examples of how resource competition, governance failures and economic marginalisation contribute to insecurity.

In Sudan, he said, the battle lines were drawn as much around gold extraction sites as around Khartoum.

In eastern DRC, he linked the resurgence and entrenchment of the M23 group to coltan, cobalt and the global competition for minerals needed for the green energy transition.

He also attributed the continued presence of Al-Shabaab in Somalia partly to governance failures that have created openings for the group to exploit.

In Mozambique’s Cabo Delgado region, he said, the area’s substantial gas wealth has not translated into meaningful benefits for local young people, who instead viewed it as another source of marginalisation.

“These are not separate, random brushfires. They are symptoms of a single, continent-wide firestorm,” he said.

Ghana News.title: CAGG demands retraction, apology from GoldBod CEO over alleged illegal mining remarks
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of the Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi

The Ghana Coalition Against Galamsey (CAGG) has called on the Office of the Attorney-General to investigate the Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) over statements it claims encouraged artisanal miners to operate without licences, provided they avoid forest reserves and river bodies.

In a press release dated October 24, 2026, the coalition condemned the reported remarks, describing them as unlawful and reckless, and warning that they could undermine efforts to combat illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey.

CAGG argued that Ghana's mining laws do not exempt miners from licensing requirements based on the location of their operations.

Citing Section 99(2)(a) of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), as amended by Act 995 of 2019, the coalition said anyone who undertakes mining without a licence granted by the Minister commits an offence.

It further cited Section 99, arguing that anyone who commands, instigates, employs or facilitates others to engage in illegal mining could face the same penalties as the illegal miner.

According to the coalition, offenders could face fines ranging from GH¢120,000 to GH¢180,000 and imprisonment of between 15 and 25 years, or both.

The coalition therefore wants the GoldBod CEO to immediately retract the alleged statement and issue an unqualified apology to the Ghanaian public.

It has also urged President John Dramani Mahama, the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, and the Minerals Commission to publicly reaffirm that mining without a licence is illegal, regardless of where the activity takes place.

CAGG further called on the Attorney-General's Office to investigate the matter for possible abetment of illegal mining, insisting that no individual should be exempt from the law.

Beyond the legal implications, the coalition warned that the reported remarks could expose farmers and landowners to encroachment on their lands.

It has consequently called on the Ministry of National Security, the Ghana Police Service and the Ministry of the Interior to strengthen protection for farmers and landowners and establish rapid-response channels for reporting encroachment.

The group is also demanding a clear national plan to protect farmlands, including legal safeguards for agricultural lands, mapping and registration of farms, support for vulnerable farmers seeking to document their land rights, and compensation and restoration for those whose lands have been destroyed.

CAGG said GoldBod was established to formalise and regulate artisanal mining, not to encourage unlicensed operations.

It warned that normalising mining without licences would weaken the regulatory framework intended to distinguish legal small-scale mining from illegal mining.

The coalition comprises civil society organisations, professional associations, environmental advocacy groups and other stakeholders.

Ghana News.title: GH¢10,000 injection: Assafuah boosts Black Challenge’s World Cup campaign

Mr Assafuah commended the players for their determination and commitment to representing Ghana on the international stage, stressing the importance of supporting their efforts to bring honour to the country.

He also pledged to help mobilise additional support for the team in the coming days, urging other stakeholders to contribute to the Black Challenge’s World Cup campaign.

The donation comes as the team continues preparations for the tournament, where Ghana will be seeking to make a strong impression against some of the world’s best amputee football nations.

The gesture highlights the importance of collective support from individuals, corporate organisations and public institutions in helping the Black Challenge achieve their ambitions and proudly fly Ghana’s flag in Mexico.

Ghana News.title: Nayi Alhassan retains NDC Tema North chairmanship as Salman Faris wins secretary

He defeated Salifu Mohammed, who polled 352 votes, and Abdul Halim Wayo Issahaku, who obtained 147 votes.

In the race for constituency secretary, Salman Faris Inusah emerged victorious with 598 votes, beating Baba Alhassan, popularly known as Mr Law, who secured 423 votes.

Mutala Hussein won the vice-chairmanship position with 476 votes, defeating Mohammed Nurideen Iddrisu, popularly known as Zaachi, who obtained 428 votes. Abdulai Abdul Rahaman received 107 votes.

Iddrisu Mohammed Nurideen won the deputy secretary position with 519 votes, narrowly beating Salman Iddrisu, who polled 502 votes.

For the treasurer position, Mateen Mohammed secured 639 votes, while Alhassan Adam, popularly known as Sahanaa, won the deputy treasurer position with 597 votes.

Baba Tahiru was elected communications officer after polling 774 votes to defeat Yussif Tikuma, who obtained 246 votes. Abdullah Abdul Rafiu, popularly known as Ras King, won the deputy communications officer position with 659 votes.

Results for other positions

In the organiser race, Mohammed A. Issahak emerged winner with 424 votes. He was followed by Issahaku Abdulai, popularly known as Captain America, with 279 votes, and Issahaku Alidu Bako, known as CR7, with 212 votes. Alhassan Abubakar, popularly known as Mr Abu, polled 88 votes, while Issah Zakaria Sasqo received nine votes.

Nashiru Iddrisu, popularly known as Prince Nash, won the deputy organiser position with 500 votes. Abdul Wadud Mohammed received 289 votes, Alhassan Abdul Latif Napari secured 123 votes, and Abdul Mumin Seidu, known as Hon Kporo, polled 106 votes.

Alidu Mohammed won the youth organiser position with 99 votes, ahead of Issahaku Amin, who received 16 votes. Husaifa Alhassan won deputy youth organiser with 82 votes, defeating Abdallah Jalil Yussif, who polled 32 votes.

Ayishatu Abdulai Yahaya emerged women's organiser with 63 votes, beating Ruhiya Adam, who secured 48 votes.

In the deputy women's organiser contest, Suweiba Iddrisu Alhassan won with 37 votes. Diana Alhassan obtained 35 votes, Memuna Sumani received 30 votes, and Sadia Abubakar polled eight votes.

Alhassan Mohammed Sadat secured 381 votes in the treasurer race, finishing behind winner Mateen Mohammed, who obtained 639 votes. In the deputy treasurer contest, Zakaria Abass, popularly known as Oly, received 423 votes, losing to Alhassan Adam, who secured 597 votes.

For deputy communications officer, Abdulai Ibrahim Danaa polled 187 votes, while Tahiru Lansah received 174 votes, both behind winner Abdullah Abdul Rafiu, who secured 659 votes.

In the Zongo Caucus election, Adizatu Suleman won with 555 votes, defeating Sulemana Ahmed, who polled 350 votes, and Amadu Mohammed, who obtained 166 votes.

The elections form part of the NDC’s nationwide constituency-level reorganisation exercise aimed at electing executives to coordinate party activities and strengthen grassroots structures ahead of the 2028 general elections

Ghana News.title: Ellen White Foundation brings free breast cancer screening to Bono East police women
Ghana News.content:
In a heartwarming display of commitment to women's health, the Ellen White Sustainable Foundation, in partnership with the Awat Foundation and the Police Ladies Association, has provided free breast cancer screening to nearly 100 female police officers across the Bono East Region.

The screening exercise, held at the Techiman Divisional Police Command, formed part of efforts to promote early detection and awareness of breast cancer among women in uniform.

The programme was held under the theme: "Investing in Women's Health, Investing in Stronger Communities."

Mrs. Ellen White Opoku, founder of the Ellen White Sustainable Foundation and a 2023 Joy Impact Makers Award recipient, said the initiative was born out of the need to reach officers who cannot easily access health facilities due to their busy schedules.

"This exercise is to help bring the screening to the doorstep of the police, who are unable to attend to health facilities for the same due to their busy work schedules," she noted.

Police Ladies Association Weighs In

ASP Beatrice Okrah, Crime Officer for the Jema District Police Command and a regional executive member of the Police Ladies Association, commended the organizers and encouraged women to prioritize their health.

She said the time had come for women to own up and get themselves screened to know their statuses and be treated when diagnosed with the condition.

"The time has come for women to own up and get themselves screened to know their statuses and be treated when diagnosed with the condition," she stated.

ASP Okrah added that the awareness talk had been helpful in creating awareness about what the condition is, equipping participants with knowledge to share with colleagues and family members.

"The talk has been helpful in creating awareness about what the condition is," she noted.

Service to Support Officers Diagnosed

In a reassuring message to personnel, ASP Okrah disclosed that officers found to have the cancer will be taken care of by the Police Service.

She explained that the welfare of officers remains a priority, and those diagnosed through the screening will receive the necessary support and care from the Service.

A Community Investment

The event reflects a growing push to make healthcare accessible to women in security services, who often sacrifice personal wellness for public duty. By investing in the health of these officers, organizers say the ripple effect will be felt across entire communities.

The Ellen White Sustainable Foundation has indicated its commitment to sustaining such initiatives, with plans to reach more districts in the Bono East Region and beyond.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s U-15 Boys thrash Uzbekistan 4-1 as Abdul Aziz Issah and Jerry Owusu hit brace each
Ghana News.content:
The National U-15 Boys team made a flying start to the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival with an emphatic 4-1 victory over Uzbekistan in their opening Group W match on Saturday.

Abdul Aziz Issah and Jerry Owusu were the heroes for Ghana, scoring a brace each to secure all three points in Azerbaijan.

Ghana dominated proceedings from the blast of the whistle, showing flair, composure and attacking intent against their Asian opponents.

Aziz Issah opened the scoring before doubling Ghana's advantage, while Jerry Owusu added two more goals to put the game beyond the reach of Uzbekistan, who managed a consolation strike late in the game.

The win gives Ghana a strong start in Group W, which also includes Myanmar, Guam, Bahamas and Kazakhstan.

Ghana will next face Myanmar and Guam on Sunday, before wrapping up the group phase against Bahamas and Kazakhstan on Monday.

The FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival, part of FIFA's Talent Development Scheme, is aimed at giving every talent a chance to showcase their skills on the world stage.

Ghana News.title: GH¢49.72m S.A. evacuation: Asafo-Adjei says government’s figures do not add up
Ghana News.content:
The Deputy Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Nana Asafo-Adjei Ayeh, has raised concerns over the GH¢49.72 million reportedly spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa, insisting that the figures presented by the government do not add up.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, the opposition lawmaker questioned the credibility of the expenditure, arguing that the inability to satisfactorily establish the number of beneficiaries raises serious concerns about the entire evacuation exercise.

"I am at this point confident in everything in me that the figures don't add up. If you cannot even establish the 1,964, then there is a problem with everything you did," he stated.

Mr Asafo-Adjei maintained that the documents presented to justify the expenditure must be subjected to thorough scrutiny, stressing that the details should support the government's public explanations.

According to him, the Minority's concerns are based on the contents of the available documentation rather than political disagreements or unrelated issues.

"The content of the document is what matters. The devil is always in the details, and that is what we are looking at, and it doesn't support your communication," he said.

The Deputy Ranking Member emphasised that his focus remains on establishing the facts surrounding the expenditure and ensuring that the government provides satisfactory explanations for the amount spent and the reported number of evacuees.

He rejected suggestions that the Minority was diverting attention from the substantive issues, insisting that his interventions have consistently centred on accountability and transparency.

"If you listen to the Minority, particularly me, I have never majored in any tangential. I am focused on this matter, and I want to get to the logical conclusion of this matter," he stressed.

His comments come amid scrutiny of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs over the reported GH¢49.72 million expenditure on the evacuation of 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa.

Ghana News.title: 2026 U17 WWC: Black Maidens book knockout spot with win over Canada
Ghana News.content:
Ghana produced a great second half performance to advance into the knockout stages of the ongoing U-17 Women’s World Cup.

The Black Maidens defeated Canada 2-0 in their final group game of the tournament to finish second in Group C after a troubling start to the tournament.

Nana Joe Adarkwa’s side came into the final group game knowing only a win was enough to get them into the next phase of the competition.

Despite a strong start to the game, the Maidens always rushed their final third decision making, leaving them with no goals after 45 minutes despite 13 attempts.

After the recess, Ghana continued to create chances in the game with Gloria Ameaa and Jessica Appiah posing dangers to the Canadian defence but both players were unable to find the back of the net.

Adarkwa called on his bench halfway through the second half, bringing on Linda Achiaa and Christiana Ashiaku.

Those changes yielded results as Achiaa scored with her first touch after the ball deflected off the crossbar, opening the scoring in the game.

In the closing stages of the encounter, Ashiaku doubled the lead for the Black Maidens with a brilliant strike, lobbing it over the goalkeeper to wrap up the victory.

The win sees Ghana finish their group campaign in second place with four points, behind Brazil who claimed seven points from three games.

Ghana also advance into the round of 16 on their return to the global stage at the U-17 level following their comeback from a two-edition ban.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Arsenal join Man City at Premier League summit, Spurs shock Chelsea 2-0
World.content:
Gunners capitalise on City’s first loss of the season, while Tottenham get second league victory at Stamford Bridge in 36 years.

Arsenal joined Manchester City at the top of the Premier League table after a 2-0 ⁠victory over Everton in torrential rain at ⁠the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, capitalising on City’s first defeat of the season earlier in the day.

City had left the door open when they fell to a 2-1 loss at Aston Villa, where Nicolas Jackson struck twice to end the visitors’ perfect start to the league campaign.

Tottenham ⁠Hotspur stunned fourth-placed Chelsea 2-0 in only their second league victory at Stamford Bridge in 36 years, while Fulham beat Coventry City 1-0 for their second league victory of the season.

With the leaders beaten in Birmingham, Arsenal seized their chance to erase the three-point gap as goals from Ezri Konsa and Gabriel secured a comfortable win over Everton in ⁠soaking north London conditions.

The result moved Mikel Arteta’s side level on 21 points with City in what is already shaping up to be a closely fought title race after eight games, but one played under a cloud amid City’s off-field financial case.

Arsenal made their strong start count when Martin Odegaard’s corner caused chaos in the Everton box.

England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford kept out the initial danger after the ball was flicked on at the near post but, with Everton unable to clear, Konsa bundled home his first goal for the club from ‌a yard out in the seventh minute.

The set-piece goal was Arsenal’s first since May, ending a run of 13 games across all competitions without one.

“I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons; I know how tough it is to play against us,” Konsa said. “It’s not surprising to me.



“We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home, and we want to win as many games here as possible.”

Arsenal’s two milestone men combined to give the Gunners a two-goal cushion in the 68th minute, with Ben White marking his 200th appearance for the club by clipping a cross to the far post, where Gabriel headed home on his 200th Premier League appearance.

Everton are ninth in the table.

Jackson braces downs City

At Villa Park, Unai Emery’s team climbed to sixth on 11 points with their first home league victory ⁠this season and third successive league win over City, who are playing under the shadow of an independent commission’s findings that they ⁠committed 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules.

City have always denied any wrongdoing, and have appealed.

Jackson took advantage of two City blunders, opening the scoring in the sixth minute when defender Marc Guehi’s heavy touch allowed Villa captain John McGinn to pounce and feed the striker, who slotted the ball into the bottom corner.

Erling Haaland equalised soon after the break when he headed home Iliman Ndiaye’s clipped cross from a ⁠free kick.

But Jackson struck the winner on the hour when Ibrahim Mbaye surged down the right before cutting the ball back for his Senegal international teammate, whose shot sneaked under the diving body of keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

“It was incredible; we got the win, which is ⁠the most important thing. Man City are a strong team, the league leaders,” Jackson told TNT Sports. “It’s just ⁠the beginning; we’re trying to work game by game.”

Tottenham get rare win at Stamford Bridge

At Stamford Bridge, Spurs got on the scoresheet in the 77th minute when Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders punched a corner into his own net in his first league start.

Chelsea were reduced to 10 men when Cole Palmer was shown a second yellow card in the 80th minute for a late challenge on Conor Gallagher.

Mathys Tel sealed the victory for Spurs in the 87th when he gained ‌possession inside his own half before embarking on a surging run down the left, gliding past two defenders and firing a low shot from outside the box into the bottom corner.

“It’s very special, because we came here a lot of times and didn’t get a win,” said Tel. “And today, we made it together, all together, we showed great ‌mentality, ‌and I’m very happy about it.”

Spurs climbed to 12th with the win.

At Coventry, Fulham appeared ready to substitute Oscar Bobb before the winger produced a moment of quality in the 80th minute, driving into the box and curling a superb finish into the far corner.



Fulham are 13th in the table, while Coventry are 19th.

World.title: Thousands of Israelis rally against Netanyahu gov’t days before election
World.content:
Share Thousands of Israelis rally against Netanyahu gov’t days before election on social media

Thousands of Israelis are protesting against the government and calling for an independent inquiry into the security failures that led to the October 7, 2023 attacks.

Demonstrators rallied in the public plaza known as Hostages Square in Tel Aviv on Saturday, three days before Israel’s first general election since the genocidal war on Gaza began.

The protest was organised by the October Council, a group founded by the families of captives taken to Gaza three years ago, to demand accountability for the government’s failure to prevent the Hamas attack that preceded the war.

“Three days before the election, we will hold the culminating event marking three years of struggle to uncover the truth, demand accountability and establish a state commission of inquiry,” the October Council wrote on X ahead of the rally.

Elsewhere in Israel, protesters were also gathering for antigovernment demonstrations, reported Haaretz newspaper.

Taking part were leading figures from opposition parties, including Gadi Eisenkot of the Yashar party, who is Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s main centre-right rival.

In Tel Aviv, Eisenkot was greeted by chants of “Who’s coming? The next prime minister”, according to The Times of Israel. The leader of the Democrats, Yair Golan, was also at the rally.

“Masses, masses of masses, flowing in the ‘Democrats’ march from Rabin Square to the Hostages Square – for change, for hope, for r-e-v-o-l-u-t-i-o-n. What energy. This time it’s ours completely!”, Israeli citizen and lawyer Dan Adin posted on X.

Polls ahead of Tuesday’s election suggest a tight race, with Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc, in power since late 2022, neck and neck with Eisenkot’s. Neither bloc is currently projected to obtain a majority of seats in Israel’s parliament.



The election could be pivotal in determining whether Israel launches another round of strikes on Iran. Eisenkot is believed to be less inclined to resume military action against Tehran if he becomes Israel’s next prime minister.

However, on most other foreign policy issues, leading Israeli parties and politicians remain united, including in their opposition to the creation of an independent Palestinian state.

Ahead of the protest, the October Council alerted law enforcement to possible “provocations” from pro-government agitators.

“We have sent an urgent letter to the Police Commissioner following alerts about attempts by entities linked to the coalition to disrupt tonight’s rally,” it wrote on X.

The October Council aims to hold Israeli officials deemed responsible for the October 7 attacks to account and deliver justice for affected families.

Netanyahu’s coalition government, however, has refused demands to establish an independent commission of inquiry. Instead, it has offered to set up a “political” commission. Half of the commission’s members would be appointed by the government, while the remainder would be appointed by opposition legislators.

Opposition leaders have said they would boycott a commission appointed by politicians.

World.title: Thousands join Paris protests as authorities clamp down on disorder
World.content:
NewsFeed Thousands join Paris protests as authorities clamp down on disorder

Thousands of protesters are on the streets of Paris for a second weekend. French authorities banned demonstrations in central areas of the city, following violence last weekend. Some 70,000 police have been deployed across France. Al Jazeera’s Virginia Pietromarchi reports.

World.title: Thousands gather at new Albanian antigovernment rally
World.content:
More than 300 protesters and police were injured in the Albanian capital Tirana’s fiercest clashes in days.

Protesters have clashed with police in rallies in the Albanian capital of Tirana, with police firing tear gas and water cannon to disperse crowds.

Several government buildings were attacked, dozens of demonstrators arrested, and more than 300 protesters and police injured, authorities said Saturday.

Protesters and police have routinely clashed since a significant wave of protests started in mid-October over poor conditions in schools and the cost of living in the small Balkan country.

While the protests in Tirana had calmed in recent days, Saturday’s demonstration escalated the situation again, with police deploying water cannon, tear gas and rubber bullets against crowds.

Thousands of people had heeded calls from organisers for students and others around Albania to attend the rally. Various groups, including university professors, artists and opposition parties, announced their support or attendance.

The country’s Ministry of Education has become a focal point of rallies, and Saturday’s gathering saw some in the crowd throwing stones and rolling burning bins at the building.

Police had introduced heightened security around the capital on Saturday, with checks being carried out on cars heading to the city, local media reported.

Albania has seen intermittent antigovernment protests since May, when news emerged of a luxury hotel project linked to United States President Donald Trump’s family.

Protesters take aim at PM

Since then, public anger has turned into a broader push against corruption and the high cost of living, with protesters calling for the resignation of Socialist Prime Minister Edi Rama.



Rama has blamed “foreign actors” for the violence and accused both Russia and Iran of driving online misinformation.

The prime minister has called for dialogue, and on Saturday red cushions were laid outside the government headquarters in a symbolic gesture for talk and dialogue. Protesters later set the cushions on fire.

Protesters have blamed the entire political class for the crisis, with some also seen holding signs decrying Rama’s opposition, centre-right leader Sali Berisha.

World.title: Kim Jong Un crosses new bridge linking North Korea and China
World.content: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un waved to crowds as he crossed a newly opened bridge linking his country with China, Chinese state media reported. The Yalu River Bridge is seen as a strategic link in expanding trade ties between the two nations.

World.title: Trump says he may move White House press corps to new location
World.content:
Trump’s remarks come amid a fractious moment between the US president and the journalists who cover him.

Share Trump says he may move White House press corps to new location on social media

United States President Donald Trump has confirmed he could move the White House press corps to a different location, possibly away from the executive residence.

In a social media post on Friday, Trump described reports that he planned to remove the White House press briefing room in favour of restoring a historic swimming pool located underneath as “Fake News”.

“I NEVER even thought to do such a stupid thing!” he wrote in a Truth Social post.

Trump, however, indicated he may relocate dozens of reporters who cover the White House “to a less obnoxious location”.

The New York Times on Tuesday reported that Trump had pitched his former press secretary, Karoline Leavitt, on an idea to move journalists out of the White House’s storied James S. Brady Press Briefing Room. That proposal did not move forward during Leavitt’s tenure, which ended on August 27.

Trump’s remarks come amid a fractious moment between him and the journalists who cover him.

Last month, Trump banned journalists from three US-based media outlets – CNN, MS NOW and POLITICO – from the White House, a move that proponents of free speech said violated First Amendment protections.

A US federal judge ruled that the order was likely unconstitutional, forcing the White House to restore the journalists’ access. The Trump administration continues to fight the ruling.

Trump has also regularly chided and denigrated members of the media he claims cover him unfairly.

The latest incident was during an Oval Office event on Tuesday when Trump attacked The Independent’s White House Correspondent Andrew Feinberg.



“What’s wrong with you? Are you a sick person? I actually think there’s something wrong with you”, Trump said as Feinberg tried to ask a question. The moment was amplified by the White House on social media.

If Trump opts to proceed with changes to the White House press briefing room, it would be the latest in a long list of controversial projects he has ordered that would transform the property.

Since returning to power last year, the US president has demolished the White House East Wing to construct a new ballroom, installed concrete pavers over the lawn centred in the White House Rose Garden and built a helipad on the South Lawn.

The Times reported Trump told aides he wanted to bring back a West Wing indoor pool constructed in 1933 for use by President Franklin D Roosevelt, who suffered from polio and often swam, according to his presidential library, to ease soreness.

In the 1970s, former President Richard Nixon had a floor constructed above the pool to accommodate a briefing room for the growing White House press corps. The pool remains beneath the floor of the briefing room.

Leavitt confirmed during a Friday interview that Trump was “flirting” with the idea of restoring the pool.

“He just, maybe, wants to restore it to all of its glory”, Leavitt said during an appearance on HBO’s “Real Time with Bill Maher”. “I don’t know if he’ll do it.”

The White House did not immediately return Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

World.title: About 25,000 rally in Madrid in support of Spain’s state pension scheme
World.content:
Demonstrators want pensions to remain indexed to inflation and the gender pension gap to be eliminated.

Share About 25,000 rally in Madrid in support of Spain’s state pension scheme on social media

Approximately 25,000 people have gathered in the Spanish capital in support of the state pension scheme, as protests continue across Europe, prompted by a range of issues, including the cost of living, school conditions and alleged corruption.

Protesters from across the country marched through Madrid on Saturday before next month’s general election.

The pressure on Spain’s state pension scheme is being driven by several factors, including an ageing population, a low birth rate and wage stagnation, as well as a declining ratio of workers to pensioners.

Demonstrators are concerned that the state pension scheme could be significantly weakened depending on who wins next month’s election. The country’s monthly pension bill hit a record high this year of almost 14.5 billion euros ($16.2bn).

Protesters marched from Atocha train station to the Gran Via, Madrid’s busiest and most famous street.

Several of the demonstrators carried banners reading “protect and guarantee our pensions”.

Emilio Delgado serves as the deputy spokesperson of the left-wing party Mas Madrid in the Assembly of Madrid. Posting on X, he said that “no pension should be below the minimum wage. A lifetime of work deserves a dignified retirement.”

Protesters want pensions to remain indexed to inflation and are calling for the gender pension gap to be eliminated.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has accused the right-wing Popular Party (PP) of planning to weaken inflation-linked pension increases if it wins next month’s election.



However, leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo said on Monday that he would continue to raise pensions in line with inflation if his party wins the vote.

Sanchez has pledged to protect pensions if he remains in office and says the current pension system is affordable.

The system has gradually become more reliant on state funding because of a growing number of pensioners and increases in monthly payments.

World.title: Serbian elections: A country where students may actually take power
World.content:
NewsFeed Serbian elections: A country where students may actually take power

Serbia is voting in an early election, where the most powerful politician in the country, in charge for 14 years, has a serious rival for the first time – students. Aleksandar Vučić, who stepped down from his second mandate as president is now running for prime minister. Al Jazeera’s Nataša Kovačev explains.

World.title: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits
World.content:
Ukraine now has a "stable connection" to Starlink, its defence minister has said, after its military suffered days of restricted connectivity on the satellite internet network.

Kyiv relies on the Starlink and its military-grade counterpart Starshield for piloting drones and operations within Ukraine, but last week accused US President Donald Trump of telling owner Elon Musk to place limits on it.

This meant drones would lose connection when travelling at 161km/h (100mph) or more, it said. Trump denied doing so before saying Musk had "put it back".

Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said that speeds of more than 400km/h were now possible on the network, indicating that full capability had been restored.

"This result is above all important for our front, for our soldiers, for the operation of drones, for logistics and for communications," he said in a statement on Saturday.

Ukraine's military uses the network of 10,000 low Earth orbit satellites extensively for military operations, particularly in remote areas on the battlefield.

Ukraine uses both the civilian service Starlink and the more secure Starshield, which Musk said was controlled by the US military when he suggested the Pentagon could be behind the recent issues.

Russia is not authorised to use Starlink, so when Ukraine sends long-range missiles or drones deep into Russia to hit oil refineries, the network does not work.

The debacle over Starlink began last week, and emerged during a broader diplomatic row between Trump and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.

Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market - a move criticised by Ukraine and its European allies.

World.title: Palestinian families displaced as Israeli forces demolish Hebron homes
World.content:
The Israeli military has launched a sweeping crackdown in the occupied West Bank, demolishing homes and businesses in the city of Hebron and displacing hundreds of families, according to local officials.

Footage shared online showed destruction caused by Israeli bulldozers, with at least one whole street appearing to have been flattened. The military has also cordoned off the city, heavily restricting the movement of its 200,000 residents.

The operation was announced by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday, in response to the killing of two Israeli soldiers by two Palestinian gunmen in an attack on a checkpoint. Three other Israeli soldiers were injured, and the gunmen were also killed.

Netanyahu said on Friday that buildings around the site of the attack and the neighbourhoods that the two gunmen were from would be "destroyed".

Hebron's Mayor Youssef al-Jaabari said more than 1,000 people had been displaced by the operation, which centred on the Ein Deir Baha and Farsh al-Hawa neighbourhoods, and targeted homes, businesses, industrial sites and infrastructure.

He said dozens of families had been forced to spend the night outside, with some told to leave without taking their vehicles, while homes were marked for demolition with spray paint.

He added that he believed the military planned to displace a total of 2,500 people from about 0.35 sq km of urban land. The city's governor and deputy mayor meanwhile said at least 200 families had been displaced.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) did not respond immediately to the BBC's request for comment. It said in a statement on social media that it had dozens of targets across the West Bank and that its operations would last for several days.

World.title: Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
World.content:
Police in the southern German state of Bavaria have detained a 33-year-old German man during a fire at Adolf Hitler's Alpine mountain retreat, the Kehlsteinhaus, also known as the Eagle's Nest.

Dispatchers in Traunstein received a fire alarm from the building at 21:15 local time (19:15 GMT) on Friday and firefighters found it engulfed in flames.

Some 200 emergency personnel were deployed to the scene where the blaze was still burning early on Saturday, as police said difficult terrain hindered efforts to bring the fire under control.

Police said they apprehended the suspect riding a motorcycle near the scene and possible motives were still being examined, German media reported. A criminal investigation has been launched.

There is currently nothing to suggest the involvement of further suspects, police official Gerhart Holzinger told a press conference on Saturday afternoon.

Public prosecutor Rainer Vietze said a psychiatric report had concluded the 33-year-old man showed signs of possible mental illness and diminished responsibility might therefore be assumed.

Vietze said a possible political motive was also being considered, but stressed the investigation was in its early stages.

The residence, above the town of Berchtesgaden, was one of several buildings in the area used by the Nazi dictator and his entourage during World War Two.

Hitler and top Nazi officials used his nearby Berghof residence to plan the invasion of the USSR in 1941 and the whole complex was considered one of his headquarters.

He also used the area as a backdrop for propaganda films portraying him as a lover of animals and nature.

Local media reported that site had been "largely destroyed" and the public was urged to avoid the area.

Bavaria's Interior Minister Joachim Herrmann told reporters that the site would "under no circumstances remain a ruin", broadcaster BR24 reported. "It is important that we continue our work of remembrance," he added.

World.title: Father who killed Oregon school gunman describes anguish over children he couldn't save
World.content:
A father who fatally shot a gunman at his daughters' school in the US state of Oregon has described his anguish over being unable to save more pupils after "hearing children pleading for their lives".

Three students and a teacher were killed by a 16-year-old former student at Silver Rail Elementary School earlier this month. The attacker was then killed by Kaylub Giamanco.

"I want to apologise for not saving their babies," Giamanco, who has been hailed as a hero, said of his thoughts for the parents of the children killed, in an interview with Oregon Public Broadcasting (OPB) that aired on Friday.

"The gratitude for saving people's children is awesome, but there were ones that I didn't save."

Giamanco, 36, said he wanted to meet the victims' families and "cry with them and hold them".

He credited a teacher who fought the attacker with giving him the chance to intervene without losing his own life.

"I would love to give her a hug because that's a real true hero," he said.

The students who were killed were all boys, aged five, eight and 11. They were among six people in total who were shot in a classroom at the school, police said. Alongside the teacher who was killed, another child and a teacher were wounded.

Giamanco told OPB that the day of the attack began with breakfast and making packed lunches. He and his wife had spent extra time getting their daughters ready because it was school picture day.

The carpenter had taken lunch to work but decided to go home to eat with his wife instead. That decision brought him past the school as the attack began.

He initially wondered whether someone carrying a long gun was playing a prank. Then he saw him fire at a pickup truck and head towards the school.

Giamanco retrieved a handgun from his vehicle and called emergency services.

"I said, 'I'm sorry, I have to go in. People are going to die'," he told the broadcaster.

He followed the attacker, who shot through the school's locked glass doors. Hearing children pleading for their lives and more gunfire, Giamanco crawled towards the building.

"I told myself this is probably the last thing that I'm ever going to do," he said.

World.title: British woman dies after trying to rescue sons swept away at sea in the Bahamas
World.content:
"She was the purest, most amazing wife, mother and friend to have ever walked this Earth," her husband said in a Facebook post.

"I will never get over this, she was my soulmate, my childhood sweetheart, my one and only. The foundation of my entire family and the strength that held us all together.

"My boys had to witness something nobody should ever have to see of any age, but they know Mum died an absolute hero."

Gregory said he had also set up a fundraising page "for my sons and security after the tragic loss".

In the post on that page he described how his wife, who he had been with for 22 years, had held on to their son until he was rescued "but didn't have the energy to save herself".

He added: "I just have to be thankful for the hero she was in life and in death, and totally grateful for the fact my boys got out safely."

World.title: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis
World.content:
Vanessa Trump, the former wife of Donald Trump Jr, has announced that she is cancer-free following her breast cancer diagnosis earlier this year.

Trump, 48, who has five children with President Donald Trump's eldest son, shared in a short video on her 19-year-old daughter Kai's Instagram account that her recent tests results "came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free".

Following the Instagram post on Friday, Vanessa and Kai Trump released a longer video on Saturday, in which they discussed breast cancer awareness, early detection and prevention.

Vanessa Trump separated from Trump Jr in 2018 and announced last year that she had begun dating US pro golfer Tiger Woods.

"October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a time to raise awareness about early detection, education, and support for those affected by breast cancer," Kai Trump wrote on Instagram.

"I sat down with my mom and Dr. Nicole Saphier to talk about my mom's journey with breast cancer and learn more about prevention and early detection," she continued.

Kai's post received over 20,000 likes and hundreds of comments from people offering support and well wishes, including from American singer and media personality Mary Millben.

Vanessa Trump explained in the YouTube video that she experienced arm pain for several months before discovering a pea-sized lump in her breast, which testing confirmed was a cancerous tumour.

"It's a process you have to deal with," she said of the days spent waiting for her test results.

"You have to be mentally strong for yourself because you're going to need the strength to fight whatever challenge it is that's coming towards you."

Trump said she was first diagnosed with breast cancer in April. She publicly announced the diagnosis in May, saying in a social media post that she had undergone surgery and was working on a treatment plan with her medical team.

She eventually had a lumpectomy and radiation treatments, she said.

According to the American Cancer Society, the average risk of a woman in the US developing breast cancer is about 1 in 8, or 13%. The disease also accounts for 30% of all new female cancers every year, according to the group.

Surgery cures most breast cancers, but if some disease remains, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and endocrine therapy can reduce the long-term risk.

Treatments have been advancing, including more targeted therapies for early breast cancer, new types of hormonal therapies, and more precise and effective radiotherapy.

World.title: Three released without charge after fatal arson attack in Ireland
World.content:
Three people, who were arrested in connection with a suspected arson attack which killed four family members in the Republic of Ireland, have been released, gardaÃ­ (Irish police) have said.

Philip and Kim English and two of their children - nine-year-old Jayden and 12-year-old Callum - died after their home in Birch Avenue, on the outskirts of Waterford was set on fire earlier this month.

A man aged in his 20s and a woman in her 30s were previously charged in connection with the attack.

On Saturday, gardaÃ­ said three people - two women in their 30s and a man in his 50s - who were arrested on Tuesday have been released without charge.

A fourth person, a man in his 20s who was arrested on Thursday, remains in custody.

World.title: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
World.content:
Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola as it handles its first ever outbreak of the disease.

A woman, aged 65, who was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo, died after being placed in quarantine, the health ministry said.

Seven other Ebola patients were receiving treatment at two isolation facilities, it added.

All the cases were within "one cluster, with no evidence of community spread", the ministry said.

More than 4,000 people have died in Africa since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease.

Kenya's latest victim had been under quarantine when she developed symptoms on 13 October, the health ministry said.

The first death, on 5 October, was that of a man who fell ill in September and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo before arriving in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi, where he died a few days later.

Those still being treated are three other relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner.

World.title: 2027: Minister threatens to deploy ‘federal might’ in Akwa Ibom election
World.content:
The Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, has declared that the federal, state and local governments will combine their powers to secure overwhelming electoral victories for the APC in Akwa Ibom State, raising questions about the neutrality of public institutions ahead of the 2027 elections.

Mr Ekpo made the declaration at a political rally in Etim Ekpo Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom State, where he introduced the APC candidate for the Akwa Ibom State House of Assembly constituency.

“This State Constituency, this Federal Constituency, this Senatorial District, this Akwa Ibom State is going to be 100 over 100. I can tell you that as a federal minister,” he told the crowd at the rally.

“We will bring federal might and join with state might and join with local government might and make sure the people of this local government, whether you like that blessing, that blessing will come to you. A man of peace is on the throne.”

The minister did not explain what he meant by combining the powers of the three tiers of government or how the proposed mobilisation would be carried out.

His remarks drew attention to longstanding concerns surrounding the use of government power and public resources to influence electoral outcomes in Nigeria, where political expressions such as “federal might” have often fuelled suspicions of possible interference in the electoral process.

Under Nigeria’s democratic architecture, elections are expected to provide a level playing field for political parties and candidates, while public institutions must operate within the law rather than serve the electoral interests of the party in power.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Ekpo’s spokesperson, Louis Ibah, did not respond to a media enquiry sent to him on WhatsApp on Friday, despite reading the message. A reminder sent on Saturday morning and a subsequent telephone call also went unanswered.

In the enquiry, PREMIUM TIMES asked Mr Ibah to clarify what the minister meant by combining federal, state and local government power in the election and how the declaration aligned with democratic competition and the neutrality of public institutions.

There was no response as of the time of filing this report.

Echoes of previous election controversies

Mr Ekpo’s remarks follow concerns about political leaders making declarations that appear to presume electoral results before voters cast their ballots.

In September, PREMIUM TIMES reported that Emmanuel Enoidem, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Akwa Ibom and a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, insisted that a federal lawmaker, Clement Jimbo, would be returned to the House of Representatives in 2027, “whether you like it or not”.

Mr Enoidem made the declaration while soliciting support for Mr Jimbo, who represents Abak/Etim Ekpo/Ika Federal Constituency. Some members of the audience reportedly rejected the appeal.

Mr Enoidem subsequently told PREMIUM TIMES that his remarks were directed at APC members, arguing that party members were expected to support their party’s candidates. He also acknowledged the right of voters to freely choose their preferred candidates.

Mr Ekpo’s expression steered political discourse in Akwa Ibom, invoking concerns about whether the machinery of government could be used to influence electoral competition in the 2027 general elections.

Mr Ekpo’s declaration is particularly noteworthy because he occupies a federal executive position and noted that he speaks from the hindsight of being a minister while openly invoking the use of federal powers for an electoral result.

Although political parties and their members are entitled to campaign for electoral victories, using public office or government institutions to confer an unfair advantage on a party would raise serious questions about electoral integrity.

Nigeria’s constitution guarantees citizens the right to participate in government, while the Electoral Act provides the legal framework for conducting elections. The credibility of the process depends, in part, on voters being able to make their choices freely, without intimidation or improper interference.

Mr Ekpo did not explicitly threaten violence in the remarks reviewed by PREMIUM TIMES. However, his reference to combining federal, state and local government “might,” coupled with his revelation that he is speaking based on his privileged position as a “federal minister,” raises questions about the means through which he intends to secure the sweeping electoral victory he predicted.

Until he clarifies his remarks, that question remains unanswered.

World.title: 2027: Makinde calls for economic, security ‘reset’ at campaign group launch
World.content:
Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde has called for a reset in Nigeria’s economy, security architecture, and education system, questioning the country’s economic gains as many citizens struggle to feed their families.

Mr Makinde made the remarks in a video message played on Saturday at the launch of the Makinde-Daura Resetter Movement in Ikeja, Lagos.

“I am with you 101 per cent towards the Reset Agenda for Nigeria. We need to reset our economy. We need to reset our security architecture. We need to reset our educational system,” he said.

He questioned the benefits of rising foreign reserves when many Nigerians could barely afford basic necessities.

Using a household analogy, Mr Makinde said it made little sense for a family head to boast about savings while household members went hungry.

He said economic progress should improve living conditions and give young Nigerians the opportunity to pursue their aspirations.

Martins James, director of media for the Progressive Youths for Makinde’s Presidency 2027 (PYFMP2027), stated that the programme was intended to prepare supporters to take the movement’s message to communities across Lagos and other parts of the country.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times
