The group had earlier unveiled its “MAD Resetter” campaign in Lagos. At the time, its members expressed confidence that the proposed ticket would defeat the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

Mr James noted that the 2027 election would give Nigerians an opportunity to choose a different direction for the country.

“The 2027 election will provide Nigerians with an opportunity to choose a new direction for the country and embrace a leadership agenda centred on development, accountability, economic opportunity and a better quality of life,” he said.

He described a “MAD Resetter” as a supporter committed to political change and improved governance, adding that the campaign would focus on policies rather than political divisions.

Emmanuel Dennis, director of volunteers, support and special interest groups at the Makinde and Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation, said rising fuel and electricity costs, insecurity, unemployment and the high cost of living were among the issues driving the movement.

He criticised the National Assembly, describing it as a rubber stamp, and questioned the role of the courts in resolving electoral disputes.

Mr Dennis said the movement would concentrate on grassroots mobilisation and issue-based campaigns rather than rallies focused on entertainment. He said “MAD” stood for “Make a Difference with Makinde and Daura”.

In a goodwill message, Laja Adeoye, the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) governorship candidate in Lagos State, urged residents to use their permanent voter cards to hold elected officials accountable.

He also warned voters against exchanging their votes for money, saying such payments would not compensate them for four years of poor governance.

Osi Iwenekhai, national coordinator of the Reset Agents Network, urged young people to participate in the 2027 elections. He said Mr Makinde had shown the commitment needed to monitor government projects.

Former Minister of Aviation Hassan Felix Hyat also criticised the federal government’s economic policies, citing hunger, unemployment and insecurity as persistent challenges.

He said Nigeria’s resources should translate into better living conditions for more citizens.

The organisers said they planned to expand the movement’s network across the country ahead of the 2027 election.

World.title: PT Health Watch: What to do as extreme heat hits Nigeria
World.content:
As temperatures rise across parts of Nigeria, health authorities are warning residents to take precautions against the effects of extreme heat.

The warning comes as the country moves from the rainy season into the hotter, drier months, when prolonged exposure to high temperatures can increase the risk of dehydration, heat exhaustion and heatstroke.

A recent report by the Climate Impact Lab estimated that Nigeria could record 31,400 additional heat-related deaths between September 2026 and February 2027.

The report, titled “451,000 at Risk: Where Action Can Save Lives During the Super El Niño,” estimated 451,000 additional heat-related deaths globally during the period.

The Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet), in a 23 October advisory, also warned of hotter days and increased heat discomfort as the country enters the dry season.

The agency said changing weather conditions, including reduced rainfall and cloud cover, could contribute to rising temperatures. It warned that excessive heat could cause dehydration, heat exhaustion and heatstroke.

People most at risk

Extreme heat can affect anyone, but some people are more vulnerable to its effects.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The World Health Organisation (WHO) identifies older people, young children, people with chronic illnesses and outdoor workers among those who face greater health risks during periods of extreme heat.

People living with heart, lung or kidney conditions, diabetes and other chronic illnesses may also experience worsening symptoms when temperatures become very high.

Outdoor workers, including farmers, construction workers, traders and others who spend long periods under the sun, can also be exposed to heat for several hours without adequate opportunities to cool down.

WHO said extreme heat places additional stress on the body as it tries to maintain a normal temperature. Prolonged exposure can increase the risk of heat exhaustion and heatstroke and may also worsen existing health conditions.

What should you do?

NiMet advised Nigerians to drink water regularly and wear lightweight, breathable clothing.

It said people should also limit prolonged exposure to direct sunlight, particularly during the hottest periods of the day, and strenuous physical activities should be moved to cooler hours.

NiMet further urged schools and workplaces to ensure adequate ventilation, provide drinking water and shaded rest areas, and allow regular breaks during hot weather.

WHO similarly advises people to avoid strenuous activity during the hottest part of the day, stay in shaded or cool places and keep their homes as cool as possible.

People should also check on relatives, neighbours and friends who may be more vulnerable, particularly older people and those living alone.

WHO urged parents to take extra care with young children. Children should not be left alone in parked vehicles, as temperatures inside vehicles can rise rapidly even when the weather outside does not appear extreme.

READ ALSO: WHO pledges support as Nigeria records first imported Ebola case

Warning signs

Symptoms of heat exhaustion may include heavy sweating, weakness, headache, dizziness and nausea. Moving the person to a cooler place, giving fluids where they are able to drink and helping them cool down can help prevent the condition from becoming more serious.

Heatstroke is different and requires urgent medical attention. According to WHO, heatstroke is a potentially fatal medical emergency. Someone with hot, dry skin, delirium, convulsions or loss of consciousness during extreme heat should receive immediate medical attention.

The Climate Impact Lab said the projections provide an opportunity for governments and humanitarian organisations to identify vulnerable populations and direct resources towards interventions that can save lives.

NiMet has also urged Nigerians to follow official weather forecasts and advisories as conditions change.

World.title: Saving Nigeria from the increasingly absurd theatrics of Jimoh Ibrahim, By Owei Lakemfa
World.content:
Ibrahim is a disaster waiting to happen. In my July column titled “Jimoh Ibrahim is uninformed: UN intervenes in nation’s internal affairs,” I had observed that his knowledge of diplomacy is weak and advised him “to read the UN Charter, its main resolutions and practices.” I had also observed that he does not appear to listen to good advice. So, I suggested that he listened to our career ambassadors in the UN. Perhaps, if he had done so, he would not continue scripting absurd pieces of drama in the world body.

This week, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu featured prominently in the newest theatre of the absurd staged by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Folorunsho Ibrahim. The stage was the Aso Rock Presidential Villa, Abuja, where, on 19 October, Ibrahim presented the seven-volume UN 2027 draft budget to President Tinubu. Ibrahim began the comedy with a big, fat lie. He claimed: “This is the first time in 66 years that Nigeria will chair the Budget and Administration Committee. It is the first time, and we do not know when it will happen again in history.” Contrary to this wild claim, the first time Nigeria chaired the UN Budget and Administration Committee was on 22 September, 1971. This is verifiable in UN records, including its digitallibrary.un.org. That 1971 date was when Ambassador Edward Olu Sanu was elected the UN Budget Committee chair. At that time, Ibrahim was a four-year-old boy.

So, contrary to Ibrahim’s claim that it took Nigeria 66 years after independence to be elected chair of the UN Budget Committee, the country was actually chair within eleven years of its independence. Ibrahim followed this falsehood with the announcement that: “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is making history by being able to receive this budget. He is the first Nigerian president in 66 years to receive the UN budget from the United Nations.” May Tinubu be the first and last Nigerian President to be subjected to this absurdity. The UN draft budget is not Nigeria’s budget. It is that of the 193 Member countries of the UN and is slated for deliberations at the UN Headquarters in New York, not in the Nigerian Presidency. So, what does Ibrahim want President Tinubu to do with the seven volumes? Sit down and read them? For what purpose? Can Tinubu amend, audit, veto or pass the UN budget? Why would Ibrahim’s publicity stunt be allowed to subject Nigeria to international ridicule?

All ambassadors report to the Foreign Affairs minister. Did Ibrahim pass through Minister Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu before presenting the unofficial UN budget to President Tinubu? Did she, as procedures dictate, even approve his journey to Abuja? If she did, was the Foreign Ministry part of this charade?

This is the second time within three months that Ibrahim would be disgracing Nigeria. In July 2026, he held a press conference and announced that: “President Tinubu will be sitting very close to Donald Trump in the front row of the United Nations General Assembly. Don’t ask me how that was arranged, but he will be sitting.” He gave the impression that the UN is a corrupt organisation where sitting positions can be purchased. Secondly, he presents the slavish mentality that it will be a rare privilege for Tinubu to sit close to Trump. Ibrahim’s claims about the sitting arrangement in the UN are false. For the UNGA meetings, the arrangement is determined alphabetically by the English name of each country. The starting position is based on a random annual lottery in which the UN Secretary-General picks the name of a Member State from a box. The country so picked is assigned the first seat in the hall, which is the far right of the front row from the podium. After this, the remaining 192 countries are seated round the hall, with each entitled to six seats: three for delegates and three for alternates.

This arrangement is valid for one year and affects the sitting arrangements for all formal meetings of the UN Committees. This month, when I was in the UN to make a case for the complete decolonisation of Western Sahara, I had the privilege of visiting the UNGA Hall.

So, Nigeria already had its allocated sixth position, sitting in the front row of the General Assembly chamber for the 2026 UNGA, before Ibrahim appeared at the Presidential Villa to claim that he had a special seat for Tinubu close to where Trump is to sit. Therefore, when Vice President Kashim Shettima, who represented Tinubu at UNGA 2026, sat in the sixth position and Ibrahim proclaimed that it was a significant diplomatic achievement, it was a lie.

The UN sitting arrangement is in line with UN principles of the sovereign equality of states. So, no country has a permanent front-row seat. Nigeria has a long, glorious history of diplomacy. As far back as 1486, that is 540 years ago, the Benin Kingdom, under Oba Ozolua in present-day Edo State, had an ambassador in the Court of King John II of Portugal. In 1526, Benin, under Oba Esigie, had an ambassador to Europe, as well as an embassy building in Lisbon. In return, Portugal sent ambassadors to the Benin Oba’s Court. The Itsekiri Kingdom in present-day Delta State had accredited ambassadors to the Vatican and European Courts. So, if territories that are now part of Nigeria had accredited ambassadors to Europe over five centuries ago, it is tragic that we would be presenting Nigeria today as a country that lacks diplomatic knowledge or experience.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It is indeed quite disgraceful that a country that had outstanding Permanent Representatives to the UN, such as Chief Simeon Adebo, Emeka Anyaoku, Ibrahim Gambari, who became one of the most outstanding UN envoys, and Joseph Garba, who was the face of the Anti-Apartheid Movement in the UN, would appoint a Jimoh Ibrahim to such a prominent position as Nigeria’s face in the world assembly.

Ibrahim is a disaster waiting to happen. In my July column titled “Jimoh Ibrahim is uninformed: UN intervenes in nation’s internal affairs,” I had observed that his knowledge of diplomacy is weak and advised him “to read the UN Charter, its main resolutions and practices.” I had also observed that he does not appear to listen to good advice. So, I suggested that he listened to our career ambassadors in the UN. Perhaps, if he had done so, he would not continue scripting absurd pieces of drama in the world body. However, this is not about Jimoh Ibrahim, who, sooner or later, will leave. This is about our country. I think the Foreign Ministry and our foreign ministers should exercise proper supervision of our ambassadors, especially the non-career ones like Jimoh Ibrahim, who may not be experienced in diplomacy. We should also ensure that people so appointed or sent to foreign missions are knowledgeable, teachable and respectable.

I have had it said a few times that President Tinubu is his own foreign minister. No! This was what was touted about President Muhammadu Buhari, and it ended up disastrous. President Tinubu should concentrate on his job of ensuring the welfare and security of Nigerians and give the Foreign Ministry and the foreign ministers he has willingly chosen a free hand to run our international affairs.

Owei Lakemfa, a former secretary general of African workers, is a human rights activist, journalist and author.

World.title: CBN grants JP Morgan approval-in-principle to set up merchant bank
World.content:
The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has granted approval-in-principle to JP Morgan to set up a merchant in the country.

The move eases the path for the US largest bank to expand its services – payments, lending, trade finance and corporate banking – in Nigeria, where it has operated a representative office for years.

JP Morgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited plans to run wholesale banking, capital markets and advisory services, Michael Akuka, the CBN’s director of corporate communications and investor relations, said in a statement on Friday.

The approval-in-principle is the first phase of the licensing process, and does not translate into an ultimate banking permit.

JP Morgan needs to clear further regulatory hurdles such as incorporation with the Corporate Affairs Commission and operational approvals before it can commence operations, the regulator stated.

The push comes amidst hordes of banking sector reforms in Africa’s most populous country, aimed at bolstering the financial system, enhancing market confidence and boosting resilience.

According to the statement, the CBN also approved the nomination of Adedapo Olagunju as the managing director of the bank and Latter Kevin George, Nzelu Chinedum Izunwanne and Syed Gabriel Murtaza as non-executive directors.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Our objective is to build a financial system that is stable, competitive and internationally connected, one that commands confidence and can effectively support investment and economic growth,” said CBN Governor Olayemi Cardoso.

“We are encouraged by the growing interest of international financial institutions in Nigeria. Our focus remains on sustaining the reforms, strengthening the credibility of our markets and creating an environment in which both domestic and international institutions can participate and thrive,” he added.

On Tuesday, Bloomberg, citing sources with knowledge of the deal, reported that JP Morgan was on course to secure a banking licence in the country after depositing N50 billion ($38 million) with the CBN.

It noted that the bank hopes to receive the licence by year-end or in early 2027, provided it is able to obtain all the requisite approvals

P Morgan’s presence in Nigeria dates back to 1961, when Chase Manhattan Bank, which later evolved into JP Morgan Chase & Co., opened a branch in Lagos, providing a wide range of commercial banking services to local businesses and individuals.

A year earlier, Chase International Investment Corporation, a unit of Chase Manhattan Bank, served as the lead partner in organising Nigerian Textile Mills in Lagos, regarded as the first major private industrial project with an American interest in Nigeria.

World.title: APC Rally: Shettima, Yari urge Nigerians to re-elect Tinubu, cite APC’s record
World.content:
Vice President Kashim Shettima has urged voters in Kaduna State to renew the mandate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), saying the party is seeking re-election based on projects and policies delivered under President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

Mr Shettima made the appeal on Saturday at the APC campaign rally in Kaduna, where he highlighted the administration’s investments in education and infrastructure as evidence that the party had kept its promises to the state.

The vice president said the administration had worked to restore Kaduna’s position as a centre of learning through the establishment and upgrade of educational institutions.

“We promise to bring back the glory of Kaduna State as the national centre of learning. Didn’t we deliver on that?” he asked supporters at the rally.

He cited the establishment of the Federal University of Applied Sciences and the transition of the Federal University of Education, Zaria, as part of the administration’s interventions in the state.

Mr Shettima also mentioned the establishment of vocational institutes in Rigachikun, Soba and Samaru, saying more than 4,000 people had graduated from the institutions.

He said the administration had also expanded education funding through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), which he said had benefited hundreds of thousands of students in universities across the country.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The vice president further listed major infrastructure projects involving the North, including the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) gas pipeline, Kano-Maradi railway, Lagos-Kano rail corridor and the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano road.

He also cited ongoing work on the Sokoto-Badagry highway, describing it as a project that would create opportunities for agricultural production and economic activity.

Mr Shettima said the APC had demonstrated its commitment to continuity by completing or advancing projects initiated by previous administrations.

He also appealed to voters in the North to support Mr Tinubu’s bid for a second term, arguing that the President had demonstrated political support for northern leaders over the years.

He recalled Mr Tinubu’s support for Atiku Abubakar when the former vice president left the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), as well as his backing of Nuhu Ribadu in the 2011 presidential election and Muhammadu Buhari in the 2015 and 2019 elections.

Mr Shettima said Mr Tinubu’s relationship with the North therefore predated his presidency.

The vice president also praised Kaduna Governor Uba Sani, saying his administration had helped promote unity across the state and spread the benefits of governance beyond metropolitan Kaduna.

He urged the people of Kaduna to maintain their support for the APC at the federal and state levels.

“We have the courage to come to Kaduna today because we have kept our promise to never relegate you,” he said.

Also speaking at the rally, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council and former Zamfara State governor, Abdul’aziz Yari, claimed that about two million farmers had committed to supporting Tinubu’s re-election.

Mr Yari said the administration’s policies on agriculture, the economy, education, healthcare and social intervention programmes would form part of the APC’s campaign message ahead of the 2027 election.

He said the party would campaign on its record rather than promises, citing what he described as improvements in the exchange rate, foreign reserves and other economic indicators.

Mr Yari, a serving senator, also pledged support for Mr Tinubu across Northern Nigeria, saying the region was committed to securing the president’s re-election in 2027.

“Northern Nigeria is 101 per cent, by God’s grace, for you, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.

The Kaduna rally is part of the APC’s nationwide mobilisation ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

World.title: APC Rally: Tinubu speaks on second term ambition, promises prosperity, development
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu on Saturday sought Nigerians’ support for his re-election in 2027, promising sustained economic recovery, prosperity and development.

Mr Tinubu made the appeal on Saturday at the flag-off of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign in Kaduna.

He thanked Nigerians for electing him in 2023, saying a renewed mandate would enable his administration to sustain ongoing reforms and development projects.

The president blamed previous administrations for the hunger and poverty criticised by opposition parties, saying his government was working to address the challenges.

He cited regular salary payments, economic recovery and efforts to combat corruption and fuel smuggling as areas of his administration’s commitment.

Mr Tinubu urged eligible voters to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and participate in the 2027 general election.

Earlier, the Minister of Works, David Umahi, said the federal government had completed more than 348 kilometres of roads in the North-west, while 1,800 kilometres had been partially completed.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Umahi said ongoing federal road projects in the zone covered 4,083 kilometres, out of about 17,000 kilometres nationwide.

He highlighted the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano road project, saying 81 kilometres of its 118-kilometre first section would be commissioned at the ceremony.

According to him, the first section was completed in 13 months, while more than 144 kilometres of the 164-kilometre second section had been completed.

Mr Umahi said the remaining 20 kilometres of the second section were expected to be completed by the end of November.

He added that Mr Tinubu had directed the installation of solar streetlights along the 375-kilometre Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano corridor.

The minister commended the president for funding the projects and Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, for his efforts towards their completion.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that highlights of the occasion was the presentation of campaign flags to the seven APC governorship candidates in the North-west.

(NAN)

World.title: APC Rally: Tinubu has delivered on key promises to Kaduna, North –  Gov Sani
World.content:
Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, has urged voters in the North to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, stating that the president has delivered on key promises on infrastructure, security, education and human capital development.

Mr San stated this at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna on Saturday, where he highlighted projects and interventions he said had changed the fortunes of the state and the North since the administration came into office.

The governor said the president’s performance should be the basis for voters’ decision in the 2027 election, rather than regional considerations.

He recalled Mr Tinubu’s campaign visit to Birnin Gwari in Kaduna State on 22 December 2022, when the area was a major security flashpoint in the North-west.

According to Mr Sani, the president had promised during that visit to reconstruct the Kaduna-Birnin Gwari road and tackle insecurity along the corridor.

He said the federal government had since released N178 billion for the 123-kilometre road project, which he said was ongoing.

Mr Sani also claimed that the security situation had significantly improved, making it possible to travel to Birnin Gwari without police escort.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“When someone came to us and said we should support him simply because he is a northerner, we asked him: can you show us your track record?” the governor said.

“But at this moment, the so-called northern candidate, what is his track record? No track record.”

He challenged the opposition to show comparable infrastructure projects delivered during its time in government, particularly in the North.

M Sani also credited the Tinubu administration with reopening schools and primary healthcare centres previously shut because of insecurity.

He said eight local government areas in Kaduna had been affected by insecurity when his administration assumed office in 2023, with more than 300 schools and 150 primary healthcare centres shut.

“Today, I’m happy to inform you that all the schools and primary healthcare centres have reopened,” he said.

The governor also cited the Zaria-Funtua and Kaduna-Abuja-Kano road projects among the federal interventions in Kaduna and the North.

He said the federal government had committed N740 billion to the reconstruction of the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano road and that about 95 per cent of the project had been completed.

Mr Sani further said Kaduna was selected as the pilot state for a metropolitan rail project, with $865 million approved and $300 million reportedly released for the project.

Beyond infrastructure, the governor highlighted the federal government’s student loan and technical and vocational education and training (TVET) interventions.

He said the North-west had received N84 billion under the student loan programme, benefiting about 414,000 students, while 34,000 people in the region had benefited from the government’s TVET programme.

READ ALSO: Shettima banters with Fulani friends over refusal to enrol children in school

Mr Sani said these interventions were particularly significant in a region where agriculture remains a major part of the economy and where many young people require skills to improve their livelihoods.

He also cautioned APC supporters against what he described as opposition attempts to deploy Artificial Intelligence in the 2027 campaign.

“The opposition have now upgraded their campaign from Facebook and Twitter to AI,” he said, urging APC supporters to be vigilant.

The warning came as the APC Presidential Campaign Council separately accused former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) of allegedly planning to use manipulated images, fake documents and AI-generated content to discredit the Kaduna rally. The council did not provide evidence for all the allegations.

The APC campaign opened in Kaduna on Saturday, with Mr Tinubu, Vice President Kashim Shettima and other party leaders attending the rally as the ruling party begins its nationwide campaign for the 2027 presidential election.

World.title: Ronaldinho returns to football with Italian third tier
World.content:
File image

Brazil legend Ronaldinho will make his playing return aged 46 next month for Ravenna, the third-division Italian club announced on Saturday.

The 2002 World Cup winner’s move to Ravenna was announced in June.

He is aiming to score his 300th career goal.

The former Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona and AC Milan playmaker retired in 2015, 10 years on from claiming the Ballon d’Or and has become a shareholder in Ravenna, situated between Venice and San Marino.

“The wait now has a date: Sunday, November 15,” Ravenna said in a statement.

“The Brazilian legend will wear the Ravenna FC shirt in the derby against Forli.

“An event that will turn the eyes of the world toward the Bruno Benelli Stadium.”

Ravenna are second in Group B of the Italian third tier, six points below leaders Spezia and are aiming for a return to Serie B for the first time since 2008.

Vanguard News

World.title: Southampton end West Ham’s unbeaten run, Burnley sack manager
World.content:
Southampton ended West Ham’s nine-match unbeaten run with a 3-2 win at the London Stadium to surge into the Championship top six despite starting the season with a four-point deduction.

Saints began the campaign with the points penalty after spying on opposition training sessions, which also cost them the chance of promotion in the play-off final last season.

Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin all struck before half-time for the visitors, who are now within three points of the automatic promotion places.

Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers, but there were swathes of empty seats and boos by full-time as they missed the chance to go top.

“This is a tough place to come, against a quality team, and we knew we needed to start strongly, so we worked on that all week,” said Saints boss Tonda Eckert after his side went 2-0 up inside the opening 10 minutes.

“They made it tough for us in the second half, so it was important that we stayed brave to bring the result over the line.”

Burnley sacked manager Nicky Hayen after just 14 games in charge following his side’s 4-1 defeat at Lincoln, which left the Clarets in the relegation zone.

Relegated from the Premier League last season, former Club Brugge boss Hayen won just one of his 12 league matches in charge.

“Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect,” the club said in just a two-sentence statement.

“The board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season.”

Swansea’s missed the chance to retake top spot after they were thrashed 5-0 by QPR at Loftus Road.

Richard Kone scored a hat-trick inside the first 15 minutes before Jimmy Dunne’s double rounded off a remarkable scoreline that nudges Rangers into the play-off places.

Adam Armstrong scored the only goal as fourth-placed Wolves beat struggling Watford 1-0 to move within two points of the automatic promotion places.

AFP

World.title: Woman killed, two injured on Plateau farm
World.content:
By Golok Nanmwa, Jos

A woman has been killed, while two others sustained injuries while harvesting groundnuts on a farm at Gwom-Ajang, Foron District, in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State.

The incident occurred at about 4pm on Saturday, according to a member of the community, Silas Bitrus, who confirmed the incident to our correspondent.

Bitrus said, “The incident occurred around 4pm while they were harvesting groundnuts on the farm.”

He added, “A woman was killed, while two others sustained injuries.”

Also confirming the incident, the National Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders, BYM, Rwang Tengwong, condemned the attacks and urged security operatives to go after the attackers.

Also in a related development, the Coalition of Plateau State Indigenous Youth Bodies has alleged a plot by some groups to launch a counter-propaganda campaign against the Department of State Services, DSS, and other security agencies operating in the state.

In a statement made available to newsmen on Saturday and signed by Amb. Ezekiel Peter Bini, Chairman, Coalition of Indigenous Youth Nationalities, Plateau State; Dalyop Solomon Mwantiri, President, Berom Youth Moulder-Association; Amb. Miri Timnan Nyantau, President, Tarok Progressive Youths Association; and Mr Jonathan Kyesmang Yusuf, President, Mwaghavul Youths Movement, the coalition said, “Following our World Press Conference held at the Nigerian Union of Journalists Secretariat in Abuja on 21st October, 2026, the Coalition has received information of a plan to launch an aggressive counter-propaganda campaign.”

The group said, “According to reliable sources, some groups are planning to stage a World Press Conference to portray the joint operations of the Department of State Services (DSS), the Mobile Police Force, and Operation Rainbow as discriminatory against a section of the population.”

The coalition further said, “The propaganda being launched must not be accepted as truth without independent verification.”

“We challenge anyone concerned about human rights and freedom to demand evidence and allow the appropriate authorities to establish the facts.”

The group added, “We stand firmly with the DSS, Mobile Police and Operation Rainbow and other security operatives.”

“We will not be distracted by propaganda, nor shall we retreat because of terror. Plateau is our heritage and must remain safe for all law-abiding citizens.”

World.title: EPL: De Zerbi hails ‘complete’ Spurs after historic win at Chelsea
World.content:
Tottenham Hotspur’s Italian head coach Roberto De Zerbi arrives for the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge in London on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP)

Roberto De Zerbi said Tottenham’s historic 2-0 victory against London rivals Chelsea proved his side have a winning mentality as they banished their dismal start to the season.

Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League for just the second time in 36 years and the first since 2018.

Trips across the capital to west London have largely been fruitless experiences for Tottenham over the last four decades.

But De Zerbi’s men enjoyed a memorable visit to the Bridge on Saturday thanks to a comical own goal from Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders and a late wonder-goal from Mathys Tel after Blues star Cole Palmer was sent off.

“It was a big moment for the fans, the club and the players also. They deserved this win, they prepared very well,” De Zerbi said.

“We are improving a lot, we are improving in the mentality, in the group and the relationships with the players and then we are improving on the pitch.”

Tottenham started the season on a dismal run of six league games without a win, raising the spectre of another relegation battle after they narrowly avoided dropping into the Championship on the final day of last season.

With the pressure mounting on De Zerbi, the Italian has drawn his players closer together thanks to meals together and a trip to Marbella.

– ‘The spirit, the belief’ –

A win against promoted Coventry on Monday lifted the tension around the north London club and vanquishing Chelsea was another reward for De Zerbi’s team-building ethos.

“Now it is a complete team. When we stay for dinner and stay together in the dressing room I see a different group, a different relationship and different atmosphere among the players,” he said.

“The character was today great but we have many, many new players. The players who stayed here last season, two or three seasons ago, they suffered the last results, two times 17th position, we are working to change the last part of the history of the club.”

Tottenham were beginning to lose the faith of their long-suffering fans after another miserable start to the season.

But De Zerbi was adamant he never doubted they would get back on track.

“I have to believe for sure in this group. I never lost the confidence in my players,” he said.

“The week in Marbella, to speak better face to face, to open ourselves and remove the mask it is important.

“It is important for the spirit, the belief. The atmosphere inside the dressing room is maybe more important than the tactics.”

For Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso, it was a painful setback as the optimism engendered by successive victories over Bournemouth and Everton was washed away on a rain-lashed evening.

Alonso’s expensively assembled team sit in fourth place but remain very much a work in progress after the third league loss of his first season in charge.

“We are all disappointed with the result, with the performance collectively and individually we were not at our best level,” he said.

“It was about the first goal and it went their way and with 10 men it was difficult but we can do better.”

Alonso refused to blame Penders and Palmer for their roles in the defeat.

“We feel for everyone, it is a team thing, a collective. We have to move on,” he said before adding he “hadn’t seen” Palmer’s two bookings.

World.title: 2027: Northern power brokers, Emirs, Imams behind Tinubu, Yari assures
World.content:
Yari

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: Director General of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC, Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, has assured President Bola Tinubu that the power brokers of Northern Nigeria, traditional rulers and Islamic clerics are solidly behind his return to office in 2027.

He spoke at the flag-off of the party’s presidential campaign in Kaduna, in the presence of the President and all the governors of Northern Nigeria.

“We have been engaging all and sundry, our traditional rulers, our ulama and our imams, to understand the importance of your return in 2027 for continuity, for the peace of this country and for Nigeria,” Yari said.

He told the President that the northern establishment had turned out in full.

“We believe in you, and those people believe in us. All the shakers and movers of this part of the country are here. In the northern part of the country, anybody who is not here today, Mr President, then there is nobody there. We are here.

“By God’s grace, Your Excellency, Mr President, we resolve, by God’s grace, that as far as Northern Nigeria is concerned, Mr President, I need your ears. Mr President, I want you to listen to us carefully. Northern Nigeria is 101 per cent for you, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, by God’s grace, Insha Allah. And the promise we have made, you are going to see it on January 16, 2027,” Yari said.

Yari described Kaduna as “the spiritual centre of politics in Northern Nigeria”, adding that the venue had drawn “all the governors of Northern Nigeria”.

On the economy, he said the President’s reforms had changed the country’s fortunes. “If we talk about the economy, we know the state of the economy when you stepped into the leadership of this country. Today, the total indices have changed completely to the advantage of Nigeria and other countries of the world.

“Mr President, I can enumerate at least a few: from the exchange rate, to the subsidy removal and many more,” Yari added.

The APC-PCC boss said the party would take its case to voters on the strength of the administration’s achievements.

“We Nigerians, at the head of this campaign, are going to campaign with our records. Our records are there. The infrastructure is there. What you did in health, education and human capital development is there. The students are there. The transparent cash and conditional cash transfers are also there for men and women,” he said.

Turning to the 2023 election, Yari said: “I would like to be a student again, to be told how you did it, because we want the country.”

He said the party was committed to justice and urged the President to listen closely to the North’s message.

World.title: Nigeria, South Korea seek stronger trade, technology partnerships
World.content:
By Favour Ulebor, Abuja

Nigeria and South Korea have called for stronger bilateral cooperation in trade, investment, technology transfer, agriculture and skills development to promote economic growth and create opportunities for their citizens.

The two countries renewed the call at a reception to mark South Korea’s National Day in Abuja on Friday, with both sides expressing commitment to expanding their longstanding diplomatic relations.

Speaking at the event, South Korea’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Jeong Yoan, said the two countries, which established diplomatic relations in 1980, had opportunities to deepen economic cooperation through partnerships that support local businesses, entrepreneurship and human capital development.

Jeong said South Korea was willing to share its development experience with Nigeria while respecting the country’s priorities and working with it as an equal partner.

He recalled that South Korea’s economy was devastated by the Korean War, with its annual per capita income below $100 in 1953, but said investment in education, hard work and international cooperation had helped the country rebuild.

The ambassador said the experience demonstrated the importance of investing in people, developing local industries and sustaining partnerships that deliver long-term benefits.

Highlighting ongoing cooperation, he said the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), in partnership with Nigeria’s Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency (SMEDAN) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), broke ground on an entrepreneurship centre in Abuja in September.

According to him, the centre is expected to support young entrepreneurs and start-ups by helping them develop business ideas and build sustainable enterprises.

He also said South Korea’s Smart School project, implemented in collaboration with the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC), had reached about 8,000 children and provided training for more than 300 teachers and school leaders.

Jeong added that KOICA and the Food and Agriculture Organisation were collaborating on an initiative to create green jobs for young Nigerians through agriculture.

He said about 2,000 Nigerian officials had also received training in South Korea through KOICA programmes, describing capacity development as a key component of the bilateral relationship.

On private sector cooperation, the ambassador identified opportunities for Korean companies to expand their engagement with Nigerian businesses in energy, manufacturing, clean water and digital technology.

He listed Daewoo E&C, LG, Samsung, Hyundai and Solpia among Korean companies working with Nigerian partners, adding that the South Korean Embassy and the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) would continue to promote investment, technology sharing and local employment.

Beyond economic and technical cooperation, Jeong highlighted the growing cultural relationship between the two countries, noting that Korean pop music, television dramas, films and beauty products had gained popularity among Nigerians.

He said South Koreans had also shown interest in Nigeria’s Afrobeats music and Nollywood films, describing cultural exchanges as an important way of bringing the people of both countries closer.

The ambassador said the theme of the celebration, “One Heaven. One Earth. One Humanity,” reflected the importance of peace, human dignity, mutual respect and international cooperation.

He explained that South Korea’s National Foundation Day, known as Gaecheonjeol, is celebrated on October 3 and commemorates the country’s traditional founding story associated with Dangun and the principle of Hongik Ingan, commonly interpreted as “to benefit all humanity.”

In her remarks, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, represented by the Chief of Protocol of the Ministry, Ambassador Babagana Wakil, commended South Korea’s achievements in technology, engineering, manufacturing and social development.

She called for stronger cooperation in agriculture, industrial manufacturing, automobile assembly, shipbuilding and technology transfer, noting that closer collaboration could support Nigeria’s development priorities.

The minister also identified education, digital technology, scholarships, technical training, academic exchanges and research as areas for expanded partnership between the two countries.

She stressed the need to strengthen maritime cooperation in areas including maritime safety, transportation, fisheries and technical capacity development.

Odumegwu-Ojukwu further called for renewed engagement under the Nigeria-South Korea Joint Commission framework to identify practical measures for increasing bilateral trade and investment.

She said closer cooperation would enable both countries to address shared development challenges while creating more opportunities for their businesses and citizens.

The reception featured a Taekwondo performance and Korean cuisine, showcasing aspects of South Korea’s cultural heritage.

The event underscored the commitment of both countries to building on more than four decades of diplomatic relations through stronger economic partnerships, capacity development and cultural exchanges.

World.title: Kaduna rally: Atiku challenges Tinubu over hunger, hardship
World.content:
Atiku Abubakar

By Luminous Jannamike

Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress, ADC, presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to explain what his administration has done to end hunger and poverty, following the President’s claim that the opposition created the problems.

Atiku said Nigerians were more concerned about the government’s record than its attempts to shift responsibility, insisting that the 2027 presidential election would put Tinubu’s handling of the economy and security under scrutiny.

In a statement on Saturday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku accused the President of blaming his political opponents for hardship that had worsened under his watch.

“Mr President, blaming the opposition for hunger is either delusion or a staggering case of political amnesia. The APC governed Nigeria for eight years before you took office. You have added another three and a half years. Nigerians know who has been in power, and hardship did not begin when the opposition started talking about it. Stop insulting their intelligence and answer for your record,” Atiku said.

On the economy, the ADC candidate challenged Tinubu to account for the consequences of petrol subsidy removal, the naira’s depreciation and rising poverty.

“Which administration removed the petrol subsidy and watched the naira fall from about ₦471 to ₦1,329 to the dollar?” he asked.

Atiku also questioned the government’s handling of public finances and the country’s poverty levels.

“Which administration has presided over a rise in poverty that led the World Bank to estimate that 63 per cent of Nigerians will be below the national poverty line in 2026? Which administration extended the 2024 budget into 2025 while also operating a separate 2025 budget?” he asked.

He further demanded explanations for what he described as questionable public spending, citing energy security expenditure, NNPC pipeline-related spending and charges associated with an Abu Dhabi financing facility.

“Which administration recorded ₦7.13 trillion under ‘energy security’ in 2024 and faces questions over ₦11.2 trillion in NNPC pipeline related spending? Nigerians deserve to know who received these sums and what was delivered,” Atiku said.

He also questioned the country’s external accounts and the charges associated with the financing facility.

“Which administration must explain the $12.4 billion gap flagged in Nigeria’s external accounts for the first half of 2026? Which administration paid $22.5 million in ‘other charges’ on the Abu Dhabi financing facility?” he asked.

On security, Atiku faulted the administration over persistent killings, kidnappings and displacement, demanding answers from the government.

“Which administration is responsible for the killings, kidnappings and displacement that continue to terrorise communities? These are the questions Nigerians are asking while your government blames the opposition,” he said.

Atiku also criticised Tinubu’s commissioning of the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway from inside a stadium, arguing that the ceremony did not establish that the project had been completed.

“Your decision to commission the unfinished Abuja to Kaduna Expressway from inside a stadium shows how far removed you are from the daily reality of Nigerians. A road cannot be completed with a speech or a ribbon-cutting ceremony,” he said.

Returning to the central issue, Atiku said the government could not avoid accountability by blaming political opponents for describing the hardship Nigerians were experiencing.

“You cannot govern for three years, make life harder, and then blame others for describing the hardship. You asked who created the hunger. Nigerians are asking what you have done to end it,” he said.

He said the 2027 presidential election would test Tinubu’s record against the experiences of Nigerians.

“The people will judge your government by the lives they are living, not by the excuses you offer at campaign rallies.

“The 2027 presidential election will be a referendum on your record. Nigerians have felt the cost of your leadership in their homes, markets and communities. Their verdict is already clear: they have rejected your administration,” he added.

World.title: Ex-envoy faults Ortom’s use of words, remarks on Alia, governance in Benue
World.content:
Tarzoor

By Peter Duru, Makurdi

Former Speaker of the Benue State House of Assembly and Nigeria’s former Ambassador to Namibia, Terhemen Tarzoor, has faulted former Governor Samuel Ortom over his reported remarks against Governor Hyacinth Alia and his administration urging political leaders to exercise restraint in their public engagements.

Tarzoor, who spoke with newsmen in Makurdi, described some of Chief Ortom’s comments during a recent television programme as inappropriate, arguing that political differences should not undermine the dignity of the office of the governor or the people of the state.

The former lawmaker, who is also the Benue State coordinator of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors for President Bola Tinubu 2027, said Ortom whom he described as an elder brother he respects, should be more measured in his public statements about the incumbent governor.

“My take is that the former governor should not call the number one citizen 419. He has no right to call him that,” Tarzoor said, reacting to Ortom’s alleged description of Alia as a “419” and a “fake Reverend Father.”

He also faulted Ortom’s reported comparison of the administration of Benue State to a Catholic parish, where priests allegedly collect offerings and spend the money without being questioned, Tarzoor, a Knight of St. John International, defended the Church’s financial management system, insisting that it operates established structures for accountability.

“As a Knight of St. John International, I want to disabuse his mind and the minds of people who listened to that programme that there is a high level of accountability in the Catholic Church,” he said.

“There is no Catholic priest that can just earn money and spend at ease in the Catholic Church,” he said, adding that political leaders should avoid statements that could be interpreted as questioning the integrity of religious institutions without sufficient knowledge of their operations.

Tarzoor also criticised what he described as an unfair comparison between Ortom’s eight-year administration and Alia’s government, which has been in office for just over three years. He argued that any meaningful assessment of their performances must take into account the period each administration has spent in office and the targets set for them.

“In comparative statistics, you talk about time-frame equality and goal equality before you can compare and contrast,” he said.

The former Speaker further expressed concern over Ortom’s reported reference to some Benue people as “shenanigans,” describing the expression as inappropriate.

“I see that as repugnant. If he has issues, he should apply the right language, apply decorum in the manner to address matters. That is the only legacy we can leave for our children, those yet unborn,” he said.

On the issue of former governors’ entitlements, Tarzoor said he was unaware of any law providing for the benefits Ortom reportedly claimed were denied him, including a house in Abuja or elsewhere in the country and sponsorship of medical check-ups.

“When I was Speaker, we never had such a law anywhere,” he said, while acknowledging that he could not speak definitively on whether such legislation had been enacted after he left office. “Any legitimate concerns over entitlements could be addressed through appropriate channels rather than public exchanges,” he said.

The former Ambassador maintained that the Alia administration was open to scrutiny, urging the media and members of the public to seek accurate information on government revenue and expenditure through established procedures, including the Freedom of Information framework.

“Governor Hyacinth Alia is open to all criticisms. The law is clear on freedom of information. You test it; the records will be there for you to see,” he said, urging political leaders to promote constructive engagement and accountability.

World.title: PSN Advocates Collaboration of Specialised Professionals for Stronger Pharmacy Practice In Nigeria
World.content:
The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) has urged collaboration of specialised branches of the profession to strengthen pharmacy practice in the country.

Speaking ahead of the society’s 99th Annual National Conference scheduled to hold from November 1st – 7th, 2026 at the International Conference Centre, Awka, Anambra State, PSN President, Pharm. Ayuba Ibrahim Tanko, noted that strengthening pharmacy practice in the country would require advanced practice, clinical collaboration, residency training, education, and the contributions of research pharmacists in pharmacotherapy, medication safety, pharmaceutical preparation and the appropriate use of medicines.

He said that translation of such professional expertise will bring about stronger patient-care services, appropriate competency development, structured practice-based training and effective collaboration with other healthcare professionals.

Tanko recognised the existence of the foundation on which the initiatives can be achieved. According to him, these include the “recognition of the Consultant Pharmacist cadre which creates an opportunity to clarify advanced practice responsibilities.’’

He also identified the PSN –West African Society of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (WASPEN) collaboration which offers opportunities for pharmacists to contribute to multidisciplinary nutrition care and specialized pharmaceutical services; as well as the West African Postgraduate College of Pharmacists (WAPCP) – Delta State University Teaching Hospital (DELSUTH) International Pharmacy Practice Residency Programme (IPPR)) which provides practical basis for strengthening supervised postgraduate training, while education, mentorship and research can support development across all these areas.

Bringing these initiatives into a common strategic discussion, Tanko posited, “can help align professional priorities without merging them into a single programme or disregarding their existing governance arrangements.’’

He explained that the Consultant Pharmacist cadre has been recognised within the Federal and State public-service scheme of service. According to him, consistent implementation requires greater clarity regarding the role, competencies, responsibilities, professional development expectations and accountability of Consultant Pharmacists.

‘’A standardised framework could support more consistent appointments, improve workforce planning and strengthen the integration of advanced pharmacists into multidisciplinary clinical teams.’’ Adding that “defining the role, scope of responsibilities, reporting relationships and expected contribution to patient care and healthcare services’’ should be given due attention.

He stressed the importance of ‘’establishing a competency and qualification framework covering advanced clinical practice, leadership, education, research and service development. Clarifying contributions to complex medication-related decisions, therapeutic optimisation, medication safety and coordinated patient care, and defining responsibilities for clinical service development, mentorship, professional education, quality improvement and performance evaluation.’’

Tanko advised said that the framework should draw on relevant international models while reflecting Nigeria’s healthcare system, regulatory environment and workforce needs saying, “any proposed clinical authority or prescribing responsibilities must remain consistent with applicable Nigerian laws and regulations.’’

Explaining the PSN–WASPEN collaboration and the emerging practice opportunities for pharmacists in the country, he said the initiative provides an opportunity to strengthen multidisciplinary nutrition care and identify appropriate roles for pharmacists in clinical nutrition and specialised pharmaceutical services.

Tanko identified areas that offer particular opportunities for professional development and service improvement including identifying and managing medication-related problems that may affect nutritional status, treatment response and recovery, and supporting the safe use of medicines in patients receiving enteral or parenteral nutrition, including compatibility, administration and monitoring considerations, contributing nutrition support protocols, medication safety systems, clinical monitoring and quality improvement.

He also highlighted sterile compounding and specialised pharmaceutical services which the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) is involved in. According to him, PSN in collaboration with relevant partners has advanced initiatives to strengthen local pharmaceutical compounding and manufacturing, beginning with non-sterile preparations. Tanko also said that the WASPEN – Pharmaceutical industry collaboration represents the second phase of this broader compounding initiative, focusing on sterile compounding and specialised pharmaceutical services, particularly the safe preparation of parenteral nutrition.

The PSN president listed the benefits to the Nigerian health system including training and competency development in aseptic technique, sterile compounding and clean room practice, developing and implementing quality systems, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and risk-management processes.

It would also be supporting the safe preparation of parenteral nutrition in collaboration with the wider nutrition support team, exploring centralised admixture services where feasible, appropriately governed and sustainable, as well as promoting technical education, clinical attachments, research and the appropriate introduction of compounding technologies.

The collaboration, he added, can also support joint workshops, webinars, conferences, mentorship and clinical attachments. Any new service should be assessed against local needs, regulatory requirements, staffing, infrastructure and sustainable financing.

On the International Pharmacy Practice Residency Programme (IPPR), he explained that it was launched at Delta State University Teaching Hospital (DELSUTH), Oghara, in May 2022 through the West African Postgraduate College of Pharmacists (WAPCP), in collaboration with DELSUTH and with engagement involving the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists (ASHP). The programme, he said, provides an opportunity to strengthen the practice-based component of postgraduate pharmacy training by connecting theoretical learning with supervised clinical experience. Its development also offers lessons for residency programme leadership, preceptor preparation, competency assessment and service improvement.

The IPPR, he further explained, would focus on strengthening learning objectives, competency assessment and structured clinical experiences., supporting preceptor development, mentorship and consistent resident feedback, and integrating multidisciplinary patient care, medication safety, quality improvement and research.

“The IPPR should complement existing WAPCP postgraduate training and residency pathways rather than be presented as evidence that traditional training lacks practical value. Decisions about expansion should be guided by documented experience, programme readiness, available preceptors, service capacity and applicable accreditation requirements. The DELSUTH programme is under ASHP review following an accreditation survey, with a decision expected by March 2027,’’ he said.

Tanko said, “to advance this initiative, inputs were obtained from relevant stakeholders, including the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, PCN, PSN, WASPEN, WAPCP, the Association of Consultant Pharmacists, the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), healthcare institutions and academic partners. Adding that a decision to identify which areas require immediate attention and which need further consultation or technical development remains salient in view of the goals and objectives of the initiative.’’

World.title: Device Checker Will Enhance Protection of Customers, Quality of Service, Says NCC
World.content:
Oghenevwede Ohwovoriole in Abuja

The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), has assured Nigerians that the Commission’s device checker policy is to enhance consumers safety and the to guarantee quality service delivery.

The Director Technical Standard and Network Integrity, Edoyemi Ogoh made the clarity at the sensitisation programme on key issues in the telecommunications industry and the country’s digital space. Organised by the Commission on Tuesday in Abuja.

The engagement is designed to provide media stakeholders with insights into the Commission’s regulatory initiatives, industry developments, and matters of interest to stakeholders across the telecommunications industry.

Edoyemi Ogoh stated that the integrity of the telecom industry does not depend solely on infrastructure.

“The integrity of the telecommunications industry depends not only on the network infrastructure but also on the quality, safety and compliance of the devices that are assessed and used on these networks. For this reason, type approval is not merely a regulatory requirement, it is a vital mechanism for protecting consumers, safeguarding performance and preserving confidence in Nigeria’s digital economy.

“The Commission has statutory responsibility to ensure that communications equipment deployed within Nigeria meets established standards.” he added

According to him the Commission derived the powers to type as approve telecommunication devices from the Nigerian Communications Act. 2003. “This obligation is reflected in the requirements governing the certification and approval of communication devices intended for use within the country. Under Section 132 Subsection 2 of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003, licenced service providers, facilities providers, equipment manufacturers and suppliers are required to obtain type approval from the Commission before communication equipment may be sold or used in Nigeria. The purpose of this regulatory instrument or requirement is straightforward

“Devices operating on Nigerian networks must meet established technical standards and comply with applicable regulatory requirements. This helps to ensure compatibility with network infrastructure, protect users, improve service quality and strengthen trust in the communications ecosystem.

“We have also ensured that devices currently in stock are appropriately onboarded and that devices imported into Nigeria going forward are properly verified and authenticated. This will provide a more effective mechanism for identifying non-compliant, cloned or fake devices and prevent them from connecting to our networks. Every consumer deserves confidence that the Commission’s devices being purchased and used meet required standards.

He also noted that the implementation of the policy will guarantee consumers confidence on telecom devices in Nigeria “Consumers should not have to worry about whether a device is technically compliant, whether it poses avoidable security risks or whether it may negatively affect their experience on telecommunications networks. By strengthening the type of overall compliance, the Commission helps address these concerns. The implementation creates an environment in which consumers can have greater confidence in the devices available within the Nigerian marketplace.

On the safety of consumers personal data, he said, “it maintains device identification information including IMEI numbers for regulatory purposes. It does not provide the Commission with access to the content of users’ devices nor does it enable the Commission to monitor personal communications. The objective of the initiative is regulatory compliance relating to communications devices strictly.

“It is not a surveillance tool and does not provide access to personal information stored on those devices.

The Head Corporate communications NCC, Olawaiye Olasumbo in her remarks called for the continued support of the media and other stakeholders in creating awareness on the initiative. “We encourage your continued supports in creating public awareness about this initiative.”

World.title: Bishop Akunna Mourns Victims of Ogoja Food Empowerment Stampede
World.content:
The Bishop of Ogoja Diocese, Anglican Communion, The Rt. Rev’d Ifeanyi Akunna, has commiserated with the family of one woman who was reportedly trampled to death on Thursday in a stampede triggered by a food distribution programme organised by the Cross River State government.

In a statement he personally signed, Bishop Akunna, said he was “deeply saddened” by the “distressing news of the tragic loss of lives and injuries sustained during the empowerment distribution in Ogoja.

“On behalf of the Anglican Diocese of Ogoja, we extend our heartfelt condolences to the families who lost their beloved ones in this unfortunate incident. No words can adequately express the pain of losing a loved one, especially under circumstances that could have been avoided,” stated the Bishop.

He continued, “Our hearts go out to the bereaved families, and we pray that the Holy Spirit, our Divine Comforter, will console, strengthen and uphold them in this difficult moment,” stressing, “May the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.”

The Bishop equally commiserated with the Government and people of Cross River State, stressing,”it is indeed heartbreaking that an initiative intended to bring relief, hope and assistance to the good people of Ogoja ended in sorrow, mourning and the needless loss of innocent lives.

“What was meant to be a gesture of goodwill and compassion has sadly turned into an occasion of grief,” he regretted.

“While we sincerely commend the Cross River State Government for its various empowerment and welfare initiatives, we also appeal that appropriate measures be taken to ensure that such a tragedy never re-occurs” urged the Bishop.

“The distribution of relief materials and other public welfare interventions must be properly coordinated, with adequate security arrangements, crowd-control measures and respect for the dignity and safety of every human life.”

He appreciated Governor Bassey Otu’s “commitment to bearing the medical expenses of those currently receiving treatment in the hospital,” adding that, “this compassionate gesture is commendable and should be sustained until the victims have fully recovered.”

Bishop Akunna commended the timely intervention of the Nigerian military and the Police, saying the move “brought the situation under control and prevented further casualties.”

World.title: Shettima: Tinubu’s Reforms More About Improving Quality Of Life of Nigerians
World.content:
.Inaugurates ultra-modern teaching hospital, schools in Borno

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

Vice President Kashim Shettima has said President Bola Tinubu’s reform agenda places strong emphasis on building enduring institutions, developing human capital and improving the quality of life of Nigerians.

He stressed why sustainable development must outlive the tenure of political officeholders, maintaining that the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Tinubu is designed to ensure that economic reforms deliver lasting social benefits, with investments in essential public services.

Shettima stated this yesterday while inaugurating the ultra-modern Kashim Ibrahim University Teaching Hospital (KIUTH) and two schools in Maiduguri, the Borno State capital.

He described investments in healthcare and education as essential to economic productivity, national development and the recovery of communities affected by insecurity.

The Vice President stated that true measure of public service lies not in the privileges of office but in the institutions established and the opportunities created for future generations.

According to him, “Someday, and that day is nearer than we imagine, we shall be judged by what survives our time in office. The offices we held, the aides who surrounded us and the length of our convoys will have surrendered their importance. What will endure are the institutions we built, the roads we constructed and the lives made better because we served.”

Commending Borno State Governor, Prof. Babagana Umara Zulum, for prioritising healthcare and education, Shettima said the newly inaugurated facilities demonstrate how purposeful investments can translate into practical benefits for citizens.

He noted that the teaching hospital would bring specialised healthcare closer to communities, reduce the burden of travelling outside the state for treatment and strengthen medical training and research.

“For a family already burdened by illness, the cost and anxiety of travelling outside the state can compound their suffering. This hospital offers the prospect of expert attention nearer home,” he said.

On education, the Vice President observed that rebuilding schools in communities affected by insurgency was fundamental to restoring hope, expanding opportunities and preparing the next generation for productive participation in the economy.

“In a state whose communities have endured the disruption of insurgency, a classroom carries a particular significance. It restores the expectation that tomorrow can be planned for,” Shettima stated.

Drawing from his experience as a former Governor of Borno State, the Vice President acknowledged the challenges of delivering development amid insecurity and praised Governor Zulum’s determination to sustain investment in critical public infrastructure.

“To improve lives and livelihoods in a state that has withstood such a climate of insecurity demands uncommon fortitude. I know the weight of that responsibility. As the street language goes, I have been there and done that,” he said.

Shettima conveyed President Tinubu’s felicitations to the government and people of Borno State, and reaffirmed the federal government’s commitment to supporting the state’s reconstruction, peacebuilding and human capital development efforts.

“Our investment in human capital proceeds from the conviction that a healthier, better educated population can produce more, earn more and contribute more. The federal government will continue to support Borno’s efforts to consolidate peace, rebuild communities and expand opportunities for its people,” he said.

The Vice President noted that Borno’s reconstruction experience offers valuable lessons in rebuilding communities emerging from conflict, particularly through the restoration of essential public institutions.

He commended the state government, healthcare professionals, educators, contractors, development partners and security personnel for their contributions to the projects.

Shettima, however, stressed that the success of the facilities would ultimately depend on their ability to deliver quality services to the people.

“The responsibility now is to keep these institutions worthy of that faith. Their value will be measured in the care patients receive and the education children acquire,” he said.

Earlier, Governor Zulum said the teaching hospital stood as one of the most tangible expressions of his administration’s commitment to providing state-of-the-art healthcare facilities for the people of Borno State.

He explained that the teaching hospital was not merely another building but a centre of learning, a provider of specialised healthcare services and a facility that would bring hope to millions of people across the North-east.

The governor said the facility would serve as a clinical training centre for the College of Health Sciences of Kashim Ibrahim University, providing training for medical students, resident doctors, nurses, midwives, pharmacists, medical laboratory scientists, physiotherapists and other healthcare professionals.

Zulum assured that the Borno State Government would continue to invest in the Kashim Ibrahim University Teaching Hospital, saying, “We have recruited and we will continue to recruit qualified healthcare professionals. We will provide equipment, utility infrastructure and an enabling environment for the hospital to function at the highest standard.”

Also, the Pro-Chancellor of Kashim Ibrahim University, Alhaji Mohammed Indimi, said the inauguration of the teaching hospital represented a remarkable achievement and a milestone in the collective commitment to providing quality healthcare services, medical education, research and professional training.

He expressed optimism that the hospital would strengthen healthcare delivery in Borno State and contribute meaningfully to the well-being of people across the North-east.

On his part, Chairman of the Governing Board of Kashim Ibrahim University Teaching Hospital, Prof. Ahmed Ahidjo, described the hospital as a landmark project of unprecedented significance in the state.

He commended Vice President Shettima for choosing Governor Zulum as his successor and applauded the governor for his bold decision to establish the teaching hospital and equip it with modern, state-of-the-art medical facilities.

Also speaking, Chief Medical Director of Kashim Ibrahim University Teaching Hospital, Prof. Ibrahim Musa Kida, said the greatness of the hospital would be determined not merely by its buildings and equipment but by the quality of its personnel and the dedication of its staff.

He also commended Shettima for his contributions to the progress and development of Borno State and Nigeria, particularly his continued commitment to peace and development in the state.

World.title: WAP TV Receives Multiple Awards in October
World.content:
Sunday Okobi

WapTV, The Family Entertainment Channel, has stated that it has many reasons to celebrate in October, 2026, from its 14th year anniversary to the awards bestowed on the TV channel.

From October 1, 2012, when it stated broadcasting to October 1, 2026, WapTV has celebrated 14 years of non-stop transmission of quality programming to the entire family.

On October 10, WapTV received Best Kiddies/Youth Programme of the Year Award presented to Nnennaand Friends show by 7th Nigerian Broadcasters Merit Award (NBMA) 2026, an award ceremony organized by the prestigious Independent Broadcasters Association of Nigeria (IBAN).

The entertainment channel also received the Voice of Inclusion Award presented by Down Syndrome Foundation of Nigeria on October 16, for WapTV’s dedication to creating awareness of the resourcefulness and astounding characteristics of people living with Down Syndrome.

To crown up the awards season, on October 19, WapTV was presented with a plaque for Outstanding Family Entertainment Media Brand of the Decade by the Edge Awards 2026.

While eulogizing its audience for the accolades, the Director of WapTV, Wale Adenuga Junior, at an event yesterday said: “We are truly grateful to all the advertisers, viewers, management and staff of WapTV who have continued to believe in, and stayed with us for 14 years.

“We implore everyone of them to continue to spread the word about how WapTV has been relentless in broadcasting exciting, entertaining and educative content over the years. The best part is we have just begun.”

WapTV boasts of millions of viewers who watch thechannel on Satellite TV, as well as over 800,000 Subscribers on its YouTube Channel ‘waptvchannel’ which has over 300,000,000 views and counting.

The 24-hour Family Entertainment Channel broadcasts across Nigeria and several African countries on a network of DStv 262, StarTimes 116, GOtv 129 andFreeTV 751.

World.title: NDC Lawyers Demand Probe of INEC Official Over Multiple Inconsistent Reports in Kano
World.content:
Ahmad Sorondinki in Kano

Lawyers to the Kano State chapter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) have petitioned the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to investigate the Head of Department, Election and Party Monitoring in Kano, Mrs. Hauwa Buhari, over alleged issuance of multiple inconsistent monitoring reports on the party’s primary elections.

The demand was contained in a press statement dated 19th October, 2026 and signed by Magaji Mato Ibrahim, SAN, I.M. Abdullahi, Siraj Hamza and two other lawyers, on behalf of the NDC Kano chapter.

The lawyers were responding to a public statement issued on 17th October by Bola Aidi, SAN & Co., solicitors to five persons claiming candidature under the NDC in Kano, who had described the petition against the INEC official as political intimidation.

According to the NDC legal team, the petition dated 16th October was issued on the clear instructions of the NDC Kano State chapter and the claims that the leadership was unaware of it are incorrect and unsupported by any documentary evidence.

On the substance of the petition, the lawyers said it complains of an objective documentary problem – the issuance by the same INEC officer of multiple signed versions of a monitoring report on the NDC Kano primary elections.

“The versions are materially inconsistent in content, some are undated, and they list persons who were not screened, cleared or nominated by the party while excluding authentic candidates whose names appear on Form EC9D signed by the National Chairman and National Secretary,” the statement said.

The lawyers added that the officer is said to have previously admitted lacunas in the report and a corrected version was reportedly forwarded to INEC headquarters without formal communication or implementation.

They also accused the five persons claiming candidature of filing suits at the Federal High Court without notice to the authentic candidates of the party, describing it as a violation of fair hearing principles which require that all interested parties must be joined at the commencement of pre-election matters.

The statement described as curious and unusual, the decision of private solicitors to candidates to mount a public defence of an INEC officer.

“Mrs. Hauwa Buhari is an officer of a constitutional body that has the institutional capacity, legal representation and statutory duty to defend its staff and its records,” the lawyers noted.

They further argued that a monitoring report cannot create a candidacy where the party’s own preconditions for participation were not met, nor can it override the official submission under section 29 of the Electoral Act, 2026.

The legal team called on the INEC Chairman to cause an immediate investigation into the circumstances surrounding the issuance of the reports, withdraw all defective versions and issue one authentic, properly dated report that reflects the true candidates nominated by the party.

World.title: Sokoto Residents Challenge ADC Candidate Dan’iya to Present Development Blueprint
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

Concerned residents of Sokoto State have challenged the governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, to move beyond criticism of Governor Ahmed Aliyu Sokoto’s administration and unveil a clear and achievable development agenda ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
