In a statement jointly signed by Comrade Ibrahim Umar Kware, Comrade Aminu Hali Tambuwal and Comrade Bello Arzika Dandange, on behalf of the group, the residents said the people of the state deserve more than political attacks from those seeking their mandate.

According to the group, the 2027 election should be defined by competing ideas, credible alternatives and concrete solutions to the challenges facing the state, rather than a campaign built solely on fault-finding and condemnation of government policies.

The residents observed that since his emergence as the ADC governorship candidate, Dan’iya has consistently criticised the policies and programmes of the present administration without presenting a comprehensive policy document detailing what he would do differently.

“Enough of criticism. Sokoto people want to know what you intend to do for them. What is your development agenda and how do you intend to deliver on your promises? It is not enough to criticise the government without providing workable alternatives,” the statement said.

They argued that aspiring to govern a state of over five million people requires thorough preparation, clear vision and a sound understanding of public administration, including realistic funding strategies, implementation timelines and measurable performance indicators.

The group further urged Dan’iya to reflect on his tenure as Deputy Governor under former Governor Aminu Waziri Tambuwal and share the lessons learnt, cautioning him against what they described as the shortcomings of his political mentor whom they accused of assuming office without adequate preparation.

While emphasising the need for accountability on the part of the incumbent administration, the residents acknowledged Governor Ahmed Aliyu’s interventions in security logistics, road construction and rehabilitation, housing and primary healthcare revitalisation as efforts that merit objective assessment.

They noted that the provision of operational vehicles, motorcycles and other security equipment to security agencies has enhanced response capacity in parts of the state, even as they admitted that insecurity remains a challenge requiring sustained action.

According to the concerned residents, while the present government must be judged on its performance, the opposition has an equal responsibility to demonstrate superior capacity and offer better alternatives rather than expecting voters to be swayed by criticism alone.

They therefore challenged the ADC candidate to publicly present his specific plans for strengthening security in vulnerable communities, supporting farmers and small businesses, tackling youth unemployment, attracting private investment and improving service delivery across the 23 local government areas of the state, stressing that Sokoto needs a prepared leader with a clear plan.

World.title: NASENI Trains, Empowers 120 Electricians in Modern Electrical Installation in Kogi
World.content:
Ibrahim Oyewale in Lokoja





The National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI) has trained, empowered no fewer 120 electricians in modern electrical installation and maintenance in Kogi State as part of efforts to tackle youths’ unemployment in the country.



The Executive Director/CEO NASENI, Professor Khalid Halilu, disclosed this at the closing ceremony of NASENI Skills Acquisition and Empowerment programme and presentation of certificate to held in Lokoja yesterday.



Professor Halilu explained that NASENI was committed to taking skills acquisition to the door steps of Nigerians, noting that industrialisation goes beyond the machine and structures, but skills acquisition to ignite the industrial revolution in Nigeria.



The executive director however, commended the Kogi State government for their cooperation.



Professor Halilu who was represented by a Coordinating Director of Finance and Account, NASENI, Ibrahim Dauda explained that the agency has trained, empowered a total of 120 electricians in modern electrical installation.



He added that NASENI also gave them money to start their own business, admonished the trainees that their skills placed them in the fastest growing sector of Nigeria economy, the construction sector, so they must key into it immediately.



He warned the trainees not to sell the starter packs, stressing it is a sustainable livelihood tools for them and this will enable start new life.



The traditional ruler and the Chairman of Lokoja Traditional Council, the Maigari of Lokoja, His Royal Highness, Ibrahim Kabir, expressed gratitude to NASENI for the trading of 120 electricians in the modern electrical installation.



“My dear participants, the training you have received from NASENI places a responsibility on you to demonstrate the value of the investment made in your professional development…In this sense, you should regard yourselves as ambassadors of NASENI.



“Your conduct, professional competence; and quality of service will help to shape public perception of the agency and the effectiveness of its training programmes therefore encourage you to put the knowledge and skills acquired here into practical use and allow your work to speak positively about the institution that has invested in you. Be worthy ambassadors through your professionalism, integrity, discipline, diligence, and good conduct.



“Your success will not only benefit you and your families; it will also demonstrate the value of NASENI’s intervention and strengthen the case for similar programmes to be extended to other trades and communities,” the traditional ruler posited.

World.title: Cape Town’s N2 wall: 94% OPPOSE plans, says survey
World.content:
A new survey claims that 94% of people polled oppose Cape Town's N2 Edge Safety Project. Images via Facebook

A survey polling thousands of participants about their stance on Cape Town’s proposed N2 Edge Safety Project has yielded alarming results – almost 94% have voiced their disapproval!

The barrier will reportedly cover a 9km stretch between the townships of Khayelitsha and Langa and will cost around R114 million, Mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis announced earlier this year.

While some have argued that the wall will protect motorists, commuters, and pedestrians from hijackings, smash-and-grabs, and stone-throwing incidents, others have claimed that it offers a short-term solution for combating crime.



N2 EDGE SAFETY PROJECT SURVEY: 94% SAY NO TO WALL

This week, author, researcher, and activist Candice Leigh King published The People’s Cost of Care Report, the results of a survey about Cape Town’s proposed N2 Edge Safety Project.

Here are some of her key findings:

17 200 people particiated in th poll, which was created on a Google form and shared on social media.

93.9% opposed the wall, 4.3% supported it, and 1.8% were unsure of their stance.

Many who opposed the wall did not believe that the project was the best way to address or solve crime. They also objected to the proposed R114 million budget allocation, which they felt could be spent elsewhere.

Preferred alternatives included education and skills development initiatives, job creation, housing, infrastructure and shelters for women who suffered gender-based violence, which ranked higher up on a list of community investment options.

Participants believe many of these alernatives could help tackle poverty and crime within the communities affected by the N2 wall.

Respondents also rejected the concept of a physical barrier.

Almost a quarter of participants live in the Cape Flats, whilst 22.4% reported having family living there.

“If we want to know what the best solution is, the best people to ask are people on the ground with lived experiences”, King told Cape Talk this week.



WHEN WILL CONSTRUCTION COMMENCE?

The City of Cape Town’s N2 Edge Safety project will cover a 9km stretch of the N2 between Baden Powell Road near Khayelitsha and Bhunga Avenue in Langa. The city has budgeted approximately R114 million for the project.

While there has been pushback from residents, political parties and activists, Cape Town Mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis has stated that the barrier will protect both local communities and commuters.

He said: “The project will not only repair safety barriers and install new ones. It will also bring various other safety improvements for adjacent communities, including pedestrian crossings, improved lighting, safer grazing practices for livestock and reduced spaces for illegal dumping.”



Construction is expected to commence in 2027.

World.title: Is TikTok distracting Bryan Leon’s form at Mamelodi Sundowns?
World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns striker Bryan Leon has struggled to replicate his explosive start to life in the Premier Soccer League (PSL), with fans questioning his dip in form.

The 26-year-old Colombian striker enjoyed an impressive introduction to South African football after joining the Brazilians in January, scoring 15 goals in 26 appearances last season.

His clinical finishing made him a nightmare for opposition defenders, with many fans and pundits believing he could have approached the 30-goal mark had he started the 2025/26 campaign with Sundowns.



However, Leon has found goals harder to come by this season, managing just three goals in nine matches. The striker has also come under scrutiny for missing several clear-cut chances.

Sundowns fans question Bryan Leon’s form

Leon’s struggles have sparked debate among football supporters, with some questioning what has changed since he arrived at Chloorkop.

Local soccer journalist Lorenz Köhler raised the issue on X, prompting several reactions from fans. Some blamed the striker’s alleged TikTok activity for distracting him from football, while others suggested opposition teams had figured him out.

@PAPALONENE wrote: “TikTok…. He spends most of the time there…. He doesn’t sleep; the time difference between South Africa and South America is the cause.”

@Honorabledawgs was critical of Leon’s performances in the opposition box, writing: “He’s turning into a rugby player, instead of scoring goals. So many fouls in the opposition box, some unnecessary.”

Meanwhile, @Mthuli4 suggested Brayan Leon may have underestimated the quality of the local league after his impressive start.



“He took our league by storm and started to undermine it, he’s starting to learn now,” the fan wrote.

@RealJAM_ also questioned Leon’s alleged social media activity, saying: “He’s on TikTok lives instead of staying behind at Chloorkop and doing shooting drills.”

Other supporters questioned his ability, with @Mothupi25Les suggesting that his initial success was driven more by hard work than technical quality.

BMW

“He came in when alot was expected from him and the team was under pressure, he was running like a mad man in the last season and not playing ball. He can’t play so he can’t score,” the fan wrote.

Brayan Leon has only scored three goals

@maverickvaks also criticised the striker, claiming he had become more focused on life away from football.

“The nice life, he become an Instagram influencer now, he’s forgotten why he came here for or maybe he’s just a fraud,” the supporter posted.

@SollyMongs similarly blamed Leon’s lifestyle for his dip in form.

“He’s enjoying SA baddies and TikTok. He forgot his job and he’s not coming back. Yanga is waiting for him. That hunger is gone,” the fan tweeted.

It remains to be seen if Brayan Leon will rediscover his form.

World.title: UPDATE: Tshwane reveals what lab tests found in tap water
World.content:
A modern kitchen sink with running water, a sleek faucet, and a vase on the countertop. Image: Pexels

The City of Tshwane has lifted the boil-water advisory affecting the Pretoria CBD and surrounding areas supplied through Findlay Reservoir.

Executive Mayor Dr Nasiphi Moya confirmed the decision in a press statement on Saturday, 24 October, after laboratory results showed that the water meets drinking water quality standards.

Tests show no trace of bacteria in the water

According to the City, the latest microbiological testing at Findlay Reservoir recorded no detectable E. coli or total coliform bacteria.



“Residents may therefore resume normal use of their tap water without boiling it,” the statement reads.

The advisory followed microbial contamination in groundwater supplied by the Fountains Springs. The City traced the problem to a damaged sewer pipe in Groenkloof.

Technical teams isolated the affected source and switched the CBD to an alternative supply from Salvokop Reservoir. They then cleaned Findlay Reservoir, applied chlorine shock treatment to the distribution network and carried out further tests.



The City kept the advisory in place after the switch because contaminated water could still have been present in parts of the network.

Mayor apologises for late warning

Moya praised the technical teams but acknowledged residents’ frustration over how the City handled the warning.

“In particular, the delay in communicating the initial boil-water advisory was unacceptable, and I sincerely apologise to affected residents,” she said.



She added that the independent investigation launched after the Bronkhorstspruit water crisis will also examine this incident, “including whether any negligence occurred and why residents were not warned timeously.”

“Where failures are established, appropriate corrective action and consequence management will follow,” Moya said.

The City stressed that the Pretoria CBD incident is unrelated to the problems in Bronkhorstspruit.



Repairs continue in Groenkloof

Work continues on the damaged sewer pipe, and the City will also rehabilitate the affected river section. Once groundwater testing confirms that the contamination is gone, the City will flush the pipeline to Findlay Reservoir before it restores the groundwater supply. Findlay Reservoir also receives water from Rand Water.

The City says routine water-quality monitoring will continue so that residents stay informed of any developments affecting their supply.

Moya also urged residents to use water sparingly and to report leaks.



“With increased pressure on the City’s water supply, avoiding unnecessary wastage and reporting leaks will help maintain a reliable supply for all communities,” she said.

World.title: City of Cape Town issues stern warning about fireworks
World.content:
In Cape Town, you are not allowed to host a public fireworks display without a valid permit. Image: Pexels

The City of Cape Town is warning residents against the illicit sale and use of fireworks.

In a statement posted on Saturday, 24 October 2026, the City revealed that its Public Emergency Communication Centre (PECC) is seeing an increase in complaints about the sale and discharge of fireworks.

FIREWORKS COMPLAINTS SKYROCKET

According to the City, the PECC recorded 13 complaints about the illegal sale of fireworks and at least 49 complaints about the illegal discharge of fireworks during the first three weeks of October.



In comparison, the PECC received three complaints about the illegal sale of fireworks and six complaints about the discharge of fireworks during the first three weeks of September.

“Hotspot areas include Manenberg, Eastridge, Beacon Valley, Atlantis, Heideveld, Hanover Park, Belhar and Bonteheuwel,” the statement reads.

This month’s complaints arrive just two weeks before two major events. Guy Fawkes Night is on 5 November 2026 and Diwali is on 8 November 2026.



‘A SOURCE OF ABSOLUTE TERROR’

Alderman JP Smith, Mayoral Committee Member for Safety and Security, called this increase “disappointing, but not entirely surprising.”

“While many people have come to understand and support efforts to snuff out the illegal use of fireworks, there are still pockets of resistance in the weeks leading up to Guy Fawkes and Diwali, and then also around New Year’s,” Smith said.

“The illegal discharge of fireworks has no place in our society. Not only is it a noise nuisance to others, but also a source of absolute terror for domestic pets and communities plagued by gun violence.”



Citing the high risk of fire and injuries, Smith is calling on Capetonians to help. Anyone with information regarding the illegal sale or use of fireworks is urged to contact the PECC on 021 480 7700 from their cellphone. Alternatively, you can contact them via the Safety and Security feature on the City App.

FIREWORKS IN CAPE TOWN

If you’re found selling, storing or discharging fireworks, you can face significant fines. Image: Pexels

In Cape Town, you are not allowed to host a public fireworks display without a valid permit. To apply, you will need to fill out an application and email it to the South African Police Service.

If approved, you must then contact the Fire and Rescue Service’s Fire Life Safety Section. A site inspection will be done to determine whether the site the display is being held is safe for fireworks.



Additionally, you are required to seek the permission of residents and businesses in the area to host a fireworks display.

Expecting a crowd larger than 200 attendees, or do you require any infrastructure to be built? Ensure that you apply for an Events permit from the City, too.

WHAT ABOUT GUY FAWKES, DIWALI?

There are no designated fireworks sites for events such as Guy Fawkes Night or Diwali in Cape Town. This has been in effect since 2019.



So, if you’re selling, storing or discharging fireworks during these events – or on other occasions – you can face hefty fines.

For example, operating a fireworks display, theatrical pyrotechnics or other fireworks without permission or a permit from the controlling authority can see you fined R1 500.

What are your thoughts about fireworks usage in Cape Town? Sound off in the comments below.
