Why the Attorney General Objects

Gonet argues that the order came on Friday evening, leaving too little time to approve each trip before Sunday. He says some river journeys have to begin on Saturday, Estadão reported.

In the filing, he said that approval within two days amounts, in practice, to no transport at all, according to Folha de S.Paulo. He added that agencies might stop trips for fear of being held responsible.

What the Prosecutor Wants Instead

The PGR asks the Supreme Court to restore earlier decisions by a federal court in Pará state and the federal government’s own transport plan. That plan has Funai, the Indigenous ministry and security forces working together.

Gonet says inspection should protect the neutrality of the vote without blocking anyone from reaching a polling station. He argues the transport plan should go ahead without waiting for case-by-case approval.

The glass facade of the electoral court building in Brasília. File photo. (Photo: Luiz Roberto/TSE, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

What It Means for US Readers

For readers following Brazil from the United States, this is a dispute about access to the ballot, not about a candidate. The main risk is to confidence in the process if remote communities cannot reach their polling stations.

Investors in Brazilian assets will watch whether the Supreme Court acts before Sunday, because court fights over voting rules can add noise to a close race.

The Supreme Court has not said when it will rule or which justice will handle the request. It is also not known how many voters depend on state-organised transport and how many trips have already left.

He asked it on Saturday 24 October to suspend part of an electoral court order on Indigenous voter transport. He says the rule cannot be met before the runoff.

Federal agencies need a judge’s prior approval for each trip. Requests must list vehicles or boats, drivers, routes, stops and times.

World.title: Brazil Court Orders Lula Shirt Videos Pulled
World.content:
The Supreme Federal Court building in Brasília seen from the side at night (Photo: Dasfour2022, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Saturday, 24 October, 2:25 pm ET · Source: Brazil’s electoral court decision, as reported by SBT News

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, elects its president in a runoff on Sunday 25 October.

What happened On Friday 23 October, electoral court minister Estela Aranha ordered the removal of social media videos linking Lula’s party to drug suspects.

The videos They show three detainees, two adults and a 17-year-old, in shirts backing Lula after an arrest in Piracicaba, São Paulo state.

The dispute Military police are accused of forcing the shirts on the detainees, and the police ombudsman is investigating.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Kalshi, regulated in the US by the CFTC, prices a Flávio Bolsonaro win by at least 1 point at 78% and a Lula win by at least 1 point at 14% (24 October, 2:25 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 84% and Kalshi at 84% (Lula: 17% and 18% ), as of 24 October, 2:20 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open The court has not ruled on the facts, and the origin of the shirts is disputed.

Brazil’s electoral court has ordered the removal of videos that show suspected drug dealers in campaign shirts of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, two days before the runoff. Minister Estela Aranha of the electoral court (TSE) decided on Friday 23 October that the posts wrongly tie Lula’s Workers’ Party (PT) to crime, SBT News reported.

Brazil Election Data Room Runoff poll average: Flávio Bolsonaro 51.0 %, Lula 49.0 % 43 national polls from 20 pollsters since 4 October, updated hourly. Every poll, free to download. Open the Data Room · Download the CSV · Embed the chart

The order lands in the last weekend of the Brazil election 2026 campaign, between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro. For readers abroad, it shows how far Brazilian judges will go to police online campaign content, which matters for platforms and investors watching the vote.

What the Court Ordered

The videos show three people detained in Piracicaba, in São Paulo state: two adults and a 17-year-old, SBT News reported. The shirts read “Professores da Apeoesp com Lula”, or “Apeoesp teachers with Lula”, according to SBT.

Senators-elect Guilherme Derrite of the Progressistas party (PP) and Carlos Jordy of the Liberal Party (PL), which backs Flávio Bolsonaro, published the videos, Tribuna do Sertão reported. They also spread on the WhatsApp channel “Tropa do Flávio”.

Lula’s coalition filed an urgent petition, SBT News reported. The order covered posts on X, Instagram and the WhatsApp channel.

Why the Judge Said the Posts Went Too Far

Aranha wrote that the content uses a specific police episode to present a link between the PT and crime as fact, O Antagonista reported. She said suspects wearing a candidate’s shirt does not allow the conclusion that a link exists with that candidate or his party, Bahia Notícias reported.

The images, in her words, “exceed, in principle, the limits of political-electoral criticism”, Tribuna do Sertão reported. The Portuguese original is “ultrapassa, em princípio, os limites da crítica político-eleitoral”.

The Dispute Over the Shirts

Military police officers are accused of forcing the three to wear the shirts after the stop, SBT News and Tribuna do Sertão reported. Bahia Notícias said the decision did not weigh the detainees’ testimony.

The teenager’s mother told SBT News that her son left home in a blue sleeveless shirt and that police forced him to change. The Civil Police registered the case as possible threat, coercion and abuse of authority, and the Military Police ombudsman opened an investigation, O Antagonista reported.

What It Means for US Readers

The ruling shows Brazil’s electoral court acting against campaign content on social platforms in the final days. If you follow Brazilian markets or ADRs, more such orders are possible until the result is certified.

Decisions like this one can also feed each side’s claims of bias before and after the vote. Our Brazil election polls page tracks the race itself.

These are bets, not polls, and they can move fast on news.

What Is Not Known

It is not known who put the shirts on the detainees, which police and the ombudsman are investigating. It is also unclear whether Derrite, Jordy or the channel will appeal.

Any effect on voters is unmeasured, since no poll has asked about this episode. The court’s ruling is about the posts, not about the detainees’ guilt or the officers’ conduct.

More: Brazil news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did Brazil’s electoral court order the videos removed?

Minister Estela Aranha ruled the posts wrongly link Lula’s party to crime. She said suspects wearing a candidate’s shirt does not prove a connection.

Who is Estela Aranha?

She is a minister of Brazil’s electoral court (TSE), the body that runs and polices elections. She decided the case on Friday 23 October.

Who posted the videos?

Tribuna do Sertão reported that senators-elect Guilherme Derrite and Carlos Jordy published them. They also spread on the “Tropa do Flávio” WhatsApp channel.

Did police force the detainees to wear the shirts?

That is disputed. Military police are accused of it, the court did not rule on it, and the police ombudsman is investigating.

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October. Lula faces Flávio Bolsonaro.

World.title: Panama Names Soldier Lost in US Invasion
World.content:
Panama: History and Justice

Key Facts Who. Roberto Adolfo Aparicio Oliva, a 21-year-old Panamanian soldier, identified by DNA.

What. Remains identified after more than 36 years of his family’s search.

Where. He died in El Chorrillo, Panama City, on the day of the US invasion.

When. Died 20 December 1989; commission announced the identification on 24 October 2026.

Status. As of 24 October 2026, 18:10 GMT

Panama has put a name to a young soldier who died on the first day of the US invasion in 1989, and whose family never stopped looking for him.

Panama’s state commission on the 1989 invasion announced on 24 October 2026 that DNA has identified the remains of Roberto Adolfo Aparicio Oliva. He was a 21-year-old soldier who died in the El Chorrillo district of Panama City on 20 December 1989, the day of the US invasion.

The US military invaded Panama that day to remove General Manuel Noriega. For American readers, this identification is a reminder that a US military operation left a human aftermath that Panama is still working through.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Panama ranks 11th of 14 with 34.2 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (64); weakest: military means (11). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What We Know

The Comisión 20 de Diciembre de 1989 is the Panamanian state commission that investigates the victims of the invasion. It said the remains were identified through DNA after more than 36 years of searching by his family.

According to the commission’s account, Aparicio served as an agent, meaning an enlisted soldier, of Batallón 2000, a unit based in Chepo. He was assigned to the reconnaissance section at the Cuartel Central, the headquarters of the Panama Defence Forces.

He was promoted after his death to cabo segundo, or second corporal, by Decree 228 of 31 May 1990. His parents were Félix Adolfo Aparicio Pérez and Lidia Maritza Oliva Gómez, and the family lived in Cerro Batea, in the San Miguelito district.

The newspapers La Prensa, La Estrella de Panamá and El Siglo, all in Panama City, reported the news on 24 October 2026. El Siglo described the case as 36 years of pain and waiting.

His family had been told that he died, but they could never find his body. They searched hospitals and cemeteries and followed exhumations for 36 years.

Sunset over the Pacific in Panama. File photo. Photo: Héctor Ruíz Palma, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

Why the Search Took 36 Years

His remains were buried in a common grave at the Jardín de Paz cemetery. They were heavily carbonised, which made recovering genetic material a scientific challenge.

The Fundación de Antropología Forense de Guatemala, a forensic anthropology foundation, extracted the DNA and built a genetic profile. Panama’s Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses, the national forensic medicine institute, then compared that profile with reference samples from the family.

The comparison took place within an investigation by the Ministerio Público, Panama’s prosecutors. The reports do not say how long the laboratory work took.

This case follows earlier work that we covered when Panama began exhuming victims of the 1989 invasion. On 19 December 2025, La Prensa reported that prosecutors had identified 11 people from remains exhumed at collective graves in the Jardín de Paz and Monte Esperanza cemeteries.

La Prensa added that 21 samples had been sent to the Guatemalan foundation at that point. The identification of Aparicio is a further result of the same slow process of DNA comparison and justice.

What Is Not Known

The commission has not said on which date the DNA match was completed. It has also not said whether the remains will be handed to the family, or when.

It is not known how many people are still missing. Details about the cause of his death are also not known.

The announcements reported so far do not settle these questions. We will report further details once Panama’s authorities publish them.

What It Means for US Readers

The invasion was a US military operation, and its victims are still being identified more than three decades later. The total number of dead has never been settled, so each identification matters to the historical record.

In December 2025, commission president Rolando Murgas Torraza said the commission should become permanent to preserve historical memory. La Prensa also reported that the commission’s funding for 2026 was uncertain.

The inquiry runs through Panamanian prosecutors and forensic scientists. Experts from Guatemala supplied the genetic analysis that made this match possible.

Identifications are slow because many remains lie in collective graves. What happens next for the commission and for this family has not been announced.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who was Roberto Adolfo Aparicio Oliva?

He was a 21-year-old enlisted soldier of Batallón 2000 who died in El Chorrillo, Panama City, on 20 December 1989. He was promoted after death to second corporal.

How was he identified?

A Guatemalan forensic foundation extracted DNA from his heavily carbonised remains. Panama’s forensic medicine institute then compared it with samples from his family.

Who announced the identification?

Panama’s Comisión 20 de Diciembre de 1989, the state commission on the invasion victims, announced it on 24 October 2026. It followed more than 36 years of searching by his family.

Will the remains be returned to the family?

The commission has not said whether the remains will be handed over, or when. That detail has not been announced.

World.title: Parliament Backs South Africa Election Body
World.content:
The Union Buildings in Pretoria, seat of South Africa's presidency, with a police vehicle parked at right (file photo from October 2024). Photo: Ruby D-Brown / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)

Three parliamentary committees said on Friday, 23 October, that South Africa’s Electoral Commission is ready for the 4 November local elections. The commission is still printing millions of extra ballots; our running coverage sits in the South Africa local elections hub.

Key Facts What: Three parliamentary committees backed the IEC’s readiness for the local elections.

When: South Africa votes on Wednesday, 4 November, 07:00–21:00 local (00:00–14:00 ET).

Ballots: About 6.6 million extra ballots are being printed after a court ruling.

Scale: More than 29 million voters; 10,526 council seats in 257 municipalities.

Prediction markets: Kalshi (CFTC-regulated) gives Helen Zille 51.0% for Johannesburg mayor, as of 1:56 p.m. ET on 24 October.

MPs Inspect the Electoral Commission

Three parliamentary committees inspected the Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) headquarters in Pretoria on Friday, 23 October. They were the Portfolio Committees on Home Affairs and on Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs, and the Select Committee on Security and Justice.

Committee chair Mosa Chabane said the MPs are confident the IEC will deliver free and fair elections, while problems could still arise. Eyewitness News reported the visit on Saturday, 24 October.

Ballots Race Against the Clock

The IEC had printed 66% of about 79 million ballot papers by mid-October, eNCA reported. A Constitutional Court ruling that put 181 excluded ANC candidates back on ballots now requires about 6.6 million extra papers.

Printing of the extra ballots is due to finish by 30 October, five days before voting. Whether it finishes on time is the main logistical risk.

Jacaranda-lined Becket Street in Pretoria, home of the IEC’s headquarters. File photo. Photo: Paul Saad, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

Election Numbers

The election is set for Wednesday, 4 November 2026, as gazetted by Cooperative Governance Minister Velenkosini Hlabisa in Government Gazette No. 55162. Voting runs from 07:00 to 21:00 South African time (00:00 to 14:00 US Eastern Time), with special votes on 2 and 3 November.

More than 29 million people are registered, and 10,526 council seats are at stake across 257 municipalities. The IEC certified 136,790 candidates on 16 September, and about 547 of 732 registered parties are contesting, SABC reported.

What the Polls Say

The eNCA/MarkData survey, published on 18 October, interviewed about 1,000 residents in each of six metros between 12 August and 10 September. In Cape Town, 60.5% said the city is run very well or averagely well, against 29.2% in Johannesburg, where 68.7% said it is run badly.

In Cape Town, the Democratic Alliance (DA) led with 52.6% against 23.6% for the African National Congress (ANC), the governing party nationally. In Johannesburg, the DA led with 35.0%, ahead of the ANC on 21.8%, uMkhonto weSizwe on 12.5%, the EFF on 11.9% and ActionSA on 10.3%.

What Prediction Markets Say

Kalshi, regulated in the US by the CFTC, priced Helen Zille at 51.0% to be Johannesburg’s mayor after the election as of 1:56 p.m. ET on 24 October, with 13,542 contracts traded. David Makhura followed at 14.0% and Herman Mashaba at 7.0%.

Polymarket’s Johannesburg market, with about US$135,000 traded, had Zille at 51.5% and Makhura at 12.8%. These prices are bets on one city, not national forecasts.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Court Rejects a Ward Challenge

The Electoral Court dismissed independent candidate Llala Peter Phoshoko’s challenge over his exclusion from the Ward 33 ballot in Polokwane, the Citizen reported. The dispute centred on whether his nomination met the signature requirement.

What It Means for US Readers

Johannesburg and Cape Town host South Africa‘s largest business districts, so who runs them matters to investors and travellers with exposure there. The Johannesburg survey shows no party near a majority, which points to coalition talks after the vote.

The parliamentary check matters because the commission is still reprinting ballots. A smooth count would support confidence in the result.

What Is Not Known

Which parties will control individual councils is unresolved, and the MarkData survey is not a national forecast. Whether the extra ballots arrive on time is not yet known.

The committees said they expect a free and fair vote but allowed that problems could arise. The effect of service-delivery complaints on turnout is not yet measurable.

When are South Africa’s local elections?

World.title: Serbia Enters Vote Silence, Polls Split
World.content:
Serbia’s campaigning ended on Thursday, 22 October, and the legal silence period began ahead of a parliamentary election that pits the ruling list against a student-led challenger. Our running coverage sits in the Serbia Election 2026 hub.

Key Facts What: Serbia votes in a snap parliamentary election on Sunday, 25 October 2026.

When: Polls close at 20:00 Central European Time, which is 15:00 Eastern Time.

Latest poll: Ipsos, for the ruling list: United Serbia 47.4%, Student List 40.0%.

Electorate: 6,450,523 registered voters choose 250 seats; 126 make a majority.

Prediction markets: Kalshi (CFTC-regulated) prices an SNS-led win at 73% and a Student List win at 29%, as of 1:56 p.m. ET on 24 October.

This story is part of our coverage of the Serbia Election 2026. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: Serbia Sets 6.45 Million Voters for Sunday

Campaign Ends With Rival Rallies

Campaigning ended on Thursday, 22 October, and the legal silence period followed. The Student List held its final rally at Slavija Square in Belgrade, where Al Jazeera reported tens of thousands of people.

Aleksandar Vučić held a rival rally the same day at a sports hall across town. Polling stations open at 07:00 on Sunday and close at 20:00 Central European Time.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Serbia Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Polls Point in Different Directions

The newest poll is an Ipsos survey of 3,624 people, taken on 20–22 October for the ruling list. It put Vučić’s United Serbia list at 47.4% and the Student List at 40.0%, with the Socialist Party list of Ivica Dačić at 3.2%.

An NSPM telephone poll of 1,050 people, taken between 25 September and 5 October, had the Student List ahead among decided voters at 44.5% against 42.7%. Its fieldwork ended almost three weeks before the vote.

The PolitPro average on 24 October showed the ruling list at 46.8% and the Student List at 40.6%. Because the Ipsos poll was commissioned by the ruling list, the two camps’ numbers are not directly comparable.

The House of the National Assembly in Belgrade, where the new parliament will sit. File photo. Photo: Kallerna, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

What Prediction Markets Say

Kalshi, a prediction market regulated in the US by the CFTC, priced an SNS-led win at 73% and a Student List win at 29% at 1:56 p.m. ET on 24 October, with 23,488 contracts traded. The two prices add up to more than 100% because each side is quoted separately.

Polymarket put Vučić’s list at 70.0% to win, with about US$4.33 million traded. Its turnout market favoured the 62–66% band at 43.5%, ahead of 66–70% at 32.5%.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Two Camps, One Contest

The ruling list is led by Aleksandar Vučić, who resigned as president on 27 September and is seeking to become prime minister. The Student List grew out of the university movement behind nearly two years of anti-corruption protests.

Ilija Srdanović, a cardiologist and professor at the University of Novi Sad, heads its list of 250 candidates. He is not described as the movement’s formal leader and would not automatically become prime minister.

The protests began after the concrete canopy of Novi Sad railway station collapsed in November 2024 and killed 16 people. The Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) has governed since 2012, and this is widely portrayed as its most serious challenge since.

What It Means for US Readers

Serbia is a test of whether a long-dominant party can lose to a youth-led movement with no single leader. The outcome will show how far public anger over the Novi Sad disaster has reshaped Serbian politics.

Traders can follow the odds on Kalshi and Polymarket as the count comes in. Official results come from the Republic Electoral Commission after polls close.

What Is Not Known

Which list will finish first is unresolved, because the polls and the markets lean toward the ruling list while one poll favours the students. Whether either side can reach 126 of the 250 seats without a coalition is also unknown.

Final turnout is unknown, and the market range is only a bet, not a forecast. No official result exists until counting begins after the 20:00 close.

World.title: Officials Count 410,000 at France Protests
World.content:
French NGO are protesting the presence of Bolsonaro government representatives at a French economic forum in June, photo by Lorie Shaull/Wikimedia CC.

France in Turmoil · Breaking

Published Saturday, October 24, 1:45 p.m. ET (7:45 p.m. Paris) · Source: Franceinfo, French Interior Ministry and Paris police figures

Key Facts National count. The Interior Ministry counted 410,000 marchers on Saturday; the CGT union said 800,000.

Paris. Police counted 110,000 marchers in the capital; the CGT said 250,000.

Last week. The ministry counted 550,000 marchers on October 17, so the official figure fell.

Security. About 70,000 police and gendarmes were deployed; 135 arrests by 7:00 a.m. ET (1:00 p.m. Paris).

Prediction markets. Polymarket, 1:28 p.m. ET: France declares a state of emergency by December 31, 15.5%.

This story is part of our coverage of the why France is in crisis. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: Paris Marchers Hit 110,000 as Clashes Spread

France’s second Saturday of mass street protests drew 410,000 people by the government’s count and 800,000 by the largest union’s, a gap that shows how contested the movement has become.

Official figures for Saturday, October 24, put turnout at 410,000 nationwide; the ministry had counted 550,000 on October 17. The CGT, one of France’s biggest trade union federations, said 800,000 people marched, in the latest of the France protests that have shaken the government.

In Paris, police counted 110,000 marchers between the Porte d’Italie and the Porte de Vincennes, while the CGT said 250,000. Our earlier reports covered the midday arrest figure and the Paris tally; this adds the national count for the day.

In plain English Hundreds of thousands of people marched across France over living costs and public services. Police and unions count crowds differently, so their numbers differ widely, and tension at the end of some marches led to tear gas and water cannon.

Why the Counts Differ So Much

The ministry’s national figure fell by about 140,000 from last Saturday. The CGT’s figure is nearly double the official one.

Demonstrators said they were marching to defend purchasing power and the freedom to protest. For more background, see why France is protesting.

File photo: placards at a Paris march on October 17.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Security Operation and Street Tension

About 70,000 police and gendarmes were deployed, with elite units and helicopters. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 135 people had been arrested by 1:00 p.m. in Paris (7:00 a.m. ET), mostly in checks on the flow of marchers and equipment seizures.

The Paris march was calm for most of the day, but tension rose when it broke up, and police reported more than 500 rioters at the Cours de Vincennes. Franceinfo reported tear gas in Lyon, Marseille and Bordeaux and water cannon in Lille.

In Lyon, about 10,000 people gathered in several unauthorised processions despite a ban on demonstrating, and police dispersed them. Bans were also in place in Nancy, Metz, Besançon, Belfort, Rouen, Le Havre and Toulon.

File photo: riot police on Boulevard Voltaire, Paris.

What It Means for US Readers

France is a major US trading partner and a NATO ally, so a prolonged cycle of street protest and heavy policing matters for investors and travellers. Anyone with plans in Paris, Lyon or Marseille should expect marches, road closures and possible transport disruption on protest days.

The fall in the official count since last Saturday is one number to watch, alongside the arrest and injury totals still to come.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, a platform where users trade real-money contracts, traders gave France a 5.0% chance of declaring a state of emergency by October 31 and 15.5% by December 31, as of 1:28 p.m. ET on October 24. About US$752,000 has been traded on that market.

On Kalshi, an exchange regulated in the US by the CFTC, a similar contract showed 11.0% before November 1 and 20.0% before January 1, 2027.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

No final national tally of arrests, injuries or property damage had been published at the time of writing, and the 135 arrests are a midday figure. The cause and extent of the tension in several cities are still being established.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many people protested in France on October 24?

The Interior Ministry counted 410,000 demonstrators nationwide, while the CGT union said 800,000. In Paris, police counted 110,000 and the CGT 250,000.

Why do police and unions give different numbers?

They count crowds with different methods and have different interests. Authorities tend to count lower, organisers higher, so the official and union figures rarely match.

Were there arrests and clashes?

Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 135 people had been arrested by 1:00 p.m. Paris time, mostly in checks. Tear gas was used in several cities, including Lyon, Marseille and Bordeaux.

How big was the protest compared with last week?

The ministry counted 550,000 on October 17 and 410,000 on October 24, a fall of about 140,000.

Sources Franceinfo · Boursorama · RTBF · Polymarket

World.title: Nigeria APC Early Campaign Opens 24 Oct
World.content:
RT Ask Rio Times This story and the bigger picture. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesWhat this means, and what's next › RT Ask Rio Times This story and the bigger picture. × Economy impact Key players Stability What's next Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. NIGERIA · ELECTIONS

Key Facts — The country Nigeria is Africa’s most populous country, and 93,469,008 people were on the electoral commission’s voter list in 2023.

— What happened The Nigeria APC early campaign began with a Kaduna rally on Saturday 24 October 2026, Premium Times reported.

— The calendar Nigeria’s electoral commission, INEC, set the presidential vote for Saturday 16 January 2027, and campaigns may open 150 days earlier, on 19 August 2026.

— Why Kaduna Kaduna State had 4,335,208 registered voters in 2023, and the seven North-West states, Kaduna included, held 22,255,562, almost a quarter of the national list.

— The opposition Atiku Abubakar leads the African Democratic Congress (ADC) ticket, while Peter Obi runs for the NDC with Rabiu Kwankwaso as his running mate.

— Prediction markets Bettors on Polymarket gave Tinubu 68.5% and Obi 24.0% to win the presidency, as of 24 October 2026, 1:21 p.m. ET.

— Still open The APC has not said why it picked Kaduna, and the vote is still 84 days away.

The Nigeria APC early campaign opened on Saturday 24 October 2026 with a rally in Kaduna. President Bola Tinubu’s All Progressives Congress (APC) staged the flag-off at the Ranchers Bees Stadium, Premium Times reported.

By the calendar the electoral commission published, the party is not early, because campaigning has been legal since 19 August 2026. The vote is on Saturday 16 January 2027, so the flag-off comes 84 days before polling day.

Is the Nigeria APC Early Campaign Really Early?

The vote itself moved forward, which makes the Nigeria APC early campaign look early to an outside reader. The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) first set 20 February 2027 and then chose 16 January 2027, the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reported.

INEC’s portal now lists the presidential and National Assembly vote for 16 January 2027 and the governorship vote for 6 February 2027. Campaigns end 24 hours before polling, so the presidential campaign closes on Friday 15 January 2027, Voice of Nigeria reported.

In 2022 the APC waited 48 days after campaigning opened on 28 September to hold its flag-off in Jos on 15 November, ThisDay reported. In 2026 the wait for the Nigeria APC early campaign was 66 days, and the rally came 84 days before polling against 102 in 2022.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Nigeria Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How the Electoral Act 2026 Sets the Clock

Nigeria’s new Electoral Act 2026 says campaigns may begin only 150 days before an election, Voice of Nigeria reported on 29 July 2026. Counting back from 16 January 2027 gives 19 August 2026, so the Nigeria APC early campaign sits inside the legal window.

Governorship and state assembly campaigns open later, on 9 September 2026, and end on 5 February 2027. INEC said the repeal of the Electoral Act 2022 and the new Act altered key statutory timelines, according to NAN.

The same 150-day rule applied under the old law, section 94(1), and INEC’s then chairman Mahmood Yakubu said no penalty existed for starting earlier. He spoke at an Abuja roundtable in September 2025, according to allAfrica.

Why the APC Chose Kaduna

Senator Abdulaziz Yari, who directs the APC’s presidential campaign council, announced the date on Friday 9 October 2026 after briefing Tinubu in Abuja. He said the flag-off would be in Kaduna on 24 October, Blueprint reported.

The announcement gave no reason for the choice, but Kaduna-based analyst Haruna Ibrahim offered one to Daily Trust. Premium Times carried his remark that Kaduna is “more or less the centre of northern Nigeria”.

He also called Kaduna relatively safe compared with other northern states, with transport links that make it easier for supporters from neighbouring states to reach. Hotel rooms in Kaduna were fully booked before the Nigeria APC early campaign launch, and many supporters spent the night outdoors, Premium Times reported.

What Kaduna Voted in 2023

Kaduna did not go to Tinubu in 2023, even though the APC governs the state now. ThisDay and ICIR reported INEC’s count: the Peoples Democratic Party’s Atiku Abubakar 554,360 votes, Tinubu 399,293 and Labour’s Peter Obi 294,494.

Atiku won 14 of Kaduna’s 23 local government areas, Obi seven and Tinubu two, ThisDay reported. Kaduna State had 4,335,208 registered voters in 2023, according to INEC’s own voter-card list.

The seven North-West states held 22,255,562 registered voters, almost 24% of the national total of 93,469,008, on that INEC list. Lagos had 7,060,195, the most of any single state.

Governor Uba Sani, an APC member, won Kaduna’s 2023 governorship by 10,806 votes, 730,002 to 719,196 over the PDP’s Isa Ashiru, ThisDay reported. The Supreme Court dismissed the PDP’s appeal in January 2024, which settled his victory.

Atiku’s ADC and Obi’s NDC Face the APC

The two best-known opposition names now run on separate tickets. Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar won the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential primary on Wednesday 27 May 2026 with 1,846,370 votes, NAN reported.

Rotimi Amaechi, a former Rivers State governor, finished second with 504,117, and he and third-placed Mohammed Hayatu-Deen rejected the result, ICIR reported. ADC chairman David Mark said the primary was not perfect but allowed a free contest.

Peter Obi, the 2023 Labour Party candidate, and Rabiu Kwankwaso left the ADC for the NDC, a newer party, ICIR reported. The Gazette reported in late May 2026 that Obi won the NDC nomination and named Kwankwaso, a former Kano governor, as his running mate.

The APC says Atiku and the ADC plotted to discredit the Nigeria APC early campaign launch with fake news and deepfakes, Daily Trust reported. Spokesman Dele Alake called a purported letter claiming N2.3 trillion (about US$1.73 billion) was released for the rally “a senseless and utterly baseless lie”.

What Comes Next on the Campaign Trail

The campaign council’s schedule, published by Blueprint, lists 37 stops, one in each of the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. After Kaduna the Nigeria APC early campaign moves to Calabar on Monday 2 November and Gombe on Tuesday 3 November.

Six more North-West stops follow by 17 December, and the tour ends in Lagos on Saturday 9 January 2027. Our news report on the Kaduna flag-off covers the day itself.

What Prediction Markets Say

Bettors on Polymarket gave Tinubu 68.5% and Obi 24.0% to win the presidency, as of 24 October 2026, 1:21 p.m. ET. Volume was US$135,959, and on Kalshi, regulated in the United States by the CFTC, Tinubu stood at 71%, Obi 17% and Atiku 3%.

A separate Polymarket bet on Kaduna’s governorship, with US$27,963 traded, gave Governor Uba Sani 64.0% and Mohammed Ashiru Isa 23.5%. The state governorship vote is set for 6 February 2027, three weeks after the presidential race.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

Investors in naira assets and bonds will get a result early in 2027, because the Nigeria APC early campaign runs toward a 16 January vote. The naira stood at about 1,329.80 to the US dollar on 24 October 2026, and its 2.1% one-day fall shows its sensitivity.

Campaign rallies draw large crowds and heavy security, so travellers to northern Nigeria can expect road closures and full hotels around such events. Zaidu Bala, media aide to the Kebbi governor, told Premium Times that hotels in Kaduna were fully booked.

What Is Not Known

The APC has not explained why it chose Kaduna. How many people filled the Ranchers Bees Stadium is still unknown.

Tinubu’s speech and any promises he made at the rally were not available when this explainer was written. The prediction-market prices were taken on the day of the rally, so they may move once voters have heard him.

More: Nigeria news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

When does Nigeria vote in 2027?

INEC’s portal lists the presidential and National Assembly elections for Saturday 16 January 2027. Governorship and state assembly elections follow on Saturday 6 February 2027.

Is the Nigeria APC early campaign legal?

Yes, the Nigeria APC early campaign is legal, because the Electoral Act 2026 puts the presidential window at 19 August 2026. The Kaduna flag-off on 24 October came 66 days after that opening.

Why did the APC pick Kaduna?

The party has not given a reason, but Kaduna-based analyst Haruna Ibrahim told Daily Trust that the state is the centre of northern Nigeria. Kaduna State had 4,335,208 registered voters in 2023, and the North-West held 22,255,562.

Who is running against Tinubu?

Atiku Abubakar leads the ADC ticket, and Peter Obi leads the NDC ticket with Rabiu Kwankwaso as running mate. Both were chosen in late May 2026, according to NAN and The Gazette.

How did Kaduna vote in 2023?

Atiku Abubakar of the PDP won Kaduna with 554,360 votes, ahead of Tinubu’s 399,293 and Obi’s 294,494. ThisDay reported the count after INEC’s declaration.

World.title: Ecuador Defender Eyes Ballon D’Or on 26 Oct
World.content:
ECUADOR · SPORT

Key Facts — What is happening Ecuadorian defender Willian Pacho of Paris Saint-Germain is one of 30 men on the Ballon d’Or list, and the winner is named Monday, 26 October in London.

— Why it matters Pacho is only the second Ecuadorian on the list in the award’s history, after Édison Méndez in 2006, and defenders rarely win.

— The numbers Thirty men are nominated, nine of them defenders, and only three defenders have won: Franz Beckenbauer twice, Matthias Sammer and Fabio Cannavaro.

— Who is who Pacho is a centre-back for PSG and Ecuador. Rivals include England’s Harry Kane of Bayern Munich, France’s Kylian Mbappé of Real Madrid and Lionel Messi of Inter Miami.

— What to watch The ceremony starts at 8 p.m. in London, about 4 p.m. Eastern, and a free US stream is carried by DAZN.

— Power Index Ecuador ranks 8th of 14 in Ecuador ranks 8th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 38.2 points (October 2026 edition).

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives Harry Kane a 71% chance of winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or and Kylian Mbappé 18.9%; Pacho is priced at 0.1% with no trades (24 October, 1:24 p.m. ET).

— What it means for you US fans can watch the ceremony free on DAZN, see Messi of Inter Miami compete, and follow Ecuador’s first nominee in 20 years.

Willian Pacho, a defender from Ecuador, is one of 30 men up for the Ballon d’Or, football’s best-known individual prize. The winner is announced in London on Monday, 26 October.

Willian Pacho, a centre-back for Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and Ecuador, is one of 30 men on the 2026 Ballon d’Or list. The winner is named at the London Palladium on Monday, 26 October, Vanguardia reports.

The Ballon d’Or is the sport’s most famous individual prize, created by the magazine France Football. Ecuador’s press says Pacho is only the second Ecuadorian ever nominated, which is why Quito papers are following the vote.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Ecuador ranks 8th of 14 with 38.2 points. Strongest pillar: military means (55); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (14). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (B); 51 homicides per 100,000. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Who Is Willian Pacho

Pacho plays in the heart of defence for PSG, the French club that won the Champions League again this year. Primicias, a Quito news site, and NBC New York report PSG beat Arsenal on penalties in the 30 May final.

He played all 17 of PSG’s Champions League games in 2025-26, Primicias and El Comercio both report. That is 1,560 minutes, the most in the squad, and Primicias also lists a Ligue 1 title.

Ecuador’s only earlier nominee was Édison Méndez, then at PSV Eindhoven, in 2006, Primicias reports. Méndez received no votes that year, when Cannavaro won.

Download the PDF checklist

How the Ballon D’Or Vote Works

An international jury of sports journalists picks the winner, Vanguardia reports. It has one voter from each of the top 100 countries in the FIFA men’s ranking.

The shortlist has 30 men, Vanguardia and Sports Illustrated both report. Pacho is the only nominee from Ecuador.

Defenders have a hard time winning. Only three have: Franz Beckenbauer in 1972 and 1976, Matthias Sammer in 1996 and Fabio Cannavaro in 2006.

Counting the published names, Pacho is one of nine defenders on this year’s list. Several PSG team-mates are also on the list, including Ousmane Dembélé, Achraf Hakimi and Vitinha.

Latin Americans and the Stars on the List

Eight of the 30 men come from Latin America, going by the list Vanguardia published. They are Luis Díaz (Colombia), Gabriel, Marquinhos and Vinícius (Brazil), Lautaro Martínez and Messi (Argentina), Pacho (Ecuador) and Julián Quiñones (Mexico).

Messi plays for Inter Miami in Major League Soccer, so the list includes a player from a US club. Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappé and Spain’s Lamine Yamal are the names bettors rate highest.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket’s Ballon d’Or market gives Harry Kane 71%, Mbappé 18.9%, Lamine Yamal 9.3% and Messi about 1% (1:24 p.m. ET, 24 October). The market has drawn about US$62.4 million in bets, the Kane contract alone about US$7.2 million.

Pacho is priced at 0.1%, an asking price with no recorded trades, so the market treats him as a very long shot. These prices are bets, not polls, and the jury’s votes decide the award.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

The ceremony is on at 4 p.m. Eastern on Monday, 26 October, with the red carpet at 2 p.m., Sports Illustrated reports. US viewers can watch free by signing up to DAZN, and CBS Sports presenter Kate Scott co-hosts with Thierry Henry.

Messi, who plays in Florida for Inter Miami, is on the list, though the market gives him little chance. The US-hosted World Cup this summer also put Pacho on American pitches.

For more on the country, see the guide to who holds power in Ecuador and the economy guide. The Andes neighbours explainer and the Ecuador hub add context.

What Is Not Known

Nobody outside the jury knows the vote, and the sources give no ranking of Pacho’s chances beyond the market price. The 30 names rest on Vanguardia and Sports Illustrated, because the official site would not open for this check.

Reports differ on PSG’s nominee count and on Pacho’s ball recoveries, so neither figure is used. The US stream and the 4 p.m. Eastern start rest on Sports Illustrated alone.

What Comes Next

The winner is announced on Monday, 26 October at the London Palladium, from 8 p.m. London time, about 4 p.m. Eastern. Britain’s clocks go back on Sunday, 25 October, so the gap to New York is four hours that day.

A win by Pacho would be a major surprise, since the market gives him 0.1%. The sources do not say whether the full top-three order will be published.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony?

It is on Monday, 26 October 2026 at the London Palladium. The official ceremony starts at 8 p.m. in London, about 4 p.m. Eastern.

Who is Willian Pacho?

Pacho is a centre-back for Paris Saint-Germain and Ecuador. He is one of 30 men on the 2026 Ballon d’Or list.

Has an Ecuadorian ever won the Ballon d’Or?

No Ecuadorian has won it. Pacho is the second nominated, after Édison Méndez in 2006, who received no votes that year.

Can a defender win the Ballon d’Or?

Yes, but only three have. They are Franz Beckenbauer, Matthias Sammer and Fabio Cannavaro.

How can US fans watch the Ballon d’Or?

Sports Illustrated reports that US viewers can watch free by signing up to DAZN. The red carpet starts at 2 p.m. Eastern.

Sources: Vanguardia, nominees and voting, 8 September; Primicias, second Ecuadorian nominated; Primicias, Pacho’s season; El Comercio, Pacho’s options; Sports Illustrated, ceremony times and US stream, 20 October; Sports Illustrated, full list of nominees; NBC New York, Champions League final, 30 May (all accessed 24 October 2026).

World.title: Costa Rica Unveils New ₡100 Coin Celebrating Limón Calypso
World.content:
Costa Rica is paying tribute to one of its most distinctive musical traditions with a new ₡100 coin celebrating Limón calypso, a genre deeply rooted in the history and cultural identity of the country’s Afro-Caribbean communities. The Central Bank of Costa Rica (BCCR) announced the release as part of its Intangible Cultural Heritage collection, an initiative designed to recognize and promote the traditions that shape Costa Rican identity.

Collector’s editions of the coin will be available to the public starting November 5, 2026, at a price of ₡8,400 each. Buyers will be able to choose between a presentation case and an acrylic display. The coin is the second release in a series of six designs announced by the Central Bank in July 2025. The collection debuted with a coin dedicated to Creole swing and will continue highlighting other cultural expressions from across the country.

Limón calypso is more than a musical genre. Through its distinctive rhythms and storytelling, it has helped preserve the experiences, traditions, and cultural identity of Afro-descendant communities along Costa Rica’s Caribbean coast. During the design process, the Central Bank’s Board of Directors reviewed references to two prominent figures associated with the development and promotion of the genre: Walter Ferguson Byfield, one of its most influential exponents, and Donald Raymond “Danny” Williams Shirley, a singer, percussionist, and promoter of calypso music.

Through this new release, the Central Bank hopes to introduce more Costa Ricans to this musical tradition and expand its recognition beyond the communities where it originated. The Intangible Cultural Heritage collection features six ₡100 coins, each dedicated to a different expression of Costa Rica’s cultural heritage.

In addition to Creole swing and Limón calypso, the series celebrates Chorotega ceramic craftsmanship, traditional oxherding and the Costa Rican oxcart, cimarrona music, and the *tope de toros* tradition in Liberia, Guanacaste. The Cultural Heritage Directorate of the Ministry of Culture and Youth selected the cultural expressions featured in the collection, while the Central Bank was responsible for developing and issuing the coins.

The coins also incorporate design and security features introduced as part of the redesign of Costa Rica’s national currency. Their obverse bears the inscriptions “Republic of Costa Rica” and “Central Bank of Costa Rica,” along with four raised bars that allow people to identify them by touch.

The collection includes coins intended for regular circulation, with a face value of ₡100, as well as special collector’s editions sold in commemorative packaging. The first collector’s coin, dedicated to Creole swing, was released in July 2025 at a price of ₡9,000. The new Limón calypso edition will cost ₡8,400, offering collectors another opportunity to celebrate Costa Rica’s cultural heritage through its currency.

World.title: JetBlue First Class Is Coming to Three Costa Rica Routes This Winter
World.content:
JetBlue’s new first-class cabin will reach Costa Rica within weeks of its debut, with BlueFirst seats scheduled on flights to Liberia starting Dec. 26 and to San José starting Jan. 5, 2027. The airline opened BlueFirst bookings on Oct. 15 on select flights across more than 30 routes. The first revenue flight leaves Boston Logan International Airport for Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport on Dec. 8. JetBlue noted that Fort Lauderdale was its first-ever destination and now becomes the first destination for BlueFirst.

Three Costa Rica routes are on the initial schedule. According to JetBlue’s published BlueFirst route list, service between Fort Lauderdale and Guanacaste’s international airport in Liberia begins Dec. 26. Flights from Fort Lauderdale to Juan Santamaría International Airport and from New York’s John F. Kennedy International Airport to Liberia both follow on Jan. 5.

JetBlue cautions that those dates reflect the earliest scheduled flights using BlueFirst-equipped aircraft. The cabin may be offered only on select flights or dates, sometimes intermittently, and aircraft assignments can change. Check that BlueFirst appears on the specific flight before you book.

BlueFirst is a dedicated two-by-two cabin at the front of the plane. The seats use Tuft & Needle foam and offer 13 centimeters (5 inches) of recline and up to 18 centimeters (7 inches) more legroom than JetBlue’s standard economy seats. Each seat has a 34-centimeter (13.3-inch) screen with Bluetooth headphone pairing, free Wi-Fi and in-seat power.

On flights of 1,447 kilometers (899 miles) or longer, passengers receive a complimentary meal called FirstFare, with a main dish, side and dessert. All three Costa Rica routes are longer than that. Premium snacks, wine, cocktails and specialty coffee and tea are offered on every BlueFirst flight and can be ordered from the seatback screen.

The cabin also comes with Group 1 boarding, dedicated overhead bin space, priority check-in and expedited security access at more than 30 participating airports. There are three fare levels. BlueFirst Base is the cheapest, with one free checked bag, free seat selection only within 24 hours of departure, and fees for changes and cancellations.

The standard BlueFirst fare adds a second checked bag, advance seat selection and no change or cancellation fees. BlueFirst Flex adds refunds to the original form of payment plus free same-day flight changes and standby. JetBlue started sales with introductory one-way fares from $249, including $299 from New York to Liberia for travel between Jan. 5 and Feb. 10. Unfortunately the promtion was short lived and ended Oct. 16.

BlueFirst does not replace Mint, JetBlue’s business class on longer flights. The airline plans to install the new cabin on aircraft that do not carry Mint, which will extend a first-class option across more of its network, including Latin America and the Caribbean. “We designed BlueFirst to deliver a more accessible first-class experience that combines the thoughtful hospitality and service customers expect from JetBlue with exceptional value and comfort,” said Joanna Geraghty, JetBlue’s chief executive officer. She added that the cabin will appear on more routes as JetBlue brings it to more aircraft.

Members of JetBlue’s TrueBlue Mosaic frequent flyer tiers will be able to redeem new Premium Upgrade Certificates for BlueFirst or Mint, and Mosaic members on eligible fares can receive free space-available upgrades before departure. JetBlue said it will share details on those upgrades ahead of launch.

The rollout is anchored in Fort Lauderdale, where JetBlue has expanded since Spirit Airlines shut down in May. That same month, JetBlue announced it would end its Orlando flights to Costa Rica. The new cabin gives travelers on JetBlue’s Costa Rica routes a first-class option, and it arrives during the busy holiday and high-season travel period. It also comes as US arrivals to Costa Rica fell for a second straight month in September.

World.title: US Embassy Links Chinese Mining to Illegal Gold Digging in Costa Rica, China Calls It Unfounded
World.content:
The United States Embassy in Costa Rica has accused Chinese mining companies operating in Nicaragua of driving illegal gold extraction across the border into northern Costa Rica, drawing a sharp rebuttal from the Chinese Embassy in San José. In a recent Facebook post, the U.S. Embassy said Chinese mining firms in Nicaragua often use abusive tactics, including forcing artisanal miners to sell their gold below market price.

According to the embassy, those practices push more Nicaraguan miners to cross into Costa Rica to dig for gold illegally, adding pressure on the northern border. The embassy said the United States supports Costa Rica in protecting its border and fighting illegal mining. The Chinese Embassy rejected the claims as unfounded.

Responding last night, it said most mining companies in Nicaragua are North American or Latin American, and that the few Chinese firms authorized to operate there hold very limited concession areas. The Chinese Embassy questioned whether Washington was applying a double standard. It added that the Chinese government requires companies operating abroad to comply with international norms and local laws and to meet their environmental and social responsibilities.

The exchange followed a visit by U.S. Ambassador Melinda Hildebrand to the northern border area of Los Chiles. There she met Attorney General Carlo Díaz, a day after his reelection, as well as the regional office of the Judicial Investigation Agency (OIJ) and mayors from the northern region, to discuss the investigation and prosecution of human trafficking cases.

At the Las Tablillas border post, Hildebrand met Vice Minister of Government and Police Omer Badilla, Border Police Director Gerald Camacho and Professional Migration Police Director Edwin Miranda to discuss strengthening border security. Costa Rica’s government had not publicly responded to either embassy’s statements as of Saturday morning.

The dispute is not new since in March, Chinese Ambassador Wang Xiaoyao denied that Chinese companies were involved in illegal gold mining at Crucitas, near the Nicaraguan border, after then-Security Minister Mario Zamora said Chinese firms in Nicaragua were buying gold illegally extracted from Costa Rica.

Wang dismissed those statements as media propaganda. She said China had received no request from Costa Rica on the matter and that mining companies in Nicaragua were mainly Canadian or from other countries. Illegal gold mining has taken hold in parts of the northern zone for years. Local reporting has documented clandestine tunnels at Cerro Conchuditas, where hundreds of Nicaraguan miners dig out soil every day and carry it to the banks of the San Juan River for processing.

Lawmakers have moved to treat illegal mining as organized crime, and a group of geologists has called for a referendum on gold mining at Crucitas. The northern border has become a growing focus of security cooperation between Costa Rica and the United States, which has also included U.S. surveillance support against drug trafficking at sea.

World.title: International News: Thousands rally for Lula and Bolsonaro as Brazil braces for tight Presidential runoff
World.content:
International News: Thousands rally for Lula and Bolsonaro as Brazil braces for tight Presidential runoff

By Zoila Palma: Thousands of supporters of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing senator Flávio Bolsonaro took to the streets today as the candidates made their final appeals ahead of a closely contested presidential runoff election. Lula supporters filled Rio de Janeiro’s Copacabana beach with the red colours of his Workers’ Party, while hundreds of bikers and other supporters rallied behind Bolsonaro in Belo Horizonte.

The rallies capped a bitter campaign that has deepened political divisions in Latin America’s largest country, AFP reports.

Lula, who turns 81 next week, waved a large Brazilian flag from a campaign truck as he addressed the crowd in Rio de Janeiro. He urged voters to choose between someone who respects Brazil’s national flag and someone who embraces the American flag.

Meanwhile, Bolsonaro’s supporters expressed confidence in his chances after he secured 47 percent of the vote in the first round, compared with Lula’s 45 percent.

A Datafolha Institute poll released during the week showed the candidates tied at 50 percent of voting intentions.

The election has drawn attention across the region as Brazil considers whether to continue under left-wing leadership or join a broader political shift toward the right.

World.title: BDF’s Lt. Col. Kenroy Smith receives prestigious Brazilian military aviation honour
World.content:
BDF’s Lt. Col. Kenroy Smith receives prestigious Brazilian military aviation honour

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A Belize Defence Force officer has been honoured by the Brazilian Air Force.

Lieutenant Colonel Kenroy Smith, Commanding Officer of the BDF Air Wing, was awarded the Order of Aeronautical Merit in the grade of Grand Officer.

The award was presented by Brazil’s Ambassador to Belize, His Excellency Olyntho Vieira, during a ceremony at the Embassy of Brazil in Belmopan on Friday, October 23, as part of Brazilian Aviation Day.

The Order of Aeronautical Merit is a distinguished decoration of the Brazilian Air Force, recognizing outstanding service and exceptional contributions to military aviation and aeronautical development.

The BDF says the honour reflects Lt. Col. Smith’s significant contributions to military aviation, regional cooperation and stronger ties between the BDF and Brazil’s armed forces.

The Commander and members of the BDF congratulated him, saying his dedication and professionalism continue to bring distinction to the Force and to Belize.

World.title: International News: Vance becomes 11th Pacific hurricane this season
World.content:
International News: Vance becomes 11th Pacific hurricane this season

By Zoila Palma: Hurricane Vance became the 11th major hurricane of the 2026 central and eastern Pacific hurricane season on Friday, as meteorologists monitored its movement toward Mexico’s west-central coast.

According to AccuWeather, the storm briefly reached Category 3 status on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale, with maximum sustained winds of at least 111 miles per hour. Forecasters are tracking multiple possible scenarios, including one in which the hurricane remains offshore and another in which it turns toward the Mexican coast.

Vance developed after an area of disturbed weather strengthened into a tropical depression on Wednesday before becoming a tropical storm four hours later. It intensified into a hurricane early Friday, with sustained winds reaching 90 miles per hour by 9 a.m. Friday.

AccuWeather Hurricane Expert Alex DaSilva said the storm could remain over open waters but warned that a northeast turn toward Mexico’s west-central coast could result in more dangerous conditions.

World.title: Belize Coast Guard cadet Elvis Solis completes major milestone in Mexico
World.content:
Belize Coast Guard cadet Elvis Solis completes major milestone in Mexico

By Zoila Palma: The Belize Coast Guard (BCG) is congratulating Cadet Elvis Solis on successfully completing four years of academic and military training in Naval Nursing at the Centro de Estudios Navales en Ciencias de la Salud (CENCIS), under Mexico’s Naval University. The achievement marks a significant milestone in his journey toward becoming a qualified naval nurse.

Solis’s accomplishment reflects the Belize Coast Guard’s continued investment in developing its future leaders and specialized personnel. The training equips cadets with the academic knowledge and military skills necessary to support healthcare services within the naval force.

Following the successful completion of this phase of training, Solis will be commissioned into the Belize Coast Guard at the rank of Lieutenant Junior Grade before proceeding to his fifth and final year of professional training.

Upon successfully completing the final year, he will qualify for a Bachelor’s Degree in Naval Nursing.

The Belize Coast Guard commended Solis for his dedication, perseverance and commitment to excellence.

The Belize Coast Guard also expressed appreciation to the Government of Mexico and the Mexican Navy for their continued partnership and support in advancing the professional development of Belizean personnel.

World.title: BDF officer cadets participate in selection process for U.S. Army Officer candidate school
World.content:
BDF officer cadets participate in selection process for U.S. Army Officer candidate school

By Zoila Palma: Belize Defence Force (BDF) officer cadets have participated in a selection process for the opportunity to attend the United States Army Officer Candidate School (OCS), marking an important step in their military careers and professional development.

The process provides aspiring officers with an opportunity to demonstrate their readiness for the responsibilities of commissioned service.

The selection process is intended to identify candidates prepared to meet the demands of military leadership and serve with dedication. For the participating cadets, the opportunity represents more than selection, as it also involves preparing to lead with integrity, accept responsibility and uphold the professional standards expected of a BDF officer.

The Commander of the Belize Defence Force commended all participating officer cadets for their dedication and willingness to undertake the challenge of pursuing professional development through OCS. The Commander noted that their ambition reflects the importance of developing capable leaders who can contribute meaningfully to the Force and the country.

The BDF Force Headquarters and Training and Doctrine Battalion extended their best wishes to the candidates as they continue their journey toward commissioned service.

World.title: Belize Defence Force Air Wing commander receives Brazilian Order of Aeronautical Merit
World.content:
Belize Defence Force Air Wing commander receives Brazilian Order of Aeronautical Merit

By Zoila Palma: Lieutenant Colonel Kenroy Smith, Commanding Officer of the Belize Defence Force (BDF) Air Wing, has been awarded the Order of Aeronautical Merit in the grade of Grand Officer (Grande Oficial) by the Government of Brazil.

The award was presented by Brazil’s Ambassador to Belize, Olyntho Vieira, during a ceremony at the Brazilian Embassy in Belmopan on October 23, 2026, as part of the observance of Brazilian Aviation Day.

The Order of Aeronautical Merit is a distinguished Brazilian Air Force decoration that recognizes outstanding service and exceptional contributions to military aviation and aeronautical development.

Smith’s recognition highlights his contributions to advancing military aviation, strengthening regional cooperation and building professional ties between the Belize Defence Force and Brazil’s armed forces.

The BDF congratulated Smith on the achievement, commending his dedication, professionalism and commitment to excellence.

The BDF also expressed appreciation to the Government and people of Brazil for their longstanding support in defence, security, training and military professional development.

World.title: Belize marks United Nations Day, celebrates work of 22 UN agencies
World.content:
Belize marks United Nations Day, celebrates work of 22 UN agencies

By Zoila Palma: Belize joins the international community today in commemorating United Nations Day, marking the 81st anniversary of the global organization.

The occasion highlights the work of 22 United Nations agencies operating in Belize, 12 of which are based in the country, supporting development initiatives in partnership with the Government, civil society and local communities.

United Nations Day commemorates the entry into force of the UN Charter on October 24, 1945, which officially established the organization.

The annual observance provides an opportunity to reaffirm the principles of peace, international cooperation, equality and sustainable development that guide the United Nations in its efforts to address global challenges and promote a better future for all.

In Belize, the work of UN agencies and their partners focuses on creating opportunities for people and building a more inclusive, resilient and sustainable country.

This year’s observance also highlights the importance of collaboration in advancing human dignity and ensuring that no one is left behind.

Special Envoy Rossana Briceno said the day celebrates the power of unity, peace and international cooperation, encouraging renewed commitment to equality and sustainable development.

World.title: International News: France deploys 70,000 police as demonstrations continue over cost of living
World.content:
International News: France deploys 70,000 police as demonstrations continue over cost of living

By Zoila Palma: Thousands of demonstrators gathered in Paris and other French cities today as authorities deployed 70,000 police officers to prevent a repeat of the riots and looting that swept across the country the previous weekend, Reuters report.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 135 people had been arrested nationwide by early afternoon, with some arrests following searches that uncovered fireworks, ball bearings and other items that could be used as weapons.

The heightened security measures included the deployment of 10,000 additional police officers and gendarmes compared with October 17, when protests over the cost of living and deteriorating public services escalated into some of France’s worst unrest in years.

While the main demonstration in Paris began peacefully, police fired tear gas at crowds in Lyon, the country’s third-largest city. Nunez warned that authorities faced significant calls for disruption from political groups and criminals.

Much of central Paris took on the appearance of a city under lockdown, with businesses boarding up storefronts, major cultural institutions closing and more than 20 metro stations shutting down.

World.title: Beenie Man faces Trinidadian backlash again, seeks to clear air
World.content:
Dancehall artiste Beenie Man

For the second time in just under two years, dancehall superstar Beenie Man is seeking to clear the air after offending the people of Trinidad and Tobago.

The Girls Dem Sugar deejay stirred controversy earlier this week when, during an interview on New York’s Hot 97, he apparently suggsted that Jamaica started carnival celebrations before Trinidad and Tobago, attributing its origins to late Jamaican music pioneer Byron Lee.

Carnival has deep historical roots in Trinidad and Tobago and several other Caribbean islands, with the celebration originating during the period of slavery. In contrast, Jamaica only began celebrating carnival on a national level in the early 1990s.

Against that background, Beenie Man has been chided across social media since his remarks surfaced online.

On Saturday, in a video posted to social media, he said his comments were misconstrued.

“Let me clear up this with love for you, I was just only speaking about my experience with carnival in Jamaica and the role that Byron Lee play in our carnival,” Beenie Man said. “I could never ever come and steal away nothing from Trinidad.

“I don’t speak with Trinidad with hate, I love Trinidad… and I know that Trinidad loves me,” he added.

He further clarified: “My experience with Byron Lee and what he has done for carnival is the big [truck] and the road march, and marching with the streets with the music… this is my experience that I grew up in my country… So please don’t get me wrong, Trinidad carnival is Trinidad carnival, it started from way back when.”

In February 2025, the dancehall icon apologised to Trinidadians over comments he made on ‘doubles’, a popular food item in the twin island republic.

READ: Beenie Man gives heartfelt apology to Trinidadians in ‘doubles’ spat

In an interview on popular US podcast Drink Champs, the Who Am I singer said that a soca artiste had told him that stray dogs won’t eat doubles and he decided to try a little behavioural experiment to test the hypothesis with the channa-and-bara favourite. But the stray dog declined.

World.title: Security forces reacted to deadly force at Sligoville – McKay
World.content:
Jason McKay

Criminologist Dr Jason McKay has warned against “Monday-morning-quarterbacking” in the wake of the deadly shootout involving members of the security forces last week, which resulted in the death of two policemen and three alleged gunmen in Sligoville, St Catherine.

McKay, a trained hostage negotiator and serving member of the Jamaica Constabulary Force (JCF) assigned to the St Catherine South Special Operations team, pointed to questions raised in the media by former commissioner of police, Rear Admiral Hardley Lewin, and Security Consultant Robert Finzi-Smith.

Addressing the deadly standoff in which a 10-year-old girl was shot and injured, allegedly used as a human shield by the occupants, Rear Admiral Lewin questioned whether “there was an alternative way of dealing with this?”, suggesting the security forces had enough time to coax a possible surrender.

“There was, available to the operation, some 12 hours of daylight,” Rear Admiral Lewin remarked, referring to the firefight sparked by a 5:15 am attempt by the security forces to apprehend “criminals and wanted persons” in the Five/Six Mile area of Sligoville.

“It’s not something that was dusk. There are things that would have to be looked at, in any hot-washer that the police would do, to look at whether there was an alternative way of dealing with this. Did the men have a chance of escaping? Who was in that room that might be innocent?” Rear Admiral Lewin asked, questioning the tactics employed by the security forces.

However, McKay, who stood by as an International Cricket Council-required JCF hostage negotiator for any eventuality that might have arisen at the 2007 Cricket World Cup staged in Jamaica, pointed to specific circumstances under which a negotiator would be called in as opposed to additional support from tactical teams.

“Hostage negotiators generally get involved if there is a lull during a shooting. There was no lull. It was either constant or sporadic gunfire coming from the house, even during what appeared to be conversations between the occupants and the security forces, creating a high level of distrust among the police during which two of their own were shot and killed.

“Hostage negotiations do not take place in the middle of shootouts. Once there is sustained or sporadic shooting, it is the tactical operators who handle active shooting scenes,” McKay pointed out.

A widely-circulated 18-minute long telephone conversation involving two men engaging members of the security forces, indicating their willingness to leave the house, while claiming there was only one shooter, has been the subject of widespread debate.

One of the men was overheard encouraging the 10-year-old to scream, which, McKay said, could have been coercion to deceive the police, pointing out that even while the men were engaging the security forces a shot rang out from inside the house, triggering gunfire from what was by then a joint military-police team.

Finzi-Smth, former senior director, safety and security, at the University of Technology, alluded to the number of rounds fired by the security forces while there were “non-combatants in the house”, an assertion McKay called out as being not from an informed position.

“It became obvious that there were non-combatants in the house,” said Finzi-Smith. “You fire aimed shots. You don’t fire shots that find wherever they want to find, especially when there are non-combatants in the way,” he stated.

McKay, however, pointed out that before such an assertion can be made, one would have to determine at which point the greater volume of firepower was laid down by the police, whether the gun battle intensified after the child was removed.

“It is difficult to determine whether the bulk of the police’s shooting was during or after the child was out of the house. There was a point in time that the situation would have become a subject barricaded with a high-powered firearm.

“It is easy to Monday-morning-quarter back but, it is my personal opinion that if you are not the one going through the experience, being mindful that two of your fellow officers were killed after the initial engagement, enough gunfire to wound other security-forces personnel, the rate of return-fire would have been unquestionably above average.

“It was a threatening situation that had already proven to be deadly,” McKay reminded, pointing to his experiences of being involved in high-risk entries as a member of a special-operations team for almost 25 years.

World.title: Holness signals imminent changes to tackle red tape
World.content:
Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness speaks during the official launch of the Jamaica Reconstruction and Resilience Oversight Committee (JAMRROC) at Jamaica House in Kingston, where he addressed the ongoing recovery of Jamaica’s education system and defended the use of outdoor spaces for learning while some schools undergo repairs following Hurricane Melissa. (Photo: Karl Mclarty)

Prime Minister Andrew Holness says in the coming days the government will be announcing measures aimed at increasing efficiency across Government, making the bureaucracy more functional and improving service delivery to Jamaicans post-Hurricane Melissa.

The prime minister says the changes are necessary to increase the capacity of the Government to respond to current challenges.

Holness gave the update when he addressed a group of private sector leaders who attended an event on Thursday at the Terra Nova Hotel in St Andrew. The event was hosted by Cabinet Minister Daryl Vaz.

“We are a free country socially, but we are not a free country economically,” Holness said. “If we are going to address the issue of poverty in our country, we must address the issue of our bureaucuracy.

“We can’t get rid of bureaucracy, but we must make our bureaucracy make sense, it must be efficient,” the prime minister said.

The prime minister pointed to red tape for the lengthy time it has taken for the delivery of modular homes to families impacted by Hurricane Melissa.

“We imported the modular houses almost six months ago, and we are still not able to have them rolled out and built quickly… between the logistics, the contracting, the permitting, procurement, it is as if no one cares that it’s an emergency,” Holness said.

He said it was critical that Jamaicans in need are able to receive assistance much more quickly to mitigate their distress and improve their well-being and welfare.

“In the coming days, the government will be making certain announcements which will signal a change in how we do business,” Holness said.

World.title: Derrick Harriott, celebrated singer and producer, dead at 87
World.content:
Derrick Harriott

KINGSTON, Jamaica — Derrick Harriott, the reggae and rocksteady singer and producer known for hits including The Loser, has died.

The iconic Jamaican singer began his career as part of a duo in his teens alongside Claude Sang, gaining recognition after winning the Vere Johns Opportunity Hour talent contest as early as 1957.

Harriott would become part of a group, the Jiving Juniors, before going solo in the 1960s and releasing hits including What Can I Do and I’m Only Human.

He was also a talented producer, presiding over successful albums for several other artistes including DJ Scotty and Dennis Brown.

Harriott, whose discography encompassed sounds of ska, rocksteady and reggae, was awarded the Order of Distinction in 2009 for his contribution to the development of music locally.

Harriott was 87 at the time of his passing

World.title: Money worries
World.content:
JETS moved to allay fears that its MultiLink system, on which automated banking machines (ABMs) heavily rely, was not impacted by a recent cyberattack on its systems.

THERE were jitters in Jamaica’s financial sector on Friday as the operators of the MultiLink debit card and Automated Clearing House (ACH) networks confirmed that sections of its system had been the subject of a cyberattack.

In an early morning release Jamaica Electronic Transfer Services (JETS) said the cyberattack, which had been circulating as a rumour since Thursday, involved a limited part of its internal administrative systems, but the MultiLink and ACH networks were not affected and both remained fully operational.

“The JETS Cyber Monitoring Team detected suspicious activity within a limited portion of the company’s domain and immediately shut down the administrative system, isolated and launched a full forensic investigation in coordination with specialist cybersecurity consultants.

“While payment networks were not affected, there were reports with payment transactions accessed by the hackers that contain information that may have exposed the names of some customers who received transfers via ACH, as well as some card numbers from historical administrative data files on the debit network,” said JETS.

“It is important to note, however, that personal identification numbers (PINs), card verification values (CVV), and expiry dates are never stored and would not have been impacted,” added JETS as it sought to allay fears of people in the financial sector and members of the public.

According to JETS, both it and its member institutions have employed necessary and vital steps to protect the integrity of the payment systems and customer information.

“Customers of member institutions are, however, encouraged to observe standard digital-safety practices and contact their individual financial institutions should they receive unsolicited communication about their card or account,” said JETS.

By mid-afternoon Friday, the Bank of Jamaica (BOJ) also moved to quiet fears in the financial sector with a media release stating that it has been engaged with JETS, its member financial institutions, and the relevant national authorities since being informed of the incident.

According to the BOJ, with JETS confirming that the MultiLink and ACH networks were not affected and remain fully operational, customers can continue to use their debit cards and make ACH payments as usual.
