World.title: Iraqi PM adviser accuses Iran of severe border violations and smuggling
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A senior adviser to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has openly accused Iran of orchestrating deliberate security breaches, widespread drug smuggling, and illicit financial flows across the border, marking a rare and pointed public rebuke from within Baghdad’s executive circle as Iraq shuttered key commercial crossing points.

Speaking to domestic media, prime ministerial adviser Abdelamir Taiban stated that Tehran has actively undermined Iraqi internal stability by allowing unauthorized, affiliated networks to bypass border protocols, inciting borderland disorder.

Taiban noted that Iraqi nationals have faced abductions after entering Iranian territory, identifying the areas surrounding the Shalamcheh terminal in Basra and the Al-Sheeb terminal in Maysan as high-risk corridors. He urged the federal government to aggressively scale electronic monitoring and comprehensive automation across every operational terminal along the shared 1,599-kilometer frontier.

The adviser characterized the inbound traffic of narcotics and counterfeit currency as the most damaging economic threat facing the nation, asserting that the resulting market sabotage has inflicted financial disruption outpacing the economic fallout previously caused by ISIS.

The remarks follow the indefinite closure of the Al-Sheeb port of entry in Maysan governorate to both travelers and commercial cargo—a measure following the precautionary shutdown of Shalamcheh in September amid regional drone incidents—which prompted demonstrations by local transport operators and cross-border truckers concerned over disrupted trade in fresh produce and construction materials.

In response, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi convened the Ministerial Council for National Security, ordering security units to safeguard peaceful assemblies while maintaining stringent checks to intercept illicit trafficking channels.

World.title: US dollar dips to 168,500 IQD following Zaidi’s remarks on cash inflows
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar retreated by approximately 1,000 dinars per $100 across parallel market trading desks on Saturday, October 24, 2026.

The softening followed public statements delivered on Friday by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, in which he disclosed that Washington will dispatch $1 billion in physical cash shipments to Iraq and assured the public that parallel rates will soon decline toward 155,000 dinars per $100.

The remarks stemmed upward momentum that had pushed dollar transactions across domestic exchange bureaus to 169,500 dinars on Thursday and Friday, driving the prevailing market benchmark down to 168,500 dinars.

Across major trading hubs in Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra, foreign exchange desks and licensed counters posted identical rates on Saturday morning, listing cash selling quotes at 169,000 dinars against buying bids of 168,500 dinars per $100.

Despite the temporary retreat, parallel figures continue to maintain a notable spread over the Central Bank of Iraq’s official statutory cash peg, which remains set at 152,000 dinars per $100.

The divergence highlights persistent liquidity dynamics and demand pressures outside central electronic settlement channels, even as executive assurances of incoming dollar consignments aim to stabilize market sentiment and curb speculative price premiums.

World.title: US State Department reissues Level 4 ‘Do Not Travel’ advisory for Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. Department of State issued a renewed travel advisory on Saturday, October 24, 2026, maintaining its highest “Level 4: Do Not Travel” warning for Iraq and urging American citizens to avoid travel to the country under any circumstances.

According to the advisory, Washington cited the inability of Iraqi authorities to guarantee the safety of foreign nationals in the event of sudden armed conflict or localized violence, while emphasizing the U.S. government’s severely constrained capacity to execute emergency evacuations or consular relief operations inside Iraqi territory.

The State Department warned of acute security and public health vulnerabilities, citing risks from terrorism, kidnappings, civil unrest, and frequent asymmetric strikes. It specified recurring hazards from improvised explosive devices (IEDs), unmanned aerial systems, and indirect rocket fire conducted by Iran-aligned armed groups and remnants of ISIS against U.S. personnel, diplomatic compounds, commercial companies, energy installations, and commercial airports.

The advisory also drew attention to regional escalation vectors—including cross-border hostilities conducted by the Houthi movement—as well as widespread unmarked minefields and UXO hazards, aviation restrictions implemented under Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) notices, and severe structural shortages across Iraq’s trauma and emergency medical infrastructure.

In response to sustained security threats, strict operating restrictions remain enforced on U.S. diplomatic personnel, requiring special authorization for in-country travel and residency within heavily fortified protocols.

For private American citizens currently residing in Iraq, the State Department urged immediate contingency planning independent of U.S. governmental assistance, including enrolling in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP), drafting emergency wills and power-of-attorney designations, leaving DNA reference samples with family medical providers, securing private medical and emergency evacuation insurance, and developing comprehensive personal departure protocols.

World.title: Iraqi FM Fuad Hussein condemns deadly church attack in Jordan’s Karak
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein held a telephone conversation on Friday, October 23, 2026, with Jordan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates, Ayman Safadi, strongly condemning the deadly armed attack that targeted mourners at a church in Jordan’s southern Karak Governorate.

During the call, Hussein conveyed Iraq’s full solidarity with the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan in confronting terrorism and violent extremism.

The Iraqi foreign minister extended the government and people of Iraq’s heartfelt condolences to the leadership, government, and citizens of Jordan, as well as to the families of the victims, while wishing a swift recovery to those injured.

The diplomatic outreach followed a shooting incident earlier on Friday, in which unidentified gunmen opened fire during a funeral service at a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hmoud, located in Karak Governorate approximately 180 kilometers south of Amman.

The attack left at least seven people dead and dozens wounded, prompting heightened security deployments and an active manhunt by Jordanian security agencies.

World.title: Ukraine says two soldiers died after arrested girl sent Russian poison
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukrainian police said Friday they had detained a 17-year-old girl suspected of helping Russia’s security services to poison Ukrainian soldiers and that two had died.

Ukraine and Russia have throughout their war since 2022 accused each other of recruiting minors for sabotage acts including poisoning.

The girl, who was not named, is suspected of having packaged deadly drugs and sending them to Ukrainian soldiers she contacted by Telegram, said a police statement.

She was arrested by police in Zhytomyr, west of Kyiv, after allegedly following instructions from a Russian handler in exchange for at least 5,000 hryvnias ($111), they said.

After receiving packages with “free drugs”, the soldiers were “instructed to take them on camera”, the statement said.

“The recipients did not know that the capsules contained a lethal dose of methadone,” it said, adding that “two soldiers died from poisoning in the Zhytomyr region.”

Police said they had identified other recipients of the packages, which “prevented four more murders” across the country.

“The young woman was notified that she is suspected of aiding and abetting the premeditated murder of two people as part of a prior conspiracy,” the police statement said.

She was also suspected of “shipping drugs and psychotropic substances for the purpose of distribution”, it said, adding that she faced up to 15 years in jail if found guilty.

Police cautioned that Russia aims “to kill our people and destabilise the situation within the country”.

“Do not accept medication or other substances, as well as food or drinks of dubious origin, from people you do not know well,” police cautioned.

Since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, Ukrainian authorities say they have opened thousands of investigations into collaboration with the enemy, and frequently arrest individuals accused of working for Moscow.

In 2023, Ukraine accused Russia of poisoning the wife of Kyrylo Budanov, who was then head of Ukraine’s military intelligence and is now a presidential advisor.

World.title: Volvo Cars shares plunge on losses, job cuts
World.content:
Stockholm – Shares in Swedish carmaker Volvo Cars plunged Friday after it said US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarter loss.

The company also said it would cut about 2,500 jobs worldwide.

Volvo Cars, controlled by Chinese group Geely, reported revenue of 66.9 billion kronor ($6.7 billion) for the third quarter, down nearly 23 percent from the same period last year.

It swung to a net loss of 5.7 billion kronor for the quarter from a net profit of 4.5 billion kronor a year earlier.

Shortly after 0800 GMT, Volvo Cars shares were down almost 30 percent.

“We continue to operate in a very tough environment with strong external challenges: de-globalisation, hypercompetition and climate change,” chief executive Hakan Samuelsson said in a statement.

In response, the company announced a new five-billion-kronor savings plan it said would lead to about 2,000 job cuts in Sweden and 500 more globally, “through natural attrition and by targeted exit packages to employees”.

The company, which had bet heavily on electric vehicles, said the removal of consumer incentives for EVs in the United States under President Donald Trump had also hit its margins.

In 2024, Volvo Cars dropped a plan to transition to exclusively EV sales by the end of the decade.

“We are convinced that we have the right long-term strategy addressing these challenges,” Samuelsson said.

“However, in the short term, with severely challenged volumes, we need to reinforce our turnaround plan with additional decisive actions, lowering our break-even point and improving cash flows to make us more resilient.”

Struggling along with other European auto companies in the face of a difficult global landscape, Volvo Cars last year announced an 18-billion-kronor cost-cutting plan.

The company said in September that Samuelsson would resign when his contract ends, with Skoda Auto CEO Klaus Zellmer set to replace him “no later” than October next year.

World.title: France braces for new protests as Macron seeks to restore order
World.content:
Paris – France was on Friday bracing for a weekend of new protests after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago, as President Emmanuel Macron sought to reclaim the initiative and restore order.

Macron, who on Thursday announced that only union demonstrations would be authorised this weekend, was to hold a meeting of his defence council of top ministers and officials and also meet security forces.

He was also set to host for the first time representatives of high school pupils, whose protests over conditions at their schools sparked a movement that has broadened nationwide into a show of anger against the government at the rising cost of living.

The protests have come at a critical moment for France six months ahead of elections to replace Macron, with a new poll underlining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the frontrunner and showing her position has been strengthened by the latest events.

Adding to tensions, Le Pen is at the weekend due to host her National Rally (RN) party congress in Orleans, with thousands of supporters expected but local authorities fearing clashes as opponents head to the city.

Macron is due to announce “additional decisions” after hosting the meeting of his defence council, on top of the limited curfews already announced, his office said.

At the meeting with students, “we will present our demands to him — which remain the same: the state of school infrastructure and an overhaul of the Parcoursup (university admissions) system,” Nathanael Combary, president of Renouveau Lyceen (High School Renewal) told AFP.

Pierre Sourzat, who heads the organisation Les Lyceens (The High School Students), was sceptical: “He’ll listen to us, pretend he’s understood us, and then nothing will come of it.”

Macron’s government has sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of protests last Saturday.

In a judicial response of unprecedented firmness, courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said.

On Thursday, Macron called for “the utmost severity” against “acts of delinquency”, accusing “ultra-left” groups of having sought to “bring down the republic” last weekend.

– ‘Police have a responsibility’ –

Demonstrations in Marseille in the south and Lyon in the southeast have been banned at the weekend, while in Paris protesters will only be allowed to march a limited route between Bastille and Nation squares.

Marseille authorities however reversed a decision to halt all public transport in the city on Saturday. But in the capital, leading museums including the Louvre will be closed on Saturday while the Art Basel art fair is being cut short.

Some 20 percent more members of the security forces will be deployed this weekend after heavy criticism of the anticipation and intelligence gathering of police last week.

“In a country governed by the rule of law, the police have a responsibility both to ensure that protests can take place peacefully and safely and to protect the public from violent disorder,” said Eva Cosse, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch, expressing alarm over reports of children being severely injured by crowd-control weapons.

The violence has tarnished the image of France ahead of elections that could be a turning point in its modern history, with the government’s debt pile also troubling investors.

A new poll by Harris Interactive for M6/RTL made after the violence showed Le Pen soaring ahead on 33-35 percent in the first round of voting for the presidential elections.

It predicted that hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon was on course to face her in the run-off where Le Pen would emerge as an easy winner on some 70 percent of the vote.

World.title: Kering shares tumble as Gucci fails to reassure investors
World.content:
Paris – Kering shares were down more than 10 percent in Paris Friday after the French luxury group published results that failed to reassure investors about a turnaround at its key Gucci brand.

At 0730 GMT, Kering shares were down 10.8 percent at 190.40 euros, their lowest since June 2025. The market’s CAC40 index was down 0.3 percent.

Kering reported late Thursday that third-quarter sales were flat at 3.34 billion euros ($3.75 billion).

Sales at Gucci, by far the group’s largest single brand, fell by four percent to 1.29 billion euros, worse than the three-percent decline registered in the second quarter.

“Gucci has not shown convincing signs of stabilisation,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note.

Italy-based Gucci is key to Kering’s fortunes, but has been in freefall since 2023 as the brand lost its luxury cachet.

World.title: No EC nod needed for voter to sue candidate over false information: Supreme Court
World.content:
The Supreme Court said that Section 125-A was inserted in the RoP Act in 2002.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A voter can now not only cast a vote in an election but can also drag an election candidate to court and initiate criminal proceedings for lying and furnishing a false declaration as Supreme Court has ruled that a complaint filed by a private person alleging an offence under Section 125-A of Representation of People Act (filing false affidavit) is maintainable and the Election Commissionâs nod was not needed.Explaining the interplay between Section 125-A of Representation of People Act and Section 195(1) of the CrPC which says that no court shall take cognisance of any offences punishable under sections 172 to 188, including the offence of furnishing false information to a public servant, the top court held that Section 125A of RoP Act does not come within the ambit of Section 195 of CrPC and a court can take cognisance of a private complaint. The courtâs ruling will further empower the electorate against candidates who lied in their affidavits.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed the Karnataka HC order which had held that âright given to the voter is only to file an election petition, and not to register a private complaint of crime which is the duty of the Election Commission, if it wants to do soâ.SC said that Section 125-A was inserted in the RoP Act in 2002, while Section 195 of CrPC was amended in 2006, and that the omission of the legislature to include Section 125-A of the RoP Act in Section 195 of CrPC was deliberate and no court would be barred from taking cognisance of an alleged offence under Section 125-A of the RoP Act, even on the complaint lodged by a private person.âShould we read into Section 195 of CrPC a prohibition in respect of Section 125-A of the RoP Act also, apart from those expressly included? If indeed it were the intention of the legislature that cognisance of any offence relating to furnishing of false information by a candidate in an affidavit with intent of being elected in an election (referred to in Section 125-A of the RoP Act) could only be taken if the complainant were a public servant, the same could have been provided by an amendment of Section 195, CrPC since Section 125-A of the RoP Act is of fairly recent origin. âSC also refused to give credence to the ECâs press note that it can take cognisance of such complaints and refer such matters to the relevant investigating authorities on a case-to-case basis. â...Even though the ECI is supreme in its own sphere and has, indeed, issued guidelines/press notes based on its understanding of the statutory provisions, interpretation of statutes is primarily the task of the courts and such guidelines/press notes do not bind us,â the court said.It said that Karnataka HC erred in holding that a private complaint cannot be filed for an offence under Section 125A of RoP Act which is punishable up to six months of jail term. The HC had interpreted the provision solely upon reading the letter issued by the Election Commission of India on the issue which was rejected by the apex court.Allaying the apprehension that allowing the lodging of a criminal complaint by a private person would be misused and frivolous cases would be filed by political rivals, SC said, âIf at all a complaint is lodged to harass an elected candidate or frivolous allegations are levelled therein, the laws of the country duly empower the competent magistrates to pass such order(s) as they deem fit and proper commensurate with the facts and circumstances of each case. â

World.title: Daughter’s inheritance rights can’t be defeated by limitation: J&K and Ladakh high court
World.content:
JAMMU: The high court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh has restored a womanâs right to inherit her fatherâs property after a 44-year-long legal battle, holding that an adverse revenue entry recorded during when she was a minor cannot automatically defeat a legitimate inheritance claim on limitation grounds.

The dispute dates back to Sept 14, 1982, when Themu, daughter of late Sonu, filed a civil suit claiming half share in land measuring 58 kanals and 11 marlas left behind by her father.

She challenged mutation no. 43 dated Oct 15, 1966, which had been entered exclusively in favour of one Shib Devi and sought declaration of her inheritance rights along with consequential possession.

On March 9, 2004, the sub-judge court in Kishtwar passed a decree recognising her entitlement.

However, the district judge reversed the decree on Nov 7, 2012, primarily on the grounds of limitation and failure to establish paternity.

Justice Shahzad Azeem of the HC, while allowing the appeal filed by Themu, set aside the judgment of the district judge, Kishtwar, observing that limitation cannot be determined on presumptions and conjectures, particularly where the claimant was a minor when her rights were initially disputed and the defendants failed to establish when the cause of action actually arose.

World.title: ‘PMLA case not examined’: ED moves Supreme Court against HC order quashing proceedings against NewsClick
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

(ED) has moved the Supreme Court challenging the

âs order

a money laundering case against news portal NewsClick and its editor-in-chief, Prabir Purkayastha, over alleged violations of foreign direct investment (FDI) rules.

The ED argued that the high court quashed its Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) without examining the merits of the case under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). It also flagged a five-month delay in the pronouncement of the judgment.

The matter is yet to be listed for hearing.

Why Delhi HC quashed ED's case against NewsClick

In a judgment dated May 29, Justice Neena Bansal Krishna of the Delhi high court described the continuation of an FIR registered by the Delhi Policeâs Economic Offences Wing (EOW) as ânothing but a gross abuse of the process of lawâ.

The judge held that quashing the FIR for the predicate offence also warranted the closure of the EDâs ECIR.

Also Read |

The court ruled that the investment was an "economic decision that did not spell out any criminal offenceâ. Citing the Union ministry of information and broadcastingâs reply to NewsClick, Justice Krishna noted there was no cap or restriction on FDI in digital media at the time.

The single-judge bench ruled that the investment followed acceptable practices and that the allegations, even if accepted, did not establish cheating or criminal breach of trust.





The alleged victim in the cheating case should have been M/s Worldwide Media Holdings LLC, but the company had filed no complaint. Instead, the complaint came from âmerely an informantâ.

Justice Krishna also rejected the fund-siphoning allegation, noting that a digital media company would naturally incur expenses on salaries, consultation fees and rent.

The high court further dismissed the EDâs attempt to sustain the money laundering case on the basis of criminal conspiracy under the IPC, holding that the agency must establish the âillegal objectiveâ or âmeansâ allegedly adopted by NewsClick and others.

âPertinently, extensive investigations were carried out by the ED for about a year and a half, and the petitioners as well as their employees have been summoned and examined many a times, but nothing incriminating till date has been found or placed on record," the order said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âAside from bald assertions of a criminal conspiracy, there is not a whisper of any incriminating allegation, which would even remotely suggest the commission of the offence punishable under Section 4 of the PMLA,â it added.

The bench further stated that the request for a copy of the ECIR had become "infructuous" after the report was quashed.

The case

The EOWâs 2020 FIR alleged that PPK Newsclick Studio Pvt Ltd, NewsClickâs parent company, received Rs 9.59 crore in FDI from US-based Worldwide Media Holdings LLC in 2018-19 in violation of foreign investment rules, causing a loss to the government exchequer.

It alleged that the companyâs shares were grossly overvalued to circumvent the 26% FDI cap for digital news websites, and that over 45% of the investment was siphoned off through salaries, consultation fees and rent for ulterior motives.

The ED subsequently registered a money laundering case against NewsClick, Purkayastha and others.

PPK Newsclick Studio sought quashing of the FIR, arguing that it contained "vague" allegations.

World.title: Starshield | The non-state sovereigns
World.content:
On October 14, Ukrainian soldiers using drones to attack Russian forces in Zaporizhzhia and elsewhere started to find many of their machines were losing satellite connectivity. Given Ukraine’s extensive and largely successful use of drones in the war, the anomaly was noticeable, forcing operators to abandon missions.

Experts later traced the problem to a satellite communications service provided by U.S.-based SpaceX, called Starshield. A week later, The Wall Street Journal reported the disruption had been deliberate: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk had personally asked for the connectivity to be throttled. Where the order first originated has been disputed, in Mr. Musk’s office or in the White House. But wherever it did, the fact remains: Mr. Musk was able to take para-state action in a war between two sovereign countries. (On October 22, U.S. President Donald Trump said he had asked Mr. Musk to restore connectivity.)

SpaceX’s Starlink satellite constellation currently consists of more than 11,000 satellites in low-earth orbit that provide Internet connectivity to users on the ground. Starshield uses the same constellation to provide secure communications important to national security, with stronger data encryption; its other services, including remote-sensing, use specialised satellites. Ukraine uses Starshield because Russia’s invasion in early 2022 has damaged the eastern European nation’s telecom infrastructure.

By December 2024, the Pentagon had also arranged for Ukraine to access Starshield through roughly 3,000 terminals. Today, its forces use the service to track enemy positions and supply routes and to intercept drones, with the Starlink satellites relaying information.

Mr. Trump has been insisting Ukraine stop attacking Russia’s oil refineries over his worries about surging international oil prices, primed by his war in West Asia. When Mr. Trump objected once more on October 10, Mr. Musk chipped in that Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had gone too far. Four days later, Ukrainian soldiers felt the pinch.

Parastate powers

For decades now, private contractors have supplied armies with arms, intelligence, and logistical support. However, the armies had physical ownership of and control over many of the weapons they purchased. With Starshield, however, the provider continued to retain the ability to change the operating conditions of the ‘assistance’ even after the customer had begun using it — like a grenade launcher that could launch grenades to 150 m on most days but suddenly launched only to five metres on one, because you were not fighting your war the way the manufacturer preferred.

The existence of such an entity is the basis of Mr. Musk’s parastate power. Ordinarily, the decision to stop or withhold a country’s military operations would involve political leaders and defence officials. Now, however, Starshield has well and truly complicated the relationship between public authority and private ownership. Perhaps it was a matter of time.

In 2022, Mr. Musk refused Ukraine’s request to activate Starlink connectivity near Sevastopol, the largest city in Crimea, which Russia has annexed, to enable Ukrainian forces to target Russia’s Black Sea Fleet. Mr. Musk later expressed some consternation about the conflict escalating — a compunction he seems to have lost since, even as his own relationship with Mr. Trump has soared and plummeted. Nonetheless, the fact that the concerns of a single non-state actor could matter at all — an absurd notion in an earlier era — has become a strategic reality. Subsequent Pentagon contracts have sought, at least in part, to formalise the relationship between Starlink and the U.S. military.

Today’s armies, and their wars, increasingly depend on satellite communications, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence, all of which private contractors can develop and package at speed and deploy at scale. Musk’s actions with Starshield last week have revealed that military action had until recently depended, perhaps passively, on the lack of such speed and scale as one kind of safeguard. Now that their importance is shrinking, armies of the present and future must deliberate on what can replace them.

World.title: Amid outcry, poll body orders re-poll at three polling stations under Agra Teachers MLC seat
World.content:
Amid uproar, the Election Commission of India (ECI), on the recommendation of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Uttar Pradesh, on Saturday (October 24, 2026) declared the poll taken at polling stations No. 20, 21 and 26 of Agra Division Teachers’ Constituency as void and fixed October 26th for taking a fresh/re-poll at these polling booths.

“I am directed to refer to your letter No. 7050310-2-14/2-2025, dated 24.10.2026, on the subject cited and to state that the Commission, having considered the matter, in exercise of powers conferred under Section 58A (2)(a) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, declares the poll taken on 23rd October, 2026 at Polling Stations No. 20, 21 and 26 of Agra Division Teachers’ Constituency as void and fixes the date 26th October, 2026 (Monday) and the time 08:00 am to 04:00 pm for taking fresh/re-poll at said polling stations. It must be ensured that the persons involved in any unlawful activities which may have caused the irregularities/lapses leading to vitiation of poll are not deputed during the said re-poll,” reads a letter issued by the Secretary, Election Commission of India, to the Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh.

Earlier, in a statement, the Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh, said, “The Returning Officer of the Agra Teachers’ Constituency has recommended re-polling at three polling stations, which has been forwarded to the Election Commission of India. The three polling stations recommended for re-polling are as follows: Polling Station No. 20-Tehsil Campus Kheragarh Room No. 1, Polling Station No. 21- Area Panchayat Office Saiya Room No. 1, Polling Station No. 26- Area Panchayat Office Fatehabad Room No. 1,”.

The recent developments comes amid, the Samajwadi Party (SP) candidate from Agra Division, Teacher’s seat, Akash Agarwal has alleged irregularities and extreme harassment of his supporters during Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections on the seat and announced to change his faith, adding he do not want to live in such a Sanatan faith where he is treated as terrorist. “It feels as though I am a terrorist. I am being harassed so much. I do not want to live in such a Sanatan faith. I will go to Lucknow’s Shahi Eidgah next month and change my faith,” said Mr. Agarwal, with tears in his eyes.

The SP Akhilesh Yadav linked Mr. Agarwal’s outcry to the Agarwal community, claiming that the entire Agarwal community of Uttar Pradesh, the country, and the world is deeply hurt by these tears and alleged that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) crossed all limits of electoral malpractice. “The entire Agarwal community of Uttar Pradesh, the country, and the world is deeply hurt by these tears. To defeat the SP candidate, Dr. Akash Agarwal, in the Teacher MLC election, BJP members, their allies, and officials crossed all limits of electoral fraud. Harassed, saddened, and humiliated, Dr. Akash Agarwal is announcing a decision that has, like him, distressed the entire Agarwal community. When the time comes, we will restore the honour and respect of the entire ‘Aggarwal community’ by giving due respect and place to Dr. Akash Agarwal ji. The corrupt rule of these treacherous BJP members and their allies, who are election robbers, will no longer endure. The public will now destroy them,” wrote Mr. Yadav, on X.

World.title: Andhra Pradesh braces for very severe cyclonic storm; landfall likely between Bapatla and Vizag on October 28
World.content:
The cyclonic storm brewing over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said. It is likely to be the second highest in terms of intensity. Last year’s Montha was classified as a ‘severe cyclonic storm’.

The maximum sustained wind speed associated with a very severe cyclonic storm is likely to be between 118 km per hour and 221 km per hour. During Montha, the wind speed recorded at Machilipatnam was 65 kmph, while the wind speed this time may go up to 130 kmph, weather experts said.

According to the IMD bulletin released at 9.30 p.m. on Saturday, the well-marked low-pressure area formed over the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal on Saturday morning concentrated into a depression by the evening.

The depression lay centred over the same region, which is about 510 km off the coast of Andaman Islands, 820 km off Vishakhapatnam coast, 910 km off Kakinada coast, 1,020 km off Machilipatnam cost and 1,100 km off Bapatla coast.

The weather system is likely to intensify into a deep depression and then gradually recurve towards the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal on Sunday. It is very likely to intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the east-central and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal by Monday morning, and further intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over west-central Bay of Bengal around October 27.

Thereafter, it is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and reach the west-central Bay of Bengal near the Andhra Pradesh coast around October 28. It is very likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh​ and​ Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam ​as a very severe cyclonic storm, with the maximum sustained wind speed of 115 kmph to 125 kmph, gusting to 140 kmph​ by October 28 noon.

Meanwhile, Andhra Pradesh is bracing for the impact. The IMD has already issued a red alert for 13 districts in the State for Otober 27 and 28.

A red alert has been issued for Krishna and Bapatla districts on October 27, and for Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalli, Kakinada, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, NTR, Krishna, Guntur and Bapatla districts on October 28.

Isolated extremely heavy rainfall is expected in these districts.

The State may receive light showers on October 25 and 26, with cyclone-induced rainfall activity expected to increase from October 27.

Andhra Pradesh recorded no major rainfall activity on Saturday, with YSR Kadapa and Anantapur districts receiving widespread moderate showers. Simhadripuram in YSR Kadapa recorded 81.5 mm of rainfall between 8.30 a.m. and 5 p.m., while Malapuram in Anantapur received 74.5 mm. Other parts of Rayalaseema and south coastal Andhra Pradesh recorded light showers.

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed the officials to remain alert and take precautionary measures to deal with the situation. He called for a comprehensive plan for flood management and water conservation.

World.title: Social security, welfare fund board pensions in Keralam to be distributed from October 26
World.content:
The distribution of welfare pensions for the month of October will begin on October 26, Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan’s office has said.

The government has sanctioned ₹1,081 crore for the distribution of the social security pensions and the welfare fund board pensions.

Of this, ₹961.64 crore has been sanctioned for the social security pensions, and ₹119.46 crore for the welfare fund board pensions, the Chief Minister’s office said.

World.title: Kerala Police book social media influencer Darren for ‘communally divisive hate speech’ on Instagram
World.content:
The Kerala Police on Saturday (October 24, 2026) registered a case against social media influencer Amrit Singh Darren on the charge of creating enmity between different religious communities by seeking to other Muslims in Kochi on his Instagram handle, “littichokha_up_”.

Mr. Darren, in a video, criticises the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government for “accepting funding from Arab countries to aid promote Islam” in Keralam. The influencer singles out Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala for reproof, accusing him of standing passively as the “dangerous situation” in Keralam seemed to “slip out of our hands” unless the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led “Central government intervened”.

Diya Krishna, another social media influencer and daughter of BJP leader and chairperson of the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC), G. Krishnakumar, seemed to second the contentious and communally schismatic Instagram content by stating “Sad Reality” in the comments section.

Ms. Krishna was not immediately available to comment. Nevertheless, after the Instagram post provoked outrage in Keralam, Ms. Krishna posted on Instagram that she had not appreciated Mr. Darren’s full post and that her comment pertained to the influencer’s first few remarks.

Gandhi and Jinnah

In the first part of the video, Mr. Darren objects to the portrait of Mahatma Gandhi juxtaposed with Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the founder and first Prime Minister of Pakistan, at Kashi Art Cafe, a popular eatery in Fort Kochi. He says Jinnah has no place in India, and his portrait in the restaurant is an affront to national pride.

Mr. Darren says he had entered the restaurant, noticed the Kashi branding, and blamed the management for serving beef. He says the management should rename the joint Karachi Art Cafe rather than use the name of the ancient city Hindus consider holy. Mr. Darren also seeks to portray Kochi as overwhelmingly Islamic, despite the Union Ministry of Tourism’s Incredible India website portraying Kochi as a historically important city sculpted over the centuries by Jewish, Muslim, and Christian cultural influences.

‘Promotes enmity’

According to the FIR registered by the Fort Kochi police, the accused acted with the knowledge that his actions can disrupt peace and harmony. The case has been registered under sections 353(2) and 192 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for circulating false information with intent to create or promote feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different religious groups and giving provocation to cause riot.

Additional Director General of Police, Law and Order, P. Vijayan told The Hindu that the 10-minute video sought to portray the Muslim population in Fort Kochi as a national threat. “The social media post prima facie reveals an attempt to create enmity between communities,” he said.

‘No place for communal hatred’

Reacting to the controversy, Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan, in a statement on ‘X’, said communal hatred has no place in Keralam.

“The recent Instagram video by a vlogger from outside the State, attempting to spread misinformation about Fort Kochi, portray our State in a negative light, and divide communities, is unacceptable,” he said. Mr. Satheesan added that the UDF government remains committed to communal harmony and justice without fear or favour.

Keralam Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan, in a statement on ‘X’, said, “Fort Kochi and Varkala are places where cultures meet, histories intertwine and diversity thrives. Now, a vlogger peddling hate for profit seeks to paint these vibrant destinations in communal colours. Having failed to divide Keralam, the Sangh Parivar is outsourcing its hate campaign to online provocateurs. But Keralam’s secular spirit will not yield to their politics of hatred. The State government must take strict legal action against those spreading communal enmity.”

Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) national president A.A. Rahim, MP, told The Hindu that Mr. Darren’s post was the latest in a series of attempts to demonise Keralam, erode its religious harmony, and inject identitarian politics into a secular polity, where Christians and Muslims, among others, make up 45% of the population. He said the Sangh Parivar had bankrolled a similar attempt in 2023, when the BJP-led Central government promoted the communally inflammatory and slanderous film Kerala Story, which sought to portray Keralam as a fertile recruiting ground for Islamists.

World.title: Jamia shifts classes online amid ongoing strike over student polls
World.content:
Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) on Saturday shifted all classes online and said the campus gates, libraries and canteens would remain closed until further notice to ensure “student safety” amid an ongoing protest demanding the restoration of student union elections. The decision followed a failed attempt by the administration to “persuade” the protesters to call off their agitation, the university said in a statement.

The protesting students and the All India Students’ Association (AISA) alleged that the university staff tried to forcibly remove them from the protest site on Saturday afternoon while police deployment outside the campus increased.

The university said the decision to move classes online with immediate effect was a precautionary measure taken in view of the prevailing situation and to ensure the safety and security of students. In a notice issued on Saturday, the office of the Dean of Students’ Welfare directed students to follow their online class schedules and avoid visiting the campus until further notice.

Several students have been on a hunger strike since October 12, demanding the restoration of student union elections, which were last held in 2006 before the union was dissolved following campus violence. JMI had constituted a high-level committee on October 18 to engage with the protesting students and look into their demands.

Mantasha, an AISA member, alleged that university staff attempted to forcibly remove the protesters while faculty members watched without intervening. “None of the professors intervened when students were being dragged. Girls were being dragged by their clothes and treated badly by the Jamia administration and its staff. They were all present there and watching. We will remember this day. The Jamia administration, staff and professors should all be ashamed,” the AISA member said.

Nausheen Farooq, a student associated with the Fraternity Movement, a youth organisation, alleged that the administration’s crackdown began around 12.30 p.m., with non-teaching staff, guards and other university personnel attempting to dismantle the protest site and remove the tents.

‘Students manhandled’

“Students were being manhandled by the staff. They were attempting to clear our protest site and remove the tents. All gates were closed and students were not being allowed to enter,” Ms. Farooq said.

The students also alleged that police deployment outside the university gates has increased and several who gathered outside the campus were detained. They said they resisted the attempts to clear the protest site and would continue their agitation until their demands are met.

“We will not leave until all our demands are met and the student union is restored,” Ms. Farooq said.

In its statement, the university expressed dismay over incidents of “vandalism and the defacement” of campus walls with what it described as “highly objectionable slogans”.

The university said a gathering of faculty members and staff unanimously adopted two resolutions in a meeting held earlier in the day, including an appeal to the protesting students to vacate the Ghalib statue lawns and call off their agitation. It mentioned that Gate No. 18 was the designated site for protests and alleged that the students had occupied the Ghalib statue lawns illegally.

‘Negotiation attempts’

The university also pointed to its October 21 notification stating that disciplinary action taken or initiated against students in connection with protests over issues arising from October 12 up to 5.30 p.m. on October 21 would be reviewed. However, the administration said the move had “failed to bring the protesters to the negotiating table”.

World.title: Delay in government order for free bus travel causes difficulty for men with disabilities
World.content:
Persons with disabilities are disappointed that a government order for free travel in buses has still not been formulated. Since its announcement in the State Budget in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly in August, 2026.

While women with disabilities are automatically covered under the Vetri Payanam scheme where women and transpersons can travel in State buses for free, men with disabilities have not been included.

The announcement made by the Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Minister K. Jegadeshwari expanded it to persons with disabilities and their companions with a UDID card. However, as there has been no G.O. published in this regard, men with disabilities continue to wait to avail themselves of the scheme.

Nethrodaya founder C. Govindakrishnan said, “The G.O. for free bus travel for persons with disabilities has not been issued even after 53 days of the announcement. This inordinate delay has prevented eligible persons with disabilities from availing the free travel in government buses.”

Jhansi Rani, State general secretary of Tamil Nadu Association for the Rights of All Types of Differently Abled and Caregivers, said the scheme is important as women with disabilities might be accompanied by male caregivers. “In this regard, they would be made to pay for their travel, increasing their expenses. Further, persons with disabilities are usually not allowed to go out due to the extra financial expenses, the delay in the G.O. to include men with disabilities adds to their reduced travel,” she said.

Govindakrishnan pointed out that a proposal to the Welfare of the Differently Abled Department Secretary was forwarded only on September 16.

He also alleged that the Commissioner of the Welfare of the Differently Abled Department had included women with disabilities in the proposal, when they were already covered in the scheme. “The proposal submitted by the Commissioner should have recommended free bus travel exclusively for men with disabilities to avoid duplication of beneficiaries. This has raised concerns about potential duplication and proper utilisation of public funds,” he added.

According to an official in the department, the delay was due to the holidays and the byelections. “The government order for scheme expansion can be expected next week,” the official said.

World.title: Delhi government school student found with severe burn injuries on campus, dies; probe under way
World.content:
A 17-year-old girl was found with severe burn injuries behind the guard room of a government school in east Delhi’s Krishna Nagar on Saturday. The Class 12 student was taken to Dr. Hedgewar Arogya Sansthan, where doctors declared her dead on arrival, the police said.

The incident came to light when school authorities heard cries coming from behind the guard room and went to check. Police said they received a PCR call at 11.57 a.m., following which personnel from Krishna Nagar police station and the fire department reached the spot.

A fire officer, Anoop Singh, said a call was received regarding a student allegedly setting herself on fire inside the school.

The girl’s family said they came to know of her death only around 12.40 p.m.

When the student did not return home by the usual time, her sister-in-law went to the school to look for her.

“No one informed me about the incident. I came to the school searching for her,” the sister-in-law said.

The girl’s sister, who had gone to drop her at school in the morning said, “I had gone to drop her at school and she looked fine. I don’t know what happened after that,” she said.

Police inspected the scene and collected samples for examination. Officials claimed they recovered a three-page note from the girl’s bag.

Police are examining CCTV footage from the school and questioning staff members, teachers and students to establish what happened before the incident.

Delhi Education Minister Ashish Sood visited the school on Saturday evening and spoke to police officers, school authorities and nearby residents.

“The tragic death of a 17-year-old student is deeply distressing and a matter of serious concern,” Mr. Sood said, adding that the school management hashanded over all available evidence to the police.

He said the exact circumstances surrounding the girl’s death could be established only after the investigation is complete.

“Our priority is to ensure a fair and thorough investigation so that all facts related to the incident come to light,” the Minister said. “Necessary action will be taken on the basis of the investigation findings.”

(With inputs from PTI)
